1. Don't die young

43 entries

This section covers three things: accidental and injury deaths — car crashes, fires, poisoning; the handful of vaccines and screenings with the hardest evidence behind them; and the body signals that mean you should go get checked. The numbers in the Benefit column come from randomly assigned trials, from studies that tracked large groups of people for many years, or from official statistics. The Cost column is the author's rough estimate at market prices — useful for comparing entries against each other, not for citing. Entries in this section are grouped by theme, with item numbers in parentheses. On the road: buckle up (item 1), wear a helmet (item 2), no speeding or drunk driving (item 9), child safety seats (item 10). Fire, gas, and electricity at home: install smoke alarms (item 3), replace gas hoses when they expire (item 4), never bring e-bikes into stairwells (item 6), keep fire extinguishers and a first-aid kit (item 26), fit the guard before using an angle grinder (item 42). Accidents involving children, the elderly, and the outdoors: window limit locks (item 11), never take your eyes off children near water (item 12), balance training after 60 (item 13), don't eat wild mushrooms (item 5), don't pick up metal objects of unknown origin (item 36), measure ice thickness before stepping onto wild ice (item 41). Vaccines: get your hepatitis B surface markers checked (item 14), tetanus (item 15), the HPV vaccine (item 16), the flu vaccine (item 20), the shingles vaccine (item 21), the pneumococcal vaccine (item 22). Screening and check-ups: measure blood pressure (item 7), fasting glucose (item 8), breast cancer screening (item 17), cervical cancer screening (item 18), colorectal cancer screening (item 19), test for *H. pylori* (item 23), low-dose chest CT (item 24), bone density scans (item 39), osteoporosis drugs (item 40). Body signals and sexual health: visible blood in urine (item 27), check your heart before treating erectile problems (item 28), losing weight and quitting smoking improve erections (item 29), condoms and never sharing needles (item 30), get tested for HIV (item 31), PrEP (item 38). Psychological crises: call 12356 if you're thinking about suicide (item 25), tell one person first if you're suicidal (item 32), gambling until you borrow to keep gambling (item 37), the cost of surviving pesticide ingestion or gas inhalation (item 33), the cost of surviving a fall from height (item 34), the cost of living with one kidney (item 35), ask people directly whether they've thought about suicide (item 43).

1

Buckle up — front seat and back

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Wearing a seat belt in the front seat roughly halves your chance of being killed in a crash. In the front of a light truck it drops by about 60%. Of the people who died in cars in the US in 2022 and whose belt use could be determined, half were unbuckled.

Cost
Free. 2 extra seconds every time you get in a car.
Benefit
NHTSA, the US road-safety authority, estimates that seat belts reduce the risk of fatal injury for front-seat car occupants by 45%. For the front of a light truck, by 60%. Among people killed in passenger cars in the US in 2022 whose belt use could be determined, 50% were unrestrained. WHO's figure is that seat belts reduce the risk of death for vehicle occupants by up to 50%. WHO estimates 248,099 road-traffic deaths in China in 2021 — 17.4 per 100,000 people
Note
Buckle up in the back too. In the same report, 60% of those killed in second-row seats were unbuckled. The 45% and 60% figures are estimates NHTSA computed from crash databases (citing Kahane 2015), not randomized trials. WHO's China death toll is a modeled estimate, several times higher than what traffic police registered. The two count different things; this book uses WHO's figure.
Sources (3 references)
NHTSA (2024). Occupant Protection in Passenger Vehicles: 2022 Data (DOT HS 813 573). https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPublication… ; WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traff… ; WHO GHO RS_196/RS_198 (China, 2021). https://ghoapi.azureedge.net/api/RS_196?$filter=SpatialDim%…
2

Wear a helmet on motorcycles and e-bikes — and fasten the strap

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A helmet with the strap fastened cuts a motorcyclist's risk of dying in a crash by roughly 40%, and head injuries by about 70%. Fasten the strap tight — a helmet dangling loose on your head doesn't count as worn.

Cost
100–300 yuan for a helmet. 5 seconds to put it on.
Benefit
A Cochrane review pooled multiple studies: helmeted motorcyclists had a 42% lower risk of death. Original value OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.68. Head injuries down 69% (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.38)
Note
The strap must be fastened — a helmet hanging from the handlebar doesn't count. The data above come from motorcycles. There is no direct research on e-bikes; the numbers are extrapolated, because the way heads get injured in a collision is the same.
Sources (1 references)
Liu BC et al. (2008). Helmets for preventing injury in motorcycle riders. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004333.pub3
3

Install a smoke alarm; if you burn coal or use gas heaters indoors in winter, add a carbon monoxide alarm

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A working smoke alarm cuts your chance of dying in a house fire by around 60%. In two out of five fatal fires the residents were asleep — your nose alone won't wake you. If you burn coal or use gas for heating in winter, add a carbon monoxide alarm. In 2018, 11,500 people in China died of CO poisoning; in the three winter months, seven in ten of those deaths happened at home.

Cost
A smoke alarm runs 30–100 yuan; a CO alarm 50–150 yuan. Replace the battery once a year after installation.
Benefit
A North Carolina study of residential fires compared households where a fire happened with those where it didn't. A working smoke alarm in the home cut the risk of death by about 60%. Original value OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.83. In US occupied-home fatal fires from 2018 to 2020, 24% of homes had no smoke alarm, and in 41% someone was asleep when the fire started. China reported 11,523 deaths from carbon monoxide poisoning in 2018. Of those deaths, 72.59% in December, 67.42% in January, and 66.48% in February occurred at home
Note
Why only B: for smoke alarms there is just this one study, which worked backwards by comparing households that had fires with those that didn't — not a randomized trial. For CO alarms themselves there is no study showing reduced mortality. The benefit here is inferred from the fact that poisoning deaths cluster in winter and at home.
Sources (3 references)
Marshall SW et al. (1998). Fatal residential fires: who dies and who survives? JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.279.20.1633 ; USFA (2022). Fatal Fires in Residential Buildings (2018-2020), Topical Fire Report Series 22(2). https://www.usfa.fema.gov/downloads/pdf/statistics/v22i2.pdf ; You J et al. (2020). Number of Deaths due to Carbon Monoxide Poisoning by Month and by Place of Death — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly. https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2020.008
4

Replace gas hoses and stoves when they expire; never modify pipes yourself; you can turn away door-to-door "gas company" salesmen

Grade CValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A compliant hose costs a few dozen yuan. Replacing it on time is a legal obligation written into China's Urban Gas Management Regulations. Modifying pipes or removing your gas meter yourself is explicitly banned by the same regulations. They also say a gas company cannot require you to buy its designated products or services. When someone shows up at your door saying you "must" buy something, you can simply refuse.

Cost
A compliant gas hose costs a few dozen yuan. Stoves need replacing every few years. When you swap one, glance at whether the other is past its date.
Benefit
The regulations make "promptly replacing gas-burning appliances and connecting hoses that the state has ordered phased out or that have reached the end of their service life" a user obligation: once your stove or hose hits its limit or is phased out, you must replace it. The regulations also list "installing, altering, or removing in-home gas facilities and gas metering devices without authorization" among prohibited acts — DIY pipe changes and meter removal included. They further state that gas suppliers may not require users to buy products they designate, nor to accept services they provide
Note
The regulation text can be checked word for word, but it only establishes that replacing hoses on time is your obligation — not how many accidents timely replacement prevents. No official statistic was found for how much on-schedule hose replacement reduces gas accidents, hence Grade C. Some people come to your door in the name of a "safety inspection" and finish by selling self-closing valves and alarms. Clause 20(6) forbids gas companies from requiring you to buy their designated products — you can refuse, and you can complain. If you smell gas: first shut the main gas valve (for bottled gas, the cylinder valve). Then open doors and windows to ventilate — don't switch on the exhaust fan. Don't turn lights or the range hood on or off, and keep lighters away. Then leave, and only call the gas company's emergency line once you're away from the scene. Carbon monoxide poisoning is a separate matter — see Section 13.
Sources (3 references)
国务院 (2010). 城镇燃气管理条例（国务院令第 583 号）第二十七条：「燃气用户应当遵守安全用气规则，使用合格的燃气燃烧器具和气瓶，及时更换国家明令淘汰或者使用年限已届满的燃气燃烧器具、连接管等」；第二十八条禁止行为含「（一）擅自操作公用燃气阀门」「（二）将燃气管道作为负重支架或者接地引线」「（四）擅自安装、改装、拆除户内燃气设施和燃气计量装置」；第二十条燃气经营者不得「（六）要求燃气用户购买其指定的产品或者接受其提供的服务」；第二十九条用户可就收费、服务向燃气管理等部门投诉，「有关部门应当自收到投诉之日起15个工作日内予以处理」. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2010/content_1758214.htm；深圳市住房和建设局 (2024). 安全用气小知识（二）：「立即关闭家里的燃气总阀门」「迅速开门、开窗进行通风」「一定不要开、关家里的电灯、抽油烟机等电器」「人员应该迅速撤离，转移到安全的地方，并且及时拨打燃气公司的报警电话」. https://zjj.sz.gov.cn/zcjzts/content/post_11882410.html；张家港市应急管理局 (2024). 燃气安全使用知识：「不要情急之下打开排气扇进行通风」「应远离现场之后才能打电话求助」. https://www.zjg.gov.cn/zjgszwz/yjaqzs/202411/72b4fad7399c48…
5

Don't pick, buy, or eat wild mushrooms — no folk test works

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

In 2025 alone there were 828 mushroom-poisoning outbreaks across China, 2,165 people poisoned, 13 dead. That same year, 34 species never before recorded as poisonous in China were newly identified. The silver-needle test, "bugs ate it so it's safe," "only colorful ones are toxic" — none of these hold up.

Cost
Free. The hard part is giving up a seasonal wild delicacy.
Benefit
China CDC investigated 828 mushroom-poisoning incidents in 2025, involving 2,165 people and 13 deaths — a case fatality rate of 0.6%, meaning 0.6% of those poisoned died. From 2019 to 2024 there were 276–676 incidents per year, with case fatality between 0.87% and 2.86%. In 2025 alone, 138 poisonous mushroom species were identified, 34 of them recorded for the first time as causing poisoning in China
Note
If you eat the wrong mushroom, vomit immediately, then get to a hospital taking the leftover mushrooms or photos of them. Mushroom poisoning comes in several distinct types, and identifying which mushroom you ate directly determines how doctors treat you. New poisonous species are recorded every year, so "the locals know which ones are safe" doesn't hold up as an assumption. The silver-needle test, boiling with garlic, "bugs ate it so it's fine," "only colorful ones are toxic" — none of these hold up.
Sources (2 references)
Mushroom Poisoning Outbreaks — China, 2025. China CDC Weekly (2026): "In 2025, China CDC investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents across 27 provincial-level administrative divisions (PLADs), affecting 2,165 individuals and causing 13 deaths - a case fatality rate of 0.6%, the lowest of the past six years. In total, 138 poisonous mushroom species were identified, including 34 newly recorded in poisoning incidents in China." "From 2019 to 2024, the annual number of incidents ranged from 276 to 676, and the case fatality rate ranged from 0.87% to 2.86%." https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2026.120；同刊 2024 年度报告 https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2025.106
6

Never bring an e-bike into the stairwell or elevator, and never charge it at home

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Wheeling an e-bike into a stairwell or elevator, or charging it at home, is explicitly banned by the Fire Safety Regulations for High-Rise Civil Buildings issued by the Ministry of Emergency Management. Individuals who don't comply face fines of 500–1,000 yuan; businesses, 2,000–10,000 yuan. The fine is the small thing — the point is that this kind of fire burns right across your only escape route.

Cost
Free. The hard part is always using the shared charging point downstairs — a few dozen extra meters of walking.
Benefit
The ministry's regulation states in so many words: "Parking electric bicycles in, or charging electric bicycles at, the public lobbies, evacuation walkways, stairwells, or emergency exits of high-rise civil buildings is prohibited." Lobbies, corridors, stairwells, and emergency exits — no parking and no charging in any of them. Those who refuse to correct it face fines of 500–1,000 yuan for individuals and non-business units, 2,000–10,000 yuan for businesses
Note
Don't buy modified batteries, don't use no-name chargers, don't charge overnight unattended. Once a lithium battery ignites, it flashes over within seconds while giving off highly toxic smoke. A bike parked in a stairwell that catches fire burns right across your only escape route. The Ministry of Emergency Management's published figures: 18,000 e-bike fires nationwide in 2021, 65 deaths. Of those, 3,782 fires were inside buildings, killing 60 — nearly all of the dead indoors. After the 2024 crackdown, fires fell 42.2% year-on-year and casualties by more than 90%; the absolute counts for that year were not published.
Sources (3 references)
应急管理部 (2021). 高层民用建筑消防安全管理规定（应急管理部令第 5 号，第三十七条、第四十七条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/01/content_562…；应急管理部 (2023). 关于政协第十三届全国委员会第五次会议第00969号提案答复的函：「2021年，全国共接报电动自行车火灾1.8万起，造成65人死亡、222人受伤，直接财产损失达2.21亿元，其中发生在建筑物内3782起，造成60人死亡、175人受伤」. https://www.mem.gov.cn/gk/jytabljggk/zxwytadfzy/2022zx/2023…；应急管理部 (2025). 2025年1月15日新闻发布会：「火灾起数同比下降42.2%，伤亡人数下降超过90%」. https://www.mem.gov.cn/xw/xwfbh/2025n01y15xwfbh_6337/
7

Measure your blood pressure; if it's high, take medication and get it to target

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

For every 10 mmHg your blood pressure comes down, your chance of a major cardiovascular event drops by about a fifth, stroke by 27%, heart failure by 28%, and death by 13%. Among Chinese people aged 35–75, 44.7% have high blood pressure; only 7.2% have it under control.

Cost
An electronic blood-pressure monitor costs 100–200 yuan; 1 reading takes 1 minute. Most blood-pressure pills run a few to a few dozen yuan a month. The hard part is keeping taking them when you feel nothing.
Benefit
Pooled across 123 trials and over 610,000 people. For every 10 mmHg drop in systolic pressure, major cardiovascular events fall by about a fifth. Original value RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.77 to 0.83. Systolic is the higher of the two numbers in a blood-pressure reading. Stroke (brain attack) down about 27% (RR 0.73). Heart failure down about 28% (RR 0.72). All-cause mortality down 13% (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.84 to 0.91). China screened 1.7 million people aged 35–75: 44.7% had hypertension. Of those, 44.7% knew it, 30.1% were on treatment, and only 7.2% had it controlled
Note
Go get one blood-pressure reading first. Fewer than 1 in 10 Chinese people with hypertension have it controlled, so that single reading is one of the highest-value moves in this book. What counts as "at target" (130 or 140) is still debated, but "knowing you have high blood pressure and bringing it down" is not.
Sources (2 references)
Ettehad D et al. (2016). Blood pressure lowering for prevention of cardiovascular disease and death: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Lancet. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)01225-8 ; Lu J et al. (2017). Prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension in China (China PEACE Million Persons Project). Lancet. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32478-9
8

If you're over 35 and overweight, get a fasting glucose test once — and every three years even if normal

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

For a few dozen yuan and one tube of blood, you can catch prediabetes before any symptoms exist. The official US screening advice: people aged 35–70 who are overweight or obese should get tested. If normal, retest every three years. The US counts overweight from BMI 25, relaxed to 23 for Asians; China's standard counts from 24.

Cost
A fasting glucose test costs a dozen-odd yuan; an HbA1c a few dozen. One blood draw at a clinic.
Benefit
The US Preventive Services Task Force is the official US body for screening recommendations. Its current advice: screen overweight or obese adults aged 35–70 for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, even with no symptoms at all. Overweight means BMI ≥25, obesity ≥30. For Asian Americans it suggests lowering the line to BMI ≥23, because at the same BMI, Asians carry higher diabetes risk. China's industry standard: BMI 24.0 to under 28.0 counts as overweight, ≥28.0 as obesity. This recommendation carries grade B. It also states: "for adults with normal blood glucose, screening every 3 years is a reasonable approach"
Note
A prediabetes finding doesn't mean you're headed for medication. A good share of people turn it around with lifestyle changes alone. Among Chinese adults, those who know they have diabetes have always been the minority — many find out only when a complication arrives
Sources (2 references)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2021). Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes. https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recomm…："at a lower BMI (≥23) if the patient is Asian American"；国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2024). 居民体重管理核心知识（2024 年版）释义：「根据《成年人体重判定》（WS/T 428-2013）行业标准……24.0≤BMI＜28.0 为超重，BMI≥28.0 为肥胖」. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202407/P02024070348151…
9

No speeding, no drunk driving

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Every 1% higher average speed raises the chance of a fatal crash by about 4%. There is no "a little is fine" line for alcohol. Risk starts climbing while blood alcohol is still very low.

Cost
Free. Driving a bit slower adds minutes to a trip. The hard part is drinking less at dinners.
Benefit
WHO's statement: every 1% increase in average speed raises the risk of an injury-crash by 4%. Drunk-driving risk starts rising from very low blood-alcohol concentrations
Note
The 1%/4% speed-death pairing comes from crash modeling, not randomized trials. For alcohol, WHO gives only direction, no numbers. "How much drinking raises risk by how much" — the original literature behind that was not verified for this entry.
Sources (1 references)
WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traff…
10

Use a child safety seat for children under 4 — don't hold them in your arms

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: highTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Infants under one in a safety seat are about 70% less likely to suffer a fatal injury in a crash. Children aged 1–4, about half. Holding them in your arms achieves nothing — you cannot hold on during a hard stop.

Cost
300–2,000 yuan, usable for several years. 1 extra minute per trip to strap the child in.
Benefit
NHTSA, the US road-safety authority, estimates that child safety seats reduce the risk of fatal injury by 71% for infants under 1 in passenger cars, and by 54% for children aged 1–4. WHO's figure is a 71% reduction in infant deaths
Note
Install the seat exactly per the manual — a wrongly installed seat is as bad as none. Under age 1 it must face backward, toward the rear of the car. The numbers above are estimates computed by US authorities from crash data.
Sources (2 references)
NHTSA (2024). Occupant Protection in Passenger Vehicles: 2022 Data (DOT HS 813 573). https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPublication… ; WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traff…
11

If you have small children, fit window limit locks and balcony guards — a screen is not a barrier

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A set of limiters costs a few dozen yuan. New York City handed out free window guards to high-risk households with home visits to explain them, and reported child falls in one borough halved within three years. New York later simply legislated that landlords must install guards in apartments where children live. A window screen pushes open with one hand — it's not protection.

Cost
A set of window limiters or childproof locks costs a few dozen yuan; ten minutes to install.
Benefit
Starting in 1972, New York City ran a program called "Children Can't Fly," distributing free window guards in high-risk neighborhoods along with door-to-door explanation. Reported falls in the Bronx dropped 50% between 1973 and 1975. New York City subsequently amended its health code to require landlords to install window guards in apartments where children aged 10 and younger live
Note
Keep beds, sofas, and boxes — anything a child can climb — away from windows and balconies. A screen stops mosquitoes, not children; it pops out with a push, so don't treat it as a guard. And it's not just high-rise dwellers: in that US dataset, most falls were from the second story or lower.
Sources (2 references)
Spiegel CN, Lindaman FC (1977). Children can't fly: a program to prevent childhood morbidity and mortality from window falls. American Journal of Public Health: "Significant reduction in falls resulted, particularly in the Bronx, where reported falls declined 50 percent from 1973 to 1975"，1976 年纽约市卫生法典修订 "to require that landlords provide window guards in apartments where children ten years old and younger reside". https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.67.12.1143；(2021). Unintentional Window Falls in Children and Adolescents. Academic Pediatrics：2007 年 1 月至 2017 年 8 月全国电子伤害监测系统 38,840 例急诊就诊，"The majority of falls occurred in children under the age of 6 and were related to falls from a second story or below". https://doi.org/10.1016/j.acap.2020.07.008
12

Never take your eyes off children near water; wear life jackets when boating or swimming in the wild

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Wearing a life jacket when you end up in the water roughly halves your chance of drowning. Drowning is still the leading cause of death for Chinese children aged 1–14. Rural drowning mortality is about double the urban rate.

Cost
A life jacket costs 50–200 yuan. The other price is the attention spent watching the child.
Benefit
A study using US Coast Guard data matched similar people into pairs for comparison. Among recreational boaters who fell overboard, those wearing life jackets had roughly half the drowning-death risk. Original value adjusted RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.74. Drowning mortality among Chinese under 20 fell from 6.60 per 100,000 in 2013 to 3.28 per 100,000 in 2021. The rural rate is about twice the urban one. Drowning remains the top killer of children aged 1–14. Of injury deaths at ages 0–19 in 2021, drowning accounted for 31.1% and road traffic 27.9%
Note
The Grade A applies to the life-jacket half only. "Never out of sight" is consensus but on its own would be Grade C — no randomized trial, and there never will be. Drowning deaths in China cluster in rural areas, in summer, and among boys aged 15–19. For playing on ice in winter, see item 41 (measure wild ice thickness first).
Sources (3 references)

China CDC Weekly. https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2024.057
13

If you're over 60, train balance and leg strength, and retrofit your bathroom and stairs

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: large

2–3 balance sessions a week — tai chi, say — cut older people's falls by about 23%, and the number of people who fell by 15%. Anti-slip work and grab bars at home cut falls by another fifth or so. Falls are the leading injury-related cause of death for Chinese people over 65, and more than half of them happen inside the person's own home.

Cost
2–3 30-minute sessions a week of tai chi or balance training. Non-slip mats, grab bars, and night lights for the bathroom run a few dozen to a few hundred yuan. The hard part is keeping it up long-term.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled 108 trials with 23,407 people. Exercise reduced the rate of falls in older adults by 23%. Original value rate ratio RaR 0.77, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.83. The number of people who fell dropped 15% (RR 0.85). Having a professional do a home safety assessment and modifications cut the fall rate by about a fifth (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.97). Tai chi specifically: fall risk down about 29% (RR 0.71). In China, falls are the top injury-related cause of death in people over 65. Of monitored falls among older people in 2018, 55.97% happened at home
Note
This entry is for people over 60 living in their own homes, not in care institutions. The studies above count falls, not deaths. From a fall to a hip fracture to death, the road is short for an older person. Poor vision also causes falls — for cataracts affecting navigation, see Section 17, item 9 (cataract surgery). For older people pulled down while walking a dog, see Section 17, item 10 (dog walking). For whether your bones can take a fall, see item 39 in this section (bone density scans).
Sources (3 references)
Sherrington C et al. (2019). Exercise for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012424.pub2 ; Gillespie LD et al. (2012). Interventions for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007146.pub3 ; Lu Z et al. (2021). Characteristics of Falls Among Older People — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly. https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2021.013
14

Get your hepatitis B panel checked; if you have no antibodies, get vaccinated

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

One test, a few dozen yuan. In the Qidong trial that ran 30 years, people vaccinated against hepatitis B at birth were 84% less likely to develop primary liver cancer later, and 72% less likely to carry the virus. Adults who test negative for antibodies get three catch-up shots over six months, one or two hundred yuan.

Cost
The test is a few dozen yuan. The adult vaccine is 3 shots totaling 100–300 yuan, completed within half a year.
Benefit
The Qidong trial randomized by community rather than individual and followed people for 30 years. Neonatal hepatitis B vaccination cut primary liver cancer by 84%, with 95% CI 23% to 97%. HBsAg positivity — the share of people testing as carrying the virus — fell 72% (95% CI 68% to 75%). Across the whole Chinese population, HBsAg positivity fell 52% from 1992 to 2014, and by 97% in children under 5
Note
This entry is for adults born before 1992 who were never vaccinated or whose antibodies have faded. The 84% liver-cancer figure comes from people vaccinated at birth. In the same trial, those who caught up as adolescents had only 21% protection against carrying the virus. For adults, the point of vaccination is avoiding new infection — don't directly apply that 84%. If you're already infected, the vaccine does nothing; go to a hepatology clinic for regular follow-up. "Already infected" means the HBsAg line on your lab report reads positive.
Sources (2 references)
Qu C et al. (2014). Efficacy of neonatal HBV vaccination on liver cancer and other liver diseases over 30-year follow-up of the Qidong hepatitis B intervention study. PLoS Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1001774 ; Cui F et al. (2017). Prevention of Chronic Hepatitis B after 3 Decades of Escalating Vaccination Policy, China. Emerging Infectious Diseases. https://doi.org/10.3201/eid2305.161477
15

Stepped on a nail or splinter, or got dirt in a wound? Deal with it the same day, and ask about a tetanus shot

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Once tetanus takes hold, roughly 1 in 10 dies. Deep wounds and dirt-contaminated wounds carry the highest risk. For a dirty wound more than 5 years past your last shot, you need 1 booster. Getting it handled the same day costs a few dozen yuan — don't wait for the wound to swell.

Cost
Registration plus wound care runs a few dozen yuan. If the doctor advises it, vaccine or immunoglobulin adds a few dozen to a few hundred.
Benefit
About 1 in 10 US tetanus cases is fatal. Deep wounds and wounds contaminated with soil are higher-risk. China's 2024 clinical guidelines split wounds into two tiers. A shallow wound treated within 6 hours with no contact with soil, feces, or animal saliva is low-risk. Treated more than 6 hours later, contaminated with any of those, or a puncture, avulsion, crush, burn, frostbite, or a wound with something left inside — high-risk. If you've had 3+ doses with the last within 5 years, nothing is needed. Past 5–10 years, high-risk wounds call for 1 booster. Past 10 years, 1 booster regardless of tier. If you haven't completed 3 doses or can't remember, complete the vaccine series — and for high-risk wounds also get passive immunization (immunoglobulin or antitoxin, i.e., an injection of ready-made antibodies)
Note
Let the doctor at the hospital decide — don't make the call yourself, and don't skip asking out of laziness. Not every wound needs a shot. The doctor grades the wound, asks when your last shot was, then decides. "Vaccinated as a kid means covered for life" is wrong. For dirty wounds, a booster is due once 5 years have passed since your last shot. So before you go, try to recall the year you last had a tetanus shot.
Sources (3 references)
美国疾病控制与预防中心. 破伤风："Tetanus bacteria can get into someone's body through broken skin, usually through injuries." "Tetanus can lead to death (1 in 10 cases in the United States are fatal)." "People who didn't complete the primary series or who aren't up to date with their 10-year tetanus booster shots are also at increased risk." "Vaccination also helps prevent tetanus in people with wounds, depending on their tetanus vaccination history." https://www.cdc.gov/tetanus/about/index.html；国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2024). 关于印发非新生儿破伤风诊疗规范（2024 年版）的通知（国卫办医急函〔2024〕381 号，风险分级见附件第 16 页，表 4 见第 20 页）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6982262…；附件 PDF（扫描件）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/P02024102348342…
16

Women: get the HPV vaccine, the earlier the better

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: highTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In Swedish data on 1.67 million women, those vaccinated against HPV before 17 later developed invasive cervical cancer at about one-eighth the rate of the unvaccinated. Even vaccinated at 17–30, only about half the rate. Earlier is worth more.

Cost
The domestic two-valent runs just over 300 yuan a dose; the imported nine-valent about 1,300. 2–3 doses in total, half a day each trip.
Benefit
Sweden followed 1.67 million women statistically: the vaccinated had lower invasive cervical cancer incidence than the unvaccinated. Vaccinated before 17: about 88% lower (IRR 0.12, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.34 — the parentheses give the original value and its confidence interval). Vaccinated at 17–30: about 53% lower (IRR 0.47, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.75)
Note
Ages 9–14 get the most benefit. At 17–30, more than half the reduction remains. After 30 the benefit shrinks steadily. Even vaccinated, you still need cervical cancer screening — the vaccine doesn't replace it; see item 18 (cervical cancer screening for women over 30).
Sources (1 references)
Lei J et al. (2020). HPV Vaccination and the Risk of Invasive Cervical Cancer. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1917338

Women: start breast cancer screening at 40, with a mammogram every two years

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

A mammogram every two years for women aged 40–74 is what the official US screening recommendation explicitly endorses. For those over 75, and for adding ultrasound or MRI for dense breasts, the official verdict is that evidence is still insufficient. When a checkup package charges extra for those, you can skip them.

Cost
A mammogram runs 200–300 yuan each time; many regions have free screening programs. Half a day every two years.
Benefit
The US Preventive Services Task Force is the official US body for screening recommendations. Its current advice: "recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years." Screening mammography is the ordinary mammogram. This recommendation carries grade B. For women 75 and older, and for supplementing ultrasound or MRI for dense breasts, it ruled the evidence insufficient
Note
Starting ages differ by country; some Chinese guidelines and local programs start at 45. Those whose parents, children, or siblings had breast cancer, and BRCA mutation carriers, are high-risk and need an individual plan from a doctor — this entry doesn't apply to them
Sources (1 references)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2024). Breast Cancer: Screening. https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recomm…

Women over 30: cervical cancer screening, HPV testing first

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In that rural-India trial, women screened for HPV just once in their lives were about half as likely to die of cervical cancer, and about half as likely to be found with late-stage cervical cancer. One or two hundred yuan, one visit, and a negative result holds for 5 years.

Cost
An HPV test runs 100–300 yuan. With a negative result, once every 5 years is enough. Sampling takes minutes.
Benefit
The rural-India trial randomized by community, not individual, covering women aged 30–59. A single round of HPV screening cut the risk of dying of cervical cancer by about 48%. Original value HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.83. The risk of being found with advanced cervical cancer fell about 53% (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.69)
Note
People who've had the HPV vaccine still need screening, because the vaccine doesn't cover every viral type. What makes this study rare: it was a randomized screening trial that used deaths as the outcome, and it screened only one round.
Sources (1 references)
Sankaranarayanan R et al. (2009). HPV screening for cervical cancer in rural India. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0808516

From 45–50, screen for colorectal cancer: a fecal immunochemical test, or a colonoscopy

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

A few dozen yuan for a stool occult-blood test every year or two cuts your chance of dying of colorectal cancer by about 16%; those who complete at least one round, by 25%. People invited for one colonoscopy saw their 10-year colorectal cancer rate go from 1.20% to 0.98%.

Cost
The stool test costs a few dozen yuan every 1–2 years. A colonoscopy runs several hundred to over a thousand; with a clean result, once per 10 years. Budget a day for bowel prep beforehand.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled multiple studies. Fecal occult-blood screening cut colorectal cancer death risk by about 16%. Original value RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.90. Those completing at least one round: about 25% lower (RR 0.75). Then the NordICC randomized trial: those invited for colonoscopy saw 10-year colorectal cancer incidence fall from 1.20% to 0.98%. Original value RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70 to 0.93
Note
Contested. NordICC counts "invited to colonoscopy": colorectal cancer deaths 0.28% vs 0.31% (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.16), a difference still within the margin of error. That suggests colonoscopy's mortality benefit was previously overestimated. The stool test actually has harder evidence on mortality. Starting ages vary by guideline between 45 and 50. Anyone with an affected close relative should start earlier.
Sources (2 references)
Hewitson P et al. (2007). Screening for colorectal cancer using the faecal occult blood test, Hemoccult. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001216.pub2 ; Bretthauer M et al. (2022). Effect of Colonoscopy Screening on Risks of Colorectal Cancer and Related Death. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2208375

People with cardiovascular disease and older adults: a flu shot every year

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In the post-heart-attack flu vaccine trial, the one-year death rate fell from 4.9% to 2.9%. People with cardiovascular disease and older adults: one shot each autumn, 50–150 yuan.

Cost
50–150 yuan a dose, once each autumn.
Benefit
A trial after myocardial infarction randomized 2,571 people; neither doctors nor patients knew who got which injection. Flu vaccine: 2.9% all-cause mortality over 12 months. Placebo: 4.9%. Original value HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.89. A placebo is a comparison injection with no active ingredient. Cardiovascular death HR 0.59. A separate pooled analysis: major cardiovascular events 3.6% with flu vaccine vs 5.4% without. Original value RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.83. Cardiovascular death RR 0.74 (95% CI 0.42 to 1.30 — still within the margin of error, so not statistically significant)
Note
Contested. The Grade A applies to people with cardiovascular disease. For healthy older adults, the Cochrane review offers only one finding: flu incidence in a season fell from 6% to 2.4%. It rates that evidence "low" certainty, and "very low" for mortality. The review is Demicheli V et al., 2018.
Sources (3 references)
Fröbert O et al. (2021). Influenza Vaccination After Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Trial. Circulation. https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.121.057042 ; Behrouzi B et al. (2022). Association of Influenza Vaccination With Cardiovascular Risk: A Meta-analysis. JAMA Network Open. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.8873；Demicheli V et al. (2018). Vaccines for preventing influenza in the elderly. Get the shingles vaccine after 50

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: highTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In phase-3 trials the vaccine blocked 97% of shingles, about evenly across age groups. The catch: two doses at 3,000–4,000 yuan, all self-paid. What that money buys is a 97% reduction in incidence.

Cost
The recombinant shingles vaccine is two doses, about 3,000–4,000 yuan in total. Entirely out of pocket.
Benefit
A phase-3 trial across 18 countries enrolled 15,400 people, randomized to vaccine or a control injection, followed for 3.2 years on average. Result: 6 shingles cases in the vaccine group, 210 in placebo. That converts to 0.3 vs 9.1 per 1,000 person-years — per 1,000 person-years meaning the cases arising among 1,000 people observed for one year. The paper states "the overall vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster was 97.2% (95% CI 93.7–99.0, P<0.001)." Efficacy by age group ran from 96.6% to 97.9%
Note
It ranks low on value for one reason: price. Shingles itself is rarely deadly — the trouble is post-herpetic neuralgia, which can hurt for months to years. After the shot, injection-site pain and fever are both common; the severest tier (grade-3 symptoms) was 17.0% vs 3.2%
Sources (1 references)
Lal H, Cunningham AL, Godeaux O, et al. (2015). Efficacy of an adjuvanted herpes zoster subunit vaccine in older adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(22), 2087-2096. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184
22

Get the pneumococcal vaccine after 65

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In a trial of 84,500 older adults, the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine blocked about 46% of pneumonia caused by the types it covers, and 75% of the most dangerous invasive infections. But it showed no effect on "pneumonia from all causes" — don't expect it to cover all pneumonia.

Cost
A few hundred yuan; free for older adults in some regions.
Benefit
The Netherlands randomized 84,500 people over 65 to compare, using the 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. Efficacy against vaccine-type pneumonia: 45.6%, with 95.2% CI 21.8–62.5. "Vaccine-type" means the bacterial strains this vaccine covers. Against invasive pneumococcal disease — the most dangerous class of infection — efficacy was 75.0% (95% CI 41.4–90.8). Against pneumonia from all causes combined, it showed no effect
Note
It only protects against covered serotypes — being vaccinated doesn't mean never getting pneumonia. What Chinese older adults commonly get is the 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine, not the 13-valent conjugate used in this trial; the efficacy numbers above don't transfer directly
Sources (1 references)
Bonten MJ, Huijts SM, Bolkenbaas M, et al. (2015). Polysaccharide conjugate vaccine against pneumococcal pneumonia in adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(12), 1114-1125. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1408544

Test for Helicobacter pylori; if positive, eradicate it

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

In the Shandong Linqu trial that ran 22 years, people who eradicated H. pylori were about half as likely to later develop stomach cancer, and about 40% less likely to die of it. One test at one or two hundred yuan; eradication is two weeks of pills.

Cost
A carbon-13 or carbon-14 breath test costs 100–200 yuan. Eradication means four drugs at once; two weeks of medication runs 200–500 yuan. The hard part is taking all of them on schedule for those two weeks.
Benefit
The randomized Linqu trial in Shandong followed people for 22 years. Those who received H. pylori eradication therapy had about half the risk of developing stomach cancer. Original value OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.71. Risk of dying of stomach cancer fell about 38% (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.99)
Note
Reinfection after eradication is possible, so have the whole household tested and treated together. The trial population lived in a high-stomach-cancer region; people in low-incidence areas gain much less in practice.
Sources (1 references)
Li WQ et al. (2019). Effects of Helicobacter pylori treatment and vitamin and garlic supplementation on gastric cancer incidence and mortality: follow-up of a randomized intervention trial. BMJ. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.l5016

Heavy smokers: a low-dose chest CT once a year

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Eligible heavy smokers getting an annual low-dose CT are 20% less likely to die of lung cancer than with chest X-rays alone, and 6.7% less likely to die overall. The price is follow-up testing after suspicious findings, and the worry in between.

Cost
200–400 yuan per scan, 10 minutes. Add the follow-ups after a scare, and the anxiety of those weeks.
Benefit
The US NLST randomized trial enrolled 53,454 people, all aged 55–74 with a 30-pack-year smoking history who quit no more than 15 years ago. A pack-year is the unit for smoking amount: one pack a day for a year is one pack-year. The results: those screened with low-dose CT had a relative 20.0% drop in lung-cancer death compared with chest X-ray. 95% CI 6.8 to 26.7. All-cause mortality fell a relative 6.7%, 95% CI 1.2 to 13.6
Note
This applies only to high-risk smokers. In the same trial, 24.2% of low-dose CT participants had suspicious findings, and of those, 96.4% were false alarms. For non-smokers, this scan is buying anxiety.
Sources (1 references)
National Lung Screening Trial Research Team (2011). Reduced Lung-Cancer Mortality with Low-Dose Computed Tomographic Screening. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1102873

If you're depressed or thinking about suicide, call 12356; don't stockpile sleeping pills or pesticides at home

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The evidence for removing lethal means from arm's reach keeps strengthening: restricting painkillers cut related suicides by 43%; barriers at frequent jumping spots, 86%. So don't stockpile sleeping pills or pesticides. When things feel unbearable, call 12356 first — it works nationwide, open at least 18 hours a day.

Cost
Free. One phone call. Also: lock the medications away, and don't keep pesticides in the house.
Benefit
A review systematically covering the last 10 years of research: evidence for restricting access to lethal means keeps growing. After painkiller controls, painkiller-related suicides fell 43%. After barriers were installed at frequent jumping sites, 86% (79% to 91%, the parentheses giving the confidence range). School-based cognitive programs cut attempted suicide by about 55% (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.85). Antidepressants and psychotherapy for depression are an important part of suicide prevention. Since May 1, 2025, dialing 12356 anywhere in China reaches a psychological-assistance hotline, open no fewer than 18 hours daily
Note
Why B: the means-restriction evidence is mostly ecological — comparing counts before and after a policy — and there's no mortality evidence for hotlines themselves. Suicidal impulses often last only minutes to hours; moving the lethal thing one step out of reach is itself an intervention. For data on that time scale, and on long-term outcomes after an attempt, see item 32 in this section (tell one person the moment a suicidal thought appears). For what surviving leaves you with, see item 33.
Sources (2 references)
Zalsman G et al. (2016). Suicide prevention strategies revisited: 10-year systematic review. Lancet Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(16)30030-X ; 国家卫生健康委 (2024). 关于应用"12356"全国统一心理援助热线电话号码的通知（国卫医政函〔2024〕259 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6994470…
26

Keep fire extinguisher, fire blanket, escape hood, and first-aid kit; check them yearly

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Fire extinguisher, fire blanket, escape hood, first-aid kit — all are on the Ministry of Emergency Management's 11-item household emergency list. A few hundred yuan, bought once. In studies with in-home safety coaching, injury rates fell by about a quarter.

Cost
Extinguisher, blanket, one hood per person, plus a first-aid kit — a few hundred yuan for the set. One purchase, then ten minutes of checking each year.
Benefit
The ministry's National Basic Household Emergency Supplies List has 11 items. "Fire extinguisher and fire blanket" are for "fighting incipient fires," and the list notes "a fire blanket can be draped over the body to escape." The "breathing hood" means a "fire-filtering self-rescue respirator, for escape from fire." "External medications" means "styptic powder, bandages, gauze, etc., for treating wounds." Cochrane pooled 98 studies, 2,605,044 people. Home-safety interventions brought injury rates to IRR 0.89, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.01. Among interventions delivered by home visits, injury rates fell about 25% (IRR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.91)
Note
Contested. In the same Cochrane pool, interventions that handed out no equipment cut injuries by about a fifth — original value IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.92 — and the groups given equipment didn't do better. What reduces injuries is mainly in-home education and modification, so the equipment's benefit is recorded as "medium," not "large." Buy extinguishers with the CCC mark; on stored-pressure models the gauge needle must sit in the green zone. Fire blankets are mostly fiberglass — grab only the two pull tabs, never the blanket surface barehanded. Using one to smother an oil-pan fire is also contested: in 2014 the Dutch regulator tested 22 brands and none reliably extinguished it when used the way an ordinary person would. For an oil-pan fire, kill the heat first and lid the pan. Smoke and CO alarms: item 3 in this section. Tourniquet use: Section 13, item 12. For how to choose, where to store, and when to replace each item, see [docs/家庭应急装备清单.md](../docs/家庭应急装备清单.md)

27

Blood visible in your urine — even if painless, even if it clears by tomorrow — get checked once

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: small

In people over 60 with one episode of visible blood in the urine, the chance it turns out to be bladder cancer is about 2.8%; at 40–59, about 1.2%. Not a high number — but high enough that you must get checked once. Even if the bleeding stops the next day.

Cost
A urinalysis is a few dozen yuan, a urinary ultrasound one to two hundred. If the doctor deems it necessary, add a cystoscopy, around a thousand.
Benefit
A UK study used electronic records from community general-practice (primary care): 4,915 bladder cancer cases against 21,718 controls. Among those presenting with visible haematuria, the share ultimately diagnosed with bladder cancer: 2.8% at over 60 (95% CI 2.5 to 3.1); 1.2% at 40–59 (0.6 to 2.3). The technical name for this share is the positive predictive value. Haematuria visible only under the microscope matters too: odds ratio 20, 95% CI 12 to 33. At over 60 that share is 1.6%, CI 1.2 to 2.1
Note
"Painless" is the key word. Blood in urine from stones or infection usually comes with flank or abdominal colic, or frequency, urgency, and burning. Tumor bleeding typically has no sensation at all, and stops on its own for days before returning — which is how people let it go. Being on anticoagulants is not a reason to skip the check. After intense exercise, or around a period, retest once before deciding. Benefit is recorded as "small" because we have detection rates, not an effect size for "how much early detection reduces death."
Sources (1 references)
Price SJ, Shephard EA, Stapley SA, Barraclough K, Hamilton WT (2014). Non-visible versus visible haematuria and bladder cancer risk: a study of electronic records in primary care. British Journal of General Practice, 64(626), e584-e589. https://doi.org/10.3399/bjgp14X681409
28

When erections fail, check your heart first — it isn't just "a bedroom matter"

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Men with erectile dysfunction later develop cardiovascular disease about 40% more often than others, and heart attacks about 60% more. The younger you are, the bigger the gap. This problem often shows up before any chest pain. So get blood pressure, glucose, and lipids checked — don't just self-medicate it away.

Cost
Registration is a few dozen yuan. Blood pressure plus glucose and lipid bloodwork, one to two hundred. One hospital trip, results in a few days.
Benefit
A meta-analysis pooled 14 cohort studies, 92,757 men, average follow-up 6.1 years. Compared with men without erectile dysfunction, those with it had these later risks: overall cardiovascular events about 44% higher (RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.27 to 1.63 — the confidence interval). Myocardial infarction about 62% higher (RR 1.62, 1.34 to 1.96). Cerebrovascular events about 39% higher (RR 1.39, 1.23 to 1.57). All-cause death about 25% higher (RR 1.25, 1.12 to 1.39). Cardiovascular death didn't separate significantly (RR 1.19, 0.97 to 1.46). The younger the age, the higher the multiplier. Men at intermediate baseline cardiovascular risk showed higher multipliers than both high- and low-risk men. Studies using questionnaires computed a multiplier of 1.61 (1.38 to 1.86); single-question studies, 1.27 (1.18 to 1.37)
Note
All 14 are cohort studies — following groups and observing outcomes — not randomized trials. So "40% more" is an association, not proven causation. One or two occasional failures don't count; three months of persistence makes it a problem. What to check is the same batch as items 7 and 8: blood pressure, fasting glucose, plus lipids, smoking, and waistline. Don't buy "potency" supplements online. The legitimate drugs in that class are prescription-only; their labels list nitrates as a contraindication — anyone on nitroglycerin-type drugs must not take them, as the combination can crash blood pressure. For how to improve, see item 29 in this section (weight loss and quitting smoking improve erectile function). Benefit recorded as "medium," not "large": 44% is a risk gap between two groups, not "how much death one checkup prevents." Nor "small": a signal like item 27 (visible blood in urine) has only detection rates, whereas the hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia found here all have ready treatments.
Sources (2 references)

Lose weight, quit smoking, control blood pressure and glucose — and erections improve along with them

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: small

Get your cardiovascular risk factors under control, and erectile function improves by itself. On the standard questionnaire, scores rise by 2–3 points on average. That questionnaire tops out at 25; 22 and above counts as normal.

Cost
Free, and possibly money-saving. The hard part is sustaining it: eat less, move more, quit smoking.
Benefit
A meta-analysis pooled 6 randomized controlled trials, 740 men. The interventions were lifestyle change or medication controlling cardiovascular risk factors, with at least 6 weeks of follow-up. Result: erectile function questionnaire (IIEF-5) scores rose 2.66 points on average (95% CI 1.86 to 3.47, the confidence interval). Dropping the 2 statin trials (143 men), the remaining 4 lifestyle-only trials (597 men) still gained 2.40 points (1.19 to 3.61). The IIEF-5 is a 5-question questionnaire scored 5–25. The original paper splits scores into five tiers: 22–25 counts as no dysfunction, 5–7 as severe
Note
The 6 trials used different interventions — some weight loss plus exercise, some medication for blood pressure and lipids. Only 740 men in total. So the direction is clear, but the size of improvement varies by person. Benefit is recorded as "small" because the endpoint was only a questionnaire score, without "fewer diseases later" numbers. The same actions have hard endpoints elsewhere: quitting smoking in Section 2, item 1 (quit smoking, the earlier the better); weight in Section 2, item 32 (keep BMI between 20–25); blood pressure in item 7 of this section (measure it, medicate if high). Medication itself isn't forbidden, provided it's doctor-prescribed. "Health supplements" sold online often smuggle in these ingredients at unknown doses — for how to tell, see Section 28, item 4 (don't buy diet pills promising fast weight loss).

Use a condom every time, start to finish; never share needles

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Using one every time, all the way through, cuts heterosexual HIV transmission by around 70% or more. "Most of the time" works about as poorly as never. Syphilis, gonorrhea, and the rest get blocked too.

Cost
One or two yuan each. The hard part isn't the money — it's using one every single time, and putting it on from the start.
Benefit
One analysis pooled 25 studies, 10,676 heterosexual couples — all couples where one partner had HIV and the other didn't, technically called serodiscordant. Compared with never using condoms, consistent every-time users had about 71% lower HIV transmission risk. Original value RR 0.29, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.43. Compared with inconsistent users, about 77% lower (RR 0.23, 95% CI 0.13 to 0.40). The authors concluded that condoms, while imperfect, "can reduce HIV transmission by 70% or more with consistent use." The same protection covers syphilis, gonorrhea, chlamydia, and other sexually transmitted infections
Note
"Inconsistent use" differs little from "no use" — it takes every time, all the way through, to work. Sharing needles is a separate high-efficiency transmission route, unrelated to sex: injection drug use, tattoos, and piercings all count. High-risk people can also use pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) — taking medication in advance to block infection. Pooling 18 studies, every trial where more than 70% of people took the pills on schedule showed PrEP users about 70% less likely to acquire HIV than placebo. Original value risk ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.45. Trials with poor adherence showed no protection. PrEP is prescription-only — ask at an infectious-disease clinic or the CDC; don't self-order online. For what to do after an exposure, see Section 13
Sources (2 references)
Giannou FK, Tsiara CG, Nikolopoulos GK, et al. (2016). Condom effectiveness in reducing heterosexual HIV transmission: a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on HIV serodiscordant couples. Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research, 16(4), 489-499. https://doi.org/10.1586/14737167.2016.1102635；Fonner VA et al. (2016). Effectiveness and safety of oral HIV preexposure prophylaxis for all populations. AIDS. https://doi.org/10.1097/QAD.0000000000001145 (pre-exposure prophylaxis, PrEP)
31

After any high-risk episode, get one HIV test — free at the CDC, results confidential

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Testing for HIV at the CDC costs nothing. Without your consent, no unit or individual may disclose your name, address, workplace, or medical history. And a positive result is not a death sentence: people who keep taking medication and suppress the virus to undetectable levels no longer transmit it to sexual partners. That study followed 700-odd couples through 70,000-odd condomless sex acts, with zero partner transmission.

Cost
Free. One trip to the CDC or a designated clinic, one tube of blood. The hard part is speaking up to get tested.
Benefit
Article 23 of the Regulations on AIDS Prevention and Control states it plainly. Local health authorities above county level designate medical institutions, and these institutions "shall provide free counseling and preliminary screening tests to persons who voluntarily accept AIDS counseling and testing." Early testing has practical value: today's antiretroviral therapy can suppress the virus below detection. WHO's position is that "people with HIV taking antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load do not transmit HIV to sexual partners." The PARTNER study followed 782 gay couples, each with one infected and one uninfected partner — serodiscordant, in the jargon. In total 1,593 couple-years (each couple's follow-up years summed). Over 76,088 condomless sex acts, 15 new infections occurred. Phylogenetic analysis comparing viral genes showed all 15 came from outside the couple: between-partner transmission was zero. Article 39 of the same regulations: "Without the consent of the person or their guardian, no unit or individual may disclose the name, address, workplace, portrait, medical history, or other information that could identify the specific identity of an HIV-infected person, an AIDS patient, or their family members."
Note
The window period decides when a test counts. Guangdong CDC's guidance: nucleic acid testing detects from about 1 week, fourth-generation combined antigen-antibody tests about 2 weeks, third-generation antibody tests about 3 weeks. Test at least 2 weeks after the event, and retest at 2–4 week intervals. Three months after the last high-risk episode, more than 99.99% of infections can be ruled out. A positive self-test kit is not a diagnosis — confirmation must come from the CDC or a proper institution. Article 3 of the regulations states that no unit or individual may discriminate against infected persons and their families, and their rights to marriage, employment, medical care, and schooling are legally protected. Article 38 also obliges infected persons to "promptly inform those with whom they have sexual relations of the fact of infection or illness." For the three-disease pregnancy screening and mother-to-child blocking, see Section 27

The moment a suicidal thought appears, tell one person around you — hand over those dozens of minutes

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Of people who attempted suicide, nearly half say no more than 10 minutes passed between the thought appearing and the act — so what you need to survive is often just those dozens of minutes. Three-quarters had contact with people around them during that window; they just didn't speak. Among those hospitalized for self-harm, about 2% die of suicide within 1 year, about 7% over 9-plus years — the overwhelming majority never die of suicide.

Cost
Free. The hard part is speaking up in the moment, and admitting you can't be alone for the next few hours.
Benefit
82 suicide-attempt survivors were interviewed within 3 days of admission: 47.6% (39 people) said that from this episode's first suicidal thought to the actual attempt, no more than 10 minutes passed. Those whose process lasted longer scored significantly higher on suicidal intent. Impulsivity scores bore no relation to process length. 76.8% (63 people) said they had some contact with a partner, family, or friends during that time. The authors' conclusion: the window for intervention is usually very short and professionals have limited room to step in at that stage, which is why recognizing signals and intervention methods must reach ordinary people. Separately, a systematic review pooled 90 follow-up studies. Among those seen for self-harm, the median proportion self-harming again without dying within 1 year was 16%. Death by suicide within 1 year: 2%. Over 9-plus years of follow-up, about 7% died of suicide
Note
Why B: Deisenhammer's study covers just 82 people from one hospital, relying on after-the-fact recall. Owens reports the middle proportion across 90 heterogeneous studies, not a pooled single number. The same review states plainly that self-harm patients' suicide risk remains hundreds of times that of the general population. So "the overwhelming majority never die of suicide" describes the group as a whole — it is not a promise about any one person, and treatment still matters. For moving lethal means away and the 12356 line, see item 25 in this section. First steps when mood sinks: Section 3, item 18. Aftermath of being rescued: item 33 here. If you suspect someone near you has such thoughts, you can ask directly — see item 43 (ask directly when someone seems off). What you can do when someone voices such thoughts: Section 8, item 15
Sources (2 references)
Deisenhammer EA, Ing CM, Strauss R, Kemmler G, Hinterhuber H, Weiss EM (2009). British Journal of Psychiatry, 181, 193-199. https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.181.3.193

Don't treat "they saved me" as a safety net: after pesticide or gas, the ER can save your life, but not your lungs and brain

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Paraquat has no antidote; over 40% of those who drink it cannot be saved. It inflames the lungs and slowly stiffens them, while the kidneys and liver take damage too. Among carbon-monoxide survivors, nearly half have worse brain function six weeks later — even with hyperbaric oxygen, a quarter still do.

Cost
Free. Just knowing this in advance.
Benefit
A systematic review of paraquat poisoning: case fatality is extremely high, because the compound is inherently toxic and effective treatment is lacking. It is actively transported into lung tissue against the concentration gradient — the technical term is active uptake against a concentration gradient — resulting in pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis, plus kidney and liver injury. The review states: gastric lavage should not be performed. Hemodialysis and hemoperfusion are unlikely to alter the clinical course. Evidence for steroids and immunosuppressants is weak. It also notes: "mortality is high in all centers despite wide variation in treatment." 10 tertiary hospitals in Bangladesh admitted 1,420 cases from 2013 to 2024; of 257 analyzable ones, case fatality was 43.2%. Common presentations: lower-limb swelling from acute kidney failure 71.2%, vomiting 65.8%, abdominal pain 58.0%. The acute carbon-monoxide trial was double-blind and randomized, 76 per group; neither doctors nor patients knew the assignment. At six weeks, cognitive sequelae remained in 19/76 (25.0%) of the hyperbaric-oxygen group vs 35/76 (46.1%) of the normobaric group, P=0.007. After adjusting for other factors, OR 0.45 (95% CI 0.22 to 0.92, the confidence range). Another study followed 73 cases consecutively: 30% had cognitive sequelae, 12% white-matter hyperintensities. China revoked the registration and production license of paraquat aqueous solution as of July 1, 2014, halting production. From July 1, 2016, the aqueous form was banned from sale and use domestically. From September 26, 2020, sale and use of the gel formulation were banned. The documents state that "paraquat ingestion suicide incidents occur from time to time" was the direct reason for tightening control
Note
Why B: these studies cover poisoning patients generally, not solely suicide-attempt populations, and the carbon-monoxide trial included accidental poisonings. So the sequelae rates above cannot be read directly as "consequence probabilities for a suicide attempt." What is certain: no method leaves you unscathed. On-scene handling of carbon monoxide: Section 13, item 19. For swallowed pesticide or medication, don't induce vomiting — bring the container to the hospital: Section 13, item 20. Not stockpiling pesticides and sleeping pills: item 25 in this section. This book does not compare lethality across methods, nor describe any specifics

Clinical and Laboratory Profile of Paraquat Poisoning: A Toxicological Crisis in Bangladesh. Hyperbaric oxygen for acute carbon monoxide poisoning. New England Journal of Medicine, 347(14), 1057-1067. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa013121；Parkinson RB, Hopkins RO, Cleavinger HB, et al. (2002). White matter hyperintensities and neuropsychological outcome following carbon monoxide poisoning. Don't gamble on "a few days in bed" after a fall from height: most trauma-ICU patients survive, and the bill is measured in years

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Of those who reach a trauma ICU after a fall from height, only 5.5% die — but they're hurt badly and treated long. Nearly half injure three or more body regions; over a third need a ventilator; the longest ICU stay was 132 days. Half fell from no more than 3 meters. Of the badly injured, fewer than six in ten later return to work.

Cost
Free. Just seeing this account clearly in advance.
Benefit
A trauma ICU (intensive care unit) in southern Xinjiang tallied its cases. From April 2020 to July 2024 it admitted 289 falls from height. Mean age 40.3. Median fall height 3 meters; 26.6% fell from above 5 meters, 11.4% from above 10. Median injury severity score (ISS) 24 — higher means worse injury; 63.3% had ISS over 20. 47.1% injured 3+ regions, 18.3% four or more. 36% needed mechanical ventilation, median duration 103.5 hours. Median ICU stay 8 days, range 1 to 132. In-hospital or 30-day mortality 5.5% (16/289). A German trauma center followed 84 polytrauma patients with ISS ≥ 25 — polytrauma meaning multiple regions injured at once. Return-to-work within the follow-up period: 58%. Age, ICU length of stay, and self-rated health were predictors. Nationally in 2024, average hospitalization cost per admission was 9,870.0 yuan, down 4.3% year-on-year at current prices. Total national health expenditure that year was 9,089.55 billion yuan, of which out-of-pocket spending was 2,500.75 billion — 27.5%
Note
Why B: the fall cohort is a retrospective tally from one hospital, not separating accidents from self-harm. The return-to-work cohort is only 84 people, in Germany. Neither can be read as "what happens to a person after jumping." The average hospitalization cost is the national mean across all admissions, not falls — cited only as a checkable lower bound. The source gives only the height distribution of this cohort, so no height-to-outcome mapping is offered here. Pressure ulcers, the thing to watch during long bed rest: Section 17, item 8. Deep-vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism: Section 13, item 11 (a leg suddenly swelling). What to do when the thought appears: item 32 here. Consequences of poisoning: item 33 (don't treat "they saved me" as a safety net). The author's own experience: a fourth-floor fall, having assumed "two weeks and I'll be fine," turned into a year hospitalized, four surgeries, steel plates, six months unable to turn over or sit up alone, and family borrowing money for it

Don't trade a kidney for money on "one less kidney is nothing": the remaining one does the work of two, and 86% of kidney sellers later report worse health

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

For properly screened donors with post-donation follow-up, 31 per 10,000 reached kidney failure after 15 years; equally healthy non-donors, 4 per 10,000. Kidney sellers get neither screening nor follow-up: 6 years on, 86% report worse health, and three-quarters are still in debt.

Cost
Free. Just seeing this account clearly in advance.
Benefit
The US compared 96,217 living kidney donors against 20,024 similarly healthy non-donors from the national nutrition survey (NHANES III). Estimated 15-year risk of reaching kidney failure: donors 30.8 per 10,000 (95% CI 24.3–38.5); healthy non-donors 3.9 per 10,000 (95% CI 0.8–8.9), P<0.001. Kidney failure is technically end-stage renal disease (ESRD) — at that point survival requires dialysis or transplant. Estimated lifetime ESRD risk: donors 90 per 10,000; unscreened general population 326; healthy non-donors 14. Norway ran a comparison too: 1,901 kidney donors with median follow-up 15.1 years against 32,621 eligible controls followed a median 24.9 years. Donors' all-cause mortality was about 30% higher (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11–1.52); cardiovascular death about 40% higher (HR 1.40, 1.03–1.91); reaching ESRD roughly tenfold higher (HR 11.38, 4.37–29.6). The donors' overall ESRD incidence was 302 per million. A separate US cohort of 3,698 donors saw 11 ESRD cases — 180 per million person-years, versus 268 in the general population of the same period. Of that cohort, 255 returned for review a mean 12.2±9.2 years after donating: 85.5% had kidney filtration (GFR) ≥ 60 ml/min/1.73 m² — 60 being the clinical lower limit of normal. 32.1% had hypertension. 12.7% had proteinuria (protein leaking into urine). In Chennai, India, 305 kidney sellers were surveyed on average 6 years after selling: 96% sold to repay debt, averaging 1,070 US dollars. Household income after the nephrectomy fell by a third (P<0.001), more people fell below the poverty line, and three-quarters were still in debt at survey time. 86% reported health worse than before the operation; 79% would not advise others to sell
Note
Contested: Ibrahim's study used ordinary people as the comparison and concluded donors' survival and ESRD risk resemble the general population. Muzaale and Mjøen swapped in "equally healthy, equally eligible to donate" comparators — and the risk stood out clearly. The disagreement is about who gets compared, not about the donors. All three studies agree the absolute risk is small (30.8 per 10,000 over 15 years). So the point isn't "donating a kidney is dangerous" — what matters are two other things. The remaining kidney does pay a price; the hypertension and proteinuria rates are right there. And every one of these numbers comes from people screened before surgery and followed after, with a hospital to return to — black-market sellers have none of the three, and the Indian follow-up shows a different ending. The source studies report only self-rated health decline, proteinuria, hypertension, and ESRD incidence — no "how many are bedridden" figures — and this book won't invent them. For kinship limits, fines, and criminal liability in legal donation, see Section 9, item 22 (don't sell your organs). For those already on dialysis: cross-province direct settlement and long-term prescriptions in Section 16, items 1–2 (take the full course as prescribed; outpatient chronic-disease cross-region registration)

Don't pick up, dismantle, or sell metal objects of unknown origin; keep away from anything marked with the trefoil warning

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Radiation has no smell, color, or temperature, and most radioactive sources look like an ordinary piece of metal — so "looks harmless" proves nothing. The odds of an ordinary person encountering one are extremely low: fewer than 1 incident per 10,000 sources per year. But once it happens, it's irreversible — in Brazil in 1987, people dismantled a radiotherapy machine from an abandoned clinic as scrap, and 4 died.

Cost
Free. Walk around unfamiliar metal cylinders, lead pig containers, and parts dismantled from equipment — don't pick them up, don't take them apart, don't pocket them.
Benefit
As of 2025, China has roughly 178,000 radioactive sources in use and 355,000 radiation devices. The annual incident rate for source radiation accidents holds below 1 per 10,000 sources. The grading: loss, theft, or loss of control of a Class I or II source constitutes a major radiation accident; Class III, a significant one; Class IV and V loss or theft, or exposing people beyond annual dose limits, a general one. Official case: in June 2020, at a blast-furnace pipeline project of a Ningxia steel group, gamma-ray flaw-detection work exposed three workers to a Class II iridium-192 source. Chen's left hand suffered acute radiation skin injury grade III. Liu's left thumb and index finger grade IV, middle/ring/little fingers grade III. Fan's left hand grades I–II. All three received doses far above national limits; the two responsible units had their radiation-safety licenses revoked and were fined 70,000 yuan. International case: Goiânia, Brazil, 1987 — a teletherapy machine from an abandoned clinic was dismantled, its 50.8 TBq cesium-137 source removed and the sealed capsule broken. About 112,000 people were monitored; 249 were internally or externally contaminated. Of those, 129 moderately to heavily; 50 required close medical surveillance. 4 died (national / international)
Note
If you do encounter one: keep your distance, note the location, don't move it, call 110. The regulations require reporting to the ecology-environment, public-security, and health authorities. Distance and time are the only effective protection — a pocket or a plastic bag blocks nothing. X-ray machines and CT scanners generate their radiation electrically and leave no residual radioactivity once powered off. The truly dangerous part is the sealed radioactive source inside the equipment: hospital radiotherapy machines, gamma flaw detectors on pipes and boilers, well-logging instruments, level gauges all contain one. Opening the housing exposes the source. And they look no different from ordinary metal parts. So don't count on recognizing a source — treat parts from unknown equipment as untouchable: don't dismantle, don't sell, don't take home. China has had unknowing pickups: in May 2014, at a factory in the Nanjing chemical park, flaw-detection work lost an iridium-192 source. A warehouse keeper picked it up on patrol and put it in his workwear pocket. He was later diagnosed with mild acute radiation sickness and acute radiation skin injury of the right leg, hospitalized for a year, and still walked on crutches years later. Two other workers said they had seen it; one, on his way to work, took it for a necklace, picked it up, looked, and tossed it. The company that lost the source was a Tianjin inspection firm. No official accident bulletin could be found. The picker's injuries come from a follow-up paper by Jiangsu CDC physicians; the picked-up-and-discarded episode exists only in a China Environment News report. People in scrap recycling, dismantling, hardware, and construction face far higher risk than average; walk around any area marked with the trefoil at work sites. Nuclear plant leaks are another class of accident, even less likely for ordinary people. The beneficiary is mainly you and the family members on the scene with you.

Gambling until you borrow to keep gambling, mood staying low — call 12356 first, then hand your bank cards and payment passwords to family

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

People who have seen a doctor for gambling problems die of suicide at 15 times the rate of their peers, and die overall at 1.8 times. The signal that predicts who will die by suicide is depression. So if you're borrowing to gamble and your mood has sunk, call 12356 first.

Cost
Free. One phone call. Handing bank cards, payment passwords, and loan apps to family. The hard part is admitting you can't control it.
Benefit
A Swedish nationwide register study identified 2,099 people diagnosed with gambling disorder at specialist clinics from 2005 to 2016 — gambling disorder meaning gambling you can't control, to the point of damaging your life. Compared with age-matched Swedes, ages 20–74, their overall mortality was 1.8 times and suicide mortality 15 times (both as standardized mortality ratios, SMR). During follow-up 67 died, 21 of them by suicide. What predicted suicide death was depression. The authors issued a 2023 correction: for men the multiplier was 12.1, for women 16.1. Since May 1, 2025, dialing 12356 anywhere in China reaches a psychological-assistance hotline, open no fewer than 18 hours daily (Sweden / national)
Note
B because there's only one study, and it counted only people who visited specialist clinics — a sicker group, so the 15× doesn't transfer to everyone who plays cards. Handing money to family is practice-based with no direct research — on its own it would be Grade C. Legal red lines of gambling: Section 9, item 13 (no rake-taking, no online gambling). Whether to repay a family member's gambling debt: Section 8, item 44 (gambling debts are not joint marital debt). What to do when a suicidal thought appears: item 32 here (tell one person first). The beneficiary is mainly you; family who spot the signs can also walk the person through this entry.
