Don't trade stocks frequently — touch nothing even more when markets boom and crash

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

The most active US households earned 11.4% a year while the market made 17.9% — the gap almost entirely fees. In China's 2014–2015 boom-bust, the smallest 85% of households traded too much, underperforming buy-and-hold by 250 billion yuan — about 30% of their principal.

Cost
Free. The hard part is resisting the itch to act on every headline, and to pile in while everyone's making money.
Benefit
The study covered 66,465 US discount-brokerage households, 1991–1996. The most-trading quintile earned 11.4% annualized; the market 17.9%, the average household 16.4%. Average turnover: 75% yearly — replacing three-quarters of holdings each year. Gross returns (before fees) differed little between frequent and infrequent traders, so the gap came mostly from transaction costs paid (US, 1991–1996). Domestic data: daily account-level records from the Shanghai Stock Exchange, all ~40 million accounts, July 2014–December 2015, 18 months. The Shanghai index rose over 150%, peaked 5,166.35 on 2015-06-12, then fell 40% by year-end. Households were quartiled by opening balance: the smallest held 85% of accounts, the largest 0.5%, with similar opening stock wealth — 880 billion vs 808 billion yuan. The smallest 85% lost 250 billion yuan through active trading; the largest 0.5% gained 254 billion. "Lost" is versus holding still through the same market. Each equals roughly 30% of its group's opening stock wealth — 28% and 31%. As contrast: the 2.5 calm years before mid-2014 show only 1%–3% of opening wealth in such gaps over any 18-month window. During the bubble, households turned over their holdings roughly every 3 weeks — nearly 18 times a year (Shanghai, 2014–2015; control 2012–2014)
Note
The US data are from the 1990s and A-share commissions and stamp duty differ, but "higher turnover, lower take-home return" holds. The domestic study doesn't say avoid stocks; it shows that in the same market, the more actively the small accounts traded, the more money flowed to the other side. Nor did institutions take it — the largest personal accounts did: retail accounts drove roughly 90% of SSE volume in that window. The internet meme "90% of retail loses" has no verifiable official statistic; not used here. For turnover context: Chinese households turned over nearly 18× yearly in the bubble versus the US cohort's three-quarters; in calm years the domestic gap ran 1%–3% — so the hottest markets are when restraint matters most. Not investment advice.
Sources (3 references)

No borrowed money, no leverage, nothing you don't understand

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Buying stocks on borrowed money, once prices fall below the line and you can't top up, means forced liquidation. Paper loss becomes real loss on the spot — no chance to "wait for it to come back." Regulation bars anyone with under 6 months of trading history and under 5 million yuan average assets over the last 20 trading days from opening a margin account. That threshold itself says the tool isn't for ordinary people.

Cost
Free. The hard part: in good markets, resisting "borrow a little, earn a little more."
Benefit
Leverage is borrowing to buy, and it amplifies losses. After margin buying, collateral value can fall below the maintenance ratio line the broker draws. Below the line without added collateral, you get force-liquidated — the broker sells for you. Paper loss becomes real loss instantly, with no "wait for recovery." Regulation states clients "with under six months of securities trading, lacking risk-bearing capacity, or average securities assets below 5 million yuan over the last 20 trading days" may not open credit accounts — the threshold itself marks the tool as not for ordinary people (China, 2015)
Note
"Don't buy what you don't understand" has no direct literature — consensus, Grade C alone. Using consumer loans or cash-advanced credit cards to invest is leverage in disguise; their rates are in item 7. Not investment advice.

Use broad index funds instead of actively managed funds as the long-term base (the money you hold and don't touch)

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

The stocks actively managed funds hold in aggregate already approximate the whole market. But their extra management fee comes straight out of your take-home return. Recomputing fund performance as if luck were reshuffled, very few funds earn back their own fees from genuine outperformance.

Cost
Free. The price is giving up the chance of "picking the star fund manager." The hard part: bearing the index's falls without bolting midway.
Benefit
US active equity funds' aggregate portfolio approximates the market portfolio: pooled, they hold roughly the whole market. But active management's high costs translate one-for-one into lower net investor returns (after fees). The study bootstrapped — repeatedly reshuffling performance to see what luck alone achieves. Few funds generated excess returns sufficient to cover costs: the extra they earned over the market didn't cover their own fees (US, published 2010). S&P Dow Jones Indices tallies yearly: in 2024, 65% of US active large-cap funds underperformed the S&P 500; across 24 years, 64% on average underperformed yearly. Over the 15 years to end-2024, no category saw a majority of active funds win
Note
Contested: a reexamination argues Fama-French's bootstrap under-samples — under its approach, even genuinely skillful funds can be judged "indistinguishable from luck," so "almost no funds have skill" may overstate. China's numbers are less one-sided: per S&P Dow Jones to June 2025, A-share large-cap active funds underperformed the S&P China A 300 by 60.5% over 1 year, 69.6% over 3, 50.8% over 5 — with only 5-year data available. So "active loses long-term" isn't settled in China; the low-fee point stands regardless. Not investment advice.

Among similar funds, prefer the low-fee one

Grade CValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Every extra percentage point of annual fees costs about 18% of your take-home after 20 years, 26% after 30. Picking the low-fee fund within a category is the one thing here you can know in advance.

Cost
Free. Before buying, glance at the sum of "management + custody + sales service" fees.
Benefit
Fee differences compound away principal — the bit deducted each year stacking yearly. One percentage point more in annual fees reduces the terminal value (what's left in the account then) by 0.99^20 ≈ 18.2% after 20 years, about 26% after 30. China's 2023-onward public-fund fee reform cut caps for active equity funds (the stock-picking kind): from 2023-07-07, newly registered ones may charge at most 1.2% management and 0.2% custody; 136 fund companies brought existing products under those lines too
Note
The formula assumes both funds earn the same before fees. Add subscription, redemption, and Class-C sales-service fees in practice. Not investment advice.

19

Don't stake everything on one stock, one platform, one property

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

When assets don't move perfectly together, spreading money keeps the average return while smoothing the account's swings. Conversely, everything on one stock, one platform, one property — when it fails, everything you have fails.

Cost
Free. The hard part is accepting that you won't happen to back the single best one.
Benefit
When assets don't rise and fall in lockstep, spreading money preserves expected return (what you earn on average) while reducing volatility (the account's swings). That is the basic portfolio-selection result Markowitz published in 1952, used ever since. Conversely, all money on one stock or platform: its variance is all your variance, and when it fails nothing hedges, nothing offsets
Note
Grade B because the classic paper is pure mathematical derivation with no measured "savings from diversifying." Diversification smooths swings; it doesn't guarantee no loss. Buying broad index funds (item 17) is the laziest diversification there is. Not investment advice.
Sources (1 references)
Markowitz, H. (1952). Portfolio Selection. The Journal of Finance, 7(1), 77–91. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1952.tb01525.x

If you pay income tax at 10% or above, open a personal-pension account — up to 12,000 yuan yearly deducted pre-tax; if you pay no tax or only 3%, it doesn't pay

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

For every yuan you deposit, the tax saved is "your bracket minus 3%." A full 12,000-yuan year saves 840 at the 10% bracket, 2,040 at 20%, 3,240 at 30%. At the 3% bracket the saving is paid back on withdrawal — locked for nothing. Non-taxpayers pay 3% on withdrawal — a net loss.

Cost
Opening is free. The real price is the money locks until retirement.
Benefit
Contributions, up to 12,000 yuan yearly, are deductible from comprehensive or business income: deposit as much as you reduce taxable income. Investment gains in the account are tax-deferred. Withdrawals aren't merged into comprehensive income but taxed separately at 3%. So you save "your marginal rate minus 3%" times what you actually contribute — marginal rate being the bracket each additional yuan hits. Marginal 10%: up to 840 yuan yearly; 20%: 2,040; 30%: 3,240. People below the taxable threshold save nothing at contribution and pay 3% on withdrawal — net loss. The 3% bracket — comprehensive income after deductions under 36,000 yuan yearly — also doesn't pay: save 3% now, pay 3% later, net zero with years of lock-up. Having income tax withheld monthly doesn't mean you're in the 10% bracket — check the full-year figure after deductions. The yearly quota accrues per calendar year, resets the next, and unused quota doesn't carry over. Nationwide since 2024-12-15 (national)
Note
The account is "closed-loop": money in doesn't come out. Only four exits: reaching pension age, total loss of work capacity, emigration, or other state-defined circumstances. It's not wealth management; it's a tax arrangement locking money for years. The tax is saved once while the lock runs to retirement — the farther from retirement, the thinner the annualized benefit. Rough math: at 10%, each yuan saves 7 fen; 30 years from retirement, barely 0.2% a year. At 20%, 1.7 fen per yuan; 10 years out, about 1.7% yearly. Compute your own marginal tax before deciding how much. Don't lock the emergency fund for the "free money" (item 27). The money inside still needs you to pick products, which can lose. Pick by items 17 and 18 (broad index funds; low fees). Deduction certificates come from the personal-pension information platform. Timing: deduct via monthly withholding, or at next year's reconciliation (item 2).

Pay gyms per visit or in short cycles — unless you have a year-plus of steady attendance

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In the three-year US dataset, members on $70-plus monthly contracts averaged 4.3 visits a month — over $17 per visit, while a 10-visit pass cost $10 each. They overpaid about $600 across their memberships. Unless you have a year-plus of steady attendance, pay per visit or short-term.

Cost
Per-visit pricing runs higher than an annual card amortized. You must honestly estimate your monthly visit count.
Benefit
The study covered 7,752 members of 3 US clubs over 3 years. Members on contracts above $70 monthly averaged 4.3 monthly visits — over $17 per visit against a $10-per-visit 10-visit card — and overpaid roughly $600 over their memberships. Monthly-payers also retained past one year 17% more than annual-payers (US, 3-year panel)
Note
One study, US data. The underlying truth is universal: people overestimate their future self-control. With a solid year of twice-weekly visits behind you, the annual card genuinely is cheaper.

Any prepayment needs a written contract; a merchant in trouble must stop collecting, and before absconding you're entitled to the unused balance back

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Merchants taking prepayment must sign a written contract with refund terms. A merchant in serious trouble must stop collecting, and must notify you before closing or relocating. Then you may demand continued service or refund of the unused balance. Violations draw fines.

Cost
Free. The hard part is insisting on the written contract on the spot — no "recharge first, details later."
Benefit
The regulation requires a written contract for prepayment, including the refund method. Merchants facing major operating risk must stop collecting prepayments. Those closing or relocating must notify consumers in advance — and consumers may demand continued performance or refund of the unused balance. Violations: fines of 1–10× illegal gains, or up to 500,000 yuan without gains
Note
The regulation arms you for after-the-fact litigation; it can't prevent. Once the merchant runs, the money is usually gone — so pre-empt by prepaying little, per this section's "pay per visit" entry, then enforce via this regulation if it happens. Article 27 of the same regulation also requires deposit terms — method, procedure, deadline — with no unreasonable conditions on return.

What you save is what you no longer want the next day. Online goods can be returned within 7 days of receipt, no reason needed. Exceptions: custom-made, fresh and perishable, unsealed digital goods, and periodicals.

Free. Things you want arrive a day later. Return shipping is usually yours. The hard part is not ordering that day.

What you save is the impulse purchases you'd regret by morning — no standard share available. Online purchases: 7-day no-reason return from receipt, with four exceptions: custom orders, perishables, unsealed digitals, periodicals (China, since 2017)

Don't stockpile for the strikethrough price or the big sale

Grade CValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

People judge how expensive something is by the first number seen, and never adjust enough afterward. So "999 crossed out, now 499" systematically inflates how cheap it feels. By regulation, the discount baseline is the store's lowest actual price in the 7 days before the promotion — that crossed-out number need never have been sold.

Cost
Free. The price is missing some genuine discounts. You must remember the everyday price of what you regularly buy. The hard part is holding back on sale day.
Benefit
Judgment anchors on the first number seen, with insufficient adjustment after. "Was 999, now 499" systematically inflates your estimate of the savings. Regulators define the discount baseline as the lowest actual transaction price at the same store within 7 days before the promotion; percentages must reference that. The crossed-out price need never have been real (China, since 2020)
Note
Anchoring is a lab finding; nobody has priced stockpiling losses. Stockpiling also carries unbooked costs: expiry, storage, and "we have plenty anyway" overuse. Stockpile only what meets all three: long shelf life, certain to be used up, genuinely cheaper than your usual price.

Prefer pure-protection insurance; treat "returns" and "dividends" as the non-guaranteed part

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Dividends and returns are not guaranteed. The illustration must state in bold: "future policy dividends are non-guaranteed benefits." The extra premium you pay for return-of-premium is money held for you by the insurer — unguaranteed returns, hard to withdraw.

Cost
Pure protection pays nothing back at expiry — it feels like money burned. The saving is your own to arrange. The hard part is accepting the money won't return.
Benefit
Regulation requires participating-product illustrations to state in bold that "future policy dividends are non-guaranteed benefits; dividend distribution is uncertain." The dividend illustration — the projection table — caps the interest spread at 4.5% minus the product's assumed rate (the guaranteed rate fixed in the contract). The extra premium on return-of-premium and participating products amounts to savings managed by the insurer: unguaranteed returns, poor liquidity, hard to exit (China, since 2023)
Note
Contested: for people who truly can't save, return-of-premium products force periodic saving — real value. The advice targets ordinary people with self-control. How much better "buy term, invest the difference" beats return-of-premium depends on the product; no citable systematic data here. Not investment advice.

Buy enough third-party liability: compulsory-insurance limits are uniform nationally and low — the excess comes out of your household

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: highTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

When you're at fault, compulsory insurance pays at most: 180,000 yuan death-and-disability, 18,000 medical, 2,000 property. Separate lines, no borrowing between them. Injury compensation easily exceeds these; the excess comes from your own pocket — so buy commercial coverage to the hilt.

Cost
Commercial third-party liability runs a few hundred to a thousand-plus yuan yearly. Higher coverage gets cheaper per yuan of coverage.
Benefit
Compulsory insurance carries nationally uniform limits, split into lines: death/disability, medical, property, plus no-fault limits. After the 2020 comprehensive auto-insurance reform, the current total limit is 200,000 yuan — 180,000 death/disability, 18,000 medical, 2,000 property. When you're not at fault: 18,000 / 1,800 / 100. Excess falls on the tortfeasor personally. Driving uninsured means vehicle detention plus a fine of 2× the minimum premium
Note
Limits are set by the financial regulator and can change; these are post-September-2020 values — re-check when buying. The structure is what matters: compulsory insurance pays line by line; unused headroom in one line can't cover another. Injury totals can dwarf it, with nothing insuring the gap. How much third-party coverage to buy, this book won't number. But it's one of the few places here where a few hundred yuan a year removes a low-probability, household-crushing event.

Park 3–6 months of living costs where you can withdraw instantly. Then job loss or illness doesn't force you into 18%-a-year borrowing or fire-sale investments. Bank deposits carry deposit insurance — up to 500,000 yuan per bank.

Free. The price is forgone returns — demand deposits, money funds, or withdrawable savings only. The hard part is not touching it while it builds.

With the emergency fund, unemployment or illness doesn't force borrowing or selling investments at a loss. Consumer-loan and minimum-payment annual rates: item 7. Bank deposits are protected by deposit insurance, top payout 500,000 yuan per bank (China, 2015)

Before prepaying the mortgage, run one comparison — don't go by feel

Grade CValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Prepaying the mortgage earns you the mortgage rate, risk-free. So ask one thing: is your long-term stable after-tax return above the mortgage rate? If yes, don't rush to repay; if not — or if you can't say — repay. With equal-installment loans, interest dominates early years, so earlier repayment saves more. The bank app's "prepayment simulator" gives the numbers directly.

Cost
Free. Half an hour of arithmetic. You must honestly estimate your achievable after-tax stable return.
Benefit
The method. Let r be the mortgage's annual rate per your contract — on 2026-08-20 the 5-year-plus LPR was 3.5%, with actual rates marked up or down from it. Let g be the after-tax annualized return of your alternative investment. Prepaying earns r for certain — every repayment locks in r. If g reliably exceeds r, keeping the money invested wins. If g is below r, or uncertain, prepaying locks a risk-free r. In equal-installment (annuity) loans, interest dominates the early payments, so earlier repayment saves more interest — see it directly in the bank app's prepayment simulator (China, 2026 rates)
Note
Method only, no verdict. Reliably beating the mortgage rate is the minority case. Whichever side you take, keep the emergency cash first. And check the contract for prepayment penalties. Not investment advice.

Merchant fraud pays 3× the price, minimum 500 yuan. Platforms that knowingly tolerate infringing sellers pay jointly. Free. Before ordering, read the after-sales and deposit terms. After delivery, keep the order, livestream screenshots, and chats. The hard part is not getting carried by the show.

Organizing fake transactions or reviews for promotion: fines up to 1 million yuan; serious cases 1–2 million plus possible license revocation. Deposits may not exceed 20% of the contract amount: buyer breach forfeits; seller breach returns double. Automated decisions using personal information may not apply unreasonable differential treatment on price — the "big-data price gouging" of lore (national)

"Which platform has the best value and least junk" has no citable official comparison — this book ranks no platforms. What's checkable is aggregate sampling (item 32, national inspection notices). The 2025 Anti-Unfair Competition Law revision moved false publicity from Article 8 to 9, and penalties from 20 to 25; effective 2025-10-15 — don't copy old article numbers. Among the Shandong cases: a firm organized "brushers" for 75 fake transactions with 680,000-odd yuan principal; the fine wasn't stated. The 7-day no-reason return is item 23.

Unsafe food pays ten times the price on top of the refund — increased compensation under 1,000 yuan counts as 1,000

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

For expired or spoiled food, the item, packaging, and receipt are your evidence — don't rush to discard. You can claim 10× the price or 3× the loss, minimum 1,000 yuan. Seller or manufacturer, your pick — whichever you approach pays first and may not deflect to the other.

Cost
Free. Keep the food, packaging, and receipt — don't toss or wash them; photograph on the spot. Go to the merchant or platform first; failing that, 12315. Litigation runs months. The hard part is not throwing the evidence away first.
Benefit
Anyone harmed by food below safety standards may claim from the operator or the producer; whoever receives the claim bears first-responsibility and must pay up front without deflection. Beyond actual losses, you may claim 10× the price or 3× the loss, and "increased compensation under 1,000 yuan is 1,000 yuan" — except "for label or instruction defects that neither affect food safety nor mislead consumers." The judicial interpretation adds: first, three conditions together — the buyer purchased for personal or family consumption, the food fails safety standards, and there's no evidence they knew at purchase. Met, "the punitive damages are 10× the price actually paid." Second, buyers who knowingly bought non-compliant food to claim get support only "within the range of reasonable living-consumption needs" — serial purchases and suits count total purchases within that range. Third, certain defects get no punitive award, provided they don't mislead on safety: irregular type sizes, typos and missing characters, nonstandard net-content marking, and missing storage instructions on foods needing none (national)
Note
Evidence beats amount: photograph and video first — packaging, production date, foreign object, purchase record — then contact merchant or platform. Don't discard or wash before communicating. 12315 mediates; it doesn't adjudicate. If the merchant stonewalls, only suit remains — small-claims procedure in Section 8, item 22. Note: whether a hair or insect counts as "below food-safety standards" is usually for market regulators or testing to decide, not you — "one hair, guaranteed 1,000 yuan" doesn't hold. Ordinary-goods fraud pays 3×, minimum 500: item 29. Selling food yourself — licenses, labels, no health claims — is Section 12, items 8–11. Conversely, turning claims into a business has clear red lines: fabricating violations to extort compensation suspects extortion, with referral to police; suing on fabricated appearances gets dismissed, and fabricated litigation draws fines, detention, and defamation countersuits. Beneficiaries: you and your household.
Sources (2 references)

Free. Minutes on the regulators' websites.
Benefit
2024 national supervision sampled 25,250 batches, 14.3% failing. E-commerce: 7,297 batches, 23.5% failing, up 1.8 points year-on-year; physical stores 8,055 batches, 15.1%. Bracelets, jade, luxury watches, designer toys: count them as money spent, not money saved

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The price already carries consumption tax: 20% on watches of 10,000 yuan and up, 5% on gold, platinum, and diamond jewelry, 10% on other jewelry and jade — VAT on top. That tax doesn't come back at resale. Buy what you love as consumption, not as investing.

Cost
Free. Just don't count "future appreciation" among your reasons. The hard part is not upping the budget for "value retention."
Benefit
The buying side first, per the consumption-tax schedule: "high-end watches" 20%; "precious jewelry and jade" — gold, platinum, diamond 5%; other precious jewelry and jade 10%. "High-end watch" means any watch at 10,000 yuan (VAT-exclusive) or more. The liquidation side follows the Pawn Administration Measures: Article 36 — pawn terms max 6 months. Article 37 — the pawn interest follows the PBOC's 6-month statutory loan rate prorated by term; interest may not be deducted upfront from your advance. Article 38 — monthly comprehensive fees for movable-property pawns (watches, jade) may not exceed 42‰ of the advance (4.2% monthly); real-estate pawns 27‰; property-rights pawns 24‰. Article 40 — neither redeeming nor renewing within 5 days of term end makes it absolute (绝当); the item stops waiting. Article 43 — absolute items appraised above 30,000 yuan go to auction; proceeds first cover auction fees and principal-plus-interest, the remainder to the pawner, shortfalls still chased (national)
Note
Pawning runs the numbers: monthly comprehensive fees cap at 42‰ of the advance — roughly half the borrowed amount over a year by straight multiplication, plus interest on top. That "half a year" is a magnitude sketch, not a precise rate. Tax and fee rates are printed numbers; whether these things appreciate long-term has no citable statistics, and this book predicts nothing and rates no category. What to block is only the investment rationale: buy for joy as consumption; upping the budget for "it'll hold value" is where the loss lives. Gold splits in two: by-weight investment bars and per-piece jewelry differ; jewelry prices carry design and craft fees that recycling typically ignores. Secondhand listings aren't transaction prices — don't read them as the market.

For jewelry and jade, trust only reports bearing the CMA mark — and verify the issuing body on the regulator's site

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Certificates can be forged — what you check is the issuing lab. Labs issuing public reports need accreditation, marked CMA on the report. The accrediting body publishes the list; you can check membership yourself. In official cases, the "national inspection certificates" shipped with goods were self-commissioned.

Cost
Free. Check the lab's credentials before ordering; minutes.
Benefit
The rules first, per the Inspection and Testing Institution Accreditation Measures: Article 2 — accreditation evaluates and licenses labs issuing "data and results with evidentiary function to society." Article 15 — the mark combines the CMA pattern with the accreditation number. Article 21 — reports with evidentiary function must carry the mark. Article 22 — the accrediting department publishes accredited institutions and certificate status on its website. Article 34 — issuing evidentiary data without accreditation draws a 30,000-yuan fine. Article 37 — forging or misusing certificates or marks, up to 30,000 yuan. Then the official cases, from SAMR's June 4, 2026 "counterfeit-purging" batch: (1) A Donghai, Jiangsu livestream claimed "natural, no acid treatment, no enhancement, Myanmar Grade A," with a "national inspection certificate" — testing found dyed quartzite, treated jadeite, glass, and plastic; the certificate was commissioned by the seller. (2) The same county: 469 suspected fake natural-crystal items seized — 210 natural, 259 synthetic. (3) A Zhenping, Henan shop made its own display board reading "GIA CMA Zhongyu Gem Center certified partner," and bought 181 "National Gems & Jewelry Quality Supervision Center" conformity labels online, sold with bangles (national)
Note
Jade names follow a national standard: conclusions read "quartzite (dyed)" or "jadeite (treated)" — the parenthetical is where the money gap lives. "Grade A," "old mine," "no enhancement" are seller talk, not findings; the dyed-quartzite room used exactly those. The same case batch shows other staging: fake mine sites, actors playing miners, shills warming the room, scripts of "urgent need for money" and "sick relative," and claims of "preventing rheumatism, boosting immunity, improving sleep, unblocking vessels" — prosecuted as false publicity. For the general big-purchase checks: item 32. For whom to pursue in livestream cases: items 29–30.

Blind boxes and card pulls: count the money as never coming back

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: small

Merchants must display draw rules, probabilities, and limited-edition counts prominently — no backend manipulation, no empty boxes. Guarantees and spending caps are only encouraged. Online blind boxes, once rules are explained and you've confirmed, lose the 7-day no-reason return once opened.

Cost
Free. Just fix the budget before buying. The hard part is stopping when the wanted one hasn't dropped.
Benefit
Per the Blind Box Business Practice Guidelines (trial): Article 9 lists key information to be displayed conspicuously — names, types, styles, draw rules, distribution, limited quantities, probabilities, value ranges — and three prohibitions: no backend manipulation of results or probability adjustments; no refusing or delaying delivery via cash-out, buyback, or exchange; no empty boxes. Article 11 merely "encourages" guarantee mechanisms via time, amount, and count caps. Article 17: for internet-sold boxes, with full disclosure and per-purchase confirmation, opening removes the 7-day no-reason return; default checkboxes may not replace confirmation. Article 21: no gambling under blind-box guise. Article 23: no sales to minors under 8; sales to minors 8+ require confirmed guardian consent (national)
Note
The guidelines direct operator conduct but aren't themselves a penalty basis; actual cases run under product-quality, anti-unfair-competition, and consumer-protection law. Three concrete complaint grounds: undisclosed probabilities, probabilities not matching reality, empty boxes. Before complaining, screen-record the listing rules and your unboxings. The opened-box return exception requires the merchant's full disclosure plus your per-purchase confirmation — default checkboxes don't count. Kids' purchases have their own rules: under 8, no sales; 8+, guardian consent. Refunds for kids' top-ups: item 9. The 24-hour cooling-off: item 23. The "excitement fades, so buy more" loop: Section 6, item 23 (don't expect purchases to fix mood).

If you care what's in your food, buy prepackaged: bulk counters aren't legally required to list ingredients

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Only prepackaged food must carry an ingredient list; bulk food doesn't. Bulk counters need only name, production date, shelf life, and producer. So "no additives listed" means only "not required to be listed." If you care, buy the prepackaged version — ingredients and additive names are printed.

Cost
Free. Prepackaged usually costs a touch more than bulk. Reading the list takes seconds.
Benefit
Food Safety Law Article 67 requires labels on prepackaged food stating nine items — the second, "ingredients," and the seventh, "the generic names in national standards of food additives used." Article 68 asks far less of bulk food: containers and outer packaging must state "name, production date or batch number, shelf life, and the producer's name, address, and contact" — no ingredient list, no additives. Frozen seafood shows the gap best: GB 2760—2024 permits phosphates as water retainers in frozen aquatic products, max 5.0 g/kg as phosphate — legal within limits. The problems are overdosing and ice-glazing for weight. After CCTV's 2025 3·15 gala exposed shrimp with "excessive water retainers (compound phosphates) and ice-glaze weight gain," regulators required labels to "clearly mark water-retainer (phosphate) ingredients, net content (minus glaze weight), and the ingredient list" (national; the law's third 2025 amendment effective 2025-12-01)
Note
"Not listed" means "not required," not "not added." Want to know: buy prepackaged. For frozen shrimp and fish blocks, prepackaged net content excludes the glaze — unit-price by that is the true price; bulk priced by sticker may shrink a chunk on thawing. Water retainers within limits are legal and not a safety issue — not poison. Overdosing and glazing are money problems: you bought water at seafood prices. Conversely, bulk counters sometimes omit even the four required items — name, date, shelf life, producer — any one missing violates Article 68: skip the purchase or dial 12315. How to label bagged food if you sell it: Section 12, item 9. Beneficiaries: you and family, top tier.

Sell losing stocks by pre-set rule too — don't "average down" your way to a comeback

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The instinct sells winners and rides losers. Across 10,000 US accounts over seven years, gainers were 50%-plus likelier to be sold than losers. The same people added to losers more eagerly — yet their held losers underperformed the sold winners by 3.4 points the next year.

Cost
Free. The hard part is admitting this one lost — and selling it.
Benefit
The study covered all trades of 10,000 accounts at a US discount broker, 1987–1993. The proportion of gains realized (PGR) was 0.148; of losses realized (PLR), 0.098; difference 0.050, t above 35. Daily, winners were 50%-plus likelier to be sold than losers. The same accounts repurchased losers more readily: 0.135 versus 0.094, t = 19. The study also tested "the held ones come back": the reverse held — sold winners outperformed held losers by 3.4 percentage points of excess return over the following year (excess meaning over the market index). The authors' worked example: selling $1,000 of the loser rather than the winner returned about 4.4% more the next year, tax-loss benefits included (US, 1987–1993)
Note
This entry governs "sell or not"; item 15 governs "don't act constantly" — no conflict; pre-set rules executed faithfully mean fewer trades. Averaging down is arithmetically fine — more shares, lower average cost. The error is treating it as a comeback: its real effect is concentrating more money in that one stock — see item 19. The tax bit is US-specific; the rest stands. US 1980s–90s account data; A-share costs and taxes differ. Not investment advice.
Sources (1 references)
Odean T (1998). Are Investors Reluctant to Realize Their Losses? The Journal of Finance 53(5):1775-1798. https://doi.org/10.1111/0022-1082.00072

For US stocks and other foreign assets, use QDII funds or Stock Connect — no offshore broker accounts, and never the yearly FX quota

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Since May 2026, offshore brokers like Tiger, Futu, and Longbridge may no longer open accounts for mainland residents. Existing accounts get two years of sell-only, withdraw-only wind-down. The FX quota may not buy foreign stocks either — violators lose the quota for the year plus two more. For foreign assets: QDII funds or Stock Connect.

Cost
Free. QDII funds buy in minutes in your banking or brokerage app. The price: fewer choices than an offshore broker.
Benefit
On 2026-05-22, eight departments issued the Plan for Comprehensively Rectifying Illegal Cross-Border Securities, Futures, and Fund Operations: "through 2 years of concentrated rectification, completely eliminate" illegal cross-border operations. Offshore institutions may not market in the mainland nor "provide account opening, order handling, funds transfer, and similar services." For existing account holders: "only one-way sell transactions and outbound transfers" — after two years, "complete shutdown of mainland websites, trading software, and supporting servers." The same day, the CSRC announced plans to confiscate all illegal gains of Tiger, Futu, and Longbridge entities and impose severe penalties, with the Q&A stating the goal of "guiding mainland investors to overseas investment via legal channels such as Stock Connect, QDII, and Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect." On the FX side, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange's personal purchase declaration states purchases may not fund "overseas property, securities investment, life insurance, and investment-return participating insurance — capital items not yet opened." Violators join the watch list, "forfeit the personal convenience quota for the year and the following 2 consecutive years," face administrative penalties, anti-money-laundering referral, and credit-record entry (national, from May 2026)
Note
These documents govern offshore institutions and name no penalties for investors. With an existing offshore account, sell and withdraw within the wind-down window. The three legal channels each have eligibility rules — ask your bank or broker first. Past US gains don't promise future ones; pick QDII by items 17 (broad index) and 19 (no single-market bets). Overseas cash withdrawal has its own quota: Section 21, item 6. Not investment advice.

Insure only the losses you can't absorb; losses you can absorb are the emergency fund's job

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Premiums don't all come back — part pays the insurer's costs and profit. So what's worth insuring is the rare, household-breaking loss: major illness, injuring someone with your car, the family earner dying. Small losses your savings can absorb belong to the emergency fund.

Cost
Free. List the household's possible big losses and see which exceed your savings. Half an hour, once.
Benefit
Only part of premiums returns as claims; the rest covers sales, operations, and profit. Regulators require sellers of short-term individual health insurance to publish the "comprehensive loss ratio" on their website half-yearly — roughly claims as a share of premiums; check the company's site to see how much it pays out. So for any given loss, insurance loses a little on long average. What it buys is spreading one crushing expense into a small yearly one. The smaller and more affordable the loss, the worse the trade. By that standard, several things already covered in this book are worth buying: one-year medical insurance, Section 7, item 20; auto third-party liability, item 26; overseas medical, Section 21, item 4; and for anyone whose household lives on your income, term life, item 40 (national, since 2021)
Note
Grade C because no official numbers price which insurance "pays"; this is a trade-off method. Screen insurance and flight-delay cover — losses of a few hundred yuan you can absorb — need not be bought by this standard. Critical-illness cover replaces income during treatment years; households with 1–2 years of runway can consider skipping. Basic medical insurance is social insurance, exempt from this trade-off — keep paying (Section 7, item 9). What covers small losses: item 27. Beneficiaries: you and family.

If anyone lives on your income, buy term life for the earner first — not for the child

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: highTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Term life covers a fixed number of years; if you die within them, the household receives a sum. It exists for family living on your income — unfinished mortgage, young children. Nobody depends on you, you don't need it. Children earn nothing, and death benefits on children are legally capped besides.

Cost
A few hundred to a few thousand yuan yearly, by age, coverage, and term (author's rough estimate, no official figure). Honest health disclosure beforehand; half an hour once.
Benefit
Regulation defines life insurance on the insured's lifetime, split into term, whole-life, and endowment. Term life pays on death within a fixed term; whole-life covers to death whenever; accident insurance pays only on accidental death or disability — illness death pays nothing, so it can't replace life insurance. Death-benefit contracts need the insured's consent and coverage acknowledgment, else void. Parents insuring minors' deaths are exempt from the consent rule, but total death benefits for a child may not exceed the regulator's cap. Coverage typically runs in the hundreds of thousands of yuan — hence "large." No official sizing exists; the author's algorithm: unpaid mortgage, plus children's costs to adulthood, plus a few years of household running costs (national, 2015 amendment)
Note
Grade C because the rules give definitions and caps only; "earner first" follows from "whose lost income sinks the household." A child's death doesn't remove income; the earner's death leaves mortgage and children's costs in place. With limited money: earner's term life and one-year medical first, children's medical next. Honest disclosure and renewal terms: Section 7, item 20. Beneficiaries: your spouse and children.

Regretted a life-insurance policy over one year? Cancel within the free-look period — premiums essentially fully refunded

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Life policies over a year carry a free-look period. Bought at a bank: 15 days from receiving the policy; cancel with at most a 10-yuan fee. Past the window, you get only the policy's cash value — usually less than paid. When the insurer's callback asks whether you understand, don't say yes until you do.

Cost
Free. One call or counter visit, a dozen-odd minutes. The hard part is calmly reading the contract within those 15 days.
Benefit
For life insurance over one year, regulation requires stating the free-look start and length, and the policyholder's rights within it. Long-term health insurance: at least 15 days. Bank-sold policies over one year: uniformly 15 days, counted in natural days from signed receipt. Covers must print: "Within 15 days of receiving this contract you may surrender in full (minus a production cost not exceeding 10 yuan). Surrender after 15 days involves loss." Past the window you may still terminate anytime; the insurer must refund the cash value within 30 days. The regulator's risk notice: after the free-look period, long-term life policies' cash value is often below total premiums paid. For new one-year-plus policies, insurers must call you back within the window to confirm you know the surrender loss and free-look rights (national, 2010, 2019)
Note
The free-look rule is for one-year-plus life insurance. One-year medical and accident policies have no such requirement — check the terms. Bought elsewhere, the contract's stated days govern; find the free-look clause first. Savings and participating policies, with their heavy premiums, are where the window pays most — item 25. "Medium" because the saving is the premium-cash-value gap, typically hundreds to thousands, no official statistics. Beneficiary: you.

42

Before signing at the bank counter, check whether you're holding a deposit or an insurance policy

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Banks may sell insurance but may not call it a deposit. Policy covers must print "insurance contract" and the insurer's name prominently, with no "deposit" or "savings" wording. If the cover names an insurer, it's not a deposit — surrender after the free-look costs you. Buyers over 65 at banks may, as a rule, only be sold fixed-benefit products.

Cost
Free. Two extra minutes on the contract cover before signing.
Benefit
The rules: banks may not bundle insurance with deposits, funds, or bank wealth management, may not compare insurance returns to deposits, and may not present uncertain returns as guaranteed. Insurance documents may not use the bank's name or logo, nor the words "deposit," "savings," or "jointly launched with the bank." Covers must print "insurance contract" in type no smaller than 72-point and the insurer's name no smaller than size 2. Three buyer groups may, in principle, only be sold fixed-benefit products: policyholders over 65; over 60 buying installment products; declared income below local per-capita disposable income. Their policies also route to manual underwriting — no instant issuance at the branch. Insurer staff may not sell insurance inside bank branches. Bank-sold one-year-plus insurance carries the 15-day free look; surrender after it means loss (national, from October 2019)
Note
Grade B because the rules are explicit but no official numbers price the misled buyers' losses. Elders depositing at banks are the prime target — check the cover when you accompany them. Already signed? Cancel within 15 days per item 41. Feeling misled: item 43. Beneficiaries: you and your elders.
Sources (1 references)
中国银保监会办公厅 (2019). 商业银行代理保险业务管理办法（银保监办发〔2019〕179 号，第三十、三十一、三十二、三十六、四十二、四十九条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-12/03/content_545…
43

To surrender a policy, go to the insurer yourself — no "surrender agents"; if misled, complain via 12378

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Online "full refund, no success no fee" outfits are mostly illegal surrender agents. They take 30–50% of the refund and demand your ID, bank card, and verification codes. Surrendered, coverage is gone too. If misled, start with the insurer's service line; failing that, 12378 — free throughout.

Cost
Free. Calling the insurer or visiting the counter yourself costs a trip or two more than outsourcing.
Benefit
In February 2026, five departments jointly warned that "full-refund" claims are false information inconsistent with the Insurance Law. "Rights-agent" outfits charge heavy service fees and may sue you for "breach" if you quit midway. They harvest your SIM cards, bank cards, policies, home address, and children's schools — data whose resale brings telecom fraud and card cloning. Ningxia's June 2026 notice adds detail: agents charge 30%–50% of the surrender amount, impose steep cancellation penalties, and coach clients to fabricate "mis-selling" or "forged signature" complaints — participants may violate public-security law and, seriously, face joint liability for false accusation or extortion. Coverage terminates immediately on surrender; repurchasing later may cost more or be refused as age and health findings accumulate. If genuinely misled: the insurer's official complaint line first, then 12378, the banking-insurance consumer hotline — free. If premiums are merely unaffordable, ask about reduced paid-up coverage or policy loans — reduced paid-up meaning no further premiums with proportionally reduced coverage (national, 2026)
Note
Hunan's 2025 notice tells of a woman talked into agency surrender by a "friend," paid "consultation fees," and still got only cash value. Three months later she was diagnosed with breast cancer — the critical-illness policy was gone. Decide by your own math: coverage still useful but unaffordable means asking about reduced paid-up. For doing it yourself within the free look: item 41. Beneficiary: you.
Sources (3 references)
金融监管总局、中央网信办、公安部、中国人民银行、中国证监会 (2026-02-06). 关于警惕不法「代理维权」短视频及直播陷阱的风险提示（中央网信办官网转载）. https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-02/06/c_1772110875635198.htm；宁夏金融监管局 (2026-06-16). 关于防范非法代理退保的风险提示. https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/ningxia/view/pages/common/It…；湖南金融监管局 (2025-07-23). 关于防范非法「代理退保」黑灰产的风险提示. https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/hunan/view/pages/common/Item…
44

Name a specific beneficiary on the policy — and remember to claim: 5 years for life insurance, 2 for others

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

No beneficiary named, or the beneficiary dies first, makes the proceeds an estate — creditors of the deceased get paid before family. "Wife, so-and-so" followed by divorce counts as unnamed at claim time. Family must know the policy exists: life insurance claims within 5 years of learning of the death, other insurance within 2.

Cost
Free. Fill once at application; changes need written notice to the insurer.
Benefit
The Insurance Law: beneficiaries are designated by the insured or policyholder (with the insured's consent). Three situations make proceeds part of the estate, distributed by succession rules: no beneficiary named or designation unclear; the beneficiary predeceases with no other; the beneficiary legally loses or waives the right with no other. When beneficiary and insured die in the same event with no order determinable, the beneficiary is presumed to have died first. Estate shares first settle the deceased's taxes and debts. The Supreme Court's interpretation: designating "name plus relationship" that no longer holds at claim time counts as unnamed. Beneficiary changes not notified to the insurer don't bind it. Limitation periods: 5 years for life insurance, 2 for others, from knowing or should have known of the insured event. Coverage typically runs hundreds of thousands — hence "large" (national, 2015 amendment, since 2021)
Note
Once the limitation lapses, the insurer may refuse and courts rarely recover. So family must at least know which companies hold your policies. After divorce, remarriage, or a birth, revisit the beneficiary. Collecting everywhere after a death: Section 25, item 9. Debts don't die with the person: Section 29, item 13. Beneficiaries: spouse and children.
Sources (3 references)
全国人大常委会 (2015 修正). 中华人民共和国保险法第二十六、三十九、四十一、四十二条. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4…；最高人民法院 (2020 修正). 关于适用《中华人民共和国保险法》若干问题的解释（三）第九条第二款第三项、第十条. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181799df4000179ac03d7…；全国人大 (2020). 中华人民共和国民法典第一千一百五十九条. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…
45

Don't put money into Bitcoin, Tether, and the like — and don't follow anyone pitching them: the trades aren't legally protected, and lawsuits won't recover losses

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

China doesn't recognize crypto as money; personal purchases can be ruled void, losses borne alone. One buyer paid about 448,000 yuan for Tether; the platform froze withdrawals; his suit to recover was dismissed. Theft is different — thieves still get convicted.

Cost
Free. No coins, no "signal groups." The price: missing the rallies.
Benefit
In February 2026, eight departments issued PBOG Notice 42 (2026): Bitcoin, Ether, Tether "have no legal-tender status and shall not and cannot circulate as currency." Yuan-for-coin, coin-for-coin, and coin-issuance financing are illegal financial activity, "strictly prohibited across the board"; offshore institutions may not serve mainland residents either. On personal investment, the notice's words: "civil legal acts by any unit or individual investing in virtual currencies, real-world asset tokens, and related financial products that violate public order and good morals are void, and the resulting losses are borne by themselves." The 2021 notice was repealed, the sentence retained. Court cases: one buyer paid roughly 448,000 yuan (exactly 448,000) for Tether from two self-styled platform merchants, 2018–2019; the platform later blocked withdrawals and logins; his refund suit was dismissed as a void investment with self-borne losses, upheld on appeal (Yixing, Jiangsu, published March 2025). Theft differs: a victim's 4-million-plus yuan of crypto was drained by "hackers"; one thief drew 7 years for theft plus a 20,000-yuan fine (Zhengzhou, Henan)
Note
"Losses self-borne" covers money disputes with sellers and signal-callers — courts won't retrieve your investment, so don't count on suing afterward. Theft and fraud are criminal matters: report them. Holders must also guard malicious QR approvals: in Lianshui, Jiangsu, someone scanned a code at a meeting and 57,000-odd Tether (worth about 394,000 yuan; exactly 393,665.461434) left the wallet — the People's Court Daily argued theft. The FBI's 2022 alert describes the pattern: a wallet prompt you approve grants unlimited transfer rights. Its advice: connect your wallet only to sites you trust, and periodically audit approvals with third-party tools. Using your bank card to receive, buy, or transfer for others is another matter, possibly criminal: Section 9, item 5. Spotting promised-return "wealth management": item 6. Legal channels for foreign assets: item 38. Not investment advice.

46

Self-paying the employee pension without an employer: the lowest tier plus full years is the best value; it's not instant profit — even the lowest tier takes about 10 years of benefits to break even

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: highTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

For flexible workers paying their own employee pension, lowest tier plus enough years is the best value. The bulk of the benefit tracks local average wages at retirement. At then-current wages, 15 years at the lowest tier with benefits from 60 breaks even in about 10 years; extra tiers above the minimum take about 17. Worth paying — not instant profit.

Cost
All yours — 20% of the contribution base, the lowest tier running a few hundred to a thousand-plus yuan monthly. Fifteen-plus years required, rising gradually toward 20 from 2030. Unwithdrawable before retirement.
Benefit
The 2005 State Council decision sets the mechanics. The self-paying (officially "flexibly employed") pay 20% of the base, 8% credited to the personal account. Since 2019 the base is self-chosen, 60%–300% of the province's all-in urban average wage. The pension has two parts. The basic pension: local prior-year average wage plus your average contribution wage, halved, times 1% per year contributed. The personal-account pension: account balance divided by the divisor — 139 at retirement age 60, 170 at 55; later retirement, smaller divisor. What follows is the author's own arithmetic, not official numbers. Assume local monthly average wage of 8,000 yuan at retirement, both averages equal; amounts at then-current wages, personal-account interest assumed to exactly track wage growth. Lowest tier, 60%: base 4,800, monthly payment 960; 15 years totals about 173,000 yuan (exactly 172,800). From 60: about 1,457 monthly — basic 960 plus personal-account about 497. About 17,500 yearly (about 17,487), breaking even in about 9.9 years — age 70 or so. At the 100% tier: 15 years totals about 288,000 yuan, paying about 2,029 monthly. The extra 115,200 yuan (exactly) buys only about 572 more monthly — about 16.8 years to break even. Reason: half the basic pension follows the local average wage regardless of your contribution — light contributors are subsidized. Each extra year at the lowest tier keeps break-even at about 9.9 years — beating tier upgrades. At the lowest tier, the basic pension dominates the benefit. Break-even is independent of local wage level: high-wage regions raise contributions and benefits proportionally. Early-year contributions were nominally small but benefits pay at then-current wages, so nominal break-even beats 9.9 years. The law: 15 cumulative years at retirement to draw monthly; short, you may continue contributing. From 2030-01-01, the minimum rises 6 months yearly toward 20. On death, the personal-account balance is inheritable. The state adjusts pensions up with wage growth and prices; shortfalls are subsidized by government (national)
Note
The worked example shows magnitude only. Your actual benefit depends on local wages, tier, account interest, and retirement year. Post-retirement adjustments aren't in the math, so real break-even comes earlier. Later retirement means smaller divisors and larger monthly account payouts. Employed workers: employer pays 16%, you pay 8%; the self-employed carry all 20%. Dying early: the account balance is inheritable, plus funeral grant and survivor allowance. If even the lowest tier is unaffordable, start with resident pension — Section 31, item 11. Subsidies for the hard-to-employ: Section 7, item 12. Lapsed payments and catch-up: Section 7, item 18. Transferring across cities: Section 19, item 19.
Sources (4 references)
国务院 (2005). 关于完善企业职工基本养老保险制度的决定（国发〔2005〕38 号，第三、六条及附件「个人账户养老金计发月数表」）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_737…；国务院办公厅 (2019). 降低社会保险费率综合方案（国办发〔2019〕13 号，第一、三部分）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-04/04/content_537…；全国人民代表大会常务委员会 (2024). 关于实施渐进式延迟法定退休年龄的决定（附件《国务院关于渐进式延迟法定退休年龄的办法》第二条）. https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202409/content_6974294.htm；全国人大常委会 (2010, 2018 修正). 社会保险法（第十、十二、十三、十四、十六、十七、十八条）. https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647616.htm

6. The don't-do list

31 entries

This section collects things that "look cheap and effective." Open the original studies and their benefit runs near zero, at zero, or negative. Order follows two things: how much people spend on them, and how hard the supporting evidence is. The earlier, the sooner to stop. Entries in this section are grouped by theme, with item numbers in parentheses. Supplements and health products: multivitamins (item 1), ordinary fish oil (item 2), vitamin D supplementation (item 3), antioxidant supplements for cancer prevention (item 4), chondroitin for knee arthritis (item 5), vitamin C against colds (item 6), big spending on health products (item 10), long-term probiotics (item 11), "detox" and colon-cleanse products (item 13), mega-dosing calcium after a fracture (item 30). Checkups and small findings: whole-body PET-CT and tumor-marker panels (item 7), generic checkup packages (item 18), high uric acid without gout attacks — don't medicate (item 19), gallstones that never hurt — don't remove (item 20), don't quit calcium to prevent kidney stones (item 21). Wellness lore: fitness trackers for weight loss (item 8), organic food (item 9), cold showers for immunity (item 12), don't force yourself to drink water (item 14), blue-light glasses (item 16), blood donation as health practice (item 17), breakfast or intermittent fasting for weight control (item 26), lifting posture to prevent back pain (item 29). Buying luck and mood: fortune-telling and horoscopes (item 15), crystals and pixiu charms (item 22), shopping to feel better (item 23), spending more to "move up a notch" (item 24). Willpower and sex: willpower as a muscle (item 25), masturbation harming the body (item 27), conversion therapy (item 28). AI answers: judging your own illness via AI chatbots (item 31).

1

Don't take multivitamins for longevity or cardiovascular protection

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

14,000-odd male physicians took multivitamins for eleven years. Major heart and vascular events and deaths — the same as non-takers. Pooling 9 trials, 50,000-odd people: no effect on death either. Not buying saves 200–700 yuan a year. People with a confirmed deficiency and pregnant women taking folic acid aren't covered here.

Cost
About 0.5–2 yuan a day, 200–700 a year. No time cost — one pill. Long use breeds a feeling that skipping a day means neglecting something.
Benefit
The PHS II trial enrolled 14,641 male physicians, followed 11.2 years (median). Takers and non-takers had identical rates of major cardiovascular events. Major cardiovascular events HR 1.01 (HR is hazard ratio; 1 means identical). The 95% CI 0.91–1.10 is that number's confidence range. Death likewise: all-cause HR 0.94 (0.88–1.02). The US body that grades preventive services, USPSTF, pooled 9 randomized trials, 51,550 people in 2022: no association between multivitamins and total mortality. Rated I — evidence insufficient to say. It looks like a deal because "one pill fills every gap" sounds tidy and costs pennies a day
Note
Contested: the same physicians were also followed for cancer. Takers had about 8% fewer cancers (0.86–0.998, P=0.04, barely clearing the "not chance" bar) and about 12% fewer cancer deaths (0.77–1.01) — a range crossing 1, so possibly chance. Small benefit, seen only in male physicians. Those with confirmed deficiency, pregnant women (folic acid), and the genuinely imbalanced diet follow doctor's orders — not this entry
Sources (3 references)
Sesso HD et al. (2012). Multivitamins in the prevention of cardiovascular disease in men: the Physicians' Health Study II randomized controlled trial. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2012.14805；US Preventive Services Task Force (2022). Vitamin, Mineral, and Multivitamin Supplementation to Prevent Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.8970；Gaziano JM et al. (2012). Multivitamins in the Prevention of Cancer in Men. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2012.14641 (the cancer result in the note)
2

Don't take ordinary fish oil to prevent cardiovascular disease

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Two big trials took 26,000 people and 15,000 people with diabetes. A daily gram of fish oil changed nothing in major cardiovascular events or deaths. "Fish is good for you" isn't "fish-oil capsules are good for you." Not buying saves 400–1,000 yuan a year.

Cost
About 1–3 yuan a day, 400–1,000 a year. No time cost.
Benefit
The VITAL trial enrolled 25,871 people on 1 g daily, followed 5.3 years (median). Major cardiovascular events and death showed no difference. Major cardiovascular events HR 0.92 (HR is hazard ratio; 1 means identical); the 95% CI 0.80–1.06 is its confidence range, crossing 1 — no difference. All-cause death HR 1.02 (0.90–1.15). The ASCEND trial took 15,480 people with diabetes, also 1 g daily, average 7.4 years, likewise nothing: serious vascular events RR 0.97 (0.87–1.08); all-cause death RR 0.95 (0.86–1.05). It looks like a deal because "fish is good" got carried straight to "fish-oil capsules are good"
Note
Contested: one trial worked. REDUCE-IT took 8,179 people with existing cardiovascular disease or diabetes, all on statins, triglycerides still high (135–499 mg/dL). On 4 g daily of prescription pure EPA, events ran 17.2% vs 22.0% — risk down about a quarter (HR 0.75, 0.68–0.83). But that's a high-dose prescription for high-risk patients, not a health-store fish oil for ordinary people. Eating fish itself isn't covered here either
Sources (3 references)
Manson JE et al. (2019). Marine n-3 Fatty Acids and Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer. NEJM. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1811403；ASCEND Study Collaborative Group (2018). Effects of n-3 Fatty Acid Supplements in Diabetes Mellitus. NEJM. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1804989；Bhatt DL et al. (2019). Cardiovascular Risk Reduction with Icosapent Ethyl for Hypertriglyceridemia. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1812792 (the high-purity prescription trial in the note)
3

Don't supplement vitamin D in people who aren't deficient, for longevity

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

People not deficient, supplementing 5 years: cancers, cardiovascular disease, and deaths all matched the non-supplementers. The confirmed-deficient, people with osteoporosis, and those with little sun exposure aren't covered — they supplement per doctor's orders.

Cost
About 0.2–0.5 yuan a day, 100–200 a year. The money is trivial; the real cost is believing you've done prevention.
Benefit
VITAL took 25,871 people on 2,000 IU daily, followed 5.3 years (median). Cancer, cardiovascular events, and death: no differences. Metastatic-cancer HR 0.96 (HR is hazard ratio; 1 means identical; 95% CI 0.88–1.06 the confidence range). Major cardiovascular events HR 0.97 (0.85–1.12). All-cause death HR 0.99 (0.87–1.12). The D-Health trial took 21,315 Australians over 60 on 60,000 IU monthly, followed 5 years — also nothing: all-cause death HR 1.04 (0.93–1.18); deaths 5.3% vs 5.1%. It looks like a deal because observational studies found low vitamin D levels correlate with more deaths, misread as "supplementing fixes it"
Note
Contested: neither trial specifically recruited deficient people, so the conclusion covers only the not-deficient. The confirmed-deficient, osteoporosis patients, the sun-deprived, and infants supplement per doctor. Only total mortality, cancer, and cardiovascular outcomes were examined here
Sources (2 references)
Manson JE et al. (2019). Vitamin D Supplements and Prevention of Cancer and Cardiovascular Disease. NEJM. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1809944；Neale RE et al. (2022). The D-Health Trial: a randomised controlled trial of the effect of vitamin D on mortality. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-8587(21)00345-4
4

Don't take antioxidant supplements (β-carotene, vitamin E, vitamin A) to prevent cancer

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

This one isn't merely useless. Pooling 78 trials, nearly 300,000 people: antioxidant-takers died slightly more. In two big trials enrolling only smokers, β-carotene raised lung cancer 18%–28% and death 8%–17%. Smokers and asbestos-exposed people especially should not take it.

Cost
About 0.5–2 yuan a day. For smokers, the real cost is lung cancer risk climbing.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled 78 randomized trials, 296,707 people. Antioxidant takers: all-cause mortality RR 1.02 (RR is risk ratio; 1 means identical; 95% CI 0.98–1.05 the confidence range). Restricted to the better-designed, less-bias-prone trials: RR 1.04 (1.01–1.07), slightly higher. β-carotene alone RR 1.05 (1.01–1.09); vitamin E alone RR 1.03 (1.00–1.05). The ATBC trial took 29,133 male smokers on 20 mg daily: lung cancer up 18% (3%–36%), total mortality up 8% (1%–16%). CARET took 18,314 smokers or asbestos-exposed: lung cancer risk up about 28% (RR 1.28, 1.04–1.57), death up about 17% (all-cause RR 1.17, 1.03–1.33). It looks like a deal because "antioxidant = anti-aging, anti-aging = cancer prevention" — each link sounds like common sense
Note
The US grading body USPSTF gave β-carotene and vitamin E a D in 2022 — recommend against. Smokers and the asbestos-exposed have already been harmed. Antioxidants naturally present in vegetables and fruit aren't covered — eat those
Sources (3 references)
Bjelakovic G et al. (2012). Antioxidant supplements for prevention of mortality in healthy participants and patients with various diseases. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007176.pub2；The Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta Carotene Cancer Prevention Study Group (1994). The effect of vitamin E and beta carotene on the incidence of lung cancer and other cancers in male smokers. NEJM. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199404143301501；Omenn GS et al. (1996). Effects of a combination of beta carotene and vitamin A on lung cancer and cardiovascular disease. NEJM. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199605023341802
5

Don't count on glucosamine/chondroitin to treat knee arthritis

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Knee-arthritis patients taking a fake pill for 24 weeks: 60% still report less pain. Glucosamine or chondroitin adds only 4–5 percentage points over that — small enough to be chance. Seven hundred to eighteen hundred a year buys essentially that 60% placebo effect.

Cost
About 2–5 yuan a day, 700–1,800 a year.
Benefit
The GAIT trial took 1,583 knee-osteoarthritis patients for 24 weeks. On placebo, 60.1% reported pain relief. Glucosamine beat it by 3.9 points (P=0.30); chondroitin by 5.3 (P=0.17); both together by 6.5 (P=0.09) — all too small to rule out chance. The active comparator celecoxib beat placebo by 10.0 points (P=0.008). It looks like a deal because "raw material for cartilage" sounds on-target, and the placebo alone already satisfies 60%
Note
Contested: in the same trial, the severe-pain subgroup on both together showed 79.2% response versus 54.3% control (P=0.002) — but the authors flag it as post-hoc data-dredging: a lead, not a conclusion. What works for knee arthritis is weight loss and muscle training — Section 2
Sources (1 references)
Clegg DO et al. (2006). Glucosamine, chondroitin sulfate, and the two in combination for painful knee osteoarthritis. NEJM. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa052771
6

Don't rely on vitamin C to prevent colds

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Daily vitamin C won't stop you catching colds, and starting after symptoms begin works erratically at best. Daily use shortens a cold by about 8% — half a day less misery; judge for yourself whether that's worth a few hundred a year. Marathon runners and soldiers marching in cold regions are the exception: their colds dropped by half.

Cost
Effervescent tablets run 1–2 yuan each, 300–700 a year.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled 29 controlled trials, 11,306 people. Daily vitamin C in ordinary people barely changes cold incidence: RR 0.97 (RR is risk ratio; 1 means identical); 95% CI 0.94–1.00 the confidence range. Trials starting after onset found "no consistent effect" — some positive, some not. In the same review, regular daily use shortened colds by about 8% in adults (95% CI 3%–12%) and 14% in children (7%–21%). Marathon runners, skiers, and soldiers in subarctic conditions are the exception: across 5 trials, 598 people, colds fell by about half — incidence RR 0.48 (95% CI 0.35–0.64). It looks like a deal because it's cheap, sweet-sour, and the "vitamin C prevents colds" line has circulated half a century
Note
Contested: the same review does show regular use shortening colds — about 8% in adults (3%–12%), 14% in children (7%–21%), roughly half a day per cold. Marathon runners, skiers, and cold-region soldiers are the exception, halving colds (RR 0.48, 0.35–0.64). Almost nobody belongs to those groups
Sources (1 references)
Hemilä H, Chalker E (2013). Vitamin C for preventing and treating the common cold. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000980.pub4
7

Don't order "whole-body PET-CT" or "tumor-marker panels" for yourself without symptoms

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In symptom-free people, what screening finds most is false alarms. Over 80% of whole-body CT recipients had at least one "abnormality"; nearly 40% were called back; most were benign. Women screened for ovarian cancer markers died of ovarian cancer slightly more often — and some got a pointless surgery out of a false alarm.

Cost
A whole-body PET-CT runs about 7,000–10,000 yuan plus a dose of ionizing radiation; tumor-marker panels a few hundred. The real cost follows: one "abnormality" that's a false alarm triggers follow-ups, biopsies, surgery — the money and misery live there.
Benefit
The US grading body USPSTF gives CA-125 plus ultrasound screening in symptom-free women a D — recommend against — based on the PLCO trial: ovarian cancer deaths 0.34% screened vs 0.29% usual care, RR 1.18 (95% CI 0.82–1.71). No benefit. False-positive surgery rates ran 0.2%–3.25% across trials, with up to 15% of those patients suffering serious surgical complications. Another study gave 1,192 symptom-free people whole-body CT: 86% had at least one "abnormality," 37% were referred for further workup — "most findings described as benign." It looks like a deal because "scan everything at once, catch it early" fits intuition exactly
Note
The tumor-marker half has randomized trials behind it. The whole-body CT and PET-CT half rests on follow-up records without controls — one grade weaker, effectively B. The screenings that do have evidence — colorectal, cervical, breast, low-dose chest CT for the high-risk — are another matter: Section 1. People with symptoms, or already diagnosed, getting PET-CT: that's diagnosis, not screening
Sources (3 references)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2018). Screening for Ovarian Cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement. JAMA（同一份建议另有 USPSTF 官方页）. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2017.21926, https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recomm…；Furtado CD et al. (2005). Whole-body CT screening: spectrum of findings and recommendations in 1192 patients. Radiology. https://doi.org/10.1148/radiol.2372041741
8

Don't count on fitness-band step tracking to lose weight

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Overweight people on identical diet-and-exercise programs: those wearing trackers lost 3.5 kg over two years; those without lost 5.9 kg. For weight loss, the device doesn't help — the exercise does.

Cost
Devices run 200–2,000 yuan, plus daily attention spent on the numbers.
Benefit
The IDEA trial took 471 overweight or obese adults for 24 months, identical diet and exercise plans, differing only in the wearable. The device group lost 3.5 kg (95% CI 2.6–4.5, the confidence range); the no-device group lost 5.9 kg (5.0–6.8) — more. Difference 2.4 kg (1.0–3.7, P=0.002). It looks like a deal because "what gets measured gets managed" sounds right, and the device is a one-time buy
Note
One trial, with early-2010s armband devices — this doesn't license "all wearables are useless." Exercise itself works: Section 2. The only conclusion: for weight loss, the device isn't a necessary expense
Sources (1 references)
Jakicic JM et al. (2016). Effect of Wearable Technology Combined With a Lifestyle Intervention on Long-term Weight Loss: The IDEA Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2016.12858
9

Don't pay the organic premium "for health"

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

No strong evidence organic food is more nutritious. Only 3 studies looked at human health outcomes after eating — none found a difference. Organic produce does show 30 percentage points lower detectable pesticide residue, but detection isn't exceeding limits. Eating more vegetables and fruit helps; organic or not doesn't change that.

Cost
Typically 1–3 times the ordinary price.
Benefit
A systematic review combined 17 human studies with 223 food-composition studies, concluding "lack of strong evidence that organic foods are significantly more nutritious than conventional." Only 3 of the human studies examined health after consumption (allergies and symptomatic infections) — no differences. Organic produce showed 30 points lower detection of pesticide residue; detection isn't exceeding limits. It looks like a deal because "no pesticides = safer = healthier," each step sounding like common sense
Note
Studies directly measuring human health outcomes are scarce, so the conclusion is "no evidence it's better," not "proven no benefit." Environmental impact, animal welfare, and taste aren't judged here. More vegetables and fruit helps regardless of organic status
Sources (1 references)
Smith-Spangler C et al. (2012). Are organic foods safer or healthier than conventional alternatives?: a systematic review. Ann Intern Med. https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-157-5-201209040-00007
10

Don't spend big on health supplements, herbal pastes, and tonics to "regulate the body"

Grade CValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The common ingredients — multivitamins, fish oil, vitamin D — were checked one by one in the first six items of this section: no demonstrated benefit. The line on the box, "health food is not medicine and cannot replace medication," is required by the regulator. The money mostly buys gifts for parents carried to their door — the affection is fine; the object is wrong.

Cost
From a few hundred to over ten thousand yuan. Gift packaging often multiplies the price several-fold.
Benefit
What you get back is the money. The reasoning is in items 1–6: the most common supplement ingredients — multivitamins, fish oil, vitamin D, antioxidants, glucosamine, vitamin C — showed no expected benefit in randomized trials; each figure sits in those items' Benefit columns. Regulations govern what claims may be made; they aren't proof of uselessness. The regulator requires health foods to devote at least 20% of the front label to: "health food is not medicine and cannot replace medication." The same rules confine their purposes to "supplementing dietary nutrients, maintaining or improving health status, or reducing disease risk factors." It looks like a deal because "doesn't treat, just regulates" can never quite be proven wrong, and gift-buying runs on sentiment, not evidence
Note
The conclusion is "no supporting evidence," not "proven ineffective" — hence C. For products with clearly listed ingredients, look up the matching item above. Those with confirmed deficiency or in treatment follow their doctor. What's rejected is the product, not the affection. If an elder already bought and takes something, and it neither replaces medication nor causes harm, don't pick that fight at their door — booking the vaccines and screenings matters more. The same money converts to things with sources in this book: annual flu shot (Section 1, item 20); shingles vaccine after 50 (item 21); pneumococcal after 65 (item 22); a blood-pressure cuff and helping them stay on medication to target (item 7); bathroom and stair retrofits plus balance training (item 13); age-appropriate cancer screenings accompanied (items 17–19); for the bed-bound, pressure-ulcer care and long-term care insurance (Section 17, items 7–8). Bring fruit, rice, and what they love instead of herbal paste. What truly must be blocked: prepaid "investment retirement" schemes, and products that displace real medication — Section 17, item 5
