Don't take probiotics long-term without a gut problem

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Pooling 45 trials in healthy adults, probiotics don't durably change gut flora — stop, and it reverts — and blood lipids don't improve. Antibiotic-associated diarrhea and other specific situations have separate evidence; not covered here.

Cost
About 2–5 yuan a day, 700–1,800 a year.
Benefit
A review pooling 45 healthy-adult trials concluded "no support for durable change to gut microbiota, nor improved lipids in healthy adults." Flora does shift — temporarily, reverting on cessation. It looks like a deal because "gut health" is elastic enough to fit anything, and a bottle a day costs little
Note
The same review found minor improvements in healthy people — better-formed stools, more vaginal lactobacilli in women. Antibiotic-associated diarrhea and specific strains for specific conditions have their own evidence. This item targets daily supplement use by the healthy
Sources (1 references)
Khalesi S et al. (2019). A review of probiotic supplementation in healthy adults: helpful or hype? Eur J Clin Nutr. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41430-018-0135-9
12

Don't force cold showers to "boost immunity"

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

In a 3,018-person trial, cold-shower takers called in sick 29% less often — but total sick days matched everyone else's, so they weren't less ill. A 2025 pool of 11 trials found inflammatory markers briefly rose after cold water, immune markers unchanged. Enjoy them if you like; just don't book them as a health investment.

Cost
Free. 30–90 daily seconds of misery; winters take willpower. People with cardiovascular disease should beware — cold stress carries risk for them.
Benefit
A Dutch randomized trial, 3,018 people, ended hot showers with 30, 60, or 90 seconds of cold. Sick-leave episodes fell 29% (IRR 0.71, an episode-rate ratio). But "no significant difference in sick days": total days ill were the same. Quality of life, work productivity, and anxiety showed no meaningful differences. A 2025 systematic review pooled 11 randomized trials, 3,177 people: immediately and one hour after cold immersion, inflammatory markers rose; immune markers unchanged; stress lower only at the 12-hour point. The authors themselves call the evidence "limited by few RCTs, small samples." It looks like a deal because it's free and "suffering must work" flows too easily
Note
Contested: the 29% fewer sick-leave episodes doesn't look like chance, but total days ill didn't fall — more likely "went to work anyway" than "less illness." Cold-water recovery for athletes is a different question. Cold showers don't harm healthy people — just don't count them as investment
Sources (2 references)
Buijze GA et al. (2016). The Effect of Cold Showering on Health and Work: A Randomized Controlled Trial. PLOS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0161749；Cain T et al. (2025). Effects of cold-water immersion on health and wellbeing: A systematic review and meta-analysis. PLOS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0317615
13

Don't buy "detox," colon-cleanse, enzyme, or alkaline-water products

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The detox industry is huge, the clinical evidence for it tiny — nobody has even trialed the commercial detox diets properly. On dietary acid-base, alkaline water, and cancer, exactly one study qualified — and found nothing.

Cost
Hundreds to thousands of yuan. The fasting-based "detoxes" can also drive blood sugar low and nutrition short.
Benefit
That review's conclusion: "despite the detox industry's rapid growth, clinical evidence is scarce," with "no randomized controlled trials of commercial detox diets." A separate systematic review on dietary acid load, alkaline water, and cancer screened 8,278 papers and admitted one qualifying study — no association. The authors wrote that "promotion of alkaline diets and alkaline water for cancer prevention or treatment is not justified." It looks like a deal because "toxins must be flushed" and "acidity causes cancer" sound like physiology
Note
Only "no supporting evidence" — hence C. Clearing metabolic waste is what the liver and kidneys already do. Absent disease in those organs, no extra "detox" is needed
Sources (2 references)
Klein AV, Kiat H (2015). Detox diets for toxin elimination and weight management: a critical review of the evidence. J Hum Nutr Diet. https://doi.org/10.1111/jhn.12286；Fenton TR, Huang T (2016). Systematic review of the association between dietary acid load, alkaline water and cancer. BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2015-010438
14

Don't force water on yourself to hit "8 glasses a day"

Grade CValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Someone chased the origin of "8 glasses a day" and found not one supporting study. Food and other drinks carry plenty of water. Drink when thirsty; check your urine color. People working heat, exercising hard, stone-formers, and elders with blunted thirst should drink proactively.

Cost
Free. A little effort remembering, and more nighttime bathroom trips.
Benefit
A review examined the "8×8" claim — 8 glasses of 8 ounces daily — concluding "no scientific studies were found" supporting it, and that surveys of thousands of adults' food and fluid intake "strongly suggest" such volumes are unnecessary, since food and other beverages already supply much water. It looks sensible because water is free, 8 is tidy, and "drink more water" offends no one
Note
What's rejected is the mandatory count, not drinking water. Thirst plus urine color suffices for most. Heat workers, heavy exercisers, stone-formers, and thirst-dulled elders drink proactively — separate matter
Sources (1 references)
Valtin H (2002). "Drink at least eight glasses of water a day." Really? Is there scientific evidence for "8 x 8"? Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol. https://doi.org/10.1152/ajpregu.00365.2002
15

Don't pay for fortune-telling, tarot, or horoscopes to make decisions

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In the classic classroom experiment, the "personal personality analysis" students received was identical for everyone — and most rated it accurate. That's why fortune-telling feels right. Astrologers pick correctly about as often as chance. The cost exceeds a few dozen yuan: one Henan fortune-telling ring collected incense money and "offering packages" up to 3,888 yuan; the ringleader drew eleven years.

Cost
Free. The hard part is giving up a shortcut for decisions and thinking for yourself.
Benefit
The classic experiment: students took a personality test and received a "personal analysis" that was the same for all — most rated it accurate. The author concluded that "acceptance by the subject or analyst does not validate the interpretation." Of 39 students scoring accuracy 0–5, 34 gave 4 or 5, averaging about 4.26 by the table's distribution. That's the Barnum effect — why fortune-telling always feels apt. Astrology was double-blind tested in Nature: astrologers had to pick which of three personality profiles matched a natal chart. Of 116 first choices, 40 hit; pure chance yields 38.5; the astrologers themselves predicted 58.5. Official case: a Henan Xixian prosecutorial notice described an online fortune-telling fraud ring — free palm reading as bait, then incense money and "offering packages" up to 3,888 yuan; 50-odd victims, 2 million-plus yuan recovered, ringleader sentenced to 11 years plus a 100,000-yuan fine
Note
Both are single studies. Forer's paper gives no mean score directly; 4.26 is computed from its Table 1. This says only "it doesn't predict" — no judgment on beliefs. A few dozen yuan as entertainment doesn't count; using it to decide quitting, marriage, or investments is where the loss lives
Sources (4 references)
Forer BR (1949). The fallacy of personal validation: A classroom demonstration of gullibility. Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 44(1):118-123 (Table 1 rating distribution: one 2, four 3s, eighteen 4s, sixteen 5s, N=39). https://doi.org/10.1037/h0059240；Carlson S (1985). A double-blind test of astrology. Nature 318:419-425 (Table 2: 116 first choices, 40 hits, chance expectation 38.5, astrologers' self-prediction 58.5; "The data are consistent with chance, inconsistent with astrological hypothesis"). https://doi.org/10.1038/318419a0, second author's site https://muller.lbl.gov/papers/Astrology-Carlson.pdf；最高人民检察院 (2026). 河南息县：历经三年持续追踪打掉一批网络算命诈骗团伙. https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202607/t20260728_732935.shtml
16

Don't buy blue-light glasses to "protect vision," and don't believe "months at a screen ruins your eyes" — but a painful, red, pressure-sore eye is an emergency

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Blue-light lenses do nothing; skipping them saves the markup. Versus ordinary lenses, wearers' eye fatigue and clarity show no difference, and no evidence protects the macula. Screen strain and dryness recover; what truly ruins eyes is welding arc, UV, laser — and acute glaucoma.

Cost
Free — and it saves the hundreds-to-thousands markup on the lenses.
Benefit
The 2023 Cochrane review took 17 randomized trials, 5–156 people each, under a day to 5 weeks of follow-up. With sparse data, heterogeneous samples, and inconsistent timing, the authors didn't pool a single estimate. All versus lenses without blue filtering: under one week, self-reported eye strain "may be no different" (low certainty). One 120-person trial differed by 9.76 units, 95% CI −33.95 to 53.47 — spanning zero, no difference. Critical flicker fusion frequency (an objective fatigue measure) "may be little to no different" (low certainty). Best-corrected visual acuity "probably not affected": 0.00 logMAR difference (95% CI −0.02 to 0.02) — one study, 156 people, moderate certainty. Daytime alertness: unclear (2 trials, 42 people, very low certainty). The review found no support for macular protection either
Note
Screens bring eyestrain and dry eye — soreness, dryness, blur after long staring — relieved by breaks and blinking. It recovers; it isn't "ruining the eyes." That sentence is ophthalmology consensus, not the Cochrane review's conclusion — Grade C on its own. What does cause rapid irreversible injury is welding arc, UV, and laser — welding flash ("arc eye") is a notifiable occupational disease; goggles and shields block it, not blue-light lenses (Section 19, item 10). One exception to "screens are harmless": an eye that aches, reddens, sees halos around lights, with headache, nausea, or vomiting is acute angle-closure glaucoma — it can crush the optic nerve within days; same-day ophthalmic emergency (Section 13, item 6). Dilated pupils in the dark, prolonged head-down posture, shallow anterior chambers, age 50+, and hyperopia are the risks. Chronic screen dry eye also becomes a treatable condition, not a sleep-it-off affair. Persistent discomfort or true vision decline: get examined — don't just swap lenses. Children's myopia prevention: Section 30, items 4, 12, 9 (2 hours outdoors daily; cycloplegic refraction; no "myopia cure" products)
Sources (1 references)
Singh S, Downie LE, Anderson AJ, Keller PR, White SJ, Ang M, Wolffsohn JS (2023). Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 8, CD013244. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013244.pub2
17

Don't treat blood donation as a health practice: "detox, lipid-lowering, heart protection" lacks trial support, and frequent donation genuinely depletes iron

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: small

Donation "detoxing," lipid-lowering, and heart protection don't hold. People able to donate repeatedly are healthier to begin with; strip that away and the mortality benefit of one extra donation yearly shrinks from nearly 20% to 7.5%. In an actual randomized comparison, deaths didn't differ. Conversely, donating too often genuinely causes fatigue and cold intolerance — iron deficiency.

Cost
Free. One donation — paperwork, draw, and rest — takes about an hour. The body spends weeks replacing the iron.
Benefit
Finland's Kuopio study followed 2,862 men aged 42–60, nearly 9 years on average. Of 153 who had donated in the prior 24 months, 1 (0.7%) had an acute myocardial infarction; of 2,529 non-donors, 316 (12.5%) did (P<0.0001). Adjusted for age and other coronary risk factors, donors ran about 88% lower infarction risk — RR 0.12 (95% CI 0.02–0.86, P=0.035). Observational, no assignment. The Nordic SCANDAT database holds 1,182,495 donors, 9,526,627 person-years, 15,401 deaths. Adjusting only for age and sex, each extra annual donation meant 18.6% lower mortality (95% CI 16.8%–20.4%); additionally adjusting for the "healthy enough to keep donating" effect left only 7.5% (5.7%–9.4%). The authors: "cannot be interpreted as conclusive evidence of benefit." The FeAST randomized trial took 1,277 patients with symptomatic peripheral arterial disease: one arm had blood drawn every 6 months to reduce iron stores, one control. All-cause death: 125/636 (20%) vs 148/641 (23%), HR 0.85 (hazard ratio; 1 means identical), 95% CI 0.67–1.08, P=0.17. Death plus nonfatal infarction and stroke: 180 (28%) vs 205 (32%), HR 0.88 (0.72–1.07, P=0.20). Neither differed. The INTERVAL randomized trial took 45,263 whole-blood donors across three donation intervals — men 12/10/8 weeks, women 16/14/12. Shorter intervals collected clearly more blood over two years (men's 8-week arm: 1.69 more units than 12-week, 95% CI 1.59–1.80). Quality of life, physical activity, and cognition showed no differences; donation-related symptoms increased — fatigue, breathlessness, faintness, dizziness, restless legs — with lower mean hemoglobin and ferritin and more deferrals for low hemoglobin (all P<0.0001). Iron deficiency impairs thermoregulation: 10 women with iron-deficiency anemia, 8 with depleted stores but no anemia, and 12 controls immersed in 28 °C water for 100 minutes. The anemic group's rectal temperature: 36.0±0.2 °C vs 36.2±0.1 (P=0.001); oxygen consumption 5.28±0.26 vs 5.99±0.29 mL·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹ (P=0.04); thyroid hormones T4 and T3 lower too (P<0.002). The claim works because donors are pre-screened healthy people, and the "bleed iron to protect the heart" hypothesis failed its randomized test
Note
What's rejected is "donating for your own body," not donation itself. Blood is for others — tier 4 (strangers) in this book's beneficiary scheme. What does return to you is the institutional share. Article 14 of the Blood Donation Law: unpaid donors skip the collection, storage, separation, and testing fees for their own hospital transfusions; spouses and immediate relatives get waivers or reductions per provincial rules. The January 2024 notice: 28 provinces now apply these reductions directly at discharge in-province. Award winners get local "three frees" — public transit, government parks, and general outpatient registration at public hospitals. Donate at legal intervals: Article 9 — 200 ml typically, 400 ml maximum, at least 6 months between donations, ages 18–55 encouraged. Don't compress intervals for honors or quotas. Women, the underweight, and heavy menstruation run tight iron budgets; repeat donors can self-pay one ferritin check. Persistent fatigue, cold intolerance, or restless legs after donating: don't guess "depleted vitality" — check blood counts and ferritin. Iron deficiency means supplementing per doctor and lengthening intervals. The thermoregulation evidence covered 10 people — it explains why, not how often
Sources (7 references)
Salonen JT, Tuomainen TP, Salonen R, Lakka TA, Nyyssönen K (1998). Donation of blood is associated with reduced risk of myocardial infarction. The Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor Study. American Journal of Epidemiology, 148(5), 445-451. https://doi.org/10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a009669；Ullum H, Rostgaard K, Kamper-Jørgensen M, et al. (2015). Blood donation and blood donor mortality after adjustment for a healthy donor effect. Transfusion, 55(10), 2479-2485. https://doi.org/10.1111/trf.13205；Zacharski LR, Chow BK, Howes PS, et al. (2007). Reduction of iron stores and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with peripheral arterial disease: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA, 297(6), 603-610. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.297.6.603；Di Angelantonio E, Thompson SG, Kaptoge S, et al. (2017). Efficiency and safety of varying the frequency of whole blood donation (INTERVAL): a randomised trial of 45 000 donors. Lancet, 390(10110), 2360-2371. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)31928-1；Beard JL, Borel MJ, Derr J (1990). Impaired thermoregulation and thyroid function in iron-deficiency anemia. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 52(5), 813-819. https://doi.org/10.1093/ajcn/52.5.813；全国人大常委会 (1997). 中华人民共和国献血法（第二、九、十四条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf5e7…；国家卫生健康委等 (2024-01-08). 关于进一步做好无偿献血者激励奖励工作的通知. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202401/content_6924875…
18

Don't rely on generic checkup packages to prevent disease; do the few evidence-backed screenings for your age and sex

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

People getting regular generic health checks die at the same rate as those who don't — same cardiovascular and cancer deaths too. Do the few evidence-backed screenings by age and sex. Over-35s get a free annual blood-pressure check; over-65s a free annual checkup.

Cost
Free — saves the annual package fee of hundreds to thousands. The obligation in exchange: remembering which screenings, at what intervals.
Benefit
The 2019 Cochrane update included 17 randomized trials. For total mortality, 11 trials pooled, 233,298 participants, 21,535 deaths: general-checkup group identical to control, RR 1.00 (risk ratio; 1 means identical), 95% CI 0.97–1.03. Cardiovascular death: 9 trials, 170,227 people, 6,237 deaths, RR 1.05 (0.94–1.16). Cancer death: 8 trials, 139,290 people, 3,663 deaths, RR 1.01 (0.92–1.12) — no differences. The authors: general health checks "are unlikely to be beneficial." The national basic public-health program gives residents 35+ a free annual blood-pressure measurement and elders 65+ a free annual checkup — physical exam, blood and urine counts, fasting glucose, ECG; liver (ALT, AST, bilirubin), kidney (creatinine, urea), lipids (total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL, HDL), plus abdominal ultrasound of liver, gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen (national)
Note
Rejected is "annual package as prevention," not all testing. The free 35+ pressure check and 65+ checkup are already state-provided — no outlay needed. Screening with reasons stays: blood pressure, glucose, hepatitis B (Section 1, items 7, 8, 14); breast, cervical, colorectal (items 17–19); H. pylori and low-dose CT (items 23–24); bone density for women 65+ (item 39); testing after high-risk exposure (item 31). Starting ages and intervals are written there. Employer-paid checkups: go. What to block is buying packages and adding items yourself. Chronic-disease patients, symptomatic people, and doctor-ordered tests are care, not screening. The package's most common evidence-free items are tumor markers and whole-body imaging — item 7. Asymptomatic high uric acid and silent gallstones: items 19 and 20. Note the Cochrane trials ran mostly in high-income countries with easy healthcare access — resource-strained regions shouldn't transplant the conclusion wholesale
Sources (2 references)
Krogsbøll LT, Jørgensen KJ, Gøtzsche PC (2019). General health checks in adults for reducing morbidity and mortality from disease. Don't start urate-lowering drugs because a checkup found high uric acid — if it has never hurt

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Uric acid above threshold, but no gout attack ever and no tophi: the American College of Rheumatology recommends not starting urate-lowering drugs. Twenty-four people would take them for 3 years to prevent one gout attack. Hoping to protect the kidneys also fails: kidney function declined just as fast on drug as on placebo. Treat after a real attack.

Cost
Free — saves lifelong medication and monitoring costs, and one unnecessary drug risk.
Benefit
The ACR 2020 gout guideline addresses asymptomatic hyperuricemia — uric acid >6.8 mg/dL with no prior attack and no subcutaneous tophi. It conditionally recommends against starting any urate-lowering therapy (allopurinol, febuxostat, probenecid), rated high certainty. The table's footnote: "on the basis of attributable risk, 24 patients would require 3 years of treatment to prevent one gout flare." The CKD-FIX randomized trial took 369 people — stage 3–4 chronic kidney disease, no gout history but at risk of progression — on 100–300 mg allopurinol daily versus placebo for 104 weeks. eGFR (kidney function, mL/min/1.73 m²) fell −3.33/year (95% CI −4.11 to −2.55) versus −3.23 (−3.98 to −2.47); difference −0.10 (−1.18 to 0.97), P=0.85 — identical decline. Serious adverse events 46% vs 44%. The PERL randomized trial took 530 people with type 1 diabetes and early-to-mid diabetic kidney disease on 3 years of allopurinol with a 2-month washout. Allopurinol truly lowered uric acid from 6.1 to 3.9 mg/dL — yet after washout the GFR difference was 0.001 mL/min/1.73 m² (95% CI −1.9 to 1.9, P=0.99). Urinary albumin was 40% higher (0 to 80) in the allopurinol group. It looks sensible because "a high number must be pushed down" runs too smoothly
Note
Rejected is "lifelong urate-lowering without ever an attack," not "hyperuricemia doesn't matter." The same guideline lists exceptions worth starting: first flare with stage-3-plus kidney disease; uric acid >9 mg/dL (about 535 µmol/L); prior urinary stones. Those with attacks, tophi, or radiographic erosion should medicate — Section 16, item 9. About 7.4% of Han Chinese carry HLA-B*5801 versus 0.7% of whites; carriers risk fatal severe rash on allopurinol, with hypersensitivity 3× in Asians. A drug you can defer isn't worth that risk — test the genotype first (Section 16, item 9). The two kidney trials covered CKD and type-1 diabetes patients, not a license for "hyperuricemia is harmless to kidneys" — they refuted only "drugging uric acid protects kidneys"

Don't have your gallbladder preventively removed because a checkup found stones that never hurt

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Stones in the gallbladder that never hurt: over nearly nine years, about 80% stay silent. Left alone, acute cholecystitis or pancreatitis runs 1–3 per thousand yearly. Surgery isn't free either: about 1.5% suffer bile-duct injury. European and UK guidelines both say: no symptoms, no surgery.

Cost
Free — spares a general-anesthetic surgery and hospital stay. The obligation: remembering which signals mean same-day hospital.
Benefit
Italy's MICOL population survey ultrasounded 11,229 people aged 29–69, finding 856 with gallstones; 580 were asymptomatic, followed 8.7 years on average. Of those, 453 (78.1%) stayed silent, 61 (10.5%) developed mild symptoms, 66 (11.4%) severe. Of 189 cholecystectomies during follow-up, 41.3% were on asymptomatic people. The authors: "expectant management remains a valid approach for most patients" — expectant meaning watch and wait. A US HMO (managed-care organization) tracked 691 confirmed gallstone patients a mean 78±61.6 months; 135 asymptomatic ones followed 58±50.2 months (median 46.3): only 10% developed symptoms and 7% had surgery. Of 50 deaths in the whole group, 2 were biliary — both in the symptomatic group. The authors: "patients with silent stones do not require surgery before symptoms." UK NICE guideline CG188, 1.2.1: for people with incidental asymptomatic gallstones and normal biliary tree, "offer no treatment before symptoms." The EASL 2016 guideline puts both sides together: the asymptomatic run 0.7%–2.5% yearly into symptoms; acute cholecystitis, pancreatitis, obstructive jaundice, or cholangitis 0.1%–0.3% yearly. After the first colic, complications rise to 1%–3% — most people hurt once before anything serious. On the surgery side: of 51,041 cholecystectomies in the Swedish register, 1.5% had bile-duct injury, one-fifth of those (0.3%) partial or complete transection. Injured-patients' 1-year mortality 3.9% versus 1.1%. Post-op, 10%–40% still have symptoms or relapse. The guideline's conclusion: surgery in the asymptomatic — open or laparoscopic — doesn't extend life, as operative death and complications exceed the risk of leaving stones; treating after symptoms also costs less. A 1983 decision analysis priced it: prophylactic removal at 30 cost an average 4 days of life versus watchful waiting; at 50, 18 days. No randomized trial has ever compared removal versus watchful waiting. It looks sensible because "it'll hurt eventually, so cut while young" runs too smoothly
Note
Contested. China's 2021 biliary-surgery consensus lists some asymptomatic stones as operative indications; the companion interpretation article names this as a core dispute. The full text is paywalled — the exact scenarios couldn't be verified (TODO: to verify). The other counterpoint is small stones: those under 5 mm correlate more with pancreatitis, and a Dutch analysis found prophylactic removal could gain or lose life depending on pancreatitis frequency and severity. The European guideline lists exceptions too: porcelain (calcified) gallbladder wall and concurrent polyps 1 cm or larger both warrant surgery; stones may be removed incidentally during other major abdominal surgery. This entry covers exactly one situation: stones in the gallbladder that never hurt. Stones in the common bile duct are another matter: guideline 1.3.1 states duct clearance plus cholecystectomy regardless of symptoms. Go same-day if: persistent right-upper or upper abdominal colic, fever with chills, yellowing whites of eyes or skin, dark urine. When a doctor recommends surgery after imaging, ask which ground — duct involvement, polyp, wall abnormality — rather than countering with this entry; it blocks only "no reason beyond stones found." The two cohort studies lack assignment but answer "what happens if left alone," which is the right question here. Follow-up ran 4–9 years; longer horizons raise the symptomatic share

Don't quit calcium to prevent kidney stones

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Calcium-oxalate stone formers are often told to eat less calcium — the trial found the opposite. Men with recurrent stones on normal calcium with less animal protein and salt relapsed at half the rate of the low-calcium dieters over 5 years. The UK guideline states plainly: don't restrict calcium.

Cost
Free. The reverse saves effort: no daily vigilance over calcium content.
Benefit
A 5-year randomized trial took 120 men with recurrent calcium-oxalate stones and high urinary calcium (idiopathic hypercalciuria). One arm ate normal calcium, 30 mmol daily, with less animal protein (52 g daily) and less salt (50 mmol sodium chloride). The other ate the traditional low-calcium diet, 10 mmol daily. Relapse over 5 years: 12/60 vs 23/60. Unadjusted relative risk 0.49 (95% CI 0.24–0.98, the confidence range), P=0.04 — half the relapse risk on normal calcium. During follow-up both arms' urinary calcium fell about 170 mg daily, but urinary oxalate diverged: the low-calcium arm rose 5.4 mg daily on average while the normal-calcium arm fell 7.2. UK NICE NG118, 1.8.1: do not restrict daily calcium intake; adults maintain 700–1,200 mg, children and adolescents 350–1,000 mg by age. Quitting calcium looks sensible because "stones are calcium, so eat less calcium"
Note
Contested: the trial covered men only, all recurrent calcium-oxalate formers with hypercalciuria — it doesn't transfer to every stone type. And the intervention arm changed three things at once (normal calcium, less animal protein, less salt), so the whole benefit can't be booked to calcium alone. What's rejected is "actively quitting calcium," not "supplement extra calcium." This concerns dietary calcium; supplements are another matter — stone formers should ask their physician. Water intake: Section 16, item 8 (2.5–3 liters daily after stones)

Don't buy crystals, bead bracelets, or pixiu charms to "turn luck," "attract wealth," or "nourish the body"

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Claims that wearing something changes luck, attracts money, or nourishes you have no checkable evidence. It's the same mechanism that makes fortune-telling feel accurate: vague enough statements you map onto yourself. Merchants who drift into healing claims commit false advertising — a livestream was prosecuted for it in 2026. As decoration, buy freely.

Cost
Free. All it takes is not counting "luck" among the reasons. The hard part is not following when everyone wears one and swears it works.
Benefit
The classic classroom experiment — everyone receives the same vague "personal analysis," most rate it accurate — is the Barnum effect, which explains where "things went smoothly after I wore it" comes from. The author's conclusion: "acceptance by the subject does not validate the interpretation." Official case: SAMR's June 4, 2026 batch of traditional-craft "counterfeit purge" cases included a Sihui, Guangdong jewelry store fabricating material claims in livestreams and asserting the goods "prevent rheumatism, boost immunity, improve sleep, unblock vessels" — scripted performances misleading consumers, violating Anti-Unfair Competition Law Article 9(1) (national)
Note
One conclusion only: the claimed powers are unverifiable, with zero measured predictive ability. No judgment on beliefs or customs, nor on gifts, keepsakes, and heirlooms. Distinguish two things: merchant efficacy claims have regulations to cite and channels to complain through; "luck" has no research and can't be disproven — only your budget discipline governs. Before buying, treat it as ordinary jewelry and ask: "if it changes nothing, is it still worth this price?" Materials and certificates: Section 5, items 33–34. Fortune-telling: item 15 here.

Don't count on shopping to fix your mood or sense of identity

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

The more people prize money and possessions, the less happy they report — but the link is weak and directionless. Other research finds buying experiences beats buying things for happiness. So when mood drops, spending on an outing or a meal with people is likelier to help than a full cart.

Cost
Free. The hard part is not ordering when feeling low.
Benefit
A meta-analysis across 259 independent samples, 753 effect sizes: the more materialistic, the lower self-reported well-being. On the most-used multidimensional scale, r = −0.19 (corrected ρ = −0.24). Money-valuation-only scales showed weaker links, r = −0.08 to −0.11. By outcome: strongest with risky health and spending behaviors and negative self-evaluation, r = −0.28 to −0.44; weakest with life satisfaction and negative affect, r = −0.13 to −0.15. Mediation analysis suggested the negative link runs through unmet psychological needs. Another study: in two surveys of different populations, respondents said money spent on experiences brought more happiness than money spent on things; lab experiments found recalling an experiential purchase produced better mood than recalling a material one (national scope inapplicable; both used foreign samples)
Note
Contested: most included studies are same-time-point surveys — no direction, and the authors themselves call for experiments and longitudinal work. So it reads "don't count on shopping to become happy," not "shopping makes you unhappy." The correlation is weak: r = −0.19 explains a few percent of variance. Both studies used foreign samples; no citable Chinese data. This isn't against buying what you love — it's against shopping as mood regulation, because it trains your first response to a bad day to be checkout. Money-saving actions: Section 5. What works for low mood: the second half of Section 22 and Section 29. Upgrading to outdo others: item 24.

Don't spend more on housing, cars, or circles to "move up a notch" among the people around you

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Among people of equal income, the more neighbors earn, the lower one's reported well-being. This happens only with neighbors of equal education whom you actually interact with. So money spent moving somewhere everyone is richer buys you a demotion. But when incomes rise together, people still feel better — absolute levels count.

Cost
Free. Just one extra question before raising the budget: am I buying the thing, or my position in this group? The hard part is not following when everyone around upgrades.
Benefit
The US National Survey of Families and Households revisited the same people twice; the author matched them to local average income (PUMA, from the 1990 census 5% sample). Netting out own income and personal characteristics: higher neighbor earnings, lower self-reported happiness. The effect is large, robust to alternative estimation, and highly significant. In the author's phrasing, neighbors' earnings gains depress well-being on the same order of magnitude as equivalent own-earnings losses. With individual fixed effects (comparing people to themselves over time), the coefficient keeps sign and size with significance at the 10% level; with state-and-wave fixed effects, results barely change — so it's neither "people who like moving somewhere poorer are happier" nor unmeasured state factors. The effect is stronger among those who interact with neighbors and insignificant among those whose friends are all outside the neighborhood. Renters and owners show no difference — undermining the "expensive areas leave less real income" explanation. Well-being falls only with the earnings of equally educated neighbors, barely responding to others'. It transmits mainly through satisfaction with one's own material situation, not family life. And when own and neighbors' incomes rise proportionally, well-being still rises
Note
Why B: panel survey data, one study, foreign sample; the outcome is self-reported well-being, not money. The author did scrub several confounds — within-person and within-state-wave comparisons — but it's still not a trial. No citable Chinese counterpart. The "medium" benefit follows item 23's sizing: the money saved may reach tens of thousands, but no numbers back "happiness bought," so not "large." This isn't against paying for a bigger home, a quieter compound, or a shorter commute — those buy the thing itself. What to block is "colleagues upgraded; I can't fall behind." Housing priorities: Section 4, item 18. Shopping for mood: item 23. Upward comparison online: Section 3, item 20.

Don't believe "willpower is a muscle that runs out"

Grade AValue: highMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The popular claim: do one self-control task and you'll cave on the next, so ration your willpower. Twenty-three labs, 2,141 participants redid the experiment on a common protocol — the result was essentially zero. Stop explaining yourself with "willpower spent for today," and don't buy courses teaching you to stockpile it.

Cost
Free. Only a saying changes.
Benefit
A multi-lab preregistered replication — 23 labs, 2,141 participants, the Sripada standardized sequential-task paradigm: a self-control-demanding task followed by another. The pooled ego-depletion effect was tiny with a 95% CI including 0 (d = 0.04, −0.07 to 0.15). The authors discuss whether the "self-control as limited resource" model survives. Another preregistered redo — 36 labs, 3,531 people — found d = 0.06, likewise too small to count.
Note
Rejected is the "self-control as depletable resource" model, not "people get tired." Sleep debt and overwork degrade performance — a different matter, per Section 3's sleep and work-hour entries. What randomized trials do support is changing the environment and the phrasing: Section 4, item 10 (move what you avoid far away) and item 1 (write when-where-what). Fixing what you wear and eat remains worth doing — near-zero cost; it saves minutes and decisions, not willpower. Other entries here count money; this one counts time and attention — no conversion between them.

Don't count on breakfast or 16:8 fasting for weight control; pick meal timing you can sustain

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

The lore says skipping breakfast triggers bingeing later and higher total intake. In trials, skippers ate 200-odd fewer daily calories and weighed slightly less. 16:8 versus simple caloric restriction: no weight difference over a year. Long-term breakfast skippers do show about 17% more cardiovascular disease, but total mortality shows no difference.

Cost
Free. Saves the daily mental wrestling with mealtimes.
Benefit
First, "skipping causes later overeating": a meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials found the breakfast-assigned group ate 259.79 kcal more daily than skippers (95% CI 78.87–440.71) and weighed 0.44 kg more (0.07–0.82) — no compensatory eating. Follow-up was short: mean 7 weeks for weight, 2 for intake. Next, 16:8-style time-restricted eating: 116 overweight adults for 12 weeks; the 12-noon-to-8-pm group versus three regular meals differed by −0.26 kg (−1.30 to 0.78), nonsignificant. A Guangzhou trial, 139 obese patients, 12 months: time restriction plus calorie control lost 1.8 kg more than calorie control alone (−4.0 to 0.4) — also nonsignificant. Finally, long-term skipping: pooling 2.38 million people, skippers ran about 17% higher cardiovascular disease (OR 1.17, 1.09–1.26) and 49% higher cardiovascular death (OR 1.49, 1.20–1.84) — observational only. In the 17–23-year source study, all-cause mortality ran HR 1.19 with CI 0.99–1.42, crossing 1: no difference.
Note
Contested. The 17% cardiovascular figure is observational — skippers also smoke, drink, sit, and earn less, imperfectly adjusted; how much is the breakfast itself is unanswerable. The all-cause figure already crossed 1. On 16:8: a pool of 30 trials, 1,341 people, found equal-calorie time restriction losing 1.46 kg more (−2.65 to −0.26) at the cost of 0.41 kg lean mass — but most trials were short, and the longest, strictest 12-month trial found no difference. Long fasts also touch the gallbladder: in a 6,547-person cross-sectional survey, each hour later of the day's first meal raised detected gallstones about 5% (OR 1.05, 1.02–1.08), and first meals between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. ran about 49% higher than earlier (OR 1.49, 1.24–1.77) — bile stasis forming stones; cross-sectional, so pre-existing gallbladder trouble could drive the habit. China's Kailuan cohort, 5.6 years, 369 GI cancers: skippers ran 2.32× colorectal cancer (1.34–4.01) and 5.43× gallbladder and extrahepatic duct cancer (1.34–21.93) — the latter's CI stretching to 21.93 marks too few events; a lead only. Net: for weight, meal timing barely matters — don't spend willpower on it. Whether lifelong skipping is harmful rests on associations only, direction consistently unfavorable; prudent is eating normally, just don't expect weight control from it. Gastritis and ulcers trace mainly to H. pylori and chronic painkillers, not empty stomachs — Section 1, item 23. Silent gallstones: item 20 here. What works for weight: Section 2, items 27, 28, 32. Diabetics, glucose-medication users, and pregnancy don't apply — missed meals risk hypoglycemia; follow medical orders. Extreme fasting and purging are another matter: Section 28, item 1.

Don't believe "masturbation harms the body" or "abstinence unlocks improvement" — what to watch is whether it costs sleep, work, and relationships

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

No study shows masturbation harms the body. A large US study actually found men with more frequent ejaculation had about 20% less prostate cancer. A UK study found higher risk with high frequency in one's twenties–thirties — so neither direction is a health program. Many who feel "addicted to porn" are mostly clashing with their own moral beliefs.

Cost
Free. Saves the money for "kidney-tonifying" remedies and abstinence courses, and the long-term anxiety of self-blame.
Benefit
The body first. A US study followed 31,925 men to 2010, self-reporting monthly ejaculation frequency. Versus 4–7 times monthly, 21+ times ran prostate cancer HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.72–0.92, about 19% lower) by frequency at ages 20–29; by ages 40–49, HR 0.78 (0.69–0.89, about 22% lower) — mostly low-grade tumors. The counter-evidence: a UK case-control of 431 men diagnosed before 60 versus 409 controls — frequent masturbation in the twenties–thirties ran higher risk, in the fifties lower. Then pornography: a systematic review and meta-analysis holds that feeling "addicted" tracks mostly the mismatch between behavior and one's beliefs, not sheer volume (US / UK)
Note
Contested: both prostate studies are observational with recalled frequency — they license only "no evidence of harm," not a prescription. The UK authors themselves say the fifties finding may reflect illness reducing frequency. The pornography review's abstract gives no effect sizes — direction only. Benefit "small": what fell was mostly low-grade prostate cancer, not death. The real signals for psychiatry or psychology: losing sleep and work and relationships over it, unable to stop. Late nights: Section 3, item 9. Erection worries: Section 1, item 28 (check the heart first). Legal consequences of sharing: Section 9, item 4. Beneficiary: you.

Don't pay for "conversion therapy," and don't send family members to it

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The American Psychological Association's task force concluded such efforts don't change sexual orientation and may harm. In a US survey, those who underwent conversion were nearly 90% more likely to have had suicidal thoughts. In China, a psychiatric hospital that forcibly admitted a man for "sexual preference disorder" was ruled liable and fined 5,000 yuan.

Cost
Free. Saves the money feeding conversion camps, clinics, and "de-gay" operations. The hard part is family insisting on sending someone.
Benefit
The APA's 2009 task force report: efforts to change sexual orientation are "unlikely to succeed and carry some risk of harm." For coercive or inpatient programs involving minors, it recommends parents and youth alike decline. A US nationally representative survey of 1,518 sexual-minority adults: about 7% underwent conversion, 80% of it from religious figures. Adjusted for age and adverse childhood experiences, those who underwent it had lifetime suicidal ideation OR 1.92 (95% CI 1.01–3.64, about 90% higher); suicide planning OR 1.75 (1.01–3.06); non-serious suicide attempts OR 1.88 (1.01–3.50). Another study of 245 young adults aged 21–25: those not subjected to conversion in adolescence — 22.0% attempted suicide; with parents trying to change them — 48.1%; with parents also sending them to therapists or religious figures — 62.8%. WHO's ICD-10 states: "sexual orientation by itself is not to be regarded as a disorder." In 2017, the Yicheng District court in Zhumadian, Henan, heard the case of a man forcibly admitted by a psychiatric hospital for "sexual preference disorder." The court held he "had a generally mild condition, with no suicidal, injurious, or destructive behavior or risk, not meeting compulsory-treatment criteria," ordered a public apology and 5,000 yuan in solatium (US / China)
Note
Contested. Sullins 2022 re-analyzed the same data, controlling for pre-conversion suicidal ideation, finding no positive association (OR 0.44, 0.20–0.94). Sullins's institution opposes homosexuality, and the original authors responded. So the harm magnitude remains disputed — but "it doesn't work" has no counter-evidence. Grade B because the harm figures come from retrospective surveys. Legally: hospitalization is voluntary in principle; only severe mental disorder with danger to self or others permits compulsion. Psychological counselors may not perform psychotherapy. Knowingly hospitalizing someone without a mental disorder brings tort liability. In 2014, a man was hypnotized and electric-shocked to "treat" homosexuality at a Chongqing counseling center; Beijing's Haidian court ordered a public apology and damages — reportedly ruling homosexuality not a mental illness and the center's cure promise false advertising. Only press reports; the judgment text wasn't found on the court's site. For lasting distress over this, psychiatry or clinical psychology treats the suffering. When a child comes out: Section 30, item 15. Beneficiary: you and your family.

Don't count on learning "correct lifting posture" or manual-handling training to prevent back pain — cut the weight and frequency, and exercise

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Workers who took lifting training reported no less back pain later than those who didn't. People who bend more while lifting don't develop more back pain. What tracks with pain is weight and frequency: each extra 10 kg per lift or 10 lifts per day adds about 10% risk. Regular exercisers run 35%–45% fewer back-pain episodes.

Cost
Free. No more fretting over back angle while lifting, no money on posture courses or back belts. Two things instead: split heavy loads or use a cart or a partner (minutes each), and exercise several times weekly (long-term).
Benefit
Training first: the 2011 Cochrane review pooled 9 randomized trials, 20,101 workers. Seven trials, 19,317 people: lifting-trainees and no-intervention controls reported similar back pain (OR 1.17, 95% CI 0.68–2.02, crossing 1). Versus video-only: RR 0.93 (0.69–1.25) — similar. Moderate-quality evidence. The authors: manual-handling advice and training, with or without aids, don't prevent back pain or disability. Bending next: a 2020 systematic review (low quality) of lumbar-flexion-during-lifting studies. The one cohort study found future back-pain and no-pain groups differed by 1.5 degrees of maximum flexion (−0.7 to 3.7), nonsignificant; 9 of 11 studies saw no difference; 7 studies using another measure found back-pain patients bent 6.0 degrees less (−11.2 to −0.9). The authors: no evidence that flexion invites pain. What to do: a meta-analysis of 8 cohorts — each 10 kg heavier per lift, back-pain OR 1.11 (1.05–1.18, about 11% higher); each 10 more lifts daily, OR 1.09 (1.03–1.15, about 9%). Another pool of 21 randomized trials, 30,850 people: exercise plus education cut back-pain episodes RR 0.55 (0.41–0.74, about 45% lower), moderate quality; exercise alone RR 0.65 (0.50–0.86, about 35%), low-to-very-low quality; education alone RR 1.03 (0.83–1.27) and back belts RR 1.01 (0.71–1.44) — nothing. The UK HSE's official guidance likewise states training alone cannot ensure safe handling, and good technique doesn't substitute for aids and task redesign.
Note
Contested: the weight-and-frequency side disagrees — a 2010 review found 4 of 9 high-quality studies showing association, 5 not, concluding occupational lifting alone unlikely to cause back pain; so "lift less heavy" has associational support only. The flexion review is low-quality, mostly cross-sectional. The training review's CIs are wide, and no randomized trial tested training for existing pain. HSE still teaches a technique — load close to the waist, feet planted, no twisting, no jerking, slight bend at back-hip-knee on rising — harmless to follow, just don't expect it alone to prevent pain. Benefit "medium": exercise's reduction qualifies as large, but exercise-alone evidence is low-quality, exercise-plus-education showed no sick-leave reduction, and back pain isn't lethal. Exercise how: Section 2, items 16 and 11. Beneficiary: you.

Don't count on mega-dosing calcium or bone broth to heal a fracture faster

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Trials of vitamin D after fracture showed no better healing. Calcium-plus-D studies are few and unclear. One big bowl of bone broth holds a few dozenths of the day's calcium. The genuinely deficient and osteoporotic are separate cases.

Cost
Free — saves the calcium tablets, vitamin D, and daily simmering. The rule: supplement only a measured deficiency.
Benefit
Vitamin D first: a 2023 systematic review, 14 studies, 2,734 fracture patients — single-agent vitamin D has little effect on union, nonunion, or functional recovery; the positive studies were mostly low quality; restricted to randomized trials, none showed benefit. One trial took 100 vitamin-D-low long-bone fracture patients: half got 100,000 IU within two weeks of injury, half placebo — nonunion struck 2 per arm, 4% total. Another, 102 patients aged 18–50 with femoral or tibial fractures across four dose arms: no healing-score differences at 3 and 12 months. Another, 32 postmenopausal women with wrist fractures: the daily-equivalent 1,800 IU high-dose arm had lower compressive stiffness at the fracture site than no supplement. Calcium next: a 2014 review found too few studies to conclude; its two calcium-plus-D studies showed higher fracture-site density or callus, not faster union. Bone broth last: a Kaohsiung, Taiwan analysis bought three bone-broth noodle dishes, soups of 450–550 g: calcium averaged 14–39 mg per bowl — 1.4%–3.9% of the 1,000 mg daily recommendation, under 5% per serving. China's recommendation: 800 mg for ages 18–49, 1,000 mg over 50, ceiling 2,000 mg — with long-term excess raising kidney-stone risk. A US trial of 36,282 postmenopausal women on 1,000 mg calcium plus 400 IU D, average 7 years: kidney stones up about 17% (HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.02–1.34); hip fracture down about 12%, nonsignificant (HR 0.88, 0.72–1.08). It looks sensible because "bones are calcium; more calcium, faster healing"
Note
Contested: two small leads. A Danish trial of 30 elderly women with proximal humerus fractures and osteoporosis or low bone mass: 800 IU D plus 1 g calcium daily produced higher fracture-site density at week 6 (0.623 vs 0.570 g/cm²) — density only, not union, and few people. The 102-person trial's post-hoc split showed slightly better function scores on high-dose D, needing confirmation. The already-deficient differ: a Dutch cohort found delayed union in 9.7% of those still deficient after supplementing, 0.3% of the never-deficient, 1.7% of the corrected — observational, no causation. Measured deficiency: supplement to normal per doctor. Diagnosed osteoporosis or fragility fracture needs anti-osteoporosis drugs — Section 1, item 40 — which calcium doesn't replace. Non-deficient long-term supplementation gains nothing: item 3. What's rejected is "extra mega-dosing," not eating less calcium — keep dietary calcium: item 21. Suspected fresh fracture: Section 13, item 41. Benefit "medium" prices a year of tablets. Beneficiary: you.

Don't count on AI chatbots to judge your own illness or legal questions — before seeing a doctor, suing, or spending big, trace every citation they give to the source

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: small

Hand an AI a complete case and it recognizes the condition over 90% of the time. But laypeople using it for symptoms identified conditions less often than those who just searched the web — and triage judgments didn't improve either. On legal questions, general-purpose AI fabricates in at least 58% of answers, and it happily follows wrong premises embedded in your question.

Cost
Free. Each verification costs minutes to half an hour. Have the AI name its statutes, guidelines, or papers, open the originals yourself, and find the sentence. The habit to break: trusting confident phrasing.
Benefit
Medicine first: a 2026 Nature Medicine randomized, preregistered trial with 1,298 UK laypeople, each judging two scripted cases — diagnosis and emergency-versus-watch. Some used AI chatbots (GPT-4o, Llama 3, Command R+); controls used their usual methods, mostly web search and the NHS site. Handed the complete case, AI identified the relevant condition 94.9% of the time and chose the right care setting 56.3%. Laypeople using the same AI: under 34.5% identified the condition, under 44.2% chose right. Controls were 1.76 times more likely than AI users to identify the relevant condition (95% CI 1.45–2.13) and 1.57× for danger-sign illnesses (1.28–1.92); triage accuracy was similar. Reading the transcripts, failure came from both ends: users under-reporting symptoms, and AI naming the right condition the user then ignored. Law next: a US team probed public models on federal-court case law in 2024 — ChatGPT 4 fabricated in 58% of answers, Llama 2 in 88%; fabrication meaning content inconsistent with legal fact, "hallucination" in the paper's terms. Models can't tell which sentence is invented. Given a false legal premise in the question, they often adopt it. The same team's 2025 test of professional legal AI tools advertising hallucination-freeness found fabrication in 17%–33%. It looks sensible because AI is always on, free, and talks like a doctor or lawyer
Note
Contested: a 2023 study had clinicians blind-rate 195 forum patient questions — 78.6% of ratings favored ChatGPT's answers over physicians'. But it compared writing quality, not whether the asker judged correctly. The trial used 2024 models; newer ones may be stronger — though the same trial found AI's solo test scores didn't predict lay-user outcomes. Why AI fabricates: OpenAI researchers' 2025 non-peer-reviewed paper explains that training and scoring reward guessing — "I don't know" scores nothing — so it sounds certain even when it isn't. The verification method: have it name the statute and article, guideline, or paper; open the original on the official site and find the sentence; unfound means unsaid. Don't embed your conclusion in the question — ask "how does the law treat this," not "am I sure to win." For sudden facial droop, one-sided weakness, or crushing chest pain, skip the AI and call 120 — Section 13, items 3 and 7. Free legal aid: Section 7, item 3. Benefit "small": only intermediate outcomes like "condition recognized," no mortality numbers. Beneficiary: you and family.

7. Living without money

22 entries

This section counts money and coverage: how much you can draw, how much waived, what services, what conditions — none converted into lifespan. Policies change yearly and vary by region, so amounts and thresholds follow your locality's current publications. Ordering: free, low-paperwork, fast-acting first; long-qualification and regionally divergent later; experience-only, no official documents, last. Entries in this section are grouped by theme, with item numbers in parentheses. Lost your job: claim unemployment insurance online (item 1), employment-difficulty certification (item 12), vocational-training subsidy (item 13). Owed wages: complain to labor inspection first (item 2), apply for legal aid (item 3), figure out who hired you (item 22). Emergency backstops: relief stations (item 4), temporary assistance (item 6), subsistence allowance/dibao (item 7), the two disability subsidies (item 8), replace a lost ID immediately (item 11), truly nowhere to sleep (item 21). Medical insurance and social insurance: don't lapse resident medical insurance (item 9), serious illness goes through insurance and medical assistance first (item 10), don't panic over lapsed contributions (item 18), add medical or critical-illness cover (item 20). Finding work and starting over: public employment services and gig markets (item 5), systematic job hunting (item 14), no deposits, no surrendered IDs (item 15), paths back after prison or bankruptcy (item 19). Housing and food: queue for public rental housing (item 16), cut housing and food to the minimum (item 17).

1

When unemployed, claim unemployment insurance online first

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Employer-plus-you contributions totaling 1 year, and not a resignation you initiated — register as unemployed and you can draw. 1–5 years: up to 12 months. 5–10: up to 18. Over 10: up to 24. While drawing, unemployment insurance pays your employee medical insurance.

Cost
Free. Apply from your phone — three entries work: the "12333" app, the electronic social-security-card mini-program in WeChat or Alipay, or the national social insurance public service platform. A social-security card or ID card suffices; most regions need no in-person visit. Prerequisite: file unemployment registration first.
Benefit
Three conditions together: unemployment insurance paid 1+ cumulative years; the job didn't end at your own initiative (legally "employment interruption not due to the person's own will"); and you've registered as unemployed with job-seeking intent. Duration follows contribution years: 1–5 years, up to 12 months; 5–10, up to 18; 10+, up to 24. Monthly amounts are set provincially and differ. The benefit sits between the local minimum wage and urban dibao, with the national goal of gradually reaching 90% of minimum wage. While drawing, you remain in employee basic medical insurance with full benefits — the premium comes from the unemployment fund, not you (national; regulation since 1999)
Note
Voluntary resignation doesn't count as "not by own will" — no benefit. So never sign "resigned for personal reasons" on leaving — Section 19, item 7. The benefit runs from the registration date: a month late is a month unpaid. First act after walking out: register. Registration needs the employer's separation certificate — Section 19, item 17. Non-compete obligations and unpaid compensation: Section 11, item 12. Employee medical insurance during the benefit period is covered by unemployment insurance. Provincial amounts differ widely — your enrollment region's publication governs. The "90% of minimum wage" comes from the 2017 MOHRSS-MOF guidance (人社部发〔2017〕71 号): "gradually raise unemployment benefit standards to 90% of minimum wage" — a goal, not the current payout. MOHRSS's original page was unreachable; verified via the Liaoning document's quotation.

2

For owed wages, complain to labor inspection first, then arbitrate — both free, most cases resolved within months

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Both routes cost nothing. First call 12333 or complain to the bureau's labor inspection: 60 working days to investigate once filed, with orders to pay on deadline plus 50%–100% extra for noncompliance. Then arbitration, concluded within 45 days. But "concluded" isn't "paid": assetless companies and absconded bosses can leave you winning nothing.

Cost
Free — both complaint and arbitration. Assemble the labor contract, pay slips, attendance records, transfer records, and chats; visit the human-resources bureau or arbitration committee 1–3 times. Arbitration carries a 1-year limitation period (statute of limitations); current employees still being underpaid face no such limit — the departed must file within 1 year of leaving. The hard part is repeated trips, document hunting, and flagging morale.
Benefit
Step one, the complaint. Call 12333 or visit the local labor inspection office. The law allows 60 working days from filing, extendable 30 more for complex cases. Verified, they can order payment on deadline; missing it adds compensation of 50%–100% of the owed amount. In 2024, inspection bodies nationwide handled 137,000 cases, recovering 8.65 billion yuan of wages for 654,000 people. With an IOU or payroll and clear facts, you can also apply directly to the basic-level court for a payment order — a court command to pay, issued within 15 days of acceptance. Step two, arbitration: 45 days from acceptance, extendable 15. Wage claims may seek advance execution — partial enforcement before full adjudication. Claims under 12× the local monthly minimum wage are final at award: the company cannot sue again. In 2024, 4.257 million arbitration cases were filed, 4.156 million concluded, 93.47 billion yuan at stake resolved; mediation success 79.6%, case-closure rate 98.2%, finality rate 73.7%. The "half a year to a year" talk describes post-arbitration court cases: 6 months first instance (3 under simplified procedure) plus 3 on appeal. In 2024, courts concluded 88,000 wage-claim cases and recovered 28.54 billion yuan; 998 people were convicted of the crime of refusing to pay wages (national)
Note
Complaints and arbitration work, but distinguish "concluded" from "paid": the 98.2% closure rate only means procedure completed. Assetless companies and absconded bosses leave judgments unenforced. The Supreme Court publishes only total enforcement recovered (2.3 trillion yuan in 2024) and "high completion rates"; how much of wage cases reached pockets isn't published. "Finality rate" is undefined in the bulletin — read here as "awarded without proceeding to court." Unpaid wages cross the criminal threshold in two ways: one worker, 3+ months, 5,000–20,000+ yuan; or 10+ workers, 30,000–100,000+ cumulative — refusal after a payment order makes the case. Provincial high courts and procuratorates set local figures within these bands and publish them; check yours and raise it when filing. Construction workers have dedicated wage accounts and general-contractor advance liability — going to the general contractor beats the labor boss. Both routes presuppose an employer; unlicensed workshops still count. Private work for households — nannying — isn't a labor relationship; that's court: item 22. Migrant workers claiming wages get legal aid without means-testing. The statute texts are quoted from tax-bureau and Guizhou reprints (both gov.cn) because the NPC site was unreachable. Criminal Law Amendment VIII failed to fetch on the NPC site; verified via curl.

Cost
Free. Legal aid charges the aided nothing.

Income below the local dibao line: apply for dibao

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Household income per head below the local dibao line, assets within limits: you can apply. At end-2024 the national averages were 798.1 yuan per person monthly urban, 593.9 rural. The payment is the gap: line minus per-head monthly income. Property, cars, savings, or children able to support you can block approval.

Cost
Free. A household member applies in writing at the township or subdistrict of your household registration; village or residents' committees can act for you. Expect income and asset verification. Usually 2–3 trips with IDs, household registers, and income/asset proof. The hard part is baring your finances to scrutiny and waiting through publication.
Benefit
Household per-head income below the local standard with assets in range qualifies. End-2024 national averages: 798.1 yuan/person/month urban, 593.9 rural; urban dibao covered 6.25 million people, rural 33.615 million. Payment is the monthly gap: standard minus per-head income — e.g., standard 798.1 and household income 500 per head means 298.1 monthly per head, not 798.1. The standard is set from the prior year's local per-capita consumption times a ratio, adjusted periodically — last year's average spending per person, discounted (national average; local figures differ)
Note
Dibao is the last safety net, applied for at the registration locality. Household property, vehicles, or savings above local standards, or children with support capacity, can block approval. Approval brings more: subsidized resident medical insurance (item 9), medical assistance for care (item 10), and means-test-free legal aid (item 3).

For serious illness, go through insurance, major-illness cover, medical assistance, and cross-region filing — not online loans

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

The order is fixed. File before cross-province hospitalization in the NHSA account; settle at discharge without fronting the full bill. Still unaffordable after reimbursement: apply for medical assistance at the township or subdistrict. Employed: 3–24 months of medical-treatment period by seniority, during which the company cannot dismiss you. Avoid online loans and high-interest private borrowing.

Cost
Free. The order is fixed. Step 1: before a cross-province hospitalization, file via the "National Cross-Region Treatment Filing" mini-program inside the "National Healthcare Security Administration" WeChat account. Step 2: settle directly at discharge. Step 3: if the remainder is still crushing, apply for medical assistance at the township or subdistrict. Step 4: if employed, take sick leave under the medical-treatment period — the sick yet un-dismissable window; work injuries go to work-injury insurance. Step 5: credit cards unpayable — proactively negotiate installments with the bank. Step 6: only then, fundraise on civil-affairs-designated personal-help platforms. Materials: diagnosis certificate, bills, settlement statements; 2–4 trips. The hard part is running errands while ill.
Benefit
The state stacks basic insurance, major-illness insurance, and medical assistance into the "triple system," catching layer by layer. Dibao recipients and the destitute get at least 70% of eligible costs assisted; patients impoverished by treatment may apply for further assistance. Cross-province filing enables direct settlement at discharge — no fronting and reimbursing back home. Sick leave carries a 3–24-month medical-treatment period by seniority, during which the employer may not terminate, and sick pay may not fall below 80% of local minimum wage. Injured workers get the wage-and-benefit-preserving recuperation period, paid monthly by the employer, generally up to 12 months. Credit-card debt beyond capacity with willingness to repay can be restructured into personalized installments up to 5 years — signed, the bank must stop collections. Personal-help fundraising platforms must be designated by the civil affairs ministry, verify the information, and pay donations only to the seeker or their designated account (national)
Note
Assistance percentages and annual caps are set by your enrollment locality. The medical-treatment period has six tiers by total and current-employer seniority; once it lapses, the company may lawfully terminate — know your tier in advance. Emergency patients are also on the filing list; the NHSA page doesn't say whether emergencies auto-file or can be filed retroactively — call your enrollment locality. No online loans or high-interest private borrowing: courts protect only up to 4× the one-year LPR (item 15) — the excess is unprotected, principal still owed — and you lack the strength to litigate from a sickbed. Acute emergencies differ: call 120 without money; hospitals may not refuse or delay rescue, and the disease-emergency-assistance fund covers that rescue — Section 24, item 8. The 劳部发〔1995〕309 号 original page was unreachable on MOHRSS; content from a provincial reprint.

Don't just send résumés — use a systematic method: learn skills, set targets, ask for help

Pooling 47 controlled job-search intervention studies (experimental or quasi-experimental designs), participants were 2.67 times as likely to land jobs (OR 2.67, an odds ratio). Interventions combining skill and motivation content worked best

Mostly Euro-American group-course formats — transplanting to China is borrowing results, not local measurement. "Social support" in practice: acquaintances introducing and referring you — don't be shy.

No deposits, no surrendered IDs, no "training loans," no pyramid schemes, no loan sharks

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Employers may not hold your ID, take deposits, or collect fees under any name. Agencies that fail to place you must refund. Pay-to-work "training loans" and headcount-commission pyramid schemes are officially named scams. Loan interest beyond 4× the one-year LPR gets no court support — but principal is still owed.

Cost
Free. Refuse on the spot: "pay first, job later," "train first, placement later," "recruit heads for money." Keep chats and transfer receipts. The hard part: the shorter of money you are, the more you want to gamble — saying no gets hard.
Benefit
Companies may not withhold IDs, require guarantors, or take money or property under other names — violations draw refund orders plus fines of 500–2,000 yuan per person. Agencies likewise; failed placements mean refunded fees. Recruitment-branded demands to prepay training or loans are the "recruit-to-train" and "training-loan" scams flagged by five departments. Headcount-commission, pay-to-join schemes are pyramid selling — participants fined up to 2,000 yuan. Private-lending interest above 4× the one-year LPR at signing gets no support, replacing the old 24%/36% three-band rules (national, from August 2020)
Note
4× LPR caps protected interest, not "borrow and don't repay" — principal stands. The interpretation was amended again in December 2020 with renumbered articles; the current text governs. Converting installment and online-loan fees to annualized rates: Section 5, item 7. The more desperate for money, the more these schemes target you — go through the legitimate channels above first: unemployment benefits, labor inspection, legal aid, relief stations, temporary assistance.

Free. Resident pension and resident medical insurance can be self-paid yearly. Broken employee contributions need no paid "affiliation" services.

Prison, bankruptcy, or the deadbeat list — the law has roads back; finish the paperwork first

Released prisoners may not be discriminated against in employment, schooling, or social insurance; the government assists the destitute. Crimes committed under 18 with sentences under 5 years are sealed — no disclosure for military or jobs. Deadbeat listings run 2 years; debt cleared means delisting within 3 working days. Adult records aren't sealed — honest disclosure required.

Cost
No fees. Released prisoners register at the judicial office or subdistrict of registration or residence and apply for resettlement assistance. Deadbeat-listed debtors repay, then apply to the executing court for delisting. Shenzhen residents enrolled 3+ years may apply for personal bankruptcy. Each step takes materials, interviews, and 1–3-year probation. The hard part: retelling your past repeatedly and outlasting probation.
Benefit
Released prisoners enjoy equal rights, free of discrimination in employment, schooling, and social security; the destitute get government placement and lawful assistance (Prison Law 2026 revision, effective November 1). The 2010 central document mandated reinforced vocational training, dibao inclusion where qualified, and transitional placement bases. Under-18 crimes with sentences under 5 years are sealed — no reporting for military or employment; certificates of no criminal record issue within 3 working days on application. Deadbeat listings run 2 years; debt settled or settlement reached means delisting within 3 working days. The Shenzhen special-zone personal bankruptcy regulation is currently the only personal-bankruptcy law: after a 3-year observation period post-adjudication, unpaid debts may be discharged. Enterprise legal persons unable to pay due debts with liabilities exceeding assets may seek reorganization, composition, or liquidation — debts die with the entity (national; personal bankruptcy Shenzhen-only)
Note
Adult records aren't sealed: Criminal Law Article 100 requires truthful disclosure of criminal punishment for military and employment. Civil servants, judges, lawyers, and teachers face additional statutory bars. The pre-November-2026 Prison Law text corresponds to Articles 37–38; numbering follows the effective text. The 2010 central document wasn't found on the central government site; taken from a district reprint. During bankruptcy probation: no first-class flights, no luxury spending, no home purchase; 8 debt classes including intentional personal-injury damages are non-dischargeable; fraudulently obtained discharges can be revoked. Delisting from the deadbeat list doesn't clean the credit record — separate systems.

These products cover the post-insurance out-of-pocket share and income stoppage. Before buying, find "guaranteed renewal" (保证续保): without it, the product can be pulled or repriced next year. Disclose health honestly — concealment voids claims. Basic insurance first; this second.

Cost
One-year expense-reimbursement medical cover for the young runs a few hundred yuan yearly — expense-reimbursement meaning it repays actual spending. Critical-illness cover starts at a few thousand (author's estimate; no official figures). Honest health disclosure; half an hour once.

Officials split the products in two: medical insurance reimburses actual costs; disease insurance pays the agreed sum on diagnosis of listed conditions. Insuring while ill without disclosure voids claims. Disclosure has a two-year clock: past two years, the insurer can no longer rescind for non-disclosure and must pay; within two years, intentional concealment means no payout and no refund. Owed wages: first establish who hired you — unlicensed workshops and labor bosses still answer to labor inspection; only private household work goes to court

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Unlicensed workshops and shops owing wages still answer to labor inspection and arbitration — the owner personally. Labor bosses underpaying subcontracted site work: the general contractor or project owner pays. Only private household work — nannying — isn't a labor dispute: that's court.

Cost
Free. Establish three things: whether the counterparty runs a business; whether the work subcontracted down from a company or site; whether you work inside someone's household. Licenses are checkable on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
Benefit
Labor Contract Law Article 2 confines "employers" to enterprises, individual economic organizations, and private non-enterprises — natural persons excluded. The Supreme Court's labor-dispute interpretation lists non-labor disputes: household-domestic-service disputes; craftsman-helper and master-apprentice disputes; rural contracting-household employment disputes. These go to court as ordinary civil disputes, 3-year limitation. Unlicensed employers aren't excepted: Article 93 obliges the unit or its investor to pay remuneration, compensation, and damages for work performed. Interpretation Article 29 lists the unit or investor as party for unlicensed, revoked, or expired-but-operating employers. Labor Inspection Regulations Article 33 puts unlicensed or revoked employers with labor usage under inspection. Illegal individual contracting harming workers: the contracting-out organization and the individual contractor bear joint liability (Article 94). Projects contracted or subcontracted to individuals or unlicensed units causing migrant-wage arrears: the project owner or general contractor pays (Migrant Wage Protection Regulations Article 36) (national)
Note
Judge in this order. Was the work subcontracted from a company or site? Go to the contracting company or general contractor — dedicated accounts and advance clearance in item 2. Is the counterparty in business — shop, factory, workshop? Licensed or not, inspection and arbitration, with the owner personally listed in arbitration. Only private household work remains for court: sue yourself, prove yourself, 6+ months at first instance. Attorney fees aren't court-awarded costs; unaffordable means legal aid — item 3. With an IOU, seek a payment order; small claims for small amounts: Section 8, item 22. The 3-year limitation: Section 8, item 19. No route guarantees payment — judgment against the assetless collects nothing.
