8. Don't put yourself on the line: law and property safety

46 entries

This section counts money and personal freedom, not lifespan. Three things: what the law makes you liable for, how following it cuts what you pay, and what procedural rights you hold when things go wrong. Article numbers are verified against official texts. Ordering: biggest one-time loss with least effort first; advance arrangements middle; experience-only, no official backing, last. Entries in this section are grouped by theme, with item numbers in parentheses. Anti-fraud: the moment you spot fraud, demand payment stop (item 2), hard anti-fraud rules (item 3), a face on video isn't verification (item 4), never lend bank or phone cards (item 8), free credit reports (item 9), scammed online or secondhand (item 22), ask the price before door-to-door repairs (item 27), never carry things for strangers (item 29), "just scan your face for me" is AB-loan fraud (item 45). Signing, lending, debt: read the whole page before signing (item 17), write a proper IOU (item 18), rights enforcement has deadlines (item 19), report assets truthfully under enforcement (item 20), the deadbeat list (item 21), never be a nominee legal representative (item 28), a family member's gambling debts (item 44). Conflict and grievance: call police at the first sign of conflict (item 10), you may fight back against unavoidable attack (item 11), don't settle scores over a grudge (item 12), never strike uninvolved people (item 13), when "take them with me" thoughts appear (item 14), when someone near you says "nobody gets to be okay" (item 15), the insure-first-then-attack road is closed (item 38). Love and marriage: think before delivering large gifts (item 23), betrothal gifts by transfer (item 24), write premarital property down (item 25), verify marital status before marrying (item 26), domestic violence: call police first (item 43). Police, accusation, evidence: lawyer first when summoned (item 5), volunteer to explain after an incident (item 6), when falsely reported (item 33), insufficient evidence means acquittal (item 34), state compensation (item 35), demand a case-filing receipt when reporting (item 39), never bribe case handlers (item 40), record conversations that may turn hostile (item 41), photograph the wide scene first (item 42). Online speech and mobbing: no insults, no rumors online (item 16), turn on protection when mobbed (item 37). Sex and extortion: no sex with someone whose consciousness is impaired (item 31), sextortion: go straight to police (item 32), victims claiming compensation: never meet the other side alone (item 36). Driving, dogs, burglary: traffic accident: stop, save, report — never flee (item 1), drinking means no steering wheel (item 7), leash your dog (item 30), fit good locks (item 46).

1

In a traffic accident: stop, help the injured, call police — never drive off

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Flee, and the accident defaults to your full fault — license revoked for life, never testable again. The practical layer: own-damage and third-party coverage never pay for hit-and-run; hundreds of thousands come out of your pocket. Staying, helping, reporting costs an hour or two.

Cost
Free. Stop, hazard lights, help, call police — waiting for traffic police costs at most an hour or two. Minor accidents without injuries or factual disputes: photograph first, note the other party's name, phone, plate, license number, insurance certificate number, and impact points; both sign, then clear the scene and negotiate.
Benefit
The fleeing party bears full liability; only proof of the other side's fault reduces it. Fleeing also revokes the license permanently. If the accident constitutes the crime of traffic offense, fleeing draws 3–7 years; if fleeing causes death, 7+. Insurance pays nothing: commercial own-damage and third-party clauses exclude "traffic-offense flight" and "deliberately destroying, fabricating the scene, or destroying evidence" — the hundreds of thousands are yours alone (national)
Note
With injuries: save first, then report. Moving the scene to save people: mark the original positions of vehicles and people first. "Bumped and felt nothing, drove on" can later count as flight — when unsure, call police. The insurance clause cites the model terms — an industry template; your actual policy governs.

The moment you realize you've been scammed, call 110 or 96110 and demand a payment stop — don't investigate first

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The brief window right after money leaves is the only one. Police can emergency-stop and fast-freeze; banks must comply. Once the money hops and scatters, recovery is basically gone. So call 110 or 96110 first — not your own inquiry. 96110 calling in is police warning you: answer.

Cost
Free. One call stating the transfer time, amount, and counterparty account. Keep transfer screenshots and chats.
Benefit
Police may conduct instant queries, emergency stops, and fast freezes on involved funds; banks and payment institutions must comply. Frozen funds return to victims by procedure. Once transferred and dispersed, recovery odds collapse — the earlier the stop, the better. 96110 is the national unified anti-fraud warning line; incoming calls are police dissuasion — answer them (national, since December 2022)
Note
Anyone claiming to be police, prosecutors, or courts and telling you to move money to a "safe account" is a scam. The law establishes the stop-and-freeze system; how much returns depends on whether the money is still in the account when you report. The "National Anti-Fraud Center" app and 96110 descriptions come from the Fujian provincial page; the MPS original was unreachable.

3

Memorize the hard anti-fraud rules: distrust callers, disclose nothing, click no links, verify transfers — the seven commonest scams share this shape

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Anything asking for transfers, screen shares, unknown app installs, link clicks, or verification codes: hang up, then call back on official numbers to verify. The seven commonest — task-brushing rebates, fake investment schemes, online loans, fake customer service, fake police/prosecutors/courts, pig-butchering, sexual-bait task scams — all want your money first. Recognizing them beforehand is far cheaper than chasing money afterward.

Cost
Free. Memorize the "three no's, one more"; read the seven types below; install the "National Anti-Fraud Center" app; always answer 96110. Anything asking you to transfer, share your screen, install unknown apps, click links, or read verification codes: hang up first, then verify via official numbers. The hard part: they rush you — resist and hang up anyway.
Benefit
The law requires government to publicize telecom-fraud methods. Police, with finance, telecom, and cyberspace authorities, run warning-and-dissuasion systems; 96110 is the national line — answer it. MPS's June 2026 briefing: the top 10 scam types account for 85% of cases; task-brushing rebates lead incidence at 25%; fake investment schemes lead losses at about 40%. Fujian police's type-by-type markers: task-brushing — "anyone inviting you to make money together mostly wants to make money off you," principal never refunded until endless tasks; fake investments — shills post gains in groups, small rebates first, then bigger asks, withdrawal "requires taxes"; online loans — "real loans never require deposits or flow-making; if asked, it's fake"; fake customer service — claims you enrolled in auto-charging memberships affecting credit, demanding transfer to cancel; fake police/courts — "no 'safe account' exists; any 'police' handling cases by phone, QQ, WeChat, or internet is fraud"; pig-butchering — "never trust a 'lover' you've never met except in photos or video," never video-chatting or meeting yet always with money emergencies; sexual-bait tasks — dates preceded by "tasks," payments mounting. Recognition beforehand beats post-hoc stops; recovery depends on money still sitting in accounts at report time — item 2 (national, since December 2022)
Note
Anyone claiming to be police, customer service, a boss, or platform risk control asking you to "cooperate with investigation," "cancel membership," "brush tasks for rebates," or share "investment tips" runs one script. Real loans need no deposits; police have no safe accounts — those two sentences block half of everything. Grade B because the mnemonic is official propaganda without measured prevention rates. The mnemonic and seven-type breakdown come from a provincial page. The MPS's other top-ten types — fake e-commerce logistics, loan-credit, game trading, online dating, fake bosses and acquaintances, ticket rebooking — all end in "transfer money." An acquaintance asking you to "face-scan for a loan" — no transfer, but debt on you — is item 45. Agency-operation scams in business: Section 12, item 24.

4

A face on video or a voice on the phone isn't verification — for anything involving transfers, hang up and call back on the old number in your own contacts

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Seeing a face, hearing a voice — none of it verifies. Anything involving transfers: hang up, call back on the old number stored in your contacts, or ask a mutual acquaintance. "Bad signal," "in a meeting," refusing live video — treat as fraud.

Cost
Free. One extra call, a few extra minutes. Post fewer full-face videos and long voice clips on public accounts. The hard part: they rush you — don't transfer on the spot.
Benefit
MPS cybersecurity gave three methods. Motion verification: ask for a continuous head turn or a full palm-cover of the face quickly removed — "current AI easily stutters, blurs, or distorts simulating these complex occlusions and lighting shifts." Voice details: "AI-generated speech sometimes lacks natural breathing pauses and emotional contour, or carries slight mechanicality, abnormal background noise." Multi-channel verification — "the core move": "hang up and dial the number you know to be theirs (never redial the suspicious incoming number), or verify sideways through a mutual third party." The mnemonic: "video and voice deserve no trust; motion-verify and cross-check." Legally, face- and voice-swapping is banned for fraud; face generation, face replacement, synthesized speech, and voice imitation must carry prominent labels on platforms, and no one may maliciously delete, alter, forge, or hide the label. But compliant parties are platforms — scammers don't label, so "no AI mark seen" can't prove a real person. MPS criminal investigation published a case: a 14-person ring caught with 50,000-odd synthetic dynamic face videos and 500,000-odd personal data records; 60 cloud servers seized (national; labeling duty since 2025-09-01)
Note
Call back on the old number in your contacts — never redial the incoming display, never use a fresh number sent in chat. "Bad signal" or "in a meeting" refusals of live video or the motion test: treat as fraud. Motion verification is auxiliary — AI keeps improving; only the third method, cross-checking, is stable. Already transferred: item 2 (call 110 for a stop). Preventing your face and voice from being harvested: Section 14. Grade B because officials give methods and cases, not measured fraud-rate drops. The MPS site returned 521s again; originals taken from Fujian reprints.

Accused or summoned: lawyer first — no private settlements, no deleting records

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: highTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

From the first questioning, you may retain a lawyer. When your lawyer requests a meeting, the detention center arranges it within 48 hours, unmonitored. Questions unrelated to the case: you may decline.

Cost
Attorney fees from a few thousand yuan; the destitute get legal-aid lawyers free. In questioning, answer only case-related questions; leave the rest to counsel. The hard part: staying calm rather than explaining yourself in panic.
Benefit
From the first interrogation or compulsory measure (loss of liberty), you may retain counsel. During police investigation, only lawyers may serve as defenders. Requested meetings: within 48 hours, unmonitored. No one may be forced to prove their own guilt. Unrelated questions may be refused. Summons or compulsory appearance: 12 hours max, 24 for major complex cases; no back-to-back summons amounting to disguised detention. Fabricating facts to falsely accuse another of criminal liability: up to 3 years; serious consequences, 3–10. Detained or arrested, then case withdrawn, not prosecuted, or acquitted: state compensation applies, paid per day at the prior year's national average daily wage (national)
Note
Don't privately seek the other party or their family — any "settlement" can read as admission. Chats, calls, and travel records are your proof of innocence; deleting them destroys your own evidence. Misremembering or reporting something later unproven isn't false accusation. This entry applies to the accused of any sex. The three expansions: items 33 (pursuing the fabricator), 34 (insufficient evidence means acquittal, plus retrial), and 35 (per-day state compensation after detention).

6

After an incident, go explain voluntarily: surrender cuts up to 40% of the sentence, minor crimes cut more or escape punishment entirely — "outlast the limitation period" is a dead end

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Surrender cuts up to 40% of the sentence; minor crimes can escape punishment outright. Truthful confession after being found cuts up to 20%. Fleeing and denial buy nothing. Outlasting the limitation period fails too: once a case is filed, your years in hiding don't count toward the clock.

Cost
Free. Turn yourself in at the police, or stay put and call, then tell it truthfully. The hard part: resisting "wait and see; maybe nobody investigates."
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 67: voluntary surrender plus truthful confession is surrender — punishable more leniently, minor crimes exempt. Truthful confession without surrender (confession) earns leniency; confession preventing especially serious consequences earns mitigation. The two supremes' sentencing guidance sets the discounts, all below the baseline sentence computed from the case. Surrender: up to 40% off; minor crimes: 40%+ off or exemption. Confession: up to 20% off; confessing the same-category heavier crime unknown to authorities: 10%–30%; preventing especially serious consequences: 30%–50%. Guilty plea with acceptance of punishment: up to 30% off; combined with surrender, major confession, restitution, or compensation-and-forgiveness: up to 60%; minor crimes: 60%+ or exemption. Limitation periods run in four tiers by statutory maximum: 5, 10, 15, 20 years (Article 87). But Article 88: once procuratorate, police, or state security files, or the court accepts the case, evading investigation or trial escapes no limitation (national; sentencing ranges since 2021-07-01)
Note
The beneficiary is yourself. Surrender is only mitigation — the crime still stands, the court sets the discount, and violent and drug crimes require strict application. Traffic accidents have their own arithmetic: staying, saving, and reporting count as voluntary surrender, but as these are statutory duties the leniency is strict; surrendering after fleeing still counts, only from the heavier statutory band as baseline — see item 1. Lawyer first and truthful confession don't conflict (item 5): the lawyer checks the transcript's accuracy, not your story.

Alcohol means no steering wheel — including e-bikes and "just moving the car"

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Drunk driving: 6-month license suspension and a 1,000–2,000 yuan fine; repeat offense, detention plus revocation. Driving while intoxicated revokes outright, no retest for 5 years, criminal liability for dangerous driving with a record that affects vetting and some careers. Insurance pays nothing for drink-driving. "Just moving the car" counts as driving.

Cost
A designated driver or taxi runs a few dozen yuan. Agree before the gathering who stays dry. The hard part: pushing back against toasts.
Benefit
Drunk driving: 6-month suspension plus 1,000–2,000 fine; repeat: up to 10 days' detention and revocation. Intoxicated driving: outright revocation, 5-year retest ban, criminal liability under dangerous driving — short custody plus fine (detention meaning short-term confinement). Commercial drivers face more: drunk, 15 days, 5,000 fine, 5-year ban; intoxicated, 10-year ban and lifetime commercial ban. Drink-caused major accidents constituting crimes: lifetime ban. Commercial auto insurance never pays for drink or drug driving (national)
Note
Intoxicated driving is a criminal record affecting vetting and some qualifications. "Drinking" versus "intoxication" lines follow the blood-alcohol national standard — this section hasn't verified the numbers; don't guess your band by feel.

Never lend bank cards, phone cards, or payment accounts to anyone — "money muling" isn't a side job

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Renting, lending, or selling bank cards, phone cards, or payment accounts is itself illegal: fines of 1–10× illegal gains, up to 200,000 without gains, up to 15 days' detention when serious, plus credit-record entries and account restrictions. Knowingly helping collect and transfer criminal money is the aiding-cybercrime crime — up to 3 years.

Cost
Free. "Borrow your card to run some money, a few hundred for you" — refuse.
Benefit
Renting, lending, buying, or selling phone cards, bank accounts, payment accounts, or internet accounts is itself illegal: confiscation of gains plus 1–10× fines; without gains, up to 200,000 yuan; serious cases, up to 15 days' detention; credit-record entries, account restrictions, suspension of non-counter services (counter-only banking). Knowingly providing payment-settlement help for cybercrime, when serious, constitutes the crime of assisting information-network criminal activity (aiding-cybercrime), punishable up to 3 years plus fines (national)
Note
"I didn't know what they'd do with the card" doesn't shield you: investigators infer knowledge from circumstances — benefit fees received, abnormal flow. Cards used to receive criminal funds freeze even without charges, with personal penalties. Face-scanning or reading codes to pass identity verification for others carries the same penalties — item 45.

At the first sign of conflict, call police — don't strike; whoever strikes first almost always loses

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Hitting someone: 5–10 days' detention plus a 500–1,000 yuan fine. Group beatings, hitting elders, pregnant women, children, or the disabled, or repeat offenses: 10–15 days, 1,000–2,000. Light injury is criminal — up to 3 years; serious injury, 3–10. Mutual fighting isn't self-defense; the first striker almost always loses. Retreating and calling police beats swinging back.

Cost
Free. Retreat to a crowded, camera-covered spot and call. The hard part: not talking back, not shoving.
Benefit
Assault or intentional injury: 5–10 days plus 500–1,000 yuan. Grouped assaults, assaults on elders/pregnant women/children/the disabled, repeat assaults or multiple victims: 10–15 days plus 1,000–2,000. Group brawling is handled as picking quarrels — up to 15 days plus 2,000. Intentional injury constituting crime: up to 3 years; serious injury: 3–10. Mutual combat isn't lawful defense — but if the other side struck first with clearly excessive means, or you tried to escape and they kept attacking, counterstrikes are generally recognized as defense. Excess becomes excessive defense only with both: clearly exceeding necessary limits AND causing major harm. Even genuine excess should be mitigated or exempted (national; Public Security Administration Punishments Law since 2026-01-01)
Note
The 2025 revision renumbered everything — assault moved from old Article 43 to new Article 51; sources citing old numbers are stale. "Light injury" thresholds follow forensic standards, unverified here. Once the attacker is down or fleeing, the attack has stopped — chasing and hitting is no defense. Carrying knives, batons, or stun guns "for protection" is itself punishable: Section 9, item 26.

11

Unavoidable attack may be met with force — but only against the person attacking, and only while they keep at it

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: highTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

While someone is attacking you or another, stopping them and injuring them carries no criminal liability. Ongoing assault, homicide, robbery, rape, or kidnapping — injuring or killing the attacker isn't excessive. But only the attacker, only while it lasts. Even when the final ruling favors you, you may be case-filed and held first.

Cost
Attorney fees from a few thousand; legal aid if destitute. The main price comes after: cases often open as intentional injury first, with investigation cooperation, sometimes days of initial detention. The hard part: staying steady through that stretch.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 20 defines lawful defense: stopping an unlawful attack on state, public, personal, or property rights, injuring the attacker — no criminal liability. The same article: "defense clearly exceeding necessary limits causing major harm bears criminal responsibility, but shall be mitigated or exempted." Another clause: against ongoing assault, homicide, robbery, rape, kidnapping, and other violent crimes gravely endangering personal safety, defense causing the attacker's death or injury is not excessive. The joint guidance refines the borders: excess requires both "clearly exceeding necessary limits" and "causing major harm" — "major harm" meaning serious injury or death of the attacker; light injury doesn't count. The attack ends only when the attacker truly loses capacity or truly abandons it. Defense must target the attacker personally. Against patently minor attacks recognizable as such, responding with means capable of grave injury or death isn't recognized as defense. Process costs have official cases. Guiding Case 47, Yu Haiming: the night of 2018-08-27, police opened an intentional-injury investigation; on September 1 the Kunshan bureau ruled lawful defense under Article 20(3) and dropped the case. Guiding Case 45, Chen: a student surrounded and beaten by 9, knife counterattack seriously injuring 3; police opened an intentional-injury case and detained him; prosecutors ruled lawful defense, denied arrest approval, and he was freed. Post-detention, police seeking arrest must refer to prosecutors within 3 days (extendable 1–4; 30 for itinerant, serial, or group suspects), with prosecutors deciding within 7 (national)
Note
The default remains item 10 — retreat and call. Mutual fighting isn't defense; neither is chasing a downed or fleeing attacker. Counterforce only at the truly cornered moment. Afterward: don't leave the scene; secure cameras and witnesses fast (the guidance requires police to collect footage and interview witnesses first); get a lawyer before formal questioning (item 5). Case dropped, not prosecuted, or acquitted: the detained days convert to per-day state compensation (item 35). Defending others is equally lawful, but bare-handed intervention in strangers' brawls carries separate risks: Section 13, item 37. Beneficiaries: you and family.

Whoever wronged you — unpaid wages, firing, scammed money — go through complaints, arbitration, suit; never settle scores

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: yesBenefit: large

The legal route's worst case: money unrecovered. Revenge's case: money still unrecovered, plus your life. The Wuxi case: Xu, denied his diploma and resentful of internship pay, stabbed 8 dead and 17 injured — death sentence, executed. Unpaid wages via complaint and arbitration recovered 8.65 billion yuan for 654,000 people in 2024.

Cost
Free — complaints and arbitration cost nothing. A trip or two, months of waiting. The hard part: keeping your hands still through those months.
Benefit
The legal route has official numbers: 2024 labor inspections handled 137,000 cases, recovering 8.65 billion yuan for 654,000; 998 people convicted of refusing to pay wages. How to complain and arbitrate: Section 7, item 2. The revenge menu is Criminal Law Article 232: "intentional homicide: death, life, or 10+ years; minor circumstances, 3–10." Official case: Xu failed his exams, received no diploma, and resented internship pay; on 2024-11-16 he returned to Wuxi Vocational Institute of Arts & Technology and stabbed 8 dead, 17 injured; first instance sentenced death with political-rights deprivation, executed 2025-01-20 upon Supreme Court approval. His grievance was with the school and the pay; the victims were classmates — and he never got the pay either (national)
Note
Student interns generally lack labor relationships — internship pay disputes go through the school or the courts, not arbitration. Private household work owed money: courts too — Section 7, item 22. How to complain about wages: Section 7, item 2. Debt-collection red lines: Section 9, item 15 (no detaining people). The legal route can also fail — concluded isn't paid. Revenge fails twice: no money, plus your life.

Driving into crowds or attacking in public is charged as endangering public safety by dangerous means. Zero casualties still means 3 years minimum; deaths mean 10+, life, or death. Zhuhai: Fan, resentful of the divorce settlement, drove into exercisers at a sports center — 35 dead, 43 injured; death sentence, executed.

Cost
Free. The hard part: suppressing the thought in the heat.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 114: arson, breaching dikes, explosions, poison, or "other dangerous methods" endangering public safety without serious consequences: 3–10 years — zero injuries still means 3 minimum. Article 115: serious injury, death, or major property loss: 10 years, life, or death. Official case: Fan, marriage broken and resentful of the property split, "resolved to vent private grievance by driving into a crowd"; on 2024-11-11 he drove into crowds exercising at the Zhuhai Sports Center — 35 dead, 43 injured; first instance death sentence with political-rights deprivation, executed 2025-01-20. The victims were runners he didn't know (national)
Note
"I don't want to live anyway" earns no sentencing discount: the Supreme Court's 2025 report line is "severely, strictly, and swiftly punish those who challenge the bottom lines of law and morality." Even threatening it is already illegal: threatening arson, explosion, or poisoning that disturbs public order — 5–10 days plus up to 1,000 yuan; threatening letters or other threats to personal safety — up to 5 days or 1,000 yuan (law effective 2026-01-01). Thoughts already there: item 14 (treat "taking someone with me" as an emergency).

When "take someone with me" or "die together" thoughts appear, treat them as an emergency: leave the scene, hand car keys and knives to someone else, call 12356

Grade BValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

The window from such a thought to action is minutes. Of 82 attempt survivors, 47.6% said under 10 minutes passed from first thought to act. So the move isn't "thinking it through" — it's putting the wheel, knife, gas valve, and rope one step away, and outlasting the ten minutes. Then call 12356.

Cost
Free. The hard part: admitting you're not okay right now, and putting the means in someone else's hands.
Benefit
The window is short: interviewed within 3 days of admission, 47.6% of 82 attempt survivors said 10 minutes or less from first thought to act. A 10-year systematic review found means-restriction evidence strengthening: painkiller controls cut related suicides 43%; barriers at jumping spots cut suicides 86% (79%–91%). Putting the wheel, knife, valve, and rope one step away is how you buy those ten minutes. 12356 is the national psychological-assistance line, open no fewer than 18 hours daily (national, since 2025-05-01)
Note
Grade B because both pieces come from suicide research, carried to impulses to harm others without direct study; Deisenhammer's covered 82 people at one hospital. Don't drive or take safety-responsible shifts while in a bad state — hand over first. Self-harm: Section 1, item 25. Low mood: Section 3, item 18.

When someone near you says "nobody gets to be okay" or "take the kids with us," don't read it as venting: close relatives may take them directly for evaluation, and police must act on the call

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

A family member saying those lines: close relatives may take them straight to a medical institution, which may not refuse diagnosis. Violence already done or imminent: hospitalization needs no consent. Unsure whether it's venting or real: call 12356 to ask, or 110 for police on scene. Covering for them isn't helping them.

Cost
Registration and consults run tens to hundreds of yuan; the escort takes half a day to a day. The hard part: talking them into going.
Benefit
Mental Health Law Article 28(2): a suspected patient harming self or others, or at risk of it — close relatives, the employer, or local police "shall immediately take measures to stop it and send them to a medical institution for diagnosis," and institutions "may not refuse" the evaluation. Article 29: keep them, assign a psychiatrist immediately, issue conclusions promptly. Article 30: hospitalization is voluntary in principle — except diagnosed severe mental disorder with "harm to others already occurred, or danger of it": hospitalization applies without consent. Threats alone justify 110: threatening letters or other threats to personal safety — up to 5 days or 1,000 yuan; threatening arson, explosion, or poisoning disturbing public order — 5–10 days plus up to 1,000 (national; punishments law since 2026-01-01)
Note
By beneficiary, this counts cohabiting spouse, parents, children — "nobody" usually includes you, and the law gives the escort power precisely to close relatives; outsiders can only call police. Escort applies to real danger signals, not quarrel venting, and never as a tool to hospitalize the disobedient: the same law says re-examination finding no severe disorder means discharge (Article 35). Unsure: call 12356 or 110. Unsure whether they're suicidal: ask directly — Section 1, item 43. Germanwings 9525's investigation concluded no authority or employer could stop the co-pilot's flight that day because "neither he nor anyone else — doctors, colleagues, or family — informed them." All 150 aboard died: 2 pilots, 4 cabin crew, 144 passengers.

Public insult or fabricated defamation: up to 5 days' detention or a 1,000-yuan fine; heavier: 5–10 days. Serious cases become the crimes of insult or defamation — up to 3 years. Forwarding doesn't excuse. Conversely, when you're mobbed, insult and defamation are prosecute-on-complaint: the screenshots are yours to gather.

Free. Ten extra seconds before posting. Under attack: screenshot, screen-record, save links and account IDs, complain to the platform, then report. The hard part: not firing back.

Public insult or fabricated defamation: up to 5 days or 1,000 yuan; heavier, 5–10 days. Forwarding still liability attaches — knowingly spreading falsehoods counts as "fabricating facts." When mobbed: item 37. The insult/defamation article moved from old 42 to new 50.

Read the whole page before signing; never sign for others; never sign blanks

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

A signature binds; a thumbprint binds the same. "Didn't read it" and "thought it was something else" almost never stand in court. So read end to end, ask, photograph. Don't sign for others, don't sign blanks, annotate ID-copy purposes. E-signatures and face-scan confirmations count as signing too.

Cost
Free. A few extra minutes reading contracts, IOUs, guarantees, onboarding papers end to end; ask about anything unclear; photograph for the file. The hard part: reading slowly to the end in front of the other party.
Benefit
Lawfully formed contracts bind both signatories. Civil Code Article 490: with contract instruments, "the contract is formed when both parties sign, seal, or thumbprint" — three parallel methods; the thumbprint forms the contract the same. "Didn't read it" fails in court. Not signing means no debt or liability that isn't yours (national)
Note
"Never sign for others, never sign blanks, annotate ID copies" is practice without a single official document — the shared purpose: keep your signature out of a legally formed contract you'd have to honor. E-signatures and face scans count. Acquaintances asking you to face-scan or co-sign loans: item 45.

Write a complete IOU for loans; before guaranteeing anyone, decide whether you'd truly repay for them

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The IOU lists all six elements. Transfers, not cash. When guaranteeing, look for the two characters "joint" (连带). An ordinary guarantee means the creditor must sue the borrower and fail at execution before reaching you; a joint-liability guarantee means they can come straight for you.

Cost
Free. One sheet: lender, borrower, amount, rate, term, repayment method, both signatures. Money moves by transfer — a trace — never cash.
Benefit
Loan contracts should be written, covering type, currency, purpose, amount, rate, term, and repayment — completeness enables suit. Guarantees unclear as to type default to ordinary: the guarantor may wait until the creditor has sued or arbitrated, executed against the borrower's assets, and still come up short. Signing "joint and several guarantee" removes that shield — the creditor comes straight to you (national)
Note
Interest beyond 4× LPR is unprotected: Section 7. Writing ID numbers and the word "loan" on IOUs is practice. The two characters "joint" decide whether you queue behind the borrower or stand beside them in collection — read before signing. Promised "guarantor" but handed a loan contract: item 45.

Rights enforcement has deadlines: 3 years civil, 1 year labor arbitration — past due, one sentence of "limitation expired" from the other side suffices

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Civil limitation runs 3 years from knowing your right was harmed. Past due, courts won't raise it themselves, but the other side's single "limitation expired" in court suffices — the money exists, just unrecoverable. One traced demand message restarts the 3 years. Labor disputes run their own 1-year clock.

Cost
Free. Demand repayment with a trace — WeChat, SMS, email, or registered mail.
Benefit
The Civil Code: "the limitation period for requesting civil-rights protection from the people's court is 3 years," running from when the holder "knew or should have known of the harm and the obligor," capped at 20 years from the harm. On expiry, "the obligor may raise the defense of non-performance" — courts don't check sua sponte, but one mention in court works. Four events interrupt and restart: demanding performance; the obligor agreeing to perform; suing or arbitrating; equivalents. Installments run from the last due date. Four claim types are unlimited: stopping infringement, removing obstacles, eliminating danger; recovering registered real property and movables; support payments; other statutory cases. Labor: 1-year arbitration limitation from knowing of the harm — except "wage disputes during the employment relationship are not subject to it; after termination, file within 1 year" (national)
Note
This is probably the cheapest thing in the book: one traced demand message restarts the 3 years; doing nothing can forfeit a winning case. Pre-agreeing "I won't raise limitation" is void, as is contractually lengthening or shortening the 3 years. Conversely, an obligor who still promises repayment after expiry can't invoke limitation, and voluntary repayments can't be clawed back. IOUs and guarantees: item 18. Enforcement stage: item 20. Overtime and untaken-leave pay under labor arbitration: Section 19, items 1–2.

Sued or under enforcement: report assets truthfully, pay what you can — don't shift houses or money to relatives or companies

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Parking the house under a company and wiring money to relatives is exactly the refusal-of-execution crime — up to 3 years, or 3–7 for especially serious cases. Relatives and companies helping hide or transfer are accomplices, and the money is still chased. Refusing or falsifying asset reports: fines up to 100,000 and 15 days for individuals. Genuinely having no money isn't this crime.

Cost
Free. Report assets per the court's order: what you have now and had in the year before the enforcement notice. Pay what's payable. Can't pay: negotiate settlement and installments with the applicant (the creditor).
Benefit
Transferring assets is itself the crime's trigger. The NPC Standing Committee's interpretation of Criminal Law Article 313 lists "concealing, transferring, deliberately destroying property, transferring gratis or at clearly unreasonably low prices, rendering judgment unenforceable" as "able but refusing, serious." The 2024 two-supreme interpretation adds ten more, including disposing of property rights via fake settlements and fake transfers, buying others' assets at clearly unreasonable high prices, and guaranteeing others' debts — all deliberately hollowing out what could pay creditors. The crime draws up to 3 years; especially serious (fake litigation, arbitration, or notarization obstructing execution; storming execution scenes; attacking, detaining, or beating execution personnel; refusals driving the applicant to suicide or self-harm), 3–7 plus fines. Non-parties knowingly colluding to hide or transfer are accomplices; misappropriated property is recovered or ordered restored. Transfers made after the defendant received notice and before judgment take effect count too. Civilly, gratis and clearly-underpriced transfers can be revoked by creditors. Refusing or falsely reporting assets: fines up to 100,000 for individuals, detention up to 15 days (national; interpretation since December 2024)
Note
The internet meme of "registering the house as company dormitory and wiring everything to relatives" isn't a loophole — it's the named gratis-transfer and fake-transfer scenarios. Helpers count as accomplices; property still gets recovered. Conversely, genuine poverty isn't the crime: "able but refusing" is measured after deducting your necessary living costs and those of your dependents. Repaying part or all before prosecution with minor circumstances can mean non-prosecution; repaying before first-instance judgment can mitigate or exempt. On lists and consumption limits: item 21. Recovery after performance: Section 7, item 19.

Under consumption restrictions or on the deadbeat list: first establish which clause ensnared you, then seek correction where possible

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

First separate the two: consumption restriction versus the deadbeat list — different things. The list admits only six scenarios, lasting 2 years; seven situations, full performance included, require deletion within 3 working days. The restriction bans nine spending classes — G-train seats included. Necessary living or business items can be applied for one by one.

Cost
Free. Query the executing court for the clause invoked. Prepare proof of performance or security materials. Necessary living or business spending needs per-instance application. The hard part: trip after trip, application after application.
Benefit
Six listing scenarios only: able but refusing; obstructing execution with forged evidence or violence; evading via fake litigation, fake arbitration, or hiding/transferring assets; violating asset-reporting rules; violating consumption-restriction orders; refusing settlement agreements without cause. With sufficient valid security, or attached assets covering the debt, the first scenario may not be used; minors may not be listed. Listing runs 2 years, extendable 1–3 for violence-obstruction or multiple breaches. Seven situations — full performance, completed settlement, terminated execution — require deletion within 3 working days; active performance or correction allows early deletion. Restricted individuals may not: fly or take soft sleepers or second-class-plus ship berths; spend at starred hotels, nightclubs, golf; buy property or build/expand/luxuriously renovate; rent high-grade offices; buy non-business vehicles; travel or vacation; send children to high-fee private schools; buy investment insurance at high premiums; take any G-train seat or first-class-plus on other trains. Life-or-business necessities require court-approved application; valid security or creditor consent can lift the restriction (national)
Note
The restriction is "high consumption" restriction — issued 2010, amended 2015 (renamed "…and Related Consumption"), written here per the current text. The 2015 changes matter thrice: ninth class added (all G-train seats); the "paying with one's own property" qualifier deleted; and when a company is restricted, its actual controllers are too — though private personal spending can be applied for. Deadbeat listing and consumption restriction are separate; you may wear only one. Neither equals a credit blemish — delisting doesn't clean credit: Section 7, item 19. Whether spouses' and children's own earnings are restricted isn't stated in the current text; ask the executing court.

Scammed online or secondhand: platform complaint first, then police, then price the lawsuit

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Platform first — deposits and penalty rules make it fastest. Then police: 3,000 yuan and up crosses the fraud threshold; below it, administrative punishment of 5–10 days. For court: online-purchase disputes file at the delivery destination; small claims conclude in 2 months, filable online.

Cost
Platform complaints and police reports are free. Suing: claims under 10,000 yuan cost a 50-yuan filing fee, halved under simplified procedure, mediation, or withdrawal. Filing, hearing, and enforcement each take half a day to a day; online filing saves trips. Keep orders, chats, transfers, and logistics records. The hard part: not giving up mid-hassle.
Benefit
Fraud of 3,000–10,000+ yuan constitutes "relatively large," punishable up to 3 years plus or instead of fines, with provinces setting local thresholds. Below criminal: 5–10 days' detention or up to 2,000 yuan; heavier, 10–15 days plus up to 3,000. Civilly, online-contract disputes file at the delivery court, not the seller's. Claims under 50% of the provincial prior-year average wage use small-claims — final at first instance, concluded within 2 months of filing; simplified procedure, 3 months. Civil litigation runs online with equal effect (national; civil procedure since January 2024, punishments law since January 2026)
Note
Pricing the suit: after-tax hourly rate × hours, plus filing fees; filing, hearing, maybe enforcement at half-day to a day each; compare against the claim, discount by collectability. Decide by that math. The punishments law renumbered theft and fraud from old 49 to new 58; the civil procedure amendment moved small claims to Article 165 — don't copy stale sources. Free. Before a large transfer, ask: loan or gift? A loan gets an IOU and a "loan" transfer memo. The hard part: saying it out loud.

Gifts are revocable before property rights transfer; after transfer, only three grounds: the recipient's grave harm to you or close relatives, failure of support obligations, or breach of stated gift conditions. Festival and birthday gifts of modest value, and daily spending expressing or deepening affection, aren't betrothal gifts and don't return on breakup (national)
Note
"520 and 1314 transfers usually count as gifts" is practitioner lore without a Supreme Court original found here — not stated as conclusion. Notarized gifts can't be freely revoked. Whether a transfer is loan or gift ends in evidence: one chat line of "let me lend you this" beats later argument.

Betrothal gifts by transfer with memos; keep the chats; money extracted through marriage can be recovered

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Extracting property through marriage is legally forbidden, and courts support return. No registration, registration without cohabitation, or premarital gifts impoverishing the giver — all returnable. Registered and cohabiting: generally not. So: transfers with memos, evidence kept by whoever paid — both sexes alike.

Cost
Free. Betrothal gifts, "three golds," and name-change money all by transfer with purpose memos; verbal agreements get chat records or family witnesses.
Benefit
The law forbids extracting property through marriage; demands framed as betrothal gifts are returnable on suit. Three return scenarios: no marriage registration; registration without genuine cohabitation; premarital gifts leaving the giver in hardship. Registered and cohabiting: generally no return — but short cohabitation with excessive amounts gets proportional return factoring spending, dowry, childbirth, and fault. Unregistered cohabitation: likewise proportional (national, since February 2024)
Note
"Excessive" is measured against the giver's local per-capita disposable income and household — no national number. Proportions are case-by-case for judges. Rules bind both sides; whoever paid keeps the evidence.

Premarital property stays personal regardless of years married. Couples may agree in writing that pre- and post-marital property stays separate. Hiding, transferring, squandering, or fabricating debts at divorce costs that party share.

A self-written property agreement is free; notarization costs extra. Parental contributions: ask for a written sentence. A few hours once. The hard part: talking money with family.

Premarital property is personal and doesn't convert through duration. Written agreements — separate, joint, or mixed — bind both. Before marrying, verify marital status; marriage-masked money extraction is fraud

Bigamous marriages are void. Marrying while spouseed, or knowingly marrying the spouseed: up to 2 years. Marriage-masked extraction is fraud: "relatively large," up to 3 years; "huge," 3–10; "especially huge," 10+ or life. Check the documents before registering.

Cost
Free. Before registration, one glance at the ID and household register's marital status. Large exchanges: keep transfers and chats.
Benefit

Door-to-door repairs, inspections, renovations: price first, then work — and watch the whole time

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Appliance repair must display fee standards, issue receipts and invoices, not fabricate faults, not replace working parts — serious violations, up to 30,000 yuan. All operators must post prices with no add-ons. So: price and parts first, receipts and old parts after. Overcharged? Call 12315 first.

Cost
Free. Before work starts, ask the fee standard and which parts get replaced; photograph the quote or get it in writing. After: repair receipt and invoice, keep the old parts. Stand by one or two hours. The hard part: not stepping away.
Benefit
Appliance-repair operators must display service and parts fees, quality standards, warranty terms, and complaint numbers; issue service vouchers and invoices; fill in items and details truthfully; not invent, exaggerate, or forge repair items, not misreport faulty parts, not deliberately replace sound parts — serious cases, up to 30,000 yuan in fines. Services must conspicuously state items, content, price, and pricing method, with no false or misleading promotion (national)
Note
Overcharged: 12315 first — commercial and market regulators punish, no private suit needed. Grade B: official rules, but "how much watching saves" is experience without numbers. Ask, keep receipts, keep old parts — for everyone, no profiling. The appliance rules cover appliances; inspections and renovations follow the price-posting rules and implementation regulation. The Consumer Protection Law backs both rights: Article 8 (right to know content, specifications, fees) and Article 10 (right to refuse forced transactions).

Leash your dog, always: unleashed incidents are strict liability (fault or not, you pay), paid to the end. Vaccinate against rabies on schedule and register the dog

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

When a dog injures someone, you pay regardless of fault — only the victim's intent or gross negligence reduces it. Unleashed, only "victim's intent" can mitigate, and heavier cases can mean detention. Missing rabies shots draw correction orders and fines. Banned fierce breeds get zero defenses.

Cost
A leash costs a few dozen yuan; rabies vaccination and registration cost more, varying locally. The hard part: leashing every walk and remembering boosters.
Benefit
Animal-keeper liability: the keeper or manager answers for injuries; only the victim's provocation or gross negligence reduces it. Violating management rules without safety measures — unleashed — leaves only "victim's intent" as mitigation. Banned fierce dogs: no defense at all. Public Security Punishments Law Article 89: failing safety measures with injury — up to 1,000 yuan; heavier, 5–10 days. Animal Epidemic Prevention Law Article 30: vaccinate dogs against rabies on schedule, register with the immunization certificate, and leash with tags outdoors. Article 92: unvaccinated dogs draw correction deadlines plus up to 1,000 yuan; uncorrected, 1,000–5,000 with agency-handled vaccination at your cost
Note
Dog-bite compensation covers medical costs, lost work, rabies vaccine and immunoglobulin — five figures common, more for severe injuries or children. Abandonment doesn't shed liability: injuries by abandoned or escaped animals still bill the original keeper. Epidemic-prevention specifics — registration, fees, booster intervals — are provincial. Post-bite handling: Section 13, item 13.

31

If the other party is drunk to unconsciousness, asleep, or possibly under 14: no sex

Grade BValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Someone drunk to unconsciousness or asleep can't consent — sex then counts legally as rape, base sentence 3–10 years, and you'll almost never prove after-the-fact consent. The only reliable move: no sex; hand the person to their own friends or family as the party breaks up. Age determination: Section 9, item 18 (under 14).

Cost
Free. The price is stopping in the moment. The hard part: stopping.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 236: rape by violence, coercion, "or other means" — 3–10 years. "Other means" isn't limited to force: incapacity to consent falls inside those words. Aggravated rape (multiple victims, vile circumstances): 10+, life, or death. The same article: intercourse with girls under 14 is rape, aggravated — age determination in Section 9, item 18. A Beijing Xicheng procuratorate explainer states that sexually assaulting women "after anesthetizing or getting them drunk likewise constitutes rape"; the key is "whether the victim's true inner will was violated" — visible resistance is "not the key." Article 237 covers forcible indecency by violence, coercion, or other means — up to 5 years or short custody (national)
Note
Grade B because the statute says only "other means"; "drunk counts as rape" comes from a procuratorate explainer, not a judicial interpretation. The rape article names women only; male victims route through forcible indecency — so no unconscious person, either sex. As the victim yourself: Section 13, item 42. Blackout-drunk, you face accusation and extortion simultaneously: item 32.

32

After sex or nude chats, threats to report, leak photos, or tell your employer get zero payment and zero deletions — report to police

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

"I'll report you / send photos to your workplace / tell your family" for money is extortion. Not one yuan, not one deletion, report immediately — the first payment buys the second. Actually leaking adds a count to their crimes. Extortion of 2,000–5,000+ yuan draws up to 3 years; 30,000–100,000+, 3–10.

Cost
Free. Screenshot accounts, chats, and payment QR codes; bring the phone to the station. The hard part: resisting "pay to make it go away."
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 274: extortion "relatively large" or repeated — up to 3 years, custody, or control, plus or instead of fines; "huge" or serious circumstances, 3–10 plus fines; especially huge, 10+ plus fines. The two-supreme interpretation (法释〔2013〕10 号) sets the bands: 2,000–5,000+ = "relatively large"; 30,000–100,000+ = "huge"; 300,000–500,000+ = "especially huge." Article 3: three extortions within 2 years count as "repeated" (national). Civil Code Articles 1032–1033: no one may probe into, disturb, leak, or publicize privacy — so leaking adds their counts. Fujian police's phrase for these cases: "preserve the evidence, dial 110 promptly, never keep transferring"
Note
The three money bands are provincially set within the interpretation's ranges; check yours. Three times in two years counts regardless of amounts. Don't delete chats, photos, accounts, or block-and-move-on — that's destroying your own evidence (item 5); under investigation, those records prove your innocence. Don't "negotiate installments" either. Sextortion is mostly offshore crews screen-recording while trojans read your contacts — "send to your family" is script, and police still file. "Outing you as gay to your family" for money is the same extortion: a Yancheng, Jiangsu man took 14,500 yuan that way off a dating-app meet and was prosecuted — twice previously convicted identically. Nude-photo coercion into sex is rape: a Xiangshan, Zhejiang man tricked nude photos from multiple women and threatened publication — 10 victims identified; one reported immediately, two had never met him, and prosecutors still charged attempted rape, final counts rape plus forcible indecency. So never send nudes to internet acquaintances. Conversely, as a victim claiming compensation, a high number isn't automatically extortion: item 36. Photos actually posted: you may notify the platform for deletion under Civil Code Article 1195 — preliminary evidence plus your real identity; platforms failing to act share liability for the expanded harm.

Insufficient evidence means acquittal by right; coerced confessions must be excluded; after judgment come petitions and retrial

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

The conviction threshold is written: evidence verified through legal procedure, and the combined record excluding reasonable doubt. Falling short means acquittal. Torture-extracted confessions and violence- or threat-extracted testimony must be excluded from judgment. After finality, you, your legal representative, and close relatives may petition.

Cost
Procedure itself is free, but petitions and retrials consume time. Lawyers from a few thousand yuan; legal aid for the destitute (item 5). The hard part: outlasting round after round.
Benefit
Criminal Procedure Law Article 55: evidence is sufficient when all case-fixing evidence is legally verified and the totality excludes reasonable doubt — no other plausible account surviving. Article 56: confessions extracted by torture and witness or victim statements extracted by violence or threats "shall be excluded," and may not ground prosecution opinions, charges, or judgments. Article 200(3): insufficient evidence requires a judgment of not guilty — the charge cannot stand. Article 252: parties, legal representatives, and close relatives may petition courts or procuratorates over effective judgments — though petitions don't stay execution. Article 253 lists the retrial triggers (national)
Note
These are the written floors; outcomes aren't guaranteed. No verifiable official acquittal or petition-reversal rates exist for China, so no ratios or case commentary here. Three things you can do: retain counsel after the first interrogation (item 5); read transcripts word by word before signing; never confess to what you didn't do for an earlier exit — guilty-plea leniency mitigates but never exempts. Meeting statutory grounds, courts must retry.

Detained, then case withdrawn, not prosecuted, or acquitted: claim state compensation, counted by the day

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Detention or arrest followed by withdrawal, non-prosecution, or acquittal means state compensation. Detained days pay by the day — from 2026-05-18, 495.94 yuan daily, about 180,000 a year. Grave consequences add solatium. Minor-circumstance non-prosecution pays nothing; neither do limitation-expired, under-age, or self-fabricated-confession cases.

Cost
Free. Apply to the organ that detained, arrested, prosecuted, or judged.
Benefit
State Compensation Law Article 17: compensation rights for — detention contrary to the criminal procedure law or beyond statutory limits, followed by withdrawal, non-prosecution, or acquittal; arrest followed likewise; retrial-acquittal after served sentences. Article 33: liberty violations pay daily at the prior year's national average daily wage. Article 35: mental harm requires eliminating effects, restoring reputation, and apologizing within the infringement's scope; serious consequences add solatium. Article 19 lists six non-compensables: self-fabricated confessions or evidence; detention of those not criminally responsible (under-age, or mentally ill at the time); statutory non-pursuit (patently minor, limitation-expired, deceased suspect; minor-crime non-prosecution; juvenile conditional non-prosecution completed; settlement-based non-prosecution); purely personal acts of officers; self-harm; other statutory cases. The 2015 two-supreme interpretation, Article 7, confirms: the not-criminally-responsible and discretionary non-prosecution classes don't compensate — though wrongly sentenced and served time after prosecution does, for the post-judgment stretch. Article 8: the burden of proving "you fabricated your own confession" or "self-harm" rests on the authorities. The Supreme People's Procuratorate's May 2026 notice: per the statistics bureau's May 15 release, the 2025 national urban non-private-sector average annual wage was about 129,000 yuan (129,441), giving 495.94 yuan daily — effective 2026-05-18, replacing 475.52 from May 2025 (national)
Note
The daily rate updates each May with the statistics bureau's wage release — check the current year's number, don't reuse this one. Receiving a non-prosecution decision, read its basis: "no criminal facts" or "insufficient evidence" compensates; "minor circumstances" or limitation-expired doesn't. Discretionary non-prosecution can be petitioned at the procuratorate within 7 days of receipt. Solatium has no formula — authorities set it by consequence. The paying organ is the one that decided your detention (police, procuratorate, or court); approach it first, then escalate procedurally. For worked arithmetic, see item 36's Guo Li decision: 1,826 days detained, paid at the decision-year rate (2016's 258.89 yuan daily) — about 473,000 yuan (472,733.14) for liberty plus about 165,000 (165,450) solatium; his requested 88.88 million for ten years of solatium was refused beyond that. Also know the non-compensables that decision listed: lost work, health claims, property loss, attorney fees, and detention-house living subsidies all fell outside state compensation.

全国人大常委会 (2012 年修正). 国家赔偿法（第十七、十九、三十三、三十五条）. https://www.stats.gov.cn/gk/tjfg/xgfxfg/202503/t20250306_19…（国家统计局转载）；最高人民检察院 (2026). 最高人民检察院公布最新侵犯公民人身自由的赔偿金标准. https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202605/t20260519_727675.…；最高人民法院、最高人民检察院 (2015). 关于办理刑事赔偿案件适用法律若干问题的解释（法释〔2015〕24 号，第七、八条）. https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/16409.html；全国人大 (2018). 刑事诉讼法（2018 年修正，第十六、一百七十七、一百八十一、二百八十四、二百九十条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml。国家赔偿法第十九条和该解释引的是 2012 年刑事诉讼法条号（第十五条、第一百七十三条第二款、第二百七十三条第二款、第二百七十九条），2018 年修正后依次对应第十六条、第一百七十七条第二款、第二百八十四条第二款、第二百九十条
36

As a victim claiming compensation: go through 12315, suit, or a lawyer — never meet the other side alone, and never bundle "pay me or I expose"

Grade BValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

A victim claiming from the injurer has legal footing — a high number doesn't automatically become extortion. But the price can be heavy: Guo Li got 5 years for extortion before retrial acquitted him. So use traced channels, never meet where they choose, and never say "pay and I won't expose" as one sentence.

Cost
Free. Via 12315, suit, or counsel; record any meetings fully. The hard part: resisting solo negotiations.
Benefit
Official case: after the 2008 melamine disclosures, Guo Li's daughter's scan showed "several punctate strong echoes in both renal central collecting systems." Guo Li repeatedly claimed from the seller and Shi'en and went to media. In June 2009 they settled — 400,000 yuan compensation against his written waiver. The company then reported him; the Chao'an court sentenced him to 5 years for extortion. Guangdong's procuratorate recommended retrial: "existing evidence is insufficient to prove Guo Li subjectively intended illegal possession"; as legal guardian he "had the right to claim from the manufacturer — his claiming has legal basis"; and "consumers may expose and criticize acts harming their lawful rights through mass media." On 2017-04-07, the Guangdong High Court acquitted him on retrial: "the original finding that Guo Li used threats or coercion to forcibly extract property is unclear in fact and insufficient in evidence; his conduct does not exceed the bounds of civil dispute." He was detained 1,826 days, 2009-07-23 to 2014-07-22 (Guangdong, 2017 retrial acquittal)
Note
Grade B: one case, no generalizable rate. It teaches two things at once — claiming is lawful, and you can still be case-filed and investigated. The lowest-risk path routes claims through a lawyer or straight to court, with no solo contact. Beware invitations to their locality to "talk it over" — filing usually happens where they are. Honor signed settlements; layering a fresh high claim on top is what reads as coercion. If case-filed: items 5, 34, 35. Being squeezed over a held leverage: item 32.

Mobbed online: protection on, evidence fixed, then choose among platform, injunction, and police

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Three immediate acts: turn on platform protections, quick-capture the content, report through the quick entrance. Then seek a court injunction to make them stop. Or sue yourself — evidence difficulty lets you request police assistance. Especially grave, vile-impact cases go to prosecution by the procuratorate, no self-proof needed.

Cost
Free. Fifteen minutes of protection and evidence-fixing on the spot. Injunctions and private prosecutions mean court trips, maybe lawyers. The hard part: preserving evidence instead of firing back.
Benefit
法发〔2023〕14 号 Article 15: with evidence of ongoing or imminent personality-rights infringement and irreparable harm absent prompt restraint, courts may issue personality-rights injunctions — orders to stop. Article 11: in private prosecution, "victims with genuine evidence difficulty may request public-security assistance"; police must identify actors and collect spread-and-impact evidence, platforms must technically assist, and "where police-assisted evidence meets acceptance conditions, the court shall file the case"; what can't be collected gets written explanation. Article 12 lists five "serious harm to social order" situations: victim or close-relative mental breakdown or suicide with vile impact; random targeting of the public with mass spread and vile comments; multiple victims or repeated spread; organized multi-platform flooding; and others. Article 4: organizing "human-flesh searches" — illegally collecting and publishing personal information to the unspecified public, serious — is the personal-information crime. The Online Violence Information Governance Rules: Article 23 requires platform options to block strangers or specific users, limit visibility, forbid reposts or comments, and gate DMs; Article 25, quick evidence-capture; Article 26, a conspicuous quick-report entrance; Article 15, reporting suspected crimes to police promptly
Note
Order by speed and cost: platform first — fix evidence and report. Court last — slowest and dearest. All three routes' process costs land on you. Injunctions require your own application; private prosecution means filing and proving yourself; procuratorial takeover requires one of Article 12's five situations. Two don'ts: don't fire back — that flips you into item 16's punished party — and don't delete your own posts: evidence. Overwhelmed: 12356, Section 1, item 25. Demanding platform deletion of your personal information: Section 14, item 8. Being filmed and posted for helping a stranger: [docs/遇到陌生人出事该不该停.md](../docs/遇到陌生人出事该不该停.md).

38

"Insure them first, then act" is legally dead end to end: no money, plus homicide and insurance fraud served consecutively — up to death

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Four gates, all shut. Secretly buying death-conditioned insurance on someone voids the contract. The policyholder intentionally causing the insured's death voids payout. Intentionally killing one's decedent forfeits inheritance. The criminal code lists the fraud separately, served with homicide — up to death. Zero money.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
Insurance Law Article 34: death-conditioned contracts without the insured's consent and amount acknowledgment are void (parents insuring minors excepted). Article 39: beneficiary designation needs the insured's consent. Article 43: policyholder intentionally causing the insured's death, injury, or illness — the insurer pays nothing; with 2+ years of premiums paid, cash value returns to other rights-holders. Beneficiaries intentionally causing death or illness, or attempting murder, forfeit benefits. Article 27(2): intentionally manufacturing the insured event lets the insurer rescind without paying and, save Article 43, without refunding premiums. Civil Code Article 1125: intentionally killing the decedent forfeits inheritance. Criminal Law Article 198(1)(5) lists "policyholders or beneficiaries intentionally causing the insured's death, injury, or illness to defraud insurance" as insurance fraud — "relatively large," up to 5 years plus 10,000–100,000 yuan fines; huge, 5–10; especially huge, 10+. Paragraph 2: acts also constituting other crimes are punished cumulatively. Article 232: intentional homicide — death, life, or 10+. Case: Zhang of Xuancheng, Anhui — in the small hours of 2016-07-18 he drove into a pond; his wife drowned. Within the prior two weeks he had insured her four times, 1 million yuan each. Arrested July 25; the court sentenced death with reprieve plus a 50,000-yuan fine for homicide and insurance fraud cumulatively
Note
The beneficiary here is you — what's avoided is death or life. Casualties and sentences come from the procuratorate's published typical case; investigative methods stay out. Non-lethal claim fraud — fabricated accidents, inflated losses — is equally criminal, helpers included: Section 9, item 21. Insuring family is normal; the thing to block is the "insure then act" thought. Impulses to harm family: items 14–15.

39

When reporting to police, demand the case-filing receipt on the spot; non-filing requires written notice: review within 7 days, re-review within 7 more, and procuratorates can order filing

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Reporting means getting the receipt — your only proof you reported. Non-filing requires a written notice. Disagree: apply for review within 7 days, re-review within 7 more. Or ask the procuratorate to supervise the police into filing.

Cost
Free. One extra sentence on the spot to secure the receipt; then chase progress by the stated dates. The hard part: asking, repeatedly.
Benefit
Criminal Case Procedure Rules Article 171: "on accepting a case, the public security organ shall create a case-acceptance register and receipt, and deliver the receipt to the person escorted in, reporting, accusing, or informing." Article 174: rapid review of accepted cases or leads. Article 178: filing requires crime facts needing criminal pursuit within jurisdiction, approved at county level or above; non-filing with a complainant requires a non-filing notice delivered within 3 days. Article 179: complainants may seek review within 7 days of the notice, decided within 30; re-review at the next level within 7 days of the review decision, decided within 30; lower organs must execute reversals. Major-complex cases extend both, "not exceeding 30 days, with written notice to the applicant." Criminal Procedure Law Article 112: non-filing requires notifying the complainant of reasons, with review rights. Article 113: victims may petition the procuratorate, which demands reasons and, finding them untenable, "shall notify the public security organ to file, and the organ shall file upon notice." Administrative Case Rules Article 61 mirrors the receipt requirement; public-order cases run 30 days from acceptance, extendable 30 with higher approval, forensic time excluded. Police Inspection Regulations Article 9: complaints of ongoing police misconduct get dispatched, handled on scene, and fed back (national)
Note
The beneficiary is you. Reporting doesn't guarantee action, but standards and deadlines are written. Three moves in order: (1) take the receipt, note the case number and accepting unit; (2) on missed deadlines, ask where the case sits — "which stage," not "why won't you help me"; (3) on a non-filing notice, read the reason, review within 7 days, re-review within 7 more, and simultaneously petition the procuratorate for filing supervision — the three don't conflict. Public-order cases (fights, petty theft) run 30 days from acceptance, extendable 30, forensic time excluded. Bad attitude routes to inspection complaints while the case itself proceeds. Found property and neighbor disputes aren't criminal cases — administrative handling, mediation, or mere registration; don't misread that as "nobody cares." Fraud payment-stops: item 2. Mobbing: item 37.

Never send money or cards to case handlers and enforcers: bribery convicts the giver too — and bribing supervision, enforcement, or judicial officers is expressly aggravated

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

"Spend a little to settle it" is an independent crime — the payer gets caught too. Bribery: up to 3 years; serious, 3–10; especially serious, 10+ or life. Bribing supervision, administrative-enforcement, or judicial personnel is on the express aggravation list. Extorted payments without gaining improper benefit aren't bribery.

Cost
Free. Just don't.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 389 defines it: "giving property to state functionaries to seek improper benefit is bribery," including economic-context gifts, rebates, and fees. The exception: "property given under extortion without obtaining improper benefit is not bribery." Article 390 (Amendment XII, effective 2024-03-01): bribery — up to 3 years plus fines; serious circumstances or major state-interest loss, 3–10 plus fines; especially serious or especially major loss, 10+ or life plus fines or confiscation. Seven aggravating situations: repeated or multi-recipient bribery; state-functionary bribers; national key-project bribery; promotion-seeking bribery; bribery of supervision, administrative-enforcement, or judicial personnel; bribery enabling crime in ecology, finance, safety, food and drug, disaster relief, social security, education, or health; laundering proceeds into bribes. The last clause leaves leniency for pre-prosecution confession: "may be mitigated; with minor crime, key investigative contributions, or major meritorious service, may be mitigated or exempted" (national)
Note
The beneficiary is you. Don't count on a bribe to erase punishment: the other side has colleagues, ledgers, cameras, and inspectors — your gift becomes evidence against them and your own crime, in the expressly aggravated band. Extorted for favors: keep the receipt and documents per item 39, and report to inspection or discipline bodies. Article 389(3)'s shield requires extortion without improper benefit — take something you shouldn't have, and it's gone. Hospital red packets follow other rules: Section 24, item 11.

For calls and meetings that may turn hostile, record from the start: conversations you're party to need no advance consent

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Loans, debts, compensation, refunds, labor disputes — said on a call and left unrecorded, months later the two of you remember differently. You may record conversations you participate in; not announcing it beforehand doesn't by itself bar the recording as evidence. What you can't do: wiretap, peep into others' privacy, break into homes to record, or coerce speech.

Cost
Free. Phone call-recording or a recorder app. Record start to finish, keep originals uncut and unoverwritten.
Benefit
Civil Procedure Law Article 66 lists audiovisual material and electronic data as evidence. The Supreme Court's interpretation, Article 106, excludes only three acquisition methods: seriously infringing others' lawful rights, violating prohibitive law, or seriously offending public order and morals. "Didn't tell them beforehand" isn't among them. The evidence rules, Article 15: audio and video evidence requires the original carrier — the phone itself. Article 90: questionable audiovisual and electronic data can't alone establish facts. A judge's article carried on the Supreme Court's site concurs: legally obtained, genuine content, uncut, case-relevant (national)
Note
Beneficiaries: you and family. Get people, events, amounts, and times aligned on tape — not just "when will you pay me," but naturally, "the 50,000 yuan I lent you last year — when do you plan to return it?" Recordings go to courts, arbitration, or police — not the internet; publishing others' words invites privacy and reputation suits (item 16). A recording doesn't guarantee winning — courts weigh it with everything else. It solves provability; whether to sue and at what cost is separate math. Pre-departure document-saving: Section 19, item 8. This entry rests on civil-procedure rules; criminal and administrative evidence follow other provisions.

When something happens on scene: wide shot first, then spatial relations, then damage and injuries — keep originals, never delete

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Close-ups of one scratch or one object on the ground tell nobody where it was days later. Shoot a wide pan first — intersection, house number, vehicles, people, surroundings — then relative positions, then details. Before moving anything, photograph. Keep originals on the phone, not just app-compressed copies.

Cost
Free. Tens of seconds to minutes of phone footage. Safety first — never delay rescue or response.
Benefit
Civil Procedure Law Article 66 lists physical evidence, audiovisual material, and electronic data; the evidence rules classify images, audio, and video as electronic data, requiring originals and original carriers. Photos and video freeze the soon-to-change scene, cross-checkable against police reports, repair records, medical records, and witnesses. The "wide, position, detail" order is practice, not statute (national)
Note
Beneficiaries: you and family. Grade C because the shooting order is experience; statute only governs admissibility and originals. Injuries, fire, gas, or any danger: save and retreat first, never delay for photos. Traffic-accident duties: item 1.

43

Domestic violence: police first for the response record, then the court for a personal-safety protection order — no divorce needed, no fee

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Of women killed worldwide, over a third die at partners' hands — usually the end of long abuse. Among battered women, those once strangled by the partner run 7-times-plus the homicide risk of those never strangled. So report, then apply for the order. Courts usually answer within 72 hours.

Cost
Free. Protection-order applications carry no court fee and no security deposit. The costs are time: reporting, injury documentation, drafting. The hardest: opening your mouth against family.
Benefit
The risk first: pooling 66 countries (systematic review), 38.6% of female homicides are intimate-partner, versus 6.3% of male — the authors call these the final step of prolonged abuse. Another study compared 506 homicides and attempted homicides with 427 battered-but-surviving women: prior non-fatal strangulation raised attempted-homicide odds 6.70-fold (OR 6.70, 95% CI 3.91–11.49) and homicide 7.48-fold (OR 7.48, 95% CI 4.53–12.35). The law: victims and close relatives may report; police must respond promptly, stop the violence, investigate and collect evidence, and assist medical care and injury assessment; minor cases draw written admonishments. Facing violence or its realistic danger, apply to court for a personal-safety protection order — ruled within 72 hours of acceptance, 24 in emergencies. Orders may ban violence, ban harassment, stalking, or contact with you and close relatives, and order the abuser out of the home. Orders run up to 6 months, extendable before expiry. No divorce prerequisite; issuance requires only "relatively large possibility" of violence. Violations: fines up to 1,000 yuan, detention up to 15 days; constituting crime, refusal-to-execute treatment. Regular insult, threat, stalking, harassment, and deprivation of warmth and food also count as domestic violence
Note
Beneficiaries: mainly you and family. The homicide ratios are foreign data — China publishes no equivalent. Evidence accumulates: response records, admonishments, injury assessments, medical records, written promises, chats, recordings (item 41). Orders need no lawyer and usually resolve within days. Divorce and compensation are separate suits — 6+ months first instance, attorney fees your own. Domestic-violence victims get legal aid, and courts may defer, reduce, or waive filing fees. An order isn't a bodyguard: with immediate danger, call 110. Victims coerced or frozen may be applied for by close relatives, police, the women's federation, or residents' and villagers' committees. For a friend or colleague: accompany them to police and hospital. Strangers being beaten behind a door: 110 suffices — don't wade in (item 10).
