Non-fatal strangulation is an important risk factor for homicide of women. Journal of Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jemermed.2007.02.065
44

A family member's gambling debts: don't rush to repay — gambling debts enjoy no legal protection, and loans taken for gambling aren't joint marital debt

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Table debts get no court protection. Lenders who knew the money was for gambling get none either. One spouse's gambling loans aren't joint debt. Without trial, courts can't make the non-borrowing spouse liable.

Cost
Free. The hard part: not paying when creditors knock and family weeps. If they actually sue, you must answer.
Benefit
The Supreme Court's 2017 notice states four points: debts from gambling, drugs, and other illegal activities get no legal protection; lenders knowing or should-have-knowing likewise; loans in one party's name funding crime can't be treated as joint marital debt; and without trial procedure, the non-borrowing party bears no civil liability (national, since 2017)
Note
Grade B: an internal court notice without numbers, and lender knowledge is evidentiary. It predates the Civil Code — current joint-debt doctrine: Section 10, item 12. Loans the lender didn't know were for gambling remain owed — by the borrower alone. Proving gambling use takes transfer records, platform records, or police materials: keep them. If sued: 6+ months ordinary, 3 simplified; attorney fees each side's own. Creditors blocking or detaining people: Section 9, item 15 — call police. If the gambler has reached wanting to die: Section 1, item 37. Beneficiaries: spouse and immediate family.
Sources (1 references)
最高人民法院 (2017). 关于依法妥善审理涉及夫妻债务案件有关问题的通知（法〔2017〕48 号，第二、四条）. https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/36982.html
45

An acquaintance asking you to "face-scan as a witness" for a loan, or to read out a verification code: refuse — this is the AB-loan; the borrower is you, not a guarantor

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

"Help me face-scan, just witness" means borrowing from the bank in your name. The borrower is you — not a guarantor; once the money passes to your acquaintance, the bank still collects from you. The broker defrauded you, but the loan contract can't be undone against an unknowing bank. The acquaintance's "I'll repay" note binds the bank not at all.

Cost
Free. The hard part: refusing family and friends to their faces. "Just witnessing, no liability" — refuse anyway. Don't hand phone, ID, or bank card to brokers; don't face-scan or sign on their arrangement; codes are yours alone, acquaintances included.
Benefit
The Fujian financial regulator's 2022 alert describes the scheme: client A fails qualification; the broker demands a "guarantor," and A recruits well-qualified B; in processing, the broker applies in B's identity, the money goes to A — "the borrower is in substance B," who "learns only upon collection that he is the borrower, not the guarantor." Shandong's 2024 alert adds brokers promising B "no responsibility whatsoever" and coaching B through the bank's pre-loan interview. Shanghai Putuo court's 2024 case: a broker's staffer downloaded the bank app on B's phone and applied in B's name; funds hit B's account, B forwarded to A, A paid 80,000-odd yuan in fees; the 8-person ring drew 10 months to 4 years for contract fraud — but the conviction doesn't transfer the loan. Civil Code Article 149: third-party fraud is rescindable only when the counterparty "knew or should have known" — the counterparty here is the bank, unknowing, so no rescission; what's rescindable must be sought within 1 year of discovering the fraud (Article 152). Borrowers repay per terms (Article 675); contracts bind only their signatories (Article 465); debt assignment needs the bank's consent (Article 551) — hence A's note binds the bank not at all, and recovering from A means your own suit. Face-scanned without reading the contract still binds: Neijiang's Shizhong court, 2025 — Jiang couldn't qualify alone; Zhang's son supplied her identity behind her back as co-borrower; the process required her own face scan, she scanned without reading; the court held she "should have foreseen the importance and legal consequences of facial recognition," jointly liable for the remaining 60,000-odd principal. The Electronic Signature Law: "reliable electronic signatures have equal legal force with handwritten signatures or seals." The Anti-Telecom-Fraud Law: no one "may provide real-name verification help" — violations draw fines, serious cases detention. Ordinary first instance concludes within 6 months, extendable; attorney fees are your own (national)
Note
Beneficiary: mainly you — the A who asks is usually family or friend. A Pudong chief prosecutor writes that B, pressed by sentiment, proceeds even knowing it's his own loan, ending as the bank's collection target. Genuinely helping: first establish your role on the paper — if it's a loan contract, don't sign; willing to guarantee, sign a guarantee contract as guarantor (item 18). Already loaned: report to police, then call the lending bank's official line, keeping chats and transfers. Checking loans in your name: item 9. Don't parrot the broker's script in the bank's interview — deception can be your own liability: Section 9, item 6. Face scans and e-confirmations count as signatures (item 17). Courts don't always bind the person: Guangzhou Internet Court, 2021 — a woman whose stolen ID was reported and frozen on the spot won because the bank couldn't prove her face scan. So report and freeze lost IDs immediately, keeping the receipt. Demanding alternatives to face scans at institutions: Section 14, item 9. Name-lending schemes generally: item 28. Phones and accounts: item 8. Grade B: regulators give scheme and cases, no victim counts or totals.
Sources (11 references)

46

Fit good locks on doors and windows, a motion light outside, and actually lock up: these prevent burglary — a lone alarm shows no effect

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

In UK data, homes with door and window locks ran one-twelfth the burglary risk of unprotected ones; adding an outside light cut it to one-thirtieth-plus. An alarm alone showed no protective effect. This covers burglary — not home-invasion robbery with people present.

Cost
Key-deadbolt door locks, window locks, and an outside motion light run tens to hundreds of yuan; a full security door, over a thousand. The hard part: actually locking up every departure, open-window summers included.
Benefit
The England and Wales crime survey asked 37,416 households (2008–2012) about security devices and compared burgled homes. Unprotected homes were just 4.9% of all households but 36.6% of burgled ones. The authors computed "protection multiples" — burglary risk as a fraction of unprotected. Door plus window locks: 12.54×, about one-twelfth the risk (door locks meaning double-locked or deadbolted — bolts needing keys). Locks plus outside motion or timer light: 34.41×. Adding indoor timer lights: 49×. Single measures: outside light about 3×, door locks about 2.8×; window locks alone showed nothing. Five devices beat a well-chosen three not at all. Alarm-only homes burgled more than unprotected ones; dummy alarm boxes correlated with more attempted break-ins. And locks must be locked: 1993–2006/07, forced-entry burglaries (lock-picking, window-breaking, door removal) fell from 31 to 7 per thousand households, −77%; unlocked walk-in burglaries held at 7 throughout (England and Wales)
Note
Contested: the alarm half has counter-data — the same authors, on 1992–1996 data, found alarms protective then, and they counsel caution: burgled homes may be the ones installing alarms. All figures are English, comparing equipped versus unequipped households without assignment — hence B. They cover burglary only; no data say locks stop home-invasion robbery. Someone inside: retreat and call police (item 10); cornered: item 11. Renters: clear lock changes and window locks with the landlord — the Civil Code lets landlords demand restoration or compensation for unconsented alterations. Security doors follow the mandatory national standard GB 17565-2022, effective 2024-01-01. Beneficiaries: you and family.

9. Legal red lines ordinary people step over

26 entries

This section counts two things: your personal freedom, and your money. What follows, ordinary people often take for "nothing much" — in fact it draws detention, fines, and at the heavy end, prison. Each entry gives the statute's specific numbers plus officially published cases. The Public Security Administration Punishments Law cited is the 2025 revision effective 2026-01-01 — article numbers differ from the old law. The criminal law follows the Beijing traffic-authority reprint "as amended by Amendment XI," with amendments noted inline. Entries run from "easiest to stumble into" plus "heaviest consequences" downward. Entries in this section are grouped by theme, with item numbers in parentheses. Posting and forwarding online: don't forward unverified disaster/epidemic/police news (item 1), don't share content insulting heroes and martyrs (item 2), close and forget what's on offshore sites (item 3), no porn in group chats (item 4). Handling money, loan fraud, claim fraud: "side jobs" collecting money on your own card (item 5), dressing up loan applications (item 6), don't withdraw on a found bank card (item 7), claim offers under your real identity (item 8), never lend your ID (item 16), faking accidents for claims (item 21). Small daily things: nothing thrown from balconies and windows (item 9), no replica guns online (item 10), register drones first (item 11), card games without rake or hosting (item 13), no wild game (item 14). Conflict and police: debt collection without detaining people (item 15), cooperate when police stop you (item 17), do the math before striking (item 19), no batons or stun guns "for protection" (item 26). Sex, children, the body: no secret filming (item 12), no sex under 14 (item 18), a child you can't raise goes through civil-affairs registration (item 20), never sell your organs (item 22), soliciting prostitution defaults to detention (item 23). Copyright and derivative works: fan translation and pirated e-books (item 24), selling fan fiction needs permission first (item 25).

1

Don't forward unverified disaster, epidemic, or police news in groups — no photoshops, no AI-fabricated scene images

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Forwarding disaster/epidemic/police news you know is false is punished as heavily as inventing it. Not your invention doesn't matter: 5–10 days' detention plus 1,000 yuan. Throwing social order into disorder: up to 3 years; serious consequences, 3–7. Photoshopped and AI-faked scene images count as your own invention.

Cost
Free. Before forwarding, check whether it's an official notice. Unsure: don't forward, don't edit images, don't add "it's said." The hard part: resisting the urge to be first with the news.
Benefit
Deliberately spreading rumors, false alarms of danger, epidemic, disaster, or police matters disturbing public order: 5–10 days, plus up to 1,000 yuan; the lighter band, up to 5 days or 1,000 yuan. Fabricating false danger/epidemic/disaster/police information and spreading it online: up to 3 years; knowingly spreading it, same band — precondition being "seriously disturbing social order." Serious consequences: 3–7 years (national)
Note
Knowing-forwarding and self-invention fall under the same provision for police. "I just forwarded it" is no defense. Photoshop and AI fakes count as invention. The MPS published several batches of disaster-rumor cases in 2025; the MPS site was unreachable during writing, so no specific cases cited.
Sources (3 references)
全国人大常委会 (2025). 治安管理处罚法（2025 年修订，第二十九条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml；全国人大常委会 (2015). 刑法修正案（九）（第三十二条，即刑法第二百九十一条之一第二款）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180205_364562.shtml；全国人大 (2020). 刑法（根据刑法修正案（十一）修正，第二百九十一条之一）. https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index…（北京市公安交通管理局转载）
2

Don't post or forward images, memes, or comments insulting heroes and martyrs; no jokes about the flag or anthem

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Jokes about martyrs, the flag, the anthem: lighter, 5–10 days or 1,000–3,000 yuan; heavier, 10–15 days. Criminal-grade: up to 3 years. One villager posted 2 lines defaming Yuan Longping in a 499-member WeChat group: 6 months' control — no cell, but restricted movement.

Cost
Free. Content touching heroes, the flag, emblem, or anthem: no comments, no edits, no forwards. The hard part: staying quiet when the group plays along.
Benefit
Insulting or fabricating against heroes' and martyrs' names, likenesses, reputation, or honor harming the public interest: 5–10 days or 1,000–3,000 yuan. Desecrating or denying their deeds and spirit, or producing and spreading content glorifying wars of aggression: same band. Heavier: 10–15 days plus up to 5,000 yuan. "Serious circumstances" become crime: up to 3 years. Publicly insulting the flag or emblem, or altering the anthem's words or music or singing it with distortion and disparagement, serious: up to 3 years. Official cases: Xiao posted 2 messages defaming Yuan Longping in a 499-member village group — 6 months' control (control meaning confinement-free punishment with restricted movement). Qiu, with 2.5-million-plus followers, posted 2 pieces distorting border-defense soldiers' deeds — 8 months plus a national-media public apology (national)
Note
The punishments-law clause arrived only in the 2025 revision; before, such matters went through criminal law or procuratorial public-interest suits. A several-hundred-member group counts as a public venue in courts' eyes.

3

Offshore sites: read and close — no screenshots, no forwarding, no carrying into groups, no joining the comments

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

These provisions punish outward transmission, not viewing. Forwarding, carrying into groups, and echoing in comments all count as dissemination in practice. Reaching the incite-subversion or incite-secession band: up to 5 years; ringleaders, 5+. Terrorist and extremist books and audiovisuals are the exception: knowingly holding them, serious, up to 3 years.

Cost
Free. Close the page and it ends. No archiving, forwarding, or republishing domestically. Don't run an identity-linked account posting political content long-term on offshore platforms. Don't take fees or funding from offshore institutions, organizations, or individuals. The hard part: not screenshotting striking content.
Benefit
Inciting subversion of state power or overthrow of the socialist system by rumor or defamation: up to 5 years; ringleaders ("principal elements") or grave crimes, 5+ with a 15-year cap. Inciting secession or undermining national unity: identical terms. Colluding with offshore institutions, organizations, or individuals: aggravated. Funding others to do so: responsible individuals, up to 5 years; serious, 5+. Stealing, spying on, buying, or illegally providing state secrets or intelligence for offshore parties: 5–10 years; especially serious, 10+ or life; lighter, under 5. Crimes endangering national security carry supplementary political-rights deprivation of 1–5 years — voting and public-office eligibility suspended — plus possible property confiscation. Administratively: no individual or organization may use networks for activities endangering national security, honor, or interests, nor incite subversion or secession; publishing or transmitting such information is punished per law and regulation (national). One class stands without transmission: knowingly holding terrorist or extremist materials — books, audio-video, or other items — serious, up to 3 years, custody, or control, plus or instead of fines, per Criminal Law Article 120-6 (added by Amendment IX)
Note
The cited provisions punish inciting, transmitting outward, providing to others — viewing is not among them. Terrorist and extremist materials are the statutory exception, criminal by mere knowing possession (Article 120-6): never archive that class. See it, and it ends there: no screenshots, no forwards, no comments, no recruiting. Forwarding and comment-echoing count as dissemination — "just forwarded" is no defense — and offshore provenance can aggravate. Unsure of truth: all the more reason not to forward (item 1). Circumvention tools: Section 11, item 11. This class of content buys nothing real and costs sentences, political rights, and property. Publicly findable cases appear only in offshore media and family-released documents — e.g., a long-term offshore-platform political blogger sentenced to 7 years in 2023; no officially verifiable judgment was obtainable, so statutes only, no case attached.

Porn: private viewing is your business — no group sharing, no selling "resources," no group-building

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Private viewing isn't in the punishment clauses. One group post counts as dissemination to the whole group: 10–15 days plus up to 5,000 yuan; serious, up to 2 years. Selling "resources" for money: up to 3 years, topping out at life. Building a dissemination group of 30+: founders, admins, and main posters all count as criminals.

Cost
Free. No forwarding, no group-file storage, no administering such groups.
Benefit
Spreading obscene information online: 10–15 days plus up to 5,000 yuan; the lighter band, up to 5 days or 1,000–3,000 yuan; content involving minors, aggravated. Dissemination reaching "serious circumstances": up to 2 years. For profit: up to 3 years plus fines; serious in that class, 3–10; especially serious, 10+ or life. Groups primarily for spreading obscene electronic information with 30+ members are handled criminally — founders, administrators, and principal posters all charged with dissemination of obscene materials (national)
Note
Both laws punish "dissemination"; private viewing isn't in the clauses. But one group post counts as dissemination to the group. The quantity thresholds for "serious" are judicially interpreted — unverified here.

5

"Side jobs" asking you to collect, withdraw, or transfer money on your own card: refuse at any fee

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

These jobs pay hundreds and cost a criminal record. One man brought his ID and 1 bank card to a designated spot to help transfer and withdraw, earning 500-odd yuan — prosecutors declined to charge, and police still detained him 10 days with a 1,000-yuan fine. Another handed his own and others' cards and SIMs to a ring for collection and withdrawal: 2 years 3 months plus a 22,000-yuan fine.

Cost
Free. Walk away from "daily hundreds, bring your card to the bank" work.
Benefit
Knowingly transferring, acquiring, or selling criminal proceeds, or otherwise helping conceal them: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines. Official cases: Wang, on instruction, brought ID and 1 card to a spot to help transfer and withdraw, earning 500-odd yuan; unprosecuted, yet police detained him 10 days and fined 1,000 under the Anti-Telecom-Fraud Law. Man surrendered his own and others' cards and SIMs to a ring for collection, transfer, and withdrawal: 2 years 3 months plus 22,000 yuan (national). Converting to crypto is the same: An and two others, on a fraud ring's instruction, received funds on their own cards, bought virtual currency on a platform, and forwarded it to designated accounts on commission — verified victim funds of 500,000-odd yuan; all three convicted of concealing criminal proceeds, 2 years 8 months to 3 years 3 months, fines of 30,000–40,000 (Tongzhou, Beijing)
Note
Lending cards and "money muling": Section 8, item 8. This entry covers your own hands withdrawing and transferring. Receiving and converting to Tether-type coins is the same act. Why your own crypto losses are unrecoverable: Section 5, item 45. "I didn't know where the money came from" doesn't necessarily hold: absurd pay, face-scan cooperation, and glaringly abnormal transactions suffice as knowledge. The floor is 10 days' detention plus a record.

Anyone recruiting you to "dress up" loan applications for a cut of the loan: refuse every one

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Helping "dress up" loan files for a share is fraud. One 126-person ring dressed up jobless people as "quality customers," defrauding 30-million-plus yuan across 80-odd banks. The signers took 30% of loan value; of 80 sentenced, 76 drew 1 year 4 months to 6 years 6 months. The debt sits in whosever name the loan was taken.

Cost
Free. Refuse outright. Don't lend your ID or credit record, don't sign unseen loan contracts, don't attend bank interviews for others.
Benefit
Obtaining loans, acceptances, letters of credit, or guarantees from banks by deception causing major loss: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; especially major loss or especially serious circumstances, 3–7 plus fines. Police file from 500,000 yuan of direct loss. Never intending repayment, using fabricated project pretexts, fake contracts, fake certificates, or fake title documents: loan fraud — 50,000 yuan files the case, up to 5 years plus 20,000–200,000 yuan fines; huge, 5–10; especially huge, 10+ to life. Forging, altering, or trading state-organ documents, certificates, or seals: up to 3 years; serious, 3–10. Official case: a 126-person ring across 16 provinces dressed jobless people as "quality customers," defrauding 30-million-plus yuan at 80-odd bank branches; the fronting "blank-credit" signers took 30% of loan value; prosecutors pursued 105 of them; of 80 sentenced at first instance in 2026, 76 drew 1 year 4 months to 6 years 6 months for loan fraud plus fines, and 4 who withdrew cash for the ring drew 2 years 4 months to 7 years 6 months for loan fraud and money laundering cumulatively (national). The fraudulent-loans-offense text here follows Amendment XI from March 2021
Note
"I meant to repay" didn't hold in that case: prosecutors established joblessness, no assets, unpayable, and the shares already spent — hence no repayment intent from the start. Withdrawing cash for the ring adds money laundering. Whose name the loan sits in, whose signature — that's the borrower; short of crime, the debt and the credit record remain yours. Fleeing abroad settles nothing: once filed, years in hiding don't bar prosecution; the unsentenced, suspects, and defendants are barred from exit; undecided civil cases and non-performing judgment debtors can be exit-restricted too. Withdrawing and transferring: item 5. Discovering impersonation loans: Section 8, item 9.

7

Don't withdraw on a found bank card; found phones and wallets go to the owner or the police — never the pocket

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Keeping found items for yourself, at "relatively large" amounts and refusing surrender: up to 2 years; huge, 2–5. Withdrawing at an ATM on a found card is heavier — "unauthorized use of another's card": relatively large alone draws up to 5 years plus 20,000–200,000 yuan. That one, police file directly — no victim complaint needed.

Cost
Free, minutes. Call the owner or deliver to a police station.
Benefit
Found property must be returned, the owner notified, or items delivered to police. Keeping lost property, "relatively large" and refusing surrender, is embezzlement: up to 2 years; huge, 2–5. Using a found card at an ATM is "unauthorized use of another's credit card," criminal as credit-card fraud: relatively large, up to 5 years plus 20,000–200,000; huge or with serious circumstances, 5–10 plus 50,000–500,000 (national)
Note
Embezzlement is "handled only upon complaint" — the owner sues; police don't act on their own. But ATM withdrawal on a found card files directly. "Relatively large" thresholds are judicially set — unverified here. Delivered items charge the owner storage costs on pickup (Civil Code Article 317).

8

Claim offers under your real identity; no virtual numbers, no batch-registered alts, no exploiting bugs for repeats

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

One real identity, one account, one claim — outside punishment. Batch-registering fake users and self-ordering-self-delivering for multiples is fraud: 3,000 yuan reaches up to 3 years; from 30,000, 3–10. One rider bought 0.1-yuan virtual numbers to brush coupons, cashing out 90,000-odd yuan — all 12 co-defendants sentenced.

Cost
Free. Walk away from "coupon-task groups." Platform bugs: don't touch. The hard part: not treating coupons as scalable income.
Benefit
Defrauding others or the public, "relatively large": up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; huge or serious circumstances, 3–10; especially huge, 10+ or life plus fines or confiscation. Bands set provincially: large 3,000–10,000+; huge 30,000–100,000+; especially huge 500,000+. Teaching methods or selling "courses": the teaching-crime offense, up to 5 years; serious, 5–10; especially serious, 10+ or life. The phone-number and verification-code supply chain: the personal-information crime, up to 3 years; especially serious, 3–7. Batch accounts, auto-switching network addresses, and SMS-receiving code platforms are banned outright by Anti-Telecom-Fraud Law Article 14; trading, renting, or lending cards and accounts and passing real-name checks sit in Article 31. Article 14 violations: confiscation plus 1–10× gains; no gains or under 50,000 yuan, up to 500,000 yuan and up to 15 days when serious. Article 31: 1–10× similarly, under 20,000 or none up to 200,000 plus detention when serious. Telecom-fraud participation short of crime: 10–15 days, confiscation plus 1–10×; under 10,000 or none, up to 100,000. Official cases: delivery rider Liu bought virtual numbers at 0.1 yuan each to register platform new-users, claimed the 29-minus-15 newcomer coupons, resold goods to small shops for cash, and cross-invited his virtual numbers for 2–20-yuan bounties — he and rider Tan defrauded 90,000-odd and 70,000-odd respectively; Shanghai Yangpu prosecutors charged 12, courts sentencing 3 years 6 months to 3 months' custody. Case two: Wang exploited the time gap between refunds and virtual-lottery-coin recovery — 1,156 refunds, 224 figurines extracted, 249,000-odd yuan, monetized on secondhand platforms; 3 years suspended 4, plus a 30,000-yuan fine, with 330,000 yuan in restitution and prepaid fines during trial. Case three: a ride-hailing platform's new-user coupons and driver subsidies defrauded via "self-ordering, self-delivering" fake runs across 19 provinces and 70-odd cities, 2-million-plus yuan; Chaoyang Longcheng district prosecutors in Liaoning charged 163, all convicted; principals Huang and Cai drew 3 years 6 months each for fraud, personal-information crime, and teaching methods cumulatively; 34 minor accomplices went unprosecuted but referred for administrative punishment (national)
Note
The line isn't "how much you grazed" but whether you faked anything. Real identity, one account, coupons used on yourself: that's the platform's offer. Fake users, fabricated transactions, or concealing prior refunds make the other side hand things over under false impressions — fraud — and amounts only set the sentence. Carmaker free charging has been grazed the same way: per August 2026 reporting, two Shanghai residents bought masses of virtual numbers, rotated them as sub-accounts on an EV maker's app, charged twice per number on "charge-now-pay-later," then unbound — bills unpaid, charging resold to truck drivers; Pudong prosecutors approved arrest as fraud, not theft; media report only, no judgment or official notice. Sub-criminal amounts still bite: bans, clawbacks, and restitution of unjust enrichment. Sub-criminal telecom-fraud participation still carries detention and fines. "The group leads, pays per order" doesn't change your share's nature. Teaching methods and trading accounts and numbers are separate counts, sentenced together. Beneficiary: you. Self-written or sold scripts: Section 11, item 3; selling cards and accounts: Section 8, item 8, and item 16 here.

Nothing goes out the balcony or window — cigarette butts, trash bags, bottles all count

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Throwing things downstairs without hitting anyone still draws 5 days and 1,000 yuan; serious, 10–15 days. Hitting someone swaps the charge: drunk from the 21st floor, one man threw bottles and glasses onto a playground, striking a 13-year-old into serious injury — 10 years. Another threw 8 bricks from the 32nd floor killing 1: death sentence approved in 2024.

Cost
Free, no time either. Butts, bags, bottles go to the indoor bin.
Benefit
Throwing objects from height, with danger to people, property, or public safety: up to 5 days or 1,000 yuan; serious, 10–15 days plus up to 1,000 more. Reaching the high-throw crime: up to 1 year plus or instead of fines. Injuries and deaths route to heavier charges. Official cases: Li, drunk on the 21st floor, threw bottles and glasses onto a school playground, striking a 13-year-old with grade-2 serious injury — endangering public safety by dangerous means, 10 years. Zhou threw 8 bricks into a crowd from the 32nd floor, killing 1 — death approved by the Supreme Court in 2024 (national)
Note
Detention without injury — the clause requires only "danger." The Civil Code adds a private-compensation provision on high-throwing (Article 1254) — unopened at writing time, uncited.

No replica guns, steel-ball guns, or air guns bought online; no "toy guns" of unknown origin

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Online-bought ball and air guns count as firearms once muzzle specific energy reaches 1.8 joules per square centimeter. Holding one without a license: up to 3 years; serious, 3–7. A couple selling "toy guns" — 18 of 43 seized were certified firearms — escaped prosecution only because knowledge couldn't be proven.

Cost
Free. Want to shoot? Go to a licensed range.
Benefit
Possessing or concealing firearms without license: up to 3 years; serious, 3–7. Non-standard guns firing non-standard rounds count as firearms at muzzle specific energy ≥1.8 J/cm² — the energy per square centimeter at the muzzle. Many online steel-ball and air guns exceed it. Since 2018 the two supremes require lower-energy air guns to be assessed comprehensively — appearance, material, price, use, the person's knowledge — before charging. Official case: Zhao and spouse sold "toy guns" at a market; of 43 seized, 18 met the firearm standard; prosecution declined for insufficient proof they knew (national)
Note
That case turned on "not knowing." An adult specifically ordering steel-ball and air guns online will find "didn't know it was a gun" a hard sell. Crossbows and controlled knives: item 26.

Bought a drone? Register it first; no flying near airports, military zones, or urban controlled airspace; no hacking the altitude cap

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Flying unregistered: correction plus up to 200 yuan; serious, 2,000–20,000. Flying in controlled airspace without approval: up to 500 yuan; serious, drone confiscated plus 1,000–10,000; heavier still, 5–10 days. One man paid to crack the altitude limit, flew near 3,000 meters to film cloud layers, and posted online: 5 days.

Cost
Registration is free, minutes. Before each flight, check via official channels whether the spot is controlled airspace.
Benefit
Unregistered flight: correction plus up to 200 yuan, serious 2,000–20,000. Unapproved flight of micro, light, or small drones in controlled airspace: stop-flight order plus up to 500 yuan; serious, confiscation plus 1,000–10,000. Violating airspace rules with heavier circumstances: 5–10 days. Official cases: Li paid to crack the altitude limit, flew to nearly 3,000 meters filming clouds and published — 5 days. Note
Micro and light drones fly in suitable airspace without approval — micro meaning under 0.25 kg empty weight. Suitable airspace is everything outside controlled zones, and airports, military facilities, and government compounds are mostly controlled. Never lend your ID; never use another's; never register, open cards, or buy tickets on others' documents

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Cost
Free. Refuse requests; annotate copies with their single purpose.
Benefit
Renting, lending, or transferring resident IDs: warning plus up to 200 yuan. A lent ID can register companies and bank cards — consequences in Section 8, items 28 and 8. Using another's ID for tickets or lodging counts as "activities requiring identity proof." Internet cafés: your own ID there too — cafés must verify and register, keep records 60+ days, retrievable by police and culture authorities; whoever's ID was used, whatever happened on that machine lands on them.

Free, no time. The hard part: those seconds before the fist.
Benefit
Assault or intentional injury: 5–10 days plus 500–1,000 yuan; grouped assaults, assaults on the disabled, pregnant, elderly, or children, repeat or multiple-victim assaults: 10–15 days plus 1,000–2,000. Light injury is intentional injury, up to 3 years, custody, or control; serious injury, 3–10. Civilly: medical costs, lost work, nursing, transport, hospital food, nutrition — plus disability compensation for lasting impairment, computed as the trying court's locality prior-year urban per-capita disposable income × 20 years, minus a year per year over 60, and 5 years flat over 75. Note
Avoiding conflict, why first-strikers lose, and defense borders: Section 8, item 10. The price of vengeance: Section 8, items 11–14. A child you can't raise has exactly one legal exit: civil-affairs registration — selling may be child trafficking, abandonment is its own crime

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

There is a legal way out, exactly one: adoption registration with civil affairs — the relationship forms only on registration. Private handovers, especially for money, can flip from "placement" to child trafficking, from 5 years up. Walking away and refusing support, vile circumstances, is abandonment: up to 5 years.

Cost
Free. Adoption registration at county-level-or-above civil affairs takes materials, review, and assessment — some time.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 240: trafficking women or children, 5–10 years plus fines; aggravated, 10+ or life plus fines or confiscation; "especially serious, death plus confiscation." The anti-trafficking opinion, Article 17, separates selling one's own child from folk placement by "whether the actor sought illegal profit." Three situations count as selling one's own child, charged as trafficking: "treating childbirth as an illegal-profit means, selling the child after birth"; "knowing the other party lacks, or not caring whether they have, child-rearing intent, 'placing' the child for money"; and "'placing' the child for sums clearly beyond 'nutrition' or 'gratitude' fees." Conversely, non-profit-driven placement under genuine hardship with modest fees is folk placement, not trafficking. Article 261: "those with support duties toward the aged, young, ill, or others unable to live independently who refuse support under vile circumstances: up to 5 years, custody, or control." Civil Code Article 1094: only three may place for adoption — orphans' guardians, child-welfare institutions, and birth parents genuinely unable to raise. Article 1105: "adoption shall be registered with county-level-or-above civil affairs; the adoptive relationship forms from registration"
Note
Whether to give birth is out of scope here. After birth, this order is cheapest: first, deliver in hospital — prenatal care and delivery in Section 27; the birth certificate precedes everything. Second, for placement, go directly to county-level-or-above civil affairs, no intermediaries — money changing hands can flip the nature. Within a year postpartum, thoughts of harming yourself or the child are emergencies: Section 27, item 7 lists same-day hospital triggers. The 42-day postpartum check doubles as depression screening: Section 27, item 16. Suicidal thoughts: 12356, Section 1, item 25. No case attached: official trafficking-one's-own-child cases weren't verified one by one this round, so statutes and the opinion only.

Never fake accidents or inflate losses for claims: it's insurance fraud — and your witnesses, repair shop, and appraisers join the count

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Invented accidents and inflated losses for claims are insurance fraud: "relatively large," up to 5 years plus 10,000–100,000 yuan. Those issuing false testimony, appraisals, or valuations are co-conspirators. In one Xuancheng, Anhui case, 8 people drew 2–4 years, each fined 10,000.

Cost
Free, no time — just don't.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 198 lists five situations: (1) policyholders fictitiously insuring nonexistent subjects; (2) fabricating false causes or inflating loss extent; (3) fabricating accidents that never occurred; (4) policyholders or insureds intentionally causing property-loss events; (5) policyholders or beneficiaries intentionally causing the insured's death, injury, or illness. "Relatively large": up to 5 years plus 10,000–100,000; huge or serious, 5–10 plus 20,000–200,000; especially huge, 10+ plus 20,000–200,000 or confiscation. The closing clause catches helpers: assessors, witnesses, and property appraisers deliberately issuing false documents enabling fraud are co-conspirators. Insurance Law Article 27: false claims let insurers rescind without premium refund; forged documents and inflated losses mean no payment on the excess, and paid sums are returned or compensated. Case: in the Xuancheng Zhang case, Wang and 7 others drew 2–4 years for insurance fraud, each fined 10,000; a linked sham litigation extracted 70,000-odd yuan on 20,000 yuan of assessed loss via a fabricated vehicle-transfer agreement — that civil judgment was reversed on retrial 2019-09-26. The Anti-Insurance-Fraud Measures require risk verification at both underwriting and claims ends, industry fraud platforms and intelligence centers, referral of suspected crimes to police, and regulator-built criminal-justice handover mechanisms (national, issued 2024-07-31)
Note
The "harmless" habits all fall inside: asking the shop to "pad the estimate," rolling old damage into this claim, staging a bump with a friend, inventing events. Auto cover: Section 5, item 26. Killing the insured after insuring them is expressly cumulative: Section 8, item 38. Medical insurance runs separately — card-swiping and account cash-outs charge as fraud: Section 5, item 13's note

Never sell your organs, and never recruit donors: the seller gets 20,000-odd, the same kidney resells for 200,000 — proceeds confiscated plus 10–20× transaction fines

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Living-organ donation is limited to spouses, lineal relatives, or collateral relatives within three generations; all trading is illegal. In one Beijing case, sellers got 20,000-odd while patients paid 180,000–220,000 per kidney. Proceeds are confiscated, plus fines of 10–20× the transaction. The bodily price of losing a kidney: Section 1, item 35.

Cost
Free, no time — just don't.
Benefit
The Human Organ Donation and Transplant Regulation, Article 5: "no organization or individual may trade human organs in any form or engage in activities related to such trade." Article 10: no harvesting living organs from anyone under 18. Article 11: living-organ recipients are limited to the donor's spouse, lineal blood relatives, or collateral blood relatives within three generations. Article 37: county-level-or-above health authorities enforce — confiscating illegal gains, then fining 10–20× the transaction value; participating medical personnel lose licenses permanently; crimes pursue criminal liability (national, since 2024-05-01, replacing the old transplant regulation). Criminal Law Article 234-1: organizing others to sell organs — up to 5 years plus fines; serious, 5+ plus fines or confiscation. Three situations route to Articles 234 and 232 as intentional injury or homicide: harvesting without consent, harvesting from anyone under 18, and forcing or deceiving donation. Case one: the Zheng Wei ring of 15, final judgment 2014-08-20 at Beijing First Intermediate Court — 51 kidneys, 10.34-million-odd yuan; the sellers "received merely 20,000–25,000 yuan"; recipients paid "18 or 19 wan per kidney before, 21 or 22 wan later"; the harvest site was a four-story building rented at 7,500 monthly, described by the ring's head nurse as "filthy, without even resuscitation equipment"; the organizer drew 12 years, the other 14 drawing 3.5–9 years. Case two: the SPP's "teenager sells kidney for iPhone" case — 17-year-old Wang's right kidney was removed in Chenzhou on the night of 2011-04-28, at a department contracted inside an unlicensed hospital; discharged May 2 with 22,000 yuan, while the recipient side paid the broker 150,000 yuan plus 10,000 US dollars, the principal profiting 56,000-odd; Wang's postoperative renal insufficiency was assessed "serious injury, grade-3 disability"
Note
The beneficiary is you. The trade reads as "20,000 once" but trades an organ for a phone: the teenager's assessment — serious injury, grade-3 disability — doesn't heal in months. Five defendants there were charged under Article 234(2) as intentional injury, partly because staff removed the right kidney without verifying the "donor" was a minor. Today, recruiters charge as organizing organ sales; harvesting from under-18s still routes to Article 234. Black-broker surgeries run in rental rooms without assessment beyond typing or any follow-up — complications with no one to answer. Genuinely donating to family: Article 11's path, at a licensed institution with ethics review, money never changing hands. Posthumous body donation is unpaid and outside this entry. The bodily price: Section 1, item 35. Broke enough to consider it: Section 7's channels first. Online-loan and "dressed-up application" traps: item 6.

Getting caught isn't a fine-and-go: the statute's default is 10–15 days plus up to 5,000 yuan. Only lighter circumstances drop to 5 days or 1,000. And soliciting while knowingly carrying syphilis or gonorrhea is a crime: up to 5 years.

Cost
Free, no time — just don't.
Benefit
Punishments Law Article 78: prostitution and soliciting — 10–15 days plus up to 5,000; lighter, up to 5 days or 1,000. Soliciting in public venues: up to 5 days or 1,000. Detention here is administrative — a detention facility, not fine-and-go. Introducers and venue providers draw the same band as clients (Article 79). Hotel and KTV staff tipping off guests: 10–15 days (Article 87). Article 360's old second paragraph — the "soliciting young girls" offense — was deleted in 2015; such cases now charge as aggravated rape (item 18). "Door-to-door massage" signage changes nothing; facts govern. STD and HIV risks: Section 1, item 30, and Section 13, item 38 (blocking drugs within 72 hours). Entertainment venues generally: Section 22.

Fan-translated comics, reposted shows, shared drive links, pirated e-books: infringement even unpaid — with ads or membership fees, prison

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Publishing translations or uploads of others' works without permission infringes even unpaid — takedown and damages. Ads or membership fees make it "for profit": 30,000 yuan earned, 500 works, or 1,000 members reach prison, up to 10 years. The YYeTs founder drew 3 years 6 months.

Cost
Free. Buy, download, read and translate for yourself — just don't publish to the public. No ad-funded or membership resource sites or groups, no selling drive links. The hard part: not becoming the next mule when "everyone's sharing."
Benefit
Civil first: the copyright law grants translation rights and network-dissemination rights; unlicensed translation and unlicensed uploading infringe — cessation plus damages. Only personal study, research, or appreciation of published works escapes license and payment. Damages run from actual loss or your gain, or court-set between 500 and 5 million yuan; intentional and serious, 1–5×; the right-holder's enforcement costs ride along. Criminal: Article 217's prerequisite is "for profit" — paid ads on pages count, membership fees count; service, membership, and advertising revenue all count as illegal gains. Any one threshold suffices: 30,000+ yuan gains; 50,000+ yuan business volume (in the YYeTs case, total membership, advertising, and hard-drive revenue); 500+ works disseminated online; 10,000+ downloads or 100,000+ clicks (the click threshold moved from 50,000 to 100,000 in the 2025 interpretation); 1,000+ registered members; or two items each at half the threshold. Ten times those numbers enters the 3–10-year band; fines typically 1–10× gains. Case one: Liang Yongping's group downloaded unlicensed shows, translated and subtitled them, and uploaded to the YYeTs site and app — 32,824 unlicensed works, 6.83 million members, 2018–2021 revenues of 2.7-million-odd membership fees, 8.8-million-odd advertising, plus 1-million-odd from pre-loaded hard drives, with a "donation" QR code that conferred membership — read by prosecutors as membership fees renamed. On 2021-11-22, Liang drew 3 years 6 months plus a 1.5-million-yuan fine; 14 others drew 1.5–3 years, all suspended, fines 40,000–350,000. Case two: Ke crawled playback addresses for 50,000-odd shows onto his site and app, free to watch, monetized through open-screen ads by impression — 350,000-odd yuan; 2023: 3 years suspended 4, fine 400,000. Case three: Huang rented servers at home for a music-download forum, uploaded 100,000-odd songs into 18 cloud drives, posted links for forum-coin redeemable by recharge — 500,000-odd yuan total; 2023: 3 years suspended 4, fine 550,000 (national; interpretation since 2025-04-26)
Note
The beneficiary is you. Reading and translating for yourself sits inside the law; the line is "publishing to the public." Unpaid subtitle and fan-translation groups miss the crime's profit prerequisite but infringe civilly — takedowns and damages. In Japan, unpaid can still be criminal: February 2018 arrests of Chinese nationals prompted the Nagasaki consulate's reminder that unlicensed translation, publication, and dissemination may violate law even without profit. Ads, memberships, or donations-for-perks drop you into "for profit." In the YYeTs case, mere translators and proofreaders were treated as witnesses; the SPP's write-up targets founders, profit-splitters, and platform managers for severity, with leniency for hired hands and non-prosecution for the temporary and minor. The 2004, 2007, and 2020 criminal IP interpretations were repealed 2025-04-26; the 2011 three-department opinion survives unnanmed but yields to the new one on conflicts — e.g., the click threshold. Publishing fan fiction: item 25. Printing others' art on merchandise: Section 12, item 21. Running a platform and receiving infringement notices: Section 26, item 9.

Publishing or selling fan fiction: get the original's permission first, or swap the borrowed names and relationships for your own

Fan fiction borrowing even just names, personalities, and relationships can be judged infringing on publication. Free hobby fan fiction gets analyzed case by case.

Cost
Free. Before publishing or selling, negotiate a license with the rights-holder; failing that, replace borrowed character names, personalities, and relationships with your own — and keep the original's name out of your titles and blurbs.
Benefit
Jiang Nan's novel used the names of Guo Jing, Huang Rong, Qiao Feng, Linghu Chong, and others from Jin Yong's works, telling their campus stories, published 2002 with the subtitle "The University Days of the Condor Heroes," selling over a million copies across editions by suit time. Jin Yong sued in 2016 for 5 million. First instance found no copyright infringement — names, relationships, and personalities divorced from plot hardly count as protected expression — but unfair competition via borrowed fame, awarding 30% of 5.6 million yuan historical royalties (1.68 million) plus 200,000 in fees. The Guangzhou IP court on appeal reversed into copyright infringement: the plots weren't substantially similar, but the ensemble of 60-odd characters — names, personalities, relationships, backgrounds — was Jin Yong's selection and arrangement, protected expression, infringing four novels; the subtitle's deliberate Condor Heroes hook added unfair competition. Appeal: stop unfair competition, publish corrective notices, 1.68 million plus 200,000; two publishers jointly liable for 330,000; no cessation ordered, but future reprints owe 30% of reprint royalties. Both sides sought retrial; on 2025-09-19 the Guangdong High Court mediated a settlement: no characterization as "plagiarism"; Jiang acknowledged lacking copyright-law knowledge, never having sought adaptation permission, harming Jin Yong; he agreed never to republish unchanged and never again to use the distinctive names and related content; all confirmed the subtitle's unfair competition; the appeal award stood paid; on the mediation document's signing, both judgments lost effect. Another case: "Ghost Blows Out the Light" author Zhang Muye (Tianxia Bachang) transferred the property rights wholesale to Xuanting in 2006, then licensed a new book "Mo Jin Xiao Wei" reusing the names, relationships, and tomb-raiding rules, with a cover using the film "Mojin" poster. Xuanting sued for 20 million; Shanghai Pudong court found independent plot — no copyright infringement — but the cover's false-association impression was false advertising: two publishers liable 900,000 (one jointly for 600,000), upheld on appeal. Statutorily, adaptation rights cover transforming works into new original ones; unlicensed adaptation, translation, or annotation carries cessation and damages (national)
Note
The beneficiary is you. Grade B because fan-fiction's legal borders remain unsettled: this case's two instances disagreed and ended in mediation, both judgments void. The presiding judge's Q&A: the settlement binds only its parties, and whether fan fiction infringes "requires concrete case-by-case analysis" — first whether what's shared is abstract idea or concrete expression, then whether that expression is original, then whether fair use applies. So borrowing a genre or a setting differs from wholesale names-personalities-relationships. For freely posted fan fiction, no officially published judgment was found, and the copyright law holds no "unpaid means no infringement" exception. Process costs count: 2016-07 to 2025-09 — 9 years, with Jin Yong dying mid-appeal. Creators who've sold their rights can still be sued by buyers over their own sequels — Tianxia Bachang's case. Winners' enforcement costs ride in damages: the 200,000 here was attorney fees. Fan translation and reposting: item 24.
Sources (4 references)
广州知识产权法院 (2023). 金庸诉江南「同人作品第一案」有何深意（转载《法制与新闻》2023 年 7 月上期）. https://www.gipc.gov.cn/front/content.action?id=7b7cb9a7b2c…；广东省高级人民法院 (2025). 「金庸诉江南」著作权及不正当竞争纠纷案在粤达成和解. https://www.gdcourts.gov.cn/xwzx/fayuanxinmeiti/content/pos…；国家版权局 (2020). 2019 年度上海十大版权典型案件发布（上海市版权局发布，案例六：「鬼吹灯」著作权侵权及不正当竞争纠纷案）. https://www.ncac.gov.cn/xxfb/ywxx/202004/t20200430_47269.html；全国人大常委会 (2020). 著作权法（2020 年修正，第三条，第十条第一款第十四项，第五十二条第六项，第五十四条）. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796…
26

Don't buy batons, stun guns, daggers, or pepper spray "for protection" — carrying them in the car counts as carrying

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Daggers, switchblades, batons, and stun guns found on you: up to 5 days. Into stations, malls, or buses: 5–10 days. Actually using them backfires: one man took a bare-fist punch and stabbed with a pre-hidden knife — excessive defense, 4 years.

Cost
Free. Already bought: leave them home, out of the car too. In trouble: retreat and call first; cornered, then defend.
Benefit
Punishments Law Article 38: illegally carrying crossbows, daggers, or other state-controlled implements — up to 5 days plus up to 1,000; lighter, warning or up to 500; into public venues or transit: 5–10 days plus up to 1,000. Criminal Law Article 130 is heavier: controlled knives into public venues or transit endangering public safety, serious — up to 3 years. The MPS's 2007 criteria list five knife classes: daggers (grip, guard, blood groove, tip under 60 degrees); three-edged scrapers; self-locking switchblades; knives with tips under 60 degrees and blades over 150 mm; tips over 60 degrees with blades over 220 mm — unsharpened martial-arts and craft knives with rounded tips excepted. Police batons are police equipment: the People's Police Law restricts them to police — others' possession means confiscation, up to 15 days or warning, plus up to 5× gains. The railway prohibited list covers batons, tear sprayers, stun guns, and defenders — neither carried nor checked. Car storage counts: one driver caught with a controlled knife at a checkpoint was administratively detained. Actual use runs the defense guidance: "whether instruments were used or readied" distinguishes defense from brawling. Official case: Yang quarreled, the other side threatened revenge, Yang went home and hid two knives; the man returned and slapped him once bare-handed; Yang stabbed chest and abdomen, killing him. The court found defensive character but — a bare fist against vitals — excessive defense: 4 years for intentional injury (national; punishments law since 2026-01-01)
Note
The beneficiary is you. Carrying a knife doesn't automatically void defense: in Guiding Case 45, the student surrounded by 9 drew a carried fruit knife and was still found lawfully defensive — what mattered was absence of mutual-combat intent, not the tool. The costs land twice: the items themselves are illegal whenever discovered, used or not; and a knife in reach turns a shove into a stabbing, where serious injury flips into excessive defense. Pepper spray: no national-level ban text found here, only the railway prohibition; whether online batons count as police batons likewise lacks a national ruling text. In trouble: Section 8, item 10 first; cornered: item 11. Robbed in the wild: Section 13, item 36.
Sources (10 references)
