10. Is dating and marriage worth it?

20 entries

This section splits "is marriage worth it" into separate accounts — money, time, health, legal risk, and relationship quality — each computed alone. Each account uses only numbers with findable sources, restricted to official statistics or meta-analyses (recomputing pooled data from many studies). No moral judgments, no conclusions on your behalf. Health accounts run on death risk, time accounts on daily minutes, legal accounts on what statutes say; the three are never converted into each other. The account-splitting method, fill-in checklist, and common mistakes are in [docs/结婚划不划算.md](../docs/结婚划不划算.md). Entries in this section are grouped by theme, with item numbers in parentheses. Meeting and dating: meet more people (item 1), stop at a clear refusal (item 2), judge interest by behavior (item 3), alternate progressively deeper questions (item 5), long-distance is no worse (item 6). Relationship quality: your own felt experience of the relationship (item 4), fight about the matter, not the person (item 17), go to couples therapy together (item 20). The worth-it accounts: registration data first (item 7), discount health benefits from observational data (item 8), time as unpaid labor (item 9), compute exit costs (item 15), marrying for elders gets its own account (item 16). Registering and premarital checks: registering needs only IDs (item 13), one premarital check (item 14). Money and debt: money defaults first (item 10), parental home contributions written as loan or gift (item 11), a spouse's large borrowings (item 12). Same-sex couples and orientation: same-sex couples arrange powers of attorney and wills (item 18), don't marry by concealing orientation (item 19).

1

Meet more people instead of betting everything on one: two people's chemistry can't be predicted before they meet

Grade AValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Two speed-dating studies had participants fill in 100-odd mate-preference questionnaires before meeting. The questionnaires could compute who generally likes people easily and who is generally liked — not whether these two click. Chemistry is only knowable in person. So meeting several beats staking everything on one.

Cost
Free. Time goes to meeting several people, not re-litigating one. The hard part: not fixating.
Benefit
In the two speed-dating studies, participants completed 100-odd mate-selection self-report scales before meeting. Random-forest models (a pattern-finding algorithm) could compute "how much a person likes others overall" — the questionnaires explained 4%–18% of variance (variance meaning person-to-person difference, of which the questionnaires explain only part) — and "how popular a person is overall," 7%–27%. But "do these two specific people click" couldn't be computed, no matter how pre-meeting traits and preferences combined. The same group's earlier speed-dating experiment had participants self-report ideal preferences — looks versus earning prospects — which failed to predict interest in any specific person on the night
Note
The studies establish only "unpredictable before meeting," not "effort is useless." Chemistry is knowable only in person, so time spent genuinely meeting several beats all-in on one. The subjects were Euro-American students; China's dating environment differs — discount accordingly.
Sources (2 references)
Joel S, Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2017). Is romantic desire predictable? Machine learning applied to initial romantic attraction. Psychological Science, 28(10), 1478-1489. https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797617714580；Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2008). Sex differences in mate preferences revisited: do people know what they initially desire in a romantic partner? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 94(2), 245-264. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.245
2

When they clearly refuse, stop — continued pursuit is an administrative offense, not "sincerity"

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

After a clear refusal, still messaging and waiting makes it an administrative offense from January 2026: up to 5 days or 1,000 yuan; heavier, 5–10 days. Police can also order no-contact; breaching adds another 5–10 days.

Cost
Free, no time. The hard part: no more messages, no more waiting outside.
Benefit
The punishments law effective 2026-01-01 lists harassment and stalking separately: "repeatedly sending obscene, insulting, or threatening information, or using harassment, pestering, or stalking to disturb another's normal life" — up to 5 days or 1,000 yuan; heavier, 5–10 days plus up to 1,000. This clause adds a layer: with police-chiefs' approval, the actor may be ordered to avoid contact with the victim for a period; violating the no-contact order draws another 5–10 days
Note
"Persistence wins them over" has no research support, while detention and no-contact orders are in black and white. The record also touches civil-service exams, vetting, and some licenses. The line between pursuit and harassment isn't your intention — it's whether they clearly refused.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大常委会 (2025 修订). 治安管理处罚法（第五十条第一款第五项、第二款）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml（最高人民检察院转载）
3

Judge interest by behavior, not "signals": who initiates, who plans, who follows up

Grade BValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

52 stranger pairs chatted 10-odd minutes and judged whether the other flirted. "Not flirting" was judged accurately; "flirting" was missed. Same result with 261 people rating videos. So skip expression-reading: watch who initiates, who plans the next date, who follows up when you stop pushing.

Cost
Free, little time. The hard part: swapping habits — record facts instead of decoding expressions and tone.
Benefit
Two studies measured flirtation-detection accuracy. In the first, 52 previously unacquainted mixed-sex pairs talked 10–12 minutes, each reporting own and perceived flirting — "interactions without flirting were judged more accurately; flirting interactions less so." The second used 26 one-minute videos rated by 261 observers, same conclusion. People reliably detect non-flirting but miss flirting
Note
Contested: other work holds that men don't overperceive women's interest — women underreport it on questionnaires. Who judges better remains open. Both camps agree: inferring minds from micro-expressions and tone is low-accuracy; visible behavior — initiating, planning next dates, following up unbidden — is far more reliable.
Sources (2 references)
Hall JA, Xing C, Brooks S (2015). Accurately detecting flirting: error management theory, the traditional sexual script, and flirting base rate. Communication Research, 42(7), 939-958. https://doi.org/10.1177/0093650214534972；Perilloux C, Kurzban R (2015). Do men overperceive women's sexual interest? Psychological Science, 26(1), 70-77. https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614555727（争议方）
4

Whether the relationship is good is mainly about how you feel inside it, not the other party's specs

Grade AValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

What best tells you whether the relationship is good is your own experience, not their specs: do they feel committed and appreciative, do you fight often. Your own feelings outpredict your partner's reports 2–4×. But whether it improves or decays — no questionnaire computes that.

Cost
Free, little time. The hard part: shifting perspective — shelve the checklist, watch the relationship itself.
Benefit
A machine-learning analysis across 29 labs and 43 longitudinal dyadic datasets (longitudinal meaning the same couples followed over time). The strongest predictors of relationship quality were all the person's own perceptions of the relationship: perceived commitment, appreciation, sexual satisfaction, perceived partner satisfaction, conflict. Among individual traits, the strongest were life satisfaction, negative affect, depression, avoidant and anxious attachment. Relationship perceptions explained up to 45% of variance at intake (variance meaning couple-to-couple quality difference) and up to 18% at study end. Self-reports outpredicted partner-reports 2–4×; beyond one's own relationship perceptions, adding individual differences and partner reports bought zero additional prediction
Note
The same study found whether relationships improved or deteriorated was essentially unpredictable from any self-report set. So judging the current relationship: ask your own experience, not their checklist — but don't expect to forecast its future. Relationship quality and physical health: item 17.
Sources (1 references)
Joel S, Eastwick PW, Allison CJ, et al. (2020). Machine learning uncovers the most robust self-report predictors of relationship quality across 43 longitudinal couples studies. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 117(32), 19061-19071. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1917036117
5

To grow closer, alternate through a set of progressively deeper questions — skip the pickup scripts

Grade BValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Two strangers alternating through 36 progressively deeper questions ended the 45 minutes clearly closer than pairs small-talking equally long. What works is alternating truth-telling, layer by layer — not scripts. It shows closeness then and there, not a long-term relationship.

Cost
Free. Takes 45 minutes.
Benefit
Paired strangers alternated through three question sets, 36 total, from "who would you most want to dinner" to "when did you last cry in front of someone." Post-session closeness significantly exceeded small-talk controls of equal length — and exceeded the average rating students gave their closest real relationships
Note
One experiment, students, short-term closeness only — no long-term development measured. The closeness came from two people alternately going deeper with true things about themselves, not scripts or one-sided performance. In conversation: "I share something true, then ask one equally deep" — alternating.
Sources (1 references)
Aron A, Melinat E, Aron EN, Vallone RD, Bator RJ (1997). The experimental generation of interpersonal closeness: a procedure and some preliminary findings. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 23(4), 363-377. https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167297234003
6

Long-distance is no worse than same-city; the real cliff is the first three months after moving in

Grade BValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: highTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Long-distance runs more stable while apart — absence idealizes. The real cliff follows the move. In tracking data, about half of long-distance couples reached co-location, the other half ended during separation; of the reunited half, a third broke up within 3 months.

Cost
Travel money and travel time; fewer meetings than same-city. The hard part: sustaining the separation.
Benefit
Two studies agree: long-distance relationships are more stable than same-city ones while apart, because idealization of the partner runs markedly higher (measured as idealization distortion, romantic love, relationship memories, perceived similarity) — the less frequent the meetings, the rosier the picture. But the stability holds only while apart; once same-city, long-distance couples break up more readily. The long-distance-to-cohabitation tracking study: roughly half reached moving in together, half ended during separation; of the reunited half, one-third broke up within 3 months. Longer gaps and stronger idealization during separation predicted post-reunion instability
Note
US college dating relationships, not marriages, and older data — don't transplant the absolute rates. Another study surveyed 717 long-distance and 425 same-city: quality differences were small, with the two individuals and the relationship itself mattering most. So don't cite "long-distance always fails" — prepare for the post-reunion months, when autonomy shrinks, knowledge deepens, and conflict and jealousy rise.
Sources (3 references)
Stafford L, Merolla AJ, Castle JD (2006). When long-distance dating partners become geographically close. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 23(6), 901-919. https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407506070472；Stafford L, Merolla AJ (2007). Idealization, reunions, and stability in long-distance dating relationships. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 24(1), 37-54. https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407507072578；Dargie E et al. (2015). Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy, 41(2), 181-202. https://doi.org/10.1080/0092623X.2013.864367（备注里那项异地研究）
7

Read the registration data before listening to elders: what the marriage and divorce rates actually measure

Grade AValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

2024: 6.106 million marriage registrations, down a fifth year-on-year; 3.513 million divorces. The internet's "divorce rate over half" divides these two numbers — about 57.5%. But the divorcing and the marrying aren't the same people; it doesn't mean half of marriages end. The bulletin's marriage rate 4.3‰ and divorce rate 2.5‰ divide by the whole population.

Cost
Free. Minutes reading the marriage-registration section of the civil-affairs annual bulletin.
Benefit
2024: 6.106 million marriage registrations, −20.5% year-on-year, marriage rate 4.3‰; 3.513 million divorces — 2.622 million registered at civil affairs, 891,000 by court judgment or mediation — divorce rate 2.5‰. The bulletin defines marriage (divorce) rate = that year's marriages (divorces) ÷ that year's average total population × 1000‰ — a "crude rate," denominator the whole population, not the married one
Note
The internet's "divorce rate over 50%" divides that year's divorces by that year's marriages, 351.3 / 610.6 ≈ 57.5% — the "divorce-to-marriage ratio." The two numbers aren't the same cohort, and the bulletin carries no such indicator, so it can't be read as "half of marriages end." Computing "the probability a given marriage eventually divorces" requires following one marriage cohort; no such official data was found.
Sources (2 references)
民政部 (2025). 2024 年民政事业发展统计公报（五（二）1 婚姻登记服务、注释 5），网页版与 PDF 版. https://www.mca.gov.cn/n1288/n1294/n1554/c16620049999800061…, https://www.mca.gov.cn/gdnps/n2445/n2451/n2458/n2681/c16620…
8

Count marriage's health benefits — but discount them as observational

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Married people run about 12% lower mortality than the unmarried; never-married run about 24% higher than married. Co-occurrence only, not causation: healthy, high-income, social people both marry more and live longer. The numbers are mostly Euro-American — magnitude reference only domestically.

Cost
Free, no time. Remember one thing: these numbers say married people die less — co-occurrence, not marriage causing longevity.
Benefit
An elderly meta-analysis pooled 53 comparisons, 250,000-odd people: married versus unmarried all-cause mortality RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85–0.91 (RR risk ratio, CI confidence range) — about 12% lower. In the same analysis: widowed 1.11, divorced or separated 1.16, never-married 1.11 — about 11%, 16%, 11% higher. No sex difference. The most conservative estimate ran RR 0.94, just 6% lower. Another meta-analysis compared never-married with married across 95 papers, 500-million-odd people: HR 1.24 (1.19–1.30), about 24% higher, shrinking with age. A third, split by sex — 21 studies, 7.89 million-odd: unmarried status co-occurred with all-cause, cancer, and cardiovascular mortality in both sexes, with larger male gaps in cardiovascular and all-cause death; unmarried men versus unmarried women ran 31% more stroke death and 9% more all-cause death
Note
The dispute: married people are selected — healthy, wealthy, social people both marry more and live longer. All three meta-analyses use observational data, tracking only, no assignment; the authors themselves flag publication bias and method limits. Roelfs found the more rigorous the study, the smaller the gap. Mostly Euro-American samples — magnitude reference only.
Sources (3 references)
Manzoli L, et al. (2007). Marital status and mortality in the elderly: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Soc Sci Med 64:77–94. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2006.08.031；Roelfs DJ, et al. (2011). The rising relative risk of mortality for singles: meta-analysis and meta-regression. Am J Epidemiol 174(4):379–389. https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwr111；Wang Y, et al. (2020). Sex differences in the association between marital status and the risk of cardiovascular, cancer, and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 7,881,040 individuals. Glob Health Res Policy 5:4. https://doi.org/10.1186/s41256-020-00133-8
9

The time account runs on "unpaid labor": settle the division before registering

Grade AValue: highMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

In the national time-use survey, unpaid work — chores and care — averaged 1 hour 52 minutes daily for men and 3 hours 29 for women. The survey doesn't split by marital status, so "how much housework marriage adds" has no official number; the gender gap serves only as an upper-bound reference. Your division can be negotiated into anything before the certificate.

Cost
Free. An hour or two before marriage to negotiate unpaid work — chores, elder and child care, whose career yields — into an explicit division, then execute it. The hard part: laying it on the table.
Benefit
The 2024 national time-use survey. Unpaid labor means chores and family care. Those doing it that day averaged 2 hours 45 minutes — men 1:52, women 3:29. Participation that day: 67.5% men, 83.9% women. Housework averaged 1:17 daily (1:59 among doers), down 28 minutes from 2018. Family care averaged 30 minutes (1:46 among doers). The 2018 figures: housework 45 minutes men, 2:06 women; child care 17 minutes men, 53 women
Note
Both surveys group by sex, urban-rural, and age — not marital status — so "how much housework marriage adds" has no official figure; the gender gap is the upper-bound proxy. The numbers are national averages; the two of you can negotiate anything else.
Sources (3 references)
国家统计局 (2024). 第三次全国时间利用调查公报（第二号、第三号）. https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html, https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957215.html；国家统计局 (2019). 2018 年全国时间利用调查公报. https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html
10

The money account starts with legal defaults, then decide on a written agreement

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Without a written agreement, the law defaults post-marriage wages, bonuses, business and investment returns, and inherited or gifted property to joint ownership. Premarital property, and bequests or gifts expressly to one side, stay personal. A written agreement splitting everything binds both. The spouse contributing more through child care and elder care may claim compensation at divorce.

Cost
Free. Read the property articles of the Civil Code's marriage-family book. If needed, sign a written property agreement — the law requires writing only, not notarization. The hard part: talking money in advance.
Benefit
The defaults absent agreement: post-marriage wages, bonuses, labor remuneration, business and investment income, intellectual-property income, and inherited or gifted property are joint (Article 1062). Premarital property, personal-injury compensation, property bequeathed or gifted expressly to one side, and one side's personal-use items are personal (Article 1063). Couples may agree in writing on separate, joint, or mixed ownership — binding (Article 1065). The party bearing more duty through child-rearing, elder care, or assisting the other's work may claim compensation at divorce (Article 1088)
Note
No official statistics on betrothal gifts, weddings, or marital homes — no numbers here. Article 1088's compensation is negotiated first, court-set on failure, no fixed formula. Written property agreements serve both sides: the higher earner and the heavier unpaid contributor alike.
Sources (2 references)
全国人民代表大会 (2020). 中华人民共和国民法典（2021 年 1 月 1 日起施行，第一千零六十二、一千零六十三、一千零六十五、一千零八十八条）. 国家法律法规数据库 https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?title=%E4%B8%AD%E5%8D%8E%E4%B…；条文全文见最高人民法院公报转载 http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6…
11

Parental home contributions: write loan-versus-gift clearly at the moment of transfer

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Premarital parental contributions default to gifts to their own child. Post-marriage contributions without agreement run as joint property. From February 2025, post-marriage full contributions by one side's parents without an only-to-our-child clause let courts award the home to the contributing side's child at divorce, then decide compensation. To count as a loan, write it that day with both signatures.

Cost
Free. On the day, one page stating whether the money gifts or lends, and to whom, signed by parents and child; a loan has both spouses sign, with the same sentence in the transfer memo.
Benefit
Premarital parental contributions count as gifts to their own child, save express gifts to both. Post-marriage contributions follow agreement; absent or unclear agreement, joint-property principles apply. From 2025-02-01 there is more: where one side's parents fully funded during marriage and the gift contract doesn't state only-to-our-child, divorce courts may award the home to the contributor's child, then weigh compensation for the other side by cohabitation and children, fault, family contribution, and market price at divorce. Partial funding by one side or funding by both: award based on contribution sources and proportions, with reasonable compensation (national)
Note
Clarity serves both sides: contributing parents needn't count on producing a retroactive IOU at divorce; under Interpretation II, whose money it was is itself the basis — whose name is on the deed no longer decides. The receiving side also learns what the money counts as before divorce. A loan must be a real loan: agreed, repayment terms set, memo written, repayment records kept where needed — miss a piece and you'll explain it in court.
Sources (3 references)
最高人民法院 (2020). 关于适用《民法典》婚姻家庭编的解释（一）（法释〔2020〕22 号，第二十九条）. https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html；最高人民法院 (2025). 关于适用《民法典》婚姻家庭编的解释（二）（法释〔2025〕1 号，第八条）. https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/452771.html；全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第一千零六十二条第一款第四项）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
12

A spouse's large borrowings, unsigned and unratified by you, don't automatically become your debt

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Money a spouse borrows behind your back, clearly beyond household daily needs, unsigned and unratified, isn't automatically yours. The creditor must prove the money went to joint life or business. But home-purchase money that truly became the jointly occupied home often clears that bar.

Cost
Free. Never sign "co-borrower" or "guarantor" on a spouse's papers, and never write "we'll repay this" in chat — it can read as ratification. The hard part: staying silent under collection pressure.
Benefit
Joint marital debts are: both signatures; after-the-fact ratification; or one party borrowing within household daily needs in their own name. One party's borrowing clearly beyond daily needs isn't joint — unless the creditor proves use for joint life, joint business, or mutual acknowledgment. Home-purchase money is clearly beyond daily needs, with the burden on the creditor; but money that became the jointly lived-in or jointly owned home often proves "joint-life use." Hence item 11's write-it-at-transfer step matters more (national, since 2021)
Note
When the other side's parents suddenly produce a loan agreement signed only by your spouse at divorce, two steps. First, whether the loan happened at all: your claim of no funds delivered, coherently reasoned, gets weighed against amounts, delivery method, both sides' means, transaction habits, asset movements, and witnesses; a transfer voucher alone still leaves the lender proving the loan. Second, if the loan stands, whether it's joint. IOUs and guarantees generally: Section 8, item 18.
Sources (2 references)
全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第一千零六十四条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml；最高人民法院 (2020 年第二次修正). 关于审理民间借贷案件适用法律若干问题的规定（第十五、十六条）. http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/94b6623974526df7d2430a3…（最高人民法院公报）
13

Registering takes an ID card plus a signed declaration — no household register, no fee, certificate on the spot

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

From May 2025, registering needs two things: your ID card, and a signed declaration of having no spouse and no lineal or within-three-generation collateral relation with the other party. No household register, no trip to a registration-place hometown. Free of charge, certificate on the spot when qualified.

Cost
Free. Both present in person; usually under an hour.
Benefit
The new marriage-registration regulation effective 2025-05-10 changed the required documents to exactly two: "(1) the person's resident ID card; (2) a signed declaration that the person has no spouse and no lineal or within-three-generation collateral blood relation with the other party." The household register is no longer required. Registration authorities are "county-level people's governments' civil affairs departments or township people's governments determined by province-level governments for convenience." The old "at a party's habitual-registration residence" restriction is gone. The regulation also states registration "may not charge fees" and that qualified parties "shall be registered on the spot and issued marriage certificates"
Note
Only four things block registration: under-age, not fully voluntary, an existing spouse, or prohibited blood relation. Only peripheral services — photos, copies — may charge. Registration itself is free: refuse and report any "production" or "rush" fees. Divorce's 30-day cooling-off: this section's exit-cost entry.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2025). 婚姻登记条例（国令第 804 号，第二、六、八、十条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017752…
14

One premarital check before marriage; major illness must be truthfully disclosed before registration

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Concealing major illness before registration lets the other side petition the court to annul the marriage — within 1 year of learning. The check itself hasn't been a registration prerequisite since 2003; attendance is voluntary. Fees follow local policy; half a day.

Cost
Free or reduced for age-eligible people in most regions; self-pay runs a few hundred yuan; half a day.
Benefit
The legal consequence is explicit: the new registration regulation states "a party suffering major illness shall truthfully inform the other before marriage registration; failing which, the other party may petition the people's court to annul the marriage under Civil Code Article 1053." The state positions premarital checks as the first gate of birth-defect prevention, with current targets "premarital examination rate and pre-pregnancy eugenics check coverage of target populations sustained above 70% and 80%," requiring co-locating check institutions with registration offices and promoting "one-stop" registration-check-guidance services. The Civil Code: a party with major illness shall truthfully inform before registration; failing which, the other may petition annulment — within 1 year of knowing or should-have-known
Note
Since 2003 the check hasn't been a registration prerequisite — voluntary. But concealment gives the other side annulment rights within the 1-year window. No national free-check mandate: the 2020 five-department notice only "actively advocates" locality-based free checks. Whether free and what's included is local — ask the maternal-child health institution or the one-stop registration window.

15

Compute the exit cost: consensual divorce has a 30-day cooling-off; litigated divorce has statutory grounds

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Consensual divorce isn't sign-and-done. Within 30 days of application, either party may withdraw; after the window, both must collect the certificate in person within another 30 days — miss it and it's withdrawn. Disagreement means litigation: mediation first, judgment only on grounds like violence, bigamy, or two years' separation.

Cost
Free. Before marriage, read once: if exit comes, how long and through what. The hard part: thinking about ending it before beginning it.
Benefit
Consensual divorce requires a written agreement and in-person application (Article 1076). Within 30 days of the authority's receipt, either party may withdraw; after expiry, both must apply for the divorce certificate in person within 30 days — unclaimed means withdrawn (Article 1077). With disagreement, litigation: courts mediate first; bigamy or cohabitation, domestic violence or abuse and abandonment, incorrigible gambling or drugs, or separation for 2 years due to estrangement — failed mediation means divorce granted; separation of another year after a denial means granted on re-filing (Article 1079). In 2024, of 3.513 million divorces, 891,000 went through court judgment or mediation
Note
The cooling-off applies to consensual divorce only; litigation has none but runs longer. Filing and attorney fees vary — no numbers here. High exit costs don't argue against marriage, but you should know them before it.
Sources (2 references)
全国人民代表大会 (2020). 中华人民共和国民法典（第一千零七十六、一千零七十七、一千零七十九条）. http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6…；民政部 (2020). 关于贯彻落实《中华人民共和国民法典》中有关婚姻登记规定的通知（民发〔2020〕116 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-12/04/content_556…；民政部 (2025). 2024 年民政事业发展统计公报. 题录同第 7 条（结婚率、离婚率各是什么口径）
16

Keep a separate account for "marrying for the elders" — don't merge it with your own

Grade CValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The elders' benefit is real — but it doesn't convert into your health or relationship quality, while the time, money, and exit-cost accounts are all yours to bear. Two columns on paper, and the task-marriage's value becomes visible at a glance.

Cost
Free. Two columns on paper: which benefits of this marriage are yours (computable from the earlier items), and which are the elders' — reassurance, face, the end of nagging. The hard part: leaving their column alone instead of merging it into yours.
Benefit
The elders' gains are real. But they don't transfer into your health (item 8) or relationship quality (item 4 — your own felt experience). The time account (item 9), money accounts (items 10–12), and exit costs (item 15) all land on the parties. Split the ledger, and whether "task marriage" pays becomes self-evident
Note
The elders' column may legitimately weigh heavily — the weighing is yours. The fill-in checklist: [docs/结婚划不划算.md](../docs/结婚划不划算.md)
Sources
作者经验，方法类建议；数据部分见本节前面各条
17

Treat relationship quality as a health account: fight about the matter, not the person — no insults, no sarcasm

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: small

Good marriages run with better health and lower mortality — small associations, roughly the size of diet's. In one experiment, couples fighting with steady hostility healed experimental wounds at only 60% the speed of mild couples.

Cost
Free. In fights, address only the matter at hand — no insults, sarcasm, or old scores. The hard part: mouth control while angry.
Benefit
Pooling 126 studies, 72,000-odd people (meta-analysis): higher marriage quality tracked better health, correlations r between .07 and .21 (0 meaning none, 1 complete lockstep). Lower mortality risk: r = .11; smaller cardiovascular reactivity during conflict: r = −.13. The authors: these effects are small — comparable to dietary habits. In the crossover experiment, 42 healthy couples were hospitalized twice for 24 hours each — once for supportive conversation, once discussing a disagreement; after conflict, blister wounds healed slower. Couples hostile on both occasions healed at only 60% the rate of low-hostility couples, and their next-morning inflammatory markers (IL-6, tumor necrosis factor) rose higher
Note
Why B: mostly tracking studies without assignment — unsortable whether bad marriage sickens or sickness sours marriage. Some studies held after adjusting for age and income; Robles flags publication bias in parts. Sex-comparing studies found essentially no differences. No pooled analysis comparing "bad marriage" against "unmarried" mortality was found — "bad marriage beats no marriage" stays inference. The wound experiment: 42 couples. "Matter-not-person, no insults or sarcasm" is the author's derivation from the hostile-behavior findings, never directly compared. Stuck in fight-cold-war cycles: item 20 (couples therapy). Violence or chronic verbal abuse isn't a communication problem — Section 8, item 43. Exit costs: item 15.
Sources (2 references)
Robles TF, Slatcher RB, Trombello JM, McGinn MM (2014). Marital quality and health: a meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0031859；Kiecolt-Glaser JK et al. (2005). Hostile marital interactions, proinflammatory cytokine production, and wound healing. Archives of General Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1001/archpsyc.62.12.1377
18

Same-sex couples: while both are lucid, arrange powers of attorney, guardianship agreements, and wills — legally you're not close relatives; without papers, no signing rights and no inheritance

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Statutory close relatives are spouses, parents, children, siblings — partners aren't among them. Without documents, a partner can't decide for an incapacitated one, and inherits nothing at death. Three papers cover the stages: power of attorney while competent, agreed guardianship after incapacity, a will afterward.

Cost
Guardianship agreements and wills at a notary run from a few hundred yuan locally; a handwritten will is free. A half-day or two. The hard part: sitting down to talk illness and death.
Benefit
Civil Code Article 1045 lists close relatives as spouses, parents, children, siblings, grandparents, and grandchildren — partners absent. Article 1127's statutory heirs: first spouses, children, parents; then siblings, grandparents — partners absent again. Article 1219 covers surgery and special examination and treatment: where the patient can't be informed or shouldn't be, medical staff inform the patient's "close relatives" and take consent. Three paths patch it: Article 33 lets adults agree in writing in advance with "other individuals willing to serve as guardians" — on incapacity, that person becomes guardian, i.e., statutory agent. Article 165 requires written powers of attorney naming the agent, matters, powers, and term, signed or sealed — terminated by death. Article 1133 permits willing property by will to persons outside the statutory heirs. An article by the Yichang judicial bureau, carried on the Hubei justice-department site, confirms same-sex partners can notarize guardianship agreements naming each other (national)
Note
A partner takes as "legatee," not heir: acceptance must be declared within 60 days of learning, silence forfeiting. The partner and interested parties can't witness the will. Multiple wills: the last governs — Section 17, item 2. Whether agreed guardians can sign surgical consent varies by hospital — ask yours in advance. Family contesting means litigation: 6+ months first instance, attorney fees yours — hence notarize where possible. Jointly bought property and savings get their own written agreements by true contribution. Arranging guardianship: Section 17, item 1. Beneficiaries: you and your partner.
Sources (2 references)
全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第二十三、三十三、一百六十五、一百七十三、一千零四十五、一千一百二十四、一千一百二十七、一千一百三十三至一千一百四十、一千一百四十二、一千二百一十九条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…（国家法律法规数据库）；宜昌市司法局 (2021). 意定监护公证：通向彩虹的公证之路. 湖北省司法厅网站「实践荟萃」栏目. https://sft.hubei.gov.cn/fbjd/sjhc/202101/t20210108_3208602…
19

Don't marry by concealing orientation, and don't treat a marriage of convenience as the easy way out: legally it's a real marriage, exit only by divorce

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Orientation-concealing marriage is legally neither void nor voidable — exit means divorce. A marriage of convenience is likewise real: post-marriage earnings and debts count as spousal. The deceived party may seek greater property share and emotional damages at divorce — court support unsettled.

Cost
Free. The hard part: years of withstanding family pressure.
Benefit
Article 1051: marriages are void only for bigamy, prohibited kinship, or under-age. Articles 1052–1053: voidable only for coercion or concealed major illness. Interpretation I, Article 17: other grounds for voidness are dismissed. Exit therefore means divorce. A registered convenience marriage is lawful: Article 1062 makes post-marriage wages and remuneration joint; Article 1064 makes co-signed and daily-need debts joint. Divorce damages under Article 1091 cover bigamy, cohabitation with another, domestic violence, abuse or abandonment, and "other grave fault"; Interpretation I, Article 2 confines "cohabitation with another" to "extra-marital opposite-sex" cohabitation — same-sex relations can only argue "other grave fault." Damages include emotional harm, claimed together with the divorce petition; denied divorce means denied damages. No published post-Code judgments were found. Under the old law, a 2013 Jiangsu High Court site article discussed a wife suing over her husband's concealed homosexuality, listing two views: one holding homosexuality outside the statutory faults, supporting neither greater share nor damages; the author endorsing the other — treating the deceived party as "without fault," favoring her in property division and granting emotional solatium (national)
Note
The greater-share and damages points rest on one analytical article without the case's outcome — actual recovery depends on the court. The Code's "other grave fault" addition gives the deceived party a hook. Statutes are Grade A; the outcomes aren't settled. Where both convenience-marriage partners have same-sex partners, those partnerships lack marriage-law protection — property written separately: item 18. Convenience divorces run the same 30-day cooling-off or litigation: item 15. Waiving damages in a consensual divorce bars later claims. Beneficiary: first the spouse who would be deceived, then you — discovery brings divorce, property division, and child custody at once.
Sources (3 references)
全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第一千零五十一至一千零五十四、一千零六十二、一千零六十四、一千零七十九、一千零八十七、一千零九十一条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…（国家法律法规数据库）；最高人民法院 (2020). 关于适用《中华人民共和国民法典》婚姻家庭编的解释（一）（法释〔2020〕22 号，第二、十七、八十六至九十条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80808177e75f880178006736…；朱来宽、王洪娟 (2013). 因同性恋导致离婚能否主张损害赔偿？江苏法院网. http://www.jsfy.gov.cn/article/26621.html
20

Stuck in repeat fights and cold wars: go to couples therapy together — waiting rarely fixes it

Grade AValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: highTime: mediumWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Stuck couples completing couples therapy end clearly more satisfied — about 70% improve. Waitlisted couples barely change. Effects fade: by year 5, about half still clearly improved and a quarter separated or divorced.

Cost
Paid. Per-session fees vary by place and hospital — no numbers here. Studies run weekly; one trial ran about 8 months end to end. The hard part: both attending and finishing.
Benefit
A 2020 meta-analysis pooled 58 studies, 2,092 couples. Completing couples therapy moved relationship satisfaction g = 1.12 (0.92–1.31) — a large effect by the authors' reading (g is effect size; see the README glossary). Waitlisted couples over the same period: g = 0.12 (−0.04 to 0.29) — nothing. Worse starting relationships improved more. A 2012 review: couples therapy improves roughly 70% of treated couples. A randomized trial took 134 long-term, severely distressed couples through about 8 months of two behavioral couple therapies: end-of-treatment satisfaction d = 0.90 and 0.71; by year 5, 50.0% and 45.9% retained "clinically significant improvement," while 25.7% and 27.9% had separated or divorced
Note
The dispute is durability: a randomized-only meta-analysis found end-of-treatment g = 0.60, 0.44 at six months; at 12 months only behavioral couple therapy held data, g = 0.06 — nearly gone. A review of 20 meta-analyses: clinically meaningful effects in 40%–50%. "70% improve" and "40–50% clearly improve" use different bars — don't mix. The 5-year trial had no no-treatment arm, so it can't say whether divorce rose or fell. The 2020 pool covered different-sex couples only; no Chinese randomized trial was found — discount accordingly. Where to go domestically: the Mental Health Law requires psychotherapy inside medical institutions, and counselors may not perform it — ask hospital psychiatry and psychology departments about couples therapy; outside institutions, check credentials and training first. With domestic violence, don't start jointly: the 2016 meta-analysis confines its conclusions to mild-to-moderate, mutually conflictual violence — control-driven or severe violence is excluded, and practitioners fear post-session retaliation. Being hit: Section 8, item 43 first. How to speak in fights: item 17; whether to leave: item 15. Beneficiaries: you and your spouse.
Sources (7 references)

Marital status and satisfaction five years following a randomized clinical trial comparing traditional versus integrative behavioral couple therapy. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 78(2), 225-235. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0018132；Rathgeber M, Bürkner PC, Schiller EM, Holling H (2019). The efficacy of emotionally focused couples therapy and behavioral couples therapy: a meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 45(3), 447-463. https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12336（争议方）；Shadish WR, Baldwin SA (2003). Meta-analysis of MFT interventions. Couples therapy for intimate partner violence: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 42(4), 567-583. https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12178；全国人大常委会 (2018 修正). 精神卫生法（第二十三、五十一条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf744…（国家法律法规数据库）

11. Red lines for programmers and technical people

19 entries

This section's metrics are personal freedom and money — what returns is "don't get locked up" and "don't pay damages." Coders and technical people often take what follows as "merely technical questions," but they map to specific crimes or specific civil liabilities. Each entry gives statutory numbers and cases published on the Supreme People's Procuratorate and Supreme People's Court sites. The criminal law follows the Beijing traffic-authority reprint "as amended by Amendment XI." Entries run by "easiest for technical people to assume it's fine × heaviest consequences." Item 1 is the universal one: how to judge before acting, and what to do first when pursued.

1

Before acting, ask one question: would the vendor, platform, or company report it? On pursuit, get a criminal lawyer immediately

Grade CValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Ask before acting: would they report? Logs, payments, and chats are all retrievable. Under criminal detention, the arrest decision comes within 37 days at most. From the first questioning you may retain a lawyer — those 37 days are when a criminal lawyer matters most.

Cost
Free. Replace "is it technically possible" with: would the vendor, platform, or company report it? The hard part: resisting "nobody bothers with something this small" — server logs, payment records, and group chats all surface by default in investigations.
Benefit
Any unit or individual discovering crime may report it; investigators finding crime facts shall file. After detention, police request arrest approval within 3 days (formal arrest by the procuratorate), extendable 1–4; itinerant offenders extend to 30; the procuratorate decides within 7 more — 37 days total at most. From first interrogation or compulsory measures, you may retain counsel; during police investigation, only lawyers. Requested meetings: within 48 hours at the detention center. Those facing control, custody, or supplementary punishment only may get bail: pay a deposit or find a guarantor and wait at home — bail up to 12 months (national)
Note
The 37 days run from detention to the arrest decision — not a custody cap; post-arrest investigation detention follows. The lawyer's leverage peaks in those 37 days: meeting, submitting a "no-arrest" opinion, seeking bail. Post-indictment is late. Every other entry in this section is the same question: does the other side have grounds to report?
Sources (1 references)
全国人大 (2018). 刑事诉讼法（2018 年修正，第三十四、三十九、六十七、七十九、九十一、一百一十、一百一十二条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml
2

Never build, sell, or distribute game cheats and assists — including "screen-reading only, no memory access" AI helpers — nor modified clients adding features to apps like WeChat

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Selling cheats to 20 person-times, or earning 5,000 yuan, reaches up to 3 years; especially serious, 3–7. One wallhack/aimbot maker sold 80,000-odd yuan in 3 months — 1 year suspended 1, fine 5,000. A private-server operator collected 20-million-odd yuan of top-ups — top sentence 4 years, fines up to 10 million yuan.

Cost
Free. The price is walking away from these gigs and "little tools." The hard part: the money comes fast, and you can't see who'd pursue.
Benefit
Providing programs or tools specifically for intruding into or illegally controlling computer systems, serious: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; especially serious, 3–7 plus fines. "Serious" thresholds: tools to 20+ person-times, or illegal gains of 5,000+. Deliberately circumventing or destroying rights-holders' technical protections may also constitute the copyright crime — up to 3 years, serious 3–10. Official cases: Wang's group built wallhack/aimbot cheats reading and modifying game memory, selling 80,000-odd yuan in 3 months for 30,000-odd profit — 1 year suspended 1, fine 5,000. Xiang sold the "TZ" cheat series for 200,000-odd yuan — 3 years suspended 3, fine 20,000. Liu's group obtained a game server program, tweaked parameters, ran a private server collecting 20-million-odd yuan in top-ups — 4 years down to 2 years 6 months, fines 10 million down to 1.3 million. Not just games: a Shanghai company's ROM added dozens of WeChat functions — auto-forwarding, liking, mass-messaging — selling 2,381 "marketing phones"; in 2019 Xuhui court fined the company 500,000 yuan for copyright infringement, and the executive drew 1 year 6 months suspended 1 year 6 months (national)
Note
Published cheat cases all involve memory read/write and anti-cheat bypass. "Screenshot-only, key-simulation" assists have no published precedent — but item 3's ticket case shows request-only, no-memory work still charges as illegal data acquisition. Whether and under which count is the investigators' call on the vendor's materials, not the author's. Twenty person-times is a very small number.

No writing or selling ticket-grabbing, flash-sale, brushing, or coupon-farming scripts — even "just automated button-clicking"

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Scripts that touch no memory and break nothing — merely faster than humans — still convict: 5,000 yuan earned or 10,000 yuan of loss suffices. One man used bought 12306 accounts to grab 200-odd tickets for 20,000-odd yuan — 1 year 6 months suspended, fine 5,000. A shop selling ticket-grabbing software paid 20,000 yuan in unfair-competition damages.

Cost
Free, no time.
Benefit
Intruding into computer systems or acquiring data by other technical means, serious: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; especially serious, 3–7. "Serious": gains of 5,000+, or losses of 10,000+. Official cases: one man used cheats to batch-import bought 12306 accounts and flood purchase requests multithreaded, grabbing 200-odd tickets for 20,000-odd yuan — illegal acquisition of computer-system data, 1 year 6 months suspended 1 year 6 months, fine 5,000. Zheng sold ticket-grabbing software for a ticketing app in an online shop — unfair competition, 20,000 yuan damages (national)
Note
The ticket script touched no memory and broke nothing — "just faster" — yet charged under Article 285. Paid grabbing and script selling both count as profit. Single personal use: no official case found.

Crawlers: public, login-free pages only — no anti-crawl bypassing, no personal information, no selling what you scrape

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Login-, token-, or signature-gated data counts as bypassing protection: up to 3 years, serious 3–7. Personal information is worse: 50 records of location, communications, credit, or assets is already serious; lodging, health, and transaction records at 500; other categories at 5,000; or 5,000 yuan earned.

Cost
Free. A crawler is a program that walks pages and extracts data. Check the robots file (the site's root-level note of what may not be scraped) and API terms first. Anything needing login, tokens (temporary access credentials), or signature-breaking: don't. The hard part: the data is right there technically — restraint is all on you.
Benefit
Bypassing protections for system data matches item 3's sentencing: up to 3 years, or 3–7. Illegally acquiring, selling, or providing citizens' personal information reaches "serious" at any of: 50+ records of whereabouts, communication content, credit, or property; 500+ of lodging, communication logs, health, or transactions; 5,000+ of other personal information; or 5,000+ yuan gains. Serious: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; especially serious, 3–7. Official cases: developer Li disguised phone-album harvesting as a "looks-rating" app, taking 1,751 face photos and reselling "social-work database" records — 3 years suspended 3. A social-work database pools leaked personal information from everywhere. A network company crawled a food-delivery platform's store and order data, causing 40,000-odd yuan of loss — prosecuted for illegal data acquisition (national)
Note
The 2017 interpretation counts "providing lawfully collected information to others without consent" as "providing" — exporting the user table to a partner company falls inside. Five thousand records is a small table.

No dev contracts for gambling, fraud, or porn apps; no building payment channels or unblocking accounts for "clients"

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

High-quote, vague-requirement jobs make you an accomplice of the gambling ring: casino-operation charges, up to 5 years, serious 5–10 — heavier than the 3-year cap for mere helping. One e-sports betting app's 28 coders drew 1 to 3 years 6 months. A QQ-unblocker for fraud rings drew 1 year 6 months plus a 20,000-yuan fine.

Cost
Free. The price: walking away from high-priced, vaguely-specified outsourcing. The hard part: the pay often towers over normal contracts.
Benefit
Knowingly providing technical support or payment settlement for cybercrime, serious: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; simultaneously constituting other crimes, the heavier count governs. Running casinos: up to 5 years plus fines; serious, 5–10. Official cases: the Zhangsheng group developed gambling games for "turnkey export," collecting site-building and reporting fees — nearly 7 billion yuan involved; Zhangsheng drew 9 years 9 months plus a 50-million-yuan fine, and outsourced-development head Wang Qiang and 78 others drew 6 months to 9 years 9 months. Chen Dong's team built and ran an e-sports betting app, coders in Hainan — 28 people drew 3 years 6 months to 1 year for casino operation plus fines. Zhang ran a studio unblocking fraud-ring QQ accounts — 1 year 6 months, fine 20,000 (national)
Note
"Knowing" doesn't require them to say it aloud: far-above-market quotes, recharge-withdraw-odds functionality, and purpose-evasive clients all feed the inference. Gambling-app developers charge as casino-operation accomplices — not the 3-year-capped aiding count. ("Aiding" is short for the aiding-cybercrime offense.)

On leaving, hand over accounts and access — no database deletion, backdoors, or password-locking the system, even if the company owes you

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Company-issued credentials don't stay usable after departure — logging in counts as illegal control, up to 3 years. Deleting data that stops the system: up to 5 years; especially grave consequences, 5+. One dismissed senior engineer used his old admin account to delete data and logs — 120,000-odd yuan of loss, 3 years suspended 5, fine 30,000.

Cost
Free. Owed wages go through labor arbitration (Section 7), not your own hands. The hard part: not touching the system in anger.
Benefit
Illegally controlling computer systems, serious: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; especially serious, 3–7. Deleting or altering functions or data causing system failure, grave consequences: up to 5 years; especially grave, 5+. Official cases: IT senior engineer Lü, dismissed, logged into the company's shared server with his old admin account, changed the password, deleted data and logs — 120,000-odd yuan loss; 3 years suspended 5, fine 30,000. Note
Company-issued credentials don't survive departure: logging in with the old account is already "illegal control." Loss computes from data-recovery costs — a few thousand yuan files the case.

On leaving, no source code, client lists, or technical docs — no personal cloud drives, no reuse at the next employer

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Code you wrote yourself belongs to the company, and client lists are trade secrets — taking them is taking company property. One leaver carried security-scanner source to a new employer: 5 years plus a 500,000-yuan fine, and the new company fined 4 million. Another exploited a vulnerability to download 33,000-odd design files — 1 year 10 months. The company can sue you separately.

Cost
Free. Wipe company materials from personal machines and drives before leaving. The hard part: some files you wrote line by line.
Benefit
Breaching confidentiality duties by disclosing or using trade secrets, serious: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; especially serious, 3–10 plus fines. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law adds: acquiring secrets by "electronic intrusion" (technical means into systems), and instigating or helping others breach confidentiality. Official cases: Sun and departing colleagues carried security-scanner source and core algorithms into the new employer's products — Sun 5 years plus a 500,000-yuan fine, the new company 4 million. Tian exploited a system flaw to download 33,000-odd design files — 1 year 10 months plus 100,000. Engineer Yang stored app-module source on personal computer and cloud, then built a competing app — prosecuted for trade-secret infringement (national)
Note
"Self-written code" belongs to the company too — item 13. Taking it is taking company property; client lists are operating information and trade secrets likewise. Beyond prison, civil claims follow.

Never run your programs on others' computers, servers, or cameras; no mining on company machines

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Controlling others' computers, servers, or cameras without permission reaches 20 machines = up to 3 years; especially serious, 3–7. Sub-criminal: up to 5 days plus 50,000–500,000 yuan. The criminally punished are barred for life from key network-security and network-operations posts.

Cost
Free, no time.
Benefit
Illegally controlling computer systems, serious: up to 3 years plus or instead of fines; especially serious, 3–7. Twenty-plus systems controlled counts as serious. Sub-criminal: confiscation, up to 5 days plus 50,000–500,000; heavier, 5–15 days plus 100,000–1 million. Those administratively punished are barred 5 years; the criminally punished, for life, from key network-security and network-operations posts. Official cases: Li bought camera IPs and controlled 105 cameras to peep — 3 years suspended 5, fine 20,000. Wu's group implanted trojans into phone mainboards, controlling 3.3-million-odd phones to harvest verification codes — 2 to 4 years 6 months (national)

Mining on company servers lacks SPP/SPC precedent — this entry runs on the unpermitted-control statute. The lifetime key-post bar rides alongside fines and prison and, for technical people, outweighs the fine.

9

No testing others' systems without written authorization — "good intent" and "reported it afterward" are not defenses

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Whether it convicts turns on authorization, not intent. 500 sets of ordinary credentials, or 5,000 yuan earned or 10,000 yuan loss, reaches up to 3 years. Exporting one user table to prove a vulnerability often clears 500 sets in a single go. Credentials in hand, use beyond scope still counts as intrusion.

Cost
Free. Before joining an SRC (a vendor's own security-response center receiving outside reports) or crowd-testing, obtain written scope, target lists, and time windows. On confirming a vulnerability, stop. The hard part: giving up "just trying one thing."
Benefit
Ordinary company and personal systems sit outside state-affairs, defense, and cutting-edge-science systems. Intruding into them or acquiring stored, processed, or transmitted data by technical means, serious: up to 3 years or custody plus or instead of fines; especially serious, 3–7 plus fines. "Serious": 10+ sets of payment, securities, or futures authentication credentials; 500+ sets of other credentials; 20+ systems controlled; 5,000+ yuan gains or 10,000+ yuan loss. Five times those numbers reaches "especially serious." Official case: Guiding Case 36 established that "logging into a computer system with credentials beyond the authorized scope constitutes intrusion." The three defendants used work-held credentials and tokens to log in remotely, download out-of-scope data, and sell it — 37,000 yuan gains; sentences of 4 years, 3 years 9 months, and 4 years, each fined 40,000 (national)
Note
Guiding Case 36 was a data-selling case, cited only for "beyond-scope login is intrusion" — not a claim that well-meaning testing draws equal sentences. Intent and after-the-fact reporting don't erase the offense; they may affect severity and prosecution. Vendor thanks and later reporting don't contradict — thanks aren't authorization. In 2016, a white hat submitted a Jiayuan vulnerability to a third-party platform; Jiayuan reported to police and he was seized — Jiayuan told reporters the report concerned data taken, its source unknown at the time. Media report only; no judgment or official notice, no official outcome. No verbatim-verifiable good-faith-testing case exists on the two supremes' sites, so this entry grades on statutes and thresholds. Do it through vendors' public SRCs or written engagements with scope, targets, and windows; prove existence with minimal evidence, no bulk extraction. The sub-criminal band still draws administrative punishment and employment bars per item 8. Handling found vulnerabilities: item 10.

10

Report vulnerabilities per the rules — no pre-patch detail disclosure, no exploit tools, no handing to foreign parties

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Individuals fall under the Network Product Security Vulnerability Regulations too. Before the vendor ships a fix, you may not publish the vulnerability or details of live systems' flaws, may not release exploit programs or tools, and when publishing must state the fix. Undisclosed vulnerabilities may not go to offshore organizations or individuals beyond the vendor.

Cost
Free. Report to the product provider or the official platform. Until the vendor patches: no details, no proof-of-concept code.
Benefit
The regulations govern three classes: domestic network-product providers, network operators, and organizations or individuals discovering, collecting, or publishing vulnerabilities. No one may use vulnerabilities to harm network security or illegally collect, sell, or publish vulnerability information. Public release obeys five rules: not before the provider ships remedies; no details of vulnerabilities in operators' live networks, systems, and devices; no exaggeration, hype, or fraud; no release of exploitation tools; and simultaneous publication of fixes or defenses. Undisclosed vulnerabilities may not be provided to offshore organizations or individuals other than the provider. The regulations encourage reporting to four official platforms: MIIT's cybersecurity threat and vulnerability sharing platform; the National Network and Information Security Notification Center's platform; CNCERT's platform; and the China Information Technology Security Evaluation Center's database. Violations are handled by MIIT and MPS; Network Security Law cases follow that law. Publishing system vulnerabilities must follow national rules — violators face correction orders and warnings plus 10,000–100,000 yuan; refusal or severity, 100,000–1 million, plus possible business suspension, rectification, site or app closure, and license revocation; directly responsible managers, 10,000–100,000 (national)
Note
The regulations name individuals — "just an amateur" is no exception. Submitting domestic-system bugs to offshore bounty platforms lands squarely on "undisclosed vulnerabilities shall not be provided offshore." Authorization to test (item 9) and handling of found vulnerabilities are separate questions: a lawfully found vulnerability can still be punished for how it's published, and an unauthorized test is wrong at both ends. The most-used channels: MIIT's platform and CNCERT. The regulations don't address "vendor notified but won't fix" — in practice, document the negotiation and file with the official platforms in parallel.

No selling circumvention tools or VPN accounts, no building such nodes for others

Grade BValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Self-built lines abroad, or international channels outside the state public network, draw police-ordered disconnection, warnings, fines up to 15,000 yuan plus confiscation. Making a business of it can charge as illegal business operation — serious, up to 5 years. This entry covers selling and node-building; personal use caps at warning plus fine.

Cost
Free, no time.
Benefit
Direct international networking must use the state public telecom network's international gateways. No unit or individual may establish or use other channels — neither building your own line abroad nor using someone else's. Violations: police-ordered disconnection and warning, plus up to 15,000 yuan and confiscation. Running it as a business can be handled as illegal business operation: serious, up to 5 years plus or instead of fines of 1–5× gains; especially serious, 5+ (national)
Note
At writing, no published circumvention precedent was found on the two supremes' sites, and local handling varies — hence B. Personal use tops out at the interim regulation's warning-plus-fine.

Signed a non-compete? If the company stops paying monthly, demand in writing; 3 months unpaid means you may rescind; roles never touching trade secrets may seek invalidation

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Non-compete means no working for competitors for up to 2 years post-departure, with monthly compensation. Unspecified amounts run at 30% of the prior 12 months' average wage, floored at local minimum. Three months unpaid for company reasons lets you seek rescission. From 2025, roles never exposed to trade secrets may seek invalidation.

Cost
Free. Keep the agreement's original and evidence of non-payment at departure.
Benefit
Non-competes bind only senior management, senior technical personnel, and others with confidentiality duties, for at most 2 years, with mandatory monthly compensation. Unspecified: 30% of the trailing 12-month average wage, not below local minimum. Three months unpaid for company reasons lets the worker rescind. Company-initiated rescission costs an extra 3 months. From 2025, workers whose roles never involved trade secrets may seek invalidation; scopes exceeding what they actually knew are void in excess. Official case: a pharmaceutical company sued its CTO for 7.1 million yuan in penalties; the court found the new employer's product non-substitutive and the scope limited to what he actually knew — claim dismissed entirely (national)
Note
In reverse: a valid agreement, paid monthly, breached by working for a competitor means paying the stipulated penalty — and possibly serving out the remaining term afterward. In-employment non-competes bind without extra pay.
Sources (4 references)
全国人大常委会 (2012). 劳动合同法（2012 年修正，第二十三、二十四条）. https://yjglj.fushun.gov.cn/008/20260622/d846d3c2-df3d-4c4c…（抚顺市应急管理局转载）；最高人民法院 (2020). 关于审理劳动争议案件适用法律问题的解释（一）（第三十六至四十条）. https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/282121.html；最高人民法院 (2025). 关于审理劳动争议案件适用法律问题的解释（二）（法释〔2025〕12 号，第十三至十五条）. https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/472691.html；最高人民法院 (2025). 劳动争议典型案例（案例四）. https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/472681.html
13

Code written on work time with company resources belongs to the company; side projects on your own time and devices, no company code mixed in

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Software built mainly on company equipment, intranet, or business data, with the company answerable, belongs to the company — you keep the authorship right, contract or no. Off-hours code that used the company laptop or data may still count as the company's. Inventions made with company resources patent to the company too.

Cost
Free. Read your contract's IP clauses at onboarding. The hard part: side projects and work often share one machine — separate them.
Benefit
Works created to fulfill work tasks are works-for-hire. Ordinarily copyright stays with the author, the unit enjoys priority use within business scope for 2 years. But two classes differ: works mainly using the unit's material-technical conditions with the unit responsible — engineering designs, software — and works contractually assigned to the unit; in both, authors keep only the attribution right. "Material-technical conditions" means company equipment, intranet, business data. Inventions from the unit's tasks or mainly its resources are service inventions — patent application rights and granted patents belong to the unit (national)
Note
Software is written directly into the "copyright to the unit" class — programmers almost never land in the "author keeps copyright, unit gets 2-year priority" band. "Off-hours" code that touched company machines, intranet, or data may still count as mainly unit-resourced. Clean side projects: your own machine, no company repos, no business overlap.
Sources (2 references)
全国人大常委会 (2020). 著作权法（2020 年修正，第十八条）. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796…；全国人大常委会 (2020). 专利法（2020 年修正，第六条）. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308800…
14

Using GPL-family open source in products: comply with the license or swap libraries — don't bet on "nobody enforces"

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Copyright infringement pays the other side's loss or your gain; intentional and serious, 1–5×. One company hired a rival's ex-employees and shipped substantially similar software, arguing the rival used GPLv2 and should have opened its source anyway. The Supreme Court held the rival's own GPL compliance irrelevant to its copyright — injunction plus 500,000 yuan.

Cost
Free. Read the license (the author's stated terms) before adopting code. The GPL family requires your product's source released too, clashing with closed-source sales — clash means replace. The hard part: dropping a comfortable library.
Benefit
Infringement damages run on the right-holder's actual loss or the infringer's gain; both unclear, by reference to a normal license price. Intentional and serious: 1–5×. Public-interest harm adds confiscation and fines. Official case: (2021) SPC IP-Final-51 — the defendant hired the plaintiff's ex-employees and built substantially similar gateway software, arguing the plaintiff's GPLv2 base required openness; the SPC held "whether the developer itself violated GPLv2 and whether it holds software copyright are two independent questions," granting the injunction and 500,000 yuan (national)
Note
The case says "they used GPL" is no excuse for copying them. Conversely, GPL authors suing closed-source commercial users already have effective judgments domestically — the originals weren't found on the SPC site, uncited. Grade B: license compliance rides on contract and general copyright law, with no dedicated statute.
Sources (2 references)
全国人大常委会 (2020). 著作权法（2020 年修正，第五十三、五十四条）. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796…；最高人民法院知识产权法庭 (2022). 涉「开源软件」著作权侵权案（（2021）最高法知民终 51 号）. https://ipc.court.gov.cn/zh-cn/news/view-3042.html
15

Apps collect only business-necessary personal information; under-14s need guardian consent; write the privacy policy clearly

Grade BValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Collect only what's necessary; under-14s need guardian consent. Violations draw correction orders and possible app suspension; refusal, up to 1 million yuan with responsible persons fined 10,000–100,000; severe cases, up to 50 million or 5% of last year's revenue, responsible persons 100,000–1 million — and coders and PMs can be the responsible persons.

Cost
Free. Before launch, reconcile the permission list with the privacy policy; drop what you can. The hard part: product's appetite for "maybe useful later" data.
Benefit
Processing personal information requires clear, reasonable purpose, direct relevance, and minimal impact. Consent or statutory basis required; under-14s need parents' or guardians' consent. Violations: regulators order correction, warning, confiscation, and app suspension or termination. Refusal: up to 1 million yuan, responsible persons 10,000–100,000. Severe: up to 50 million or 5% of prior-year revenue; responsible persons 100,000–1 million, possibly barred from director, supervisor, and senior-management posts. Selling or providing personal information criminally: item 4 (national)
Note
"Directly responsible persons" in practice lands on coders and PMs. MIIT periodically delists violating apps; specific bulletins unverified here, uncited.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大常委会 (2021). 个人信息保护法（第六、十三、三十一、六十六条）. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088…
16

Before launching a site or app: ICP filing first, and keep 6+ months of logs per multi-level protection

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Filing costs nothing, takes weeks via the cloud vendor; domestic servers without filing get shut down. Charged for "free" filing: 100,000–1 million yuan fines. Logs must run 6+ months; refusal or harm, 10,000–100,000 yuan.

Cost
Filing is free via cloud vendors, weeks. Multi-level protection ("dengbao" — the state's tiered security-management regime graded by system importance) testing is fee-by-level; small sites usually skip testing.
Benefit
Commercial internet information services run on licenses; non-commercial, on filing. Neither without. Unfiled: telecom regulators order correction, then closure. Unlicensed operation: confiscation plus 3–5× gains, or 100,000–1 million yuan. Missing filing number on the homepage: 5,000–50,000. Operators must, under dengbao, maintain security-management systems, defend attacks, retain network logs no less than 6 months, and classify, back up, and encrypt data. Non-compliance: correction and warning; refusal or consequence, 10,000–100,000 yuan, managers 5,000–50,000 (national)
Note
Domestic servers without filing don't resolve at all. How to file, unposted-number fines, and checking vendor credentials: Section 26, item 4. Two common traps: filing as personal non-commercial while actually charging; and un-updated filings after domain or entity changes. Six-month logs are duty and self-defense both — proving it wasn't you.
Sources (2 references)
国务院 (2011). 互联网信息服务管理办法（2011 年修订，第四、十九、二十二条）. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1860864.htm；全国人大常委会 (2025). 网络安全法（2025 年修正，2026 年 1 月 1 日施行，第二十三、六十一条；2016 年文本为第二十一、五十九条）. https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm
17

Before offering generative AI to the public: security assessment and algorithm filing per the rules, and label generated content

Grade BValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Generative-AI services with public-opinion or mobilization capacity need pre-launch security assessment, algorithm filing, and change/cancellation filings. Generated images and videos need labels. Private, non-public tools are exempt. Violations punish under the Network Security Law and its siblings.

Cost
Free but time-consuming through the cyberspace administration. Personal tools not opened to the public trigger none of this.
Benefit
Providing generative AI with public-opinion or social-mobilization attributes requires state-prescribed security assessment, algorithm filing under the recommendation-management rules, and subsequent change and cancellation procedures. "Public-opinion or mobilization capacity" means shaping public views or organizing people. Providers must label generated images and videos. The measures took effect 2023-08-15 (national)
Note
The measures set no fines themselves; punishment routes back through the network, data, and personal-information laws — hence B. Civil cases of AI-generated content infringing copyright or likeness weren't verified on the SPC site, uncited. Low-price resellers of offshore model APIs: item 19.
Sources (1 references)
国家互联网信息办公室等七部门 (2023). 生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法（第十二、十七条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891752…
18

No tools that auto-skip or block other apps' ads — free and offline can still be unfair competition

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Software skipping or blocking other apps' ads draws unfair-competition suits. Unpaid can still count — "business operators" in the law include individuals providing services. A browser default-blocking Mango TV's pre-roll ads paid 800,000 yuan. An app skipping Mango TV's splash ads paid 80,000 in losses.

Cost
Free. The price: walking away from a popular little tool. The hard part: feeling you earned nothing, merely clicking "skip" on users' behalf.
Benefit
The law bars operators from using technical means to obstruct or disrupt other operators' lawfully provided network products or services. "Operators" includes natural persons supplying goods or services. Damages run on the other side's actual loss or your gain, plus their enforcement costs. Market regulators can add 100,000–1 million yuan; serious, 1–5 million. Official cases: 720 Browser's built-in default blocking of Mango TV's pre-roll and pause ads — first instance dismissed; Guangzhou IP court reversed into unfair competition, 800,000 yuan in losses and costs; the SPC listed it as a 2021 typical case. The "Lan Jingling" app let users skip Mango TV's splash ads directly — first instance: cease, 80,000 losses plus 10,000 costs; April 2024 Beijing IP court upheld, finding actual blocking of the splash ad, not merely clicking "skip" for users (national)
Note
Both judgments cite pre-amendment numbering; the 2025 revision moved this to Article 13 and added data, algorithms, and platform rules. The appeal court judged blocking — users clicking "skip" themselves unaffected. In August 2023, the free Android skip-tool "Li Tiaotiao" received Tencent's cease-and-desist alleging ad-blocking and demanding delisting within 48 hours; the developer called it non-profit, reportedly taking only sporadic tips, yet announced indefinite suspension, with siblings following — media report only, no suit or judgment. Individual developers receiving such letters: stop, or fund your own defense — 6+ months first instance, attorney fees usually yours. Self-written, self-use scripts: no pursued case found. Ticket-grabbing software: item 3. Beneficiary: you.
