19

CO alarm sounding, or the whole household headachy and nauseous at once: get outside first, then phone

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Alarm sounding, or everyone headachy, nauseous, dizzy together: move everyone outdoors, then call. Don't stay in hunting causes or return to shut valves. Symptoms mimic a cold; "better once outside" is the strongest tell. China reported 11,523 carbon-monoxide deaths in 2018, winter-heaviest, mostly at home.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
China CDC's death-surveillance system reported 11,523 CO-poisoning deaths in 2018: January heaviest (2,845), February (2,321), December (2,010); across those three winter months, 66%–73% died at home. These are reported counts, not population estimates. The US: 400-plus yearly deaths from non-fire unintentional CO poisoning, 100,000-plus emergency visits, 14,000-plus hospitalizations
Note
Symptoms mimic colds and drunkenness. A whole household unwell together, better outside — the strongest tell. Don't stay in hunting causes or go back for valves; people out first, calls after. Alarm placement: Section 1, item 3.

20

Swallowed cleaners, pesticides, medication: don't induce vomiting; bring the bottle, seek care at once; eyes and skin get 15+ minutes of running water

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Swallowed: no vomiting — corrosives re-burn the esophagus on the way up. Drink some milk or egg white, bring the bottle and label, go immediately. Skin or eyes: copious running water at least 15 minutes; eyes flushed with lids held open, never rubbed. Disinfectant mixed with toilet cleaner releases chlorine gas.

Cost
Free. Store cleaners, disinfectants, pesticides, and medicines high or locked, never decanted into drink bottles.
Benefit
China CDC's occupational-health and poisoning institute gives four routes. Ingestion: immediately drink suitable milk or egg white, "remember: do not induce vomiting"; seek care promptly with the packaging or label "so physicians can quickly identify components and plan treatment." Inhalation: move to ventilated air, loosen the collar; severe cough, breathlessness, or dyspnea means immediate care. Skin: flush the contact site with copious water at least 15 minutes, keeping rinse-off from splashing eyes or intact skin. Eyes: flush with copious water or saline at least 15 minutes, lids held open so the flow bathes the eyeball and lid lining — "never rub" — then straight to ophthalmology. High-risk products by pH: below 3 — toilet cleaners, descalers, floor cleaners, stainless polishers, some strong drain openers with dilute sulfuric acid; above 11 — drain openers, heavy-duty kitchen degreasers, dishwasher powders, oxygen bleaches, scouring powders. And the instant-disaster combination: disinfectant with hydrochloric-acid toilet cleaner releases chlorine gas, irritating airways with violent cough and breathlessness, potentially lethal
Note
Grade B: official guidance covers handling and recognition without outcome numbers. The no-vomiting logic: corrosives re-burn the esophagus (the throat-to-stomach tube) on the way up. Unsure what was swallowed: bring bottle, label, and vomitus together. Prevention beats rescue: separate storage away from food and drink, caps tightened, empties discarded, never into water bottles; rubber gloves and goggles in use, ventilation, no mixing types. CO: item 19; burns: item 14. Acid and alkali splashes — clothing and durations: item 21.

21

Acid, alkali, or other chemicals on the body: strip contaminated clothing immediately, flood with running water; eyes flushed with lids open, full duration before leaving

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Three steps. Strip contaminated clothing, shoes, and socks at once — pooled fabric burns worst. Flood with copious running water: skin and eyes 15 minutes minimum, Hunan's emergency authority giving 20–30 — take the longer. Eyes: lids held open, full contact, then straight to ophthalmology. Cool water, never hot.

Cost
Free. Locate eyewash stations and showers on day one of the job — not after the accident.
Benefit
Three field steps. Strip contaminated garments: poisons keep absorbing through skin, and pooled fabric burns deepest. Copious running water: China CDC's floor is "at least 15 minutes" for skin and eyes alike; Hunan's emergency authority gives 20–30 minutes for wounds, "longer for strong chemicals" — take the longer. Eyes: "hold the lids open ensuring the flow fully contacts the eyeball and lid lining," "never rub," then immediate ophthalmology. Room-temperature or tepid water; hot water forbidden. No ointments, mercurochrome, or anything on fresh wounds, and no dirty wraps — they obscure depth assessment. Legally, chemical skin and eye burns both sit in the statutory occupational-disease catalog, routing work cases through occupational disease and work injury; acute hazard incidents obligate the employer to "organize treatment, health checks, and medical observation, bearing the costs" (national)
Note
Grade B: durations split between official sources — 15 minutes versus 20–30 — no unified national figure. Bring the chemical's name, packaging, or safety data sheet (SDS) to hospital; physicians plan by it. Never grab another acid or alkali to "neutralize" — mixing releases heat, and dosing is uncontrolled. Hunan's "neutralizing solution" means employer-stocked specialty rinses, not improvised counter-agents. Dry powders — lime, cement — brush off before flushing. (Some emergency pages extend this to wiping concentrated sulfuric acid first; sources disagree, so this book doesn't.) Household cleaners and ingestion: item 20. Pre-job protection and exams: Section 19, items 9–10.

22

Heat: dizziness, nausea, no sweat, or confusion — move to shade, strip, douse; the unconscious get no water, call 120

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Hot red skin, slurring, confusion — heatstroke. Dizziness to coma can take tens of minutes, with extreme fatality. Move to shade and airflow, strip clothes, cool with water and wet towels, call 120. The unconscious get not a sip — aspiration.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
The US National Weather Service: heat stroke is "a severe medical emergency" — body temperature above 103°F (39.4°C), confusion, slurring, hot red skin; call emergency, move somewhere cool, cool with water and wet cloths, "do not give liquids." Heat exhaustion — heavy sweat, weakness, cool moist skin, fast weak pulse — moves to cool, loosened clothing, sips of water; vomiting, worsening, or over an hour unrelieved means care. Yunnan's CDC: move to shade and ventilation, cool with cold wet towels, salted drinks if alert, emergency call if severe; severe heatstroke carries "extremely high fatality." China CDC: cool first, transport later — cool within the "golden half hour" after loss of consciousness; where conditions allow, cold-water immersion for young, healthy adults; elders and the chronically ill, skin-spraying with evaporative cooling. The Wilderness Medical Society's 2024 heat guidelines call cold-water immersion the most important treatment for severe heat illness, cooling fastest; without ice water, use the coolest available, or spray-and-fan at roughly half the immersion rate
Note
Don't wait to "shake it off" — dizziness to coma can take tens of minutes. No pouring water into the unconscious — aspiration. Ice-pack placement differs by source: China CDC says neck, armpits, and groin; the Wilderness Medical Society says research shows no cooling effect at those sites, recommending full-body packing when only ice packs exist, with cheeks, palms, and soles next. Both endorse cold-water immersion where possible.

23

Heat-exhausted and alert: small repeated drinks of cool weak-salty water or sports drink — no chugging, no alcohol, no high-sugar drinks

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Only the alert drink. Cool weak-salty water or sports drink, small and repeated, 500–1,000 ml per hour. No chugging — vomit aspirating is deadlier than the heat. No alcohol or high-sugar drinks; both lose you more fluid. Cool sponging and ice packs at neck, armpits, groin first; rehydration second. The confused or slurring get nothing by mouth.

Cost
Free. A sports drink runs a few yuan.
Benefit
China CDC's public heat-illness guide (2014): "drink at least 2–4 cups of cool water hourly (500–1000ml), not too warm, in small repeated amounts," "do not drink alcohol or heavily sugared beverages — they cause further fluid loss; also avoid very icy drinks," and for heatstroke explicitly "do not give the patient water." US NIOSH: heat exhaustion — "encourage frequent sips of cool water"; heat cramps — a carbohydrate-electrolyte sports drink every 15–20 minutes, "no salt tablets"
Note
Plain water alone after heavy sweating dilutes blood sodium — hence a little salt. Chugging invites vomiting, and vomit in the airway kills faster than heat. "No ice-cold drinks" comes from China CDC's 2014 guide on gastric-spasm grounds, without quantified evidence — don't misread it as "no cold anything." Item 22's cooling methods — cool sponging, cold-water immersion, ice packs at neck, armpits, groin — are exactly the officially recommended first-tier cooling, applied to the body, never poured into mouths. Cooling always precedes rehydration. The confused or slurring get nothing by mouth

24

Fire: crawl low, touch the door before opening, a hot door stays shut; stairs not elevators; once out, never go back

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Drop and crawl beneath the smoke toward the exit. Before any door, feel the handle and panel — hot, or smoke seeping through, means don't open it; take the second route. Open slowly; slam shut at thick smoke. Stairs, never elevators — power loss traps you inside. Out means out — no returning for things. Clothes on fire: stop, drop, and roll, hands shielding the face.

Cost
One or two standalone smoke alarms, tens of yuan. Glance at the corridor's two exits in advance.
Benefit
FEMA's escape text: "get low to the ground and crawl to the exit." Feel doors first — "if it is hot, or there is smoke coming through the cracks, don't open the door; use a second way out." Open slowly, closing at heavy smoke. Clothes afire: "stop, drop, and roll," hands over the face. Trapped: shut the door, block gaps and vents with cloth or tape, phone in your location. The emergency ministry's guidance concurs: no elevators, run downstairs when fire is small, cover nose and mouth with a wet towel or mask, crawl or stoop low
Note
No elevators — power loss traps. No returning for property. No running upstairs unless the roof door is confirmed open. No jumping. Wet towels fold to 8 layers without over-soaking — a soaked towel suffocates. Against dense toxic smoke, towels fail too.

Someone drowning: shout for help and call 110/120 first; reach with a pole, throw floats — never enter the water yourself

Grade CValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Drowning people instinctively push rescuers under; rescuers drown too. The order: shout → call 110/120 → extend a long pole or rope → throw rings, empty jugs, water bottles → once ashore without breathing, compress. No human chains into the water. About 300,000 drown yearly worldwide — the fourth-leading killer of 1-to-4-year-olds.

Cost
Free. The hard part: resisting the plunge.
Benefit
WHO: about 300,000 drowning deaths yearly, 92% in low- and middle-income countries; drowning ranks fourth for ages 1–4 and third for 5–14. WHO's recommended intervention is "safe rescue and resuscitation training" — learning the water-free rescue first. Order: shout → call → extend poles and ropes, throw rings, jugs, bottles → ashore and breathless, compress
Note
Grade C: no official text found for "never enter" beyond WHO's death figures and "safe rescue" direction. No hand-in-hand chains. Untrained people shouldn't tow — the drowning drag rescuers down. "Never enter" is self-interest too: a drowned rescuer helps nobody, whoever they jumped for. The likely rescue is your own child — prevention at Section 1, item 12. Ice holes: never walk onto the ice — Section 1, item 41.

Choking and unable to speak, over 1 year old: stand behind, alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts; on collapse, CPR

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

First ask "are you choking, can you speak?" Able to cough or vocalize: let them cough. Over 1 and unable to speak: stand behind, 5 back blows then 5 abdominal thrusts, alternating until the object comes out or they collapse. Collapsed: CPR while someone calls emergency. Pregnant or very obese: chest thrusts instead. Never blind-sweep the mouth.

Cost
Free. Watch the move once: fist above the navel, other hand wrapped, quick inward-and-upward thrusts.
Benefit
The US National Library of Medicine: first ask "are you choking, can you speak." "Do not interfere with someone who can cough forcefully or speak" — coughing itself usually expels. Unable to speak: "repeat 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is dislodged or the person loses consciousness." "If they lose consciousness, begin CPR" while others call. Pregnancy and obesity: chest thrusts
Note
Never blind-finger-sweep — it pushes objects deeper. Never slap someone still coughing. Choking clusters at the family table; the beneficiary is family. The domestic Red Cross teaches the same cycle for over-1s: 5 back blows plus 5 abdominal thrusts. Older online tutorials teaching thrusts alone are outdated. Under 1 year: chest compressions instead of abdominal — item 43.

27

Lost or broken down in gobi, desert, or trackless country: stay put or with the vehicle; report position first, then shade, warmth, water discipline — no wandering

Grade CValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: highTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Stay with the vehicle — the biggest shade available. Order: with signal, send position before calling → shade and warmth → water discipline, move only in the cool of night → no wandering → signal with mirrors, smoke, three fires. Before entering, leave route, destination, return date, vehicle, and plate with someone.

Cost
Before entering, tell someone your route, destination, return date, vehicle, and plate. 4 liters of water per person per day, minimum. Satellite communicators or Beidou short-message units run 1,000+ yuan, rentals a few hundred. The hard part: holding to "stay put."
Benefit
The National Park Service's Mojave page: "at least one gallon (about 3.8 L) of water per person per day; hikers and cyclists two gallons"; "tell someone your route, destination, return date, vehicle and plate"; "cell service is intermittent." Death Valley: "avoid hiking in the valley and at low elevations when it is hot," wilderness areas have "almost no cell service," satellite phones recommended. The desert-driving page: "in an emergency, staying with your vehicle is the single most important thing you can do" — uncommon, but people have died of heat or cold exposure walking back toward paved roads. Five priorities: (1) report safety and coordinates — position first, call second; (2) shade and warmth, the vehicle your biggest shelter; (3) water — still by day, move by cool night; (4) no wandering; (5) signals. Chongqing's emergency authority: three fires in a triangle is the international distress signal; nearby, shout "three short, three long, three short," repeating each minute; with sun, flash mirrors or tin lids. The culture-and-tourism ministry urges caution entering trackless regions, multi-vehicle convoys, and rented satellite phones
Note
Grade C: official advice, not research data. Water amounts, trip-filing, signal coverage, staying with the vehicle, distress signals — all official phrasing. The circulating "three shouts in sets" found no official source, replaced by the official three fires and three-short-three-long-three-short. No midday route-hunting. No drinking urine. No rationing yourself into dehydration.

Shivering, slurred speech, staggering — hypothermia: swap wet clothes, wrap up, warm the core first, hot sweet drinks — never alcohol

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Core temperature below 35°C is hypothermia: shivering, slurring, staggering, muddled thinking. Swap wet clothes, wrap in blanket or dry layers, warm the trunk first — never hands and feet first. Hot sweet drinks; no alcohol, which suppresses shivering. Stopped shivering isn't improvement — it's worsening. Unconscious: CPR.

Cost
A foil survival blanket runs a few yuan, plus a spare dry layer. Reading the signs is free.
Benefit
The US National Weather Service: below 95°F (35°C) is hypothermia — "if you feel cold and sluggish or confused, see a doctor immediately." Management: "seek medical attention, move the person indoors to warmth, rewarm from the body's center first," hot drinks. "Alcohol reduces shivering" — none. "Unconscious: CPR." Frostbite rewarms in warm water or body heat — "not hot water or radiative heat like fireplaces." The Wilderness Medical Society's 2019 hypothermia guidelines are the practice reference
Note
Never rub hands and feet. No hot baths. No rough dragging — deeply hypothermic hearts arrest on jostling. Never read "stopped shivering" as improvement — shivering cessation is deterioration. The WMS full text is paywalled; only the abstract verified this round.

Wilderness & Environmental Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wem.2019.10.002

Snakebite: sit still, remove rings and watches, reach antivenom care fast — no cutting, no sucking, no strangulating ties

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Sit still and immobilize the bitten limb. Remove rings and watches first — swelling follows. Reach an antivenom hospital fast; antivenom is the only agent reversing most envenoming. No incisions, no mouth suction, no ice, no tourniquets strangling the limb purple. No alcohol, no running. Photograph the snake from afar if possible — never catch it.

Cost
Free. Know in advance which nearby hospital stocks antivenom. The hard part: leaving the wound alone.
Benefit
WHO, three sentences: "immobilize the bitten body part completely and seek immediate medical attention"; "avoid tourniquets and cutting the wound"; "treat with appropriate antivenom for local species" — "quality antivenom is the most effective treatment to prevent or reverse most of the venom's effects." About 81,000–138,000 snakebite deaths yearly worldwide, with amputations and permanent disability roughly triple the deaths. China's 2024 snakebite guideline estimates 250,000–280,000 venomous bites yearly, mainly hitting those over 50. Hospitals across the Yangtze basin and 11 southern provinces admitted 40,817 snakebite patients 2017–2021, with 23 in-hospital deaths (0.06%)
Note
Photograph from a distance if possible; never catch. No alcohol, no running, no mouth suction, no ice, no purple-strangling ties. No national death statistics exist for China. The 11-province in-hospital mortality looks low, but one-in-ten patients self-discharged mid-treatment and left the statistics.

30

Earthquake: first read your building — code-compliant blocks shelter in place; collapsible old housing with the door steps away, exit

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

First, what building are you in? Post-2001 code-compliant towers needing stairs or lobbies to exit: shelter in place — protect head and neck under a sturdy table, grip a leg. Single-story, old brick, or unengineered self-builds with the door steps away: exit. Never in any case: jump, ride elevators, or descend stairs mid-shake.

Cost
Free. Glance in advance: steps to the door, the route, the sturdiest table.
Benefit
The China Earthquake Administration's film "Earthquake: shelter or run?" teaches "shelter nearby during the shake, evacuate quickly after," expressly limited to "buildings meeting seismic-fortification requirements" — such buildings "rarely collapse wholesale," and "falling components and decorations pose the greatest threat to life," while "blind unprotected running during the shake" invites being struck by ceilings and pendant fans. Shelter: "protect the head and neck with hands or soft objects" and "grip a table leg firmly"; without a table, "huddle against a load-bearing wall, avoiding outer walls, windows, and balconies." Outdoors: "evacuate immediately to open ground." The reverse case: the 1988 Armenian earthquake collapsed Soviet precast blocks wholesale; its case-control study found "leaving the building after the first shock was protective." Staying indoors ran 4.40 times the injury odds of exiting (OR 4.40, 95% CI 2.24–8.71); being inside a building, 12.20 times outdoors (3.62–63.79); floors above five, 3.65 times lower floors (2.12–6.33)
Note
Contested — two conclusions for two building classes. The CEA itself conditions sheltering on "buildings meeting seismic requirements" and asks for "local conditions and person." Armenia's blocks collapsed wholesale — sheltering nowhere, exiting winning. US FEMA, for its housing stock: "drop, cover, and hold on; don't run outside" — injuries there come from falling objects and falls while moving. Northridge adds: reaching for objects or bracing on "seemingly stable" things worsens injury. So don't ask "run or not" — ask "will this building collapse, and can you reach open ground in seconds." Post-2001 compliant towers needing stairs or lobbies: shelter. Single-story, old brick, unengineered: door steps away, exit. The Armenian study compared injured versus uninjured survivors, excluding the dead, and floor effects may be unadjusted — those able to run may live lower; discount the numbers. Never: jump, elevators, stairs mid-shake. Outdoors: clear of tall buildings, viaducts, poles, glass curtain walls, and billboards.

Bears, wild boars, dog packs: don't run — turn sideways and back away slowly

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Don't run — bears race horses uphill and down. Don't climb — black and brown bears both climb. Stand, keep talking in a low voice, and when the bear stills, back away sideways. Brown bear charging: play dead — face down, hands clasped behind the neck, legs apart. Black bear charging: never play dead — run for car or building, or fight with whatever's at hand. Dog scratches and bites: item 13's washing and shots.

Cost
Free. Carry a trekking pole in the hills, hike in company, make noise — let animals know you're coming. The hard part: standing still instead of running.
Benefit
The National Park Service on bears, six sentences: "don't run — bears can run as fast as a racehorse, uphill or down"; "stay calm — most bears want nothing to do with you"; "keep talking to the bear in low tones"; "when the bear stands still, back away sideways, keeping an eye on it without tripping"; "make yourself look as large as possible"; "don't climb — grizzlies and black bears both climb." Brown-bear attack: "play dead, lying face down with hands clasped behind your neck and legs apart." Black-bear attack: "do not play dead — escape to a car or building; if you can't, fight back with anything available." Dog bites: item 13
Note
Grade B covers bears only. Boars and dog packs' "no running, slow retreat, put barriers or height between" is practice — Grade C — with no national or local forestry authority text found this round. Never bait with food, never approach for photos, never bring dogs into boar country. China's bears are mostly black and brown — play-dead splits by species.

Thunderstorm outdoors: get into a hard-top vehicle or building; avoid ridgelines, lone trees, water, and metal

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Within a thunderstorm's reach, no outdoor spot is safe. Get into a hard-top vehicle or building — convertibles, motorcycles, tents, pavilions, under trees, and under overhangs don't count. Avoid open ground, ridge tops, isolated tall trees, water, and iron railings. Groups that can't move spread out. Thunder means withdraw; thirty minutes past the last rumble means safe.

Cost
Free. The price: your itinerary losing half an hour or more. The hard part: turning back while thunder still sounds distant.
Benefit
No safe place exists outdoors within a thunderstorm's reach. Thirty minutes past the last thunder restores safety
Note
Tents, pavilions, trees, and rock overhangs aren't shelter. Hard-top cars are; convertibles and motorcycles aren't. Withdraw at the first thunder, before the rain.

Altitude: climb by sleeping elevation, descend on worsening symptoms — never push through

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

What counts is where you sleep, not how high you passed by day. Sleeping above 2,450 m brings altitude-illness risk. Past 3,000 m: sleeping altitude climbs only 500 m per night, plus one acclimatization day per 1,000 m. Headache with nausea, staggering gait, altered awareness, or breathlessness at rest: descend. Descent outranks oxygen and pills.

Cost
One to two extra days acclimatizing. Prophylaxis is prescription — ask a doctor before departure. The hard part: leaving those days in a tight itinerary.
Benefit
Sleeping above 2,450 m carries altitude-illness risk. High-altitude cerebral and pulmonary edema (fluid in brain or lungs) kill without descent
Note
Count sleeping elevation, not daytime peaks. Headache with nausea, staggering, altered awareness, or breathless at rest all say descend. Descent outranks oxygen and medication — oxygen while ascending higher is wrong.

Tick attached: pull straight out with fine-tipped tweezers at the skin — no oil, no flame

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Grip the tick's head at the skin with fine tweezers and pull steadily outward. No oil, no flame, no twisting — agitation squeezes pathogen-laden fluids into the skin and snaps mouthparts off inside. Record the date. Fever, rash, or fatigue in the following weeks: tell the doctor about the bite unprompted.

Cost
A pair of fine-tipped tweezers.
Benefit
Oils, flames, and twisting agitate ticks into forcing infected fluids into the skin and leave embedded mouthparts behind. Ticks in China transmit severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome: 2024 logged 6,602 cases and 306 deaths, both records since discovery; 2010–2024 average fatality 4.79%, rising with age to 9.15% past 85
Note
Record the removal date. Fever, rash, or fatigue in the following weeks: volunteer the bite history — unasked and untold, it gets treated as a cold.

Wild water: always boil — one rolling minute suffices; no extra time for altitude

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Every waterborne pathogen dies within seconds at boiling temperature. The extra rolling minute is margin for misjudging the boil — not altitude time. No stove: filters or tablets, each missing some pathogens — boiling when possible. Clear-looking streams and snowmelt still carry parasites.

Cost
The weight of stove and fuel.
Benefit
All waterborne pathogens are inactivated within seconds at boiling temperature. "High altitude undercooks water" is a common misconception
Note
The same page notes true boiling isn't required — 60°C held for 30 minutes equals it, with boiling simply the visible endpoint needing no thermometer. Without fire: filters or chemical tablets, each with uncovered pathogens — boil when possible. Clear streams and snowmelt carry parasites; never judge by looks.

Strangers demanding property in remote country: hand it over, no fighting, note features, report after escaping

Grade CValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Hand it over, no fighting, no backtalk. For a few hundred yuan they risk robbery — from 3–10 years; armed, home-invasion, or injury-causing, 10+ to death. Once they take the money and turn away, chasing and striking is no longer defense. After escaping: note features, accent, plate, direction — call 110.

Cost
The cash on you. The hard part: holding your temper.
Benefit
Life outweighs money, and they wager a felony for hundreds. Criminal Law Article 263: robbery by violence, coercion, or other means — 3–10 years plus fines; armed, home-invading, or causing grave injury or death — 10+ to death. Article 20's lawful defense protects only "stopping unlawful infringement in progress" — once they take the money and turn away, pursuit isn't defense. After escape: features, accent, plate, direction, 110
Note
Grade C: "yield, don't fight" has no direct literature; statutes show only their risk and your boundary. Don't follow anyone to secluded spots "to get money." Don't surrender phone passwords. Don't get in their vehicle. Yielding applies only when cornered and threatened — report after escaping. Online leverage extortion is the reverse — not one yuan — Section 8, item 32. Forget carried batons, stun guns, and daggers: carrying them is itself punishable — Section 9, item 26.

37

Stumbling into a brawl: back off and leave — no pulling fighters apart, no spectating, no picking up weapons; reporting 110 happens from safe distance

Grade BValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The moment you lay hands, peacemaking becomes brawling. Group fighting draws up to 3 years; large numbers, public roads, or weapons, 3–10. Spectators catch stray blows. The move: back off and leave. Willing to report: call 110 from safe distance — location, how many, knives or clubs, anyone down.

Cost
Free. The hard part: resisting both the urge to pull someone back and the urge to watch. Reporting may cost a callback statement — half a day at most.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 292: group brawls — ringleaders and active participants, up to 3 years, custody, or control; repeat brawls, large scale with vile social impact, serious public-order chaos in public places or arteries, or weapons — 3–10 years. Group brawls causing grave injury or death charge as intentional injury or homicide. The punishments law adds: assault, 5–10 days plus 500–1,000 yuan; group brawls as picking quarrels, up to 15 days plus 2,000. The defense guidance, Article 5: unlawful infringement "includes not only infringement against oneself but against the state, the public interest, or others." Article 9: where one side strikes first with clearly excessive means, or continues despite the other's avoidance efforts, the counterstriker "should generally be recognized as acting in defense"
Note
Grade B: consequences have hard statutes, but "back off, don't intervene" has no official text — inferred from the provisions and mutual-combat doctrine. "I was peacemaking" is no amulet; determination reads hands and targets. Chasing the downed or fleeing isn't defense. Watching someone beaten one-sidedly: the law does allow you to stop it — defense protects others too — but bare-handed intervention mostly adds a casualty; shouting, distant video, and police serve better. "No hands, no spectating" costs you nothing. Calling 110 mostly benefits the person on the ground — this book's lowest beneficiary tier — spend the time or not, your call. Before deciding: testimony duty already exists (Criminal Procedure Law Article 62 — whoever knows the case must testify; not calling doesn't dissolve it); grave injury or death brings surveillance pulls that register bystanders anyway; reporting parties wishing anonymity "shall be kept secret" (Article 111); state location, numbers, weapons and hang up — no need to stay; contempt-level detention (Article 193) requires court summons plus refusal without cause — rare for passersby. Not reporting isn't illegal: Article 110's "right and duty" carries no penalty, and no statute punishes ordinary silence — walking away is lawful. Two red lines after leaving: harboring or falsifying proof (Article 310, up to 3 years; serious, 3–10) and perjury when called (Article 305, up to 3; serious, 3–7). Silence and truth are safe; fabrication is not. Your own conflicts: Section 8, item 10; stranger extortion: item 36; helping's costs: item 39.

Possible HIV exposure: get blocking drugs within 72 hours — the earlier the better

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: highTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Suspecting HIV transmission, 72 hours is the hard line — ideally medicating within 2. The course runs 28 days. Past 72 hours the road closes; don't sleep on the decision.

Cost
A 28-day course runs 1,000+ yuan, self-paid in most regions, plus a hospital trip that night. The hard part: admitting the possibility and leaving immediately.
Benefit
The Beijing government's AIDS-education page: post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) should "begin within 2 hours where possible, ideally within 24, and no later than 72," taken "continuously for 28 days." Beyond 72 hours, initiation is no longer recommended — a hard deadline
Note
Where to get it: the CDC-designated HIV institutions, usually infectious-disease (STD/AIDS) clinics; many cities run 24-hour clinics — Chongqing publicly lists 29 across 26 districts, 14 around-the-clock. Call the local CDC for which hospital stocks it; don't burn hours in general emergency. Qualifying exposures include unprotected sex, condom failure, needlesticks, and blood on mucosa — physicians judge. The full 28 days matter; missed doses degrade protection. Follow-up at 4–6 weeks and 3 months per orders. PEP is remedial — daily prevention and testing: Section 1, items 30–31.

Injured or out-of-pocket from helping: pursue the perpetrator and insurance first, then file for acting-bravely recognition

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Helping doesn't mean eating the loss. The injured rescuer gets treated first, billed later; medical costs bill the perpetrator, with basic insurance covering the absconded or insolvent; with no perpetrator, the person you saved owes appropriate compensation. File for recognition in parallel — the injured receive work-injury benefits.

Cost
Free. Filing means materials, waits, and trips — weeks to months.
Benefit
Civil Code Article 183: "those harmed protecting others' civil rights — the infringer bears civil liability, and the beneficiary may give appropriate compensation; with no infringer, or one who absconds or cannot pay, when the victim requests compensation, the beneficiary shall give appropriate compensation." The 2012 state-council opinion on protecting such persons: green channels under "treat first, bill later"; emergency medical costs "borne by the perpetrator or responsible party; absent, absconded, or insolvent — resolved through the basic medical-security system per regulations"; deaths meeting martyr criteria "evaluated as martyrs per law," with work-injury equivalence bringing the one-time death benefit plus a special survivor subsidy of 40 months' wages; the disabled receiving work-injury benefits where qualified, otherwise civil-affairs grading and benefits; employment "prioritized into assistance with key support" and public-welfare posts; housing "prioritized into the guarantee system, preferential allocation of guaranteed housing or rental subsidies"
Note
Grade B: national documents fix entitlements, but award amounts and recognition procedures run on provincial regulations — numbers vary, unverified province by province this round. File with the local police or the acting-bravely work organ (foundation). Recognition rides evidence: police receipts, scene footage, witnesses' names and numbers, hospital records — captured on the spot. Litigation: acting-bravely civil claims sit inside free legal aid. National death-benefit standards and disability grading: Section 19, items 14–15. Legal aid: Section 7, item 3.

Knife, rebar, or glass embedded in the body: press around the object to stop bleeding — never pull it out

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Pulling out may trigger massive hemorrhage and blinds the surgeon's depth assessment. Instead: call 120, press around the object with hands or dressings, and stabilize it against movement. Abdominal wounds with exposed organs: never reinsert — cover with a clean moist dressing. Bubbling chest wounds: don't seal with plastic — sealing may collapse the lung.

Cost
Free. The hard part: suppressing the pull-it-out instinct and staying with the person until the ambulance.
Benefit
The IFRC's 2025 international first-aid guidelines: "first aiders should apply pressure around the embedded object (such as a knife), stabilizing it, and should not remove it"; "do not remove any embedded object from abdominal or chest wounds — removal can cause massive bleeding and makes it harder for medical professionals to assess the severity"; "objects embedded in the body should be stabilized; if the object moves with the pulse, let it, securing it loosely"; "first aiders should not push protruding organs back into the body." Open chest wounds not actively gushing "may be left uncovered without a dressing, as sealing may cause air to accumulate in the chest cavity, partially or completely collapsing the lung (pneumothorax)." All penetrating chest and abdominal wounds mean immediate emergency call
Note
Grade B: guideline consensus without randomized trials — no one splits patients into pull and don't-pull arms. The sole exception: an object obstructing the airway with the person unable to breathe. At hospital, go straight to triage and say "penetrating injury" — immediate-resuscitation tier, no registration queue (Section 24, item 7). Call 120: the ambulance pre-notifies the hospital. Hemorrhage control and tourniquets: item 12.
Sources (1 references)
International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025，第 256–257、267–268 页. https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20Int…
41

Suspected fracture: stop moving the part — support in place, cool under 20 minutes, never self-straighten

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Treat any limb injury as a fracture first — standing and moving don't exclude it. Keep the part still, support by hand or splint in position, cool once under 20 minutes. Never straighten it yourself; bone through skin gets bleeding control, never pushed back. X-rays miss fractures; normal films with persistent suspicion get follow-up or MRI per the doctor.

Cost
Free. Find a rigid board, rolled magazine, or clothing as support; cold packs go over cloth.
Benefit
The IFRC's 2025 guidelines: "any injury to an arm or leg should be treated as a potential fracture"; "an X-ray is the only accurate way to diagnose a fracture — when in doubt, treat as a fracture"; splinting "minimizes movement and pain"; cooling "a maximum of 20 continuous minutes to relieve pain — longer may damage skin"; "with femur fractures, blood loss from the bone alone can be life-threatening" — marked pain or swelling, shock signs, femur fractures, or gross deformity mean emergency call. Angulated fractures get field straightening only when both: remote settings with a cold, pale limb below the angle or splinting impossible for transport, and a trained rescuer. Open fractures prioritize hemorrhage control and infection prevention. A clean first X-ray doesn't exclude fracture: NICE's hip guideline — normal films with suspicion get "MRI," or CT within 24 hours if unavailable; its fracture guideline — suspected scaphoid fractures, "consider MRI first after careful examination" (the scaphoid being a small wrist bone); a Cochrane review: "initial X-rays cannot exclude fracture" — among X-ray-normal, clinically-suspected scaphoids, the median true-fracture share ran 20%; the American College of Radiology's knee criteria — X-ray-negative with suspected hidden fracture or internal derangement usually warrant MRI next, "accurate for occult fracture, meniscal, and ligament injury"
Note
Grade B: consensus practice. Pre-hospital femur traction rests on one retrospective study of low certainty — less transfusion and shorter stays within 24 hours, mortality and complications indistinguishable; straighten-versus-splint-in-place found no evidence at all. Three common myths to shed: standing and walking don't exclude fracture; cold only, never heat or alternating; sprains don't "walk off" — rest first. No smoking before union — Section 2, item 1. No mega-calcium or bone broth for faster healing — Section 6, item 30. Elder fall-moving contraindications: item 2. Post-cast leg swelling: item 11 (clots). Disability grading and certificates after treatment: Section 24, items 9–10.

42

After sexual assault: get somewhere safe and call 110; before the exam — no bathing, no laundry, no tidying; hospital within 72 hours

Grade BValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: yesBenefit: large

The traces on your body, clothes, and in the room are the evidence that identifies the perpetrator. Before the forensic exam: no bathing, no laundry, no tidying — call 110 early. Emergency contraception is at the pharmacy, earlier is better. Hospital within 72 hours for the blocking-drug call.

Cost
Reporting is free. Emergency contraception is over-the-counter. The blocking course runs 1,000+ yuan — physicians judge, item 38. The hard part: speaking up then, and not showering immediately.
Benefit
Beijing prosecutors: "whether minor or adult, on encountering assault, dial 110 first." Timely reporting and care "enable investigators to promptly survey the scene, extract physical evidence, and fix the record." Guizhou's civil-affairs reprint of the People's Daily manual: "the most important thing after sexual assault is preserving evidence" — retain "body fluids, hair, skin debris, communications," and "do not bathe, wash clothes, tidy the room, or discard things"; acquaintance cases retain calls and messages, including later threats or buyoffs. Beijing Xicheng procuratorate: "avoid bathing before the physical examination." WHO: emergency contraception applies "when a woman is sexually assaulted without effective contraceptive protection," within 5 days, earlier better; levonorgestrel regimens ran 1.2%–2.1% pregnancy; domestic levonorgestrel is OTC; Wuhan's health commission: "within 72 hours, the earlier the better." HIV blocking within 2 hours where possible, 72 at the latest (national)
Note
Grade B: official case-handling experience and medication guidance, without conviction-rate numbers. Beneficiaries: you and family. The 72-hour contraception window is the domestic label; WHO allows 5 days, degrading with delay — don't stall. Already pregnant, emergency contraception does nothing. Report truthfully — no concealment, no exaggeration. Later buyoff approaches and threats: keep records, delete nothing. Reporting later is allowed, but evidence decays; hospital within the windows regardless. Recordings: Section 8, item 41. Post-assault photo or report extortion is likewise criminal — Section 8, item 32. A friend so assaulted: accompany to police and hospital — never "shower and rest first."

43

Infant under 1 choking soundlessly: face-down 5 back blows, flip, 5 chest thrusts, alternating — never abdominal thrusts

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Still coughing or crying: let them cough, watch closely. Soundless crying or bluing: someone calls 120 while you lay the baby face-down along your forearm, heel of hand delivering 5 blows between the shoulder blades. Not out: flip, 5 quick chest thrusts center-sternum, alternating — never the belly. Unresponsive: switch to CPR.

Cost
Free. Watch the moves once or take an infant first-aid class, minutes to half a day. The hard part: getting the baby prone first in the panic.
Benefit
The 2025 AHA-AAP pediatric basic life support guidelines: choking "is a leading cause of death in infants and children," liquids predominating in infants. Coughing or vocalizing means mild — let them cough while monitoring. Weak or absent cough, no cry, bluing means severe — call emergency first, then "repeat 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts until the object is expelled or the infant becomes unresponsive." Abdominal thrusts aren't recommended for infants — organ-injury risk. Chest thrusts now use the heel of one hand, pressing deeper than the old two-finger technique. Unresponsive: CPR starting with compressions, no pulse-check; visible objects removed before breaths — "never blind finger sweeps." The IFRC's 2025 guidelines match: up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades, then up to 5 chest thrusts, then immediate emergency call — their chest technique the two-thumb encircling hold. Fujian's Red Cross training center: under 1 year means "5 back blows + 5 chest thrusts," baby prone on the forearm, head below trunk
Note
Grade B: the technique rests on case reports, without lives-saved numbers. Benefit "large" is judgment: a fully blocked airway stops the heart within minutes. The beneficiary is almost always your own child. Over 1 year and adults: abdominal thrusts — item 26. Chest-technique variants differ: the US guidelines and the new domestic Red Cross use one-hand heel, the IFRC two thumbs, older tutorials two fingers — the 2025 US guidelines dropped two fingers for insufficient depth; any beats none. Even after expulsion, see a doctor — fragments may linger in the lungs. Coins and small toys go out of reach. Unresponsive infants: item 44.

44

Infant under 1 unresponsive with abnormal breathing: speakerphone 120, infant CPR — 30 compressions, 2 breaths

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

No response to foot-flicks, no normal breathing: speakerphone 120, hands moving. Two thumbs encircling the chest, or one-hand heel when too small to encircle, pressing about 4 cm at roughly 2 per second. Every 30 compressions, seal mouth over nose and mouth for 2 breaths. Infant arrests mostly follow airway failure — compression-plus-breath CPR saves more.

Cost
Free. Infant CPR takes one class, half a day to a day. The hard part: sealing your mouth over the tiny face, and pressing hard enough.
Benefit
The 2025 AHA-AAP guidelines: infant and child arrest still stems mainly from respiratory causes. Out-of-hospital infant arrest survives to discharge at only 6.6%. Laypersons encountering an unresponsive infant or child with abnormal breathing and no signs of life "should begin CPR immediately," no pulse-check; compression depth at least one-third the chest depth — infants "about 1.5 inches (4 cm)" — at 100–120 per minute; solo rescuers, 30:2; two rescuers, 15:2; one-hand heel or two-thumb encircling for infants, heel where encircling fails; two-finger technique discontinued for insufficient depth. The guidelines add: for out-of-hospital pediatric arrest, adding breaths to compressions improves survival. A US registry of 3,900 out-of-hospital arrests under 18 — 59.4% infants — found bystander CPR's adjusted survival-to-discharge at 13.2% versus 9.5% (adjusted OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.25–1.96); among infants, compression-plus-breath CPR associated with higher survival and better neurological recovery — compression-only approximated no CPR. The IFRC's 2025 guidelines: check infant responsiveness by lifting or flicking the soles; alone with a phone, speakerphone it; no phone reachable, 1 minute of CPR before calling. The Capital Institute of Pediatrics' explainer, carried by Beijing's health commission: "if only one person is present, perform 2 minutes of CPR before calling 120"; infant depth "4 cm"; under-1 breaths "mouth to nose and mouth"
Note
Grade B: survival figures come from observational registries pooling all children; infant-specific numbers absent from the abstract. Benefit "large" follows the pooled figures: discharge survival 9.5% to 13.2%, about 40% relative. The beneficiary is almost always your own child. Three differences from item 1: infants need breaths — compression-only underperforms; two thumbs or one-hand heel to about 4 cm, never stacked adult hands; alone and unable to call while pressing, press first — how long differs: Capital Institute and the US solo algorithm say 2 minutes, the IFRC 1; speakerphone dissolves the problem. The European council teaches 5 rescue breaths before compressions, the US compressions first — both beat nothing. Old domestic tutorials' two-finger technique was dropped by the 2025 US guidelines. Choking-related arrests: check the mouth before breaths, removing only visible objects — item 43.

14. Accounts and information security

10 entries

Metrics: money and personal information. When someone logs into your account, money goes first; they'll also use your account to defraud your contacts — and your identity effectively walks away with them.

1

Turn on two-factor authentication for email, payment, and social accounts — app-popup approval first, SMS codes second

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Two-factor means a second confirmation beyond the password at login. A popup on your phone that you tap blocks over 90% of phishing takeovers. Answering "where did you last log in" and "what's your backup email" blocks only about 10%.

Cost
Free. One setup per account, 2–3 minutes.
Benefit
Google analyzed 350,000 real account-takeover attempts. Device-based verification — phone popups you confirm, or plugged-in security keys — blocked "over 94% of phishing-based takeover attempts and 100% of automated ones" (phishing meaning fake-site password harvesting; automated meaning bulk tries with leaked passwords). Knowledge-based verification — last-login locations, backup emails — "blocked as little as 10% of phishing takeovers and 73% of automated"
Note
The same study found such challenges sometimes lock out the true owner — 52% of legitimate users failed the first try, though 97% eventually got in. Enable it on email first: most other accounts recover through email. Verification codes are yours alone — the cost of reading codes or face-scanning for others: Section 8, item 45.
Sources (1 references)
Doerfler P, Thomas K, Marincenko M, et al. (2019). Evaluating Login Challenges as a Defense Against Account Takeover. The World Wide Web Conference (WWW '19). https://doi.org/10.1145/3308558.3313481
2

Your email password stands alone — never reused anywhere

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Passwords stolen from other sites get replayed straight against your email. Once your email falls, every account recoverable through it falls too. So the email password is used nowhere else.

Cost
Free. A password manager remembers it for you. The hard part: breaking the one-password habit.
Benefit
Replaying leaked credentials site by site — credential stuffing — is the cheapest attack, and your email gets tried. One email breach cascades into every email-recoverable account. The US CISA's advice: a different strong password per account, at least 16 characters, stored in a password manager
Note
Use your browser's built-in password manager if nothing else — far better than one password everywhere. Don't store passwords in WeChat favorites or notes apps.
Sources (1 references)
US CISA. Use Strong Passwords. https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world/use-strong-passwords
3

Set a lock-screen password on the phone and a PIN on the SIM

Grade CValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The SIM is the little card inside — SMS verification codes arrive through it. Lose the phone, and whoever finds it pops the card into their own phone, harvests your codes, and resets account after account. A SIM PIN requires the code at every power-up in a new phone — closing the road.

Cost
Free. One setup each.
Benefit
After a lost phone, the finder's fastest route is your SIM in their phone collecting SMS codes — with codes, accounts reset one by one. A SIM PIN demands the code on boot in any new device, cutting the finder off
Note
The PIN lives under "SIM card lock" in settings; factory defaults are usually 1234 or 0000; three wrong entries demand the carrier's PUK — write both down on paper first.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献
4

Phone lost — this order: suspend the SIM, remote-lock, change passwords, report, freeze cards

Grade CValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Order beats speed. Suspend the SIM first — the code lifeline dies. Remote-lock the phone next, change email and payment passwords from a computer, report to police for the receipt, then freeze bank cards as needed. Borrow any phone to call the carrier.

Cost
Free. The whole sequence takes a dozen-odd minutes.
Benefit
Order beats speed. Step one, suspend the SIM — codes stop arriving for anyone. Step two, remote-lock and wipe. Step three, change email and payment passwords from a computer. Step four, police report with receipt. Finally, freeze cards as needed. The US FCC concurs: remote-lock even if you think it's merely lost; when stolen, report immediately with model and IMEI (the phone's identity number) and notify the carrier at once
Note
Save the three carriers' numbers now: China Mobile 10086, Unicom 10010, Telecom 10000. Note which city your number was registered in — the hotline will ask. Any borrowed phone works for suspension.
Sources (1 references)
US FCC. Protect Your Smart Device. https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/protect-your-mobile-de…；步骤顺序是作者经验；补办身份证见第 7 节，冒名贷款见第 8 节关于征信的一条
5

Card fraud: suspend and freeze first, report second, then demand the bank pay — proving "you did it yourself" is the bank's burden

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

You don't have to prove "that wasn't me" — the bank must prove the transaction was yours or authorized, or pay. The precondition: you suspended on discovery. Delaying, you eat the added losses.

Cost
Free. On suspicious activity: freeze immediately. Keep the report, suspension, and transaction notifications. With the card still in hand, make one small transaction nearby to prove possession at the time. The hard part: suspending before arguing with customer service.
Benefit
The Supreme Court's provisions split the burden. You claim card-counterfeit or online fraud — you produce initial evidence: effective legal documents, the true card's location and the transaction's location, statements, notifications, police and suspension records. Conversely, when the issuing bank or payment institution asserts the cardholder did or authorized the transaction, the evidence is theirs to produce. Where the bank failed to verify promptly after your notice, or failed to preserve slips and footage, the evidentiary failure is theirs. Established: debit-card holders may reclaim the stolen principal and interest plus damages; credit-card holders may reclaim charged overdraft principal, interest, and penalties plus damages — banks demanding repayment of that overdraft get no court support — and may demand prompt removal of the adverse credit record (national; effective 2021-05-25)
Note
Two situations leave you liable: your own fault in safeguarding card, password, or codes ("failure of proper custody with fault") — proportionate to the fault, so never share passwords or forward codes (item 1's popup first); and failure to suspend promptly, eating the expansion. So step one is always suspension, never argument. Third-party payment institutions follow the same rules — concrete, explicit "advance compensation" promises in their materials bind them. Money you were tricked into transferring yourself takes another route: Section 8, item 2.
Sources (1 references)
最高人民法院 (2021). 关于审理银行卡民事纠纷案件若干问题的规定（第四、五、七、十四、十五条）. https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/304771.html
6

Periodically review logged-in devices and authorized apps — clear what's unused

Grade CValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

"Logged-in devices" are the phones and computers that can still use your account. Takers usually lurk before acting. An unfamiliar device or long-dead app still linked: log out everywhere, change the password.

Cost
Free. Minutes per review. The hard part: remembering without reminders.
Benefit
Takeovers rarely act immediately — the intruder lurks. The device list records which phones and computers currently reach the account; the authorized-apps list records which third-party software you permitted. Unfamiliar devices and dead third-party apps are the most visible traces
Note
WeChat, Alipay, email, and Apple/Android accounts all carry these entries. On anything unfamiliar: log out everywhere, then change the password.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献
7

Don't tap "agree to all" for an app: non-essential information may not be leveraged against service

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

If the information isn't necessary for the service, refusing it can't be held against you — and collection is limited to what's genuinely needed. Maps need location; a flashlight doesn't need your contacts.

Cost
Free. The hard part: resisting "agree to all."
Benefit
The law states two things: refusal or withdrawal of consent may not justify denying product or service, save where processing is necessary to provide it; and collection is limited to the minimum scope implementing the purpose — only what's needed
Note
The test is necessity for the service — maps and location yes, flashlights and contacts no. After installing, switch off non-essential permissions in the app-permissions page, granting "just once" when genuinely needed.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大常委会 (2021). 个人信息保护法. 中国人大网. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088…：第六条「收集个人信息，应当限于实现处理目的的最小范围，不得过度收集个人信息」；第十六条「个人信息处理者不得以个人不同意处理其个人信息或者撤回同意为由，拒绝提供产品或者服务；处理个人信息属于提供产品或者服务所必需的除外」；第十五条「基于个人同意处理个人信息的，个人有权撤回其同意。个人信息处理者应当提供便捷的撤回同意的方式」
8

You may view, copy, correct, and delete your personal information — refusal can be sued

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

You may demand viewing, copying, correction, and deletion of your information. Service ended, retention expired, consent withdrawn — they should delete on their own. Refusal requires stated reasons; continued refusal, sue directly. Account cancellation and information deletion are two things — file deletion separately after canceling.

Cost
Free. Complaints and suits come only on stonewalling — litigation runs months with your own attorney fees, so complain first. The hard part: repeated pushing when they stall.
Benefit
Several situations oblige active deletion: service ended, retention expired, consent withdrawn, purpose achieved. Undeleted, you may demand deletion; refused, reasons must be stated; you may sue directly
Note
Cancellation and deletion are separate — after canceling, file deletion separately. Before switching or selling phones: log out and unbind everything, then factory reset. The law grants after-the-fact deletion; it can't recall what already leaked.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大常委会 (2021). 个人信息保护法. 中国人大网. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088…：第四十五条「个人有权向个人信息处理者查阅、复制其个人信息……个人请求查阅、复制其个人信息的，个人信息处理者应当及时提供」；第四十六条更正、补充权；第四十七条列了五种应当主动删除的情形，含「（一）处理目的已实现、无法实现或者为实现处理目的不再必要」「（二）个人信息处理者停止提供产品或者服务，或者保存期限已届满」「（三）个人撤回同意」，「个人信息处理者未删除的，个人有权请求删除」；第五十条「个人信息处理者应当建立便捷的个人行使权利的申请受理和处理机制。拒绝个人行使权利的请求的，应当说明理由」「个人可以依法向人民法院提起诉讼」
9

Face-scanning is never mandatory: alternatives exist means face-only is barred — disagreement must earn you another way

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Where another method achieves the same purpose, face-only verification is barred. Refusing the face must earn you card, password, or ID alternatives — no "then no service" coercion. Hotel rooms, public baths, changing rooms, and toilets admit no facial-recognition devices for anyone.

Cost
Free. When asked to scan, ask "is there another verification?" On "no," demand one. The hard part: asking aloud.
Benefit
The facial-recognition security measures state: "where other non-facial-recognition means achieve the same purpose or equivalent business requirements, facial recognition may not be the sole verification method; where an individual disagrees with facial-identity verification, other reasonable and convenient means shall be provided," and "no organization or individual may mislead, defraud, or coerce individuals into accepting facial-identity verification on grounds of business handling or service quality." Processing facial data on consent requires "separate consent, voluntarily and explicitly given with full knowledge" — asked about this one thing, agreed to this one thing. Consent is withdrawable, with convenient withdrawal. Minors under 14 need parental or guardian consent. Public installations "must be necessary for public safety" with conspicuous signage; hotel rooms, public baths, changing rooms, and toilets — private spaces within public venues — admit no installations, full stop. Facial data must be stored on-device, never transmitted over the internet, save statutory provisions or separate consent (national; effective 2025-06-01)
Note
The commonest encounters: compound gates, rental platforms, gyms, hotels. On "the system only supports faces," recite the measures: "where other non-facial-recognition means achieve the same purpose or equivalent business requirements, facial recognition may not be the sole verification method" — then demand card, password, or ID. Still refused: report to the local cyberspace administration. Sectors with separate state rules — some finance and government services — follow those. The deepest difference between faces and passwords: leaked faces can't be changed — treat them more carefully than passwords. Operators holding 100,000-plus facial records must file with provincial-plus cyberspace authorities within 30 working days — itself a question worth asking. View-correct-delete rights: item 8. Lending your face to someone else's loan is another matter entirely: Section 8, item 45.
Sources (1 references)
国家互联网信息办公室、公安部 (2025). 人脸识别技术应用安全管理办法（第 19 号令，第十条、十二条、十三条，2025 年 6 月 1 日起施行）. https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-03/21/c_1744174262156096.htm
10

Never hand code, keys, or private material to an unknown "AI relay" — especially with AI auto-executing commands

Grade BValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The relay sits between you and the model vendor, seeing and able to alter both your prompts and the replies. A study measured 400-plus relays: 9 injected malicious code into replies, and 17 touched honey-trap cloud keys. With AI auto-executing commands, one altered command can own the machine.

Cost
Official direct connections usually cost more and top up less conveniently. The hard part: relays are cheap and fan out to several models from one entrance.
Benefit
The state security ministry's June 2026 notice: some relays retain user data, secretly intercepting and reselling it to other model vendors for training; some hide backdoors planting malware to steal account keys and cloud credentials, even remote-control programs. The advice: official direct connections and properly licensed platforms only; sanitize private and project material before submission; manage and rotate keys; on abnormal billing, unexplained bans, or data anomalies — stop, rotate keys, scan for malware, preserve evidence. UCSB-led researchers' 2026 measurement: buying 28 paid relays from Taobao, Xianyu, and offshore shops plus 400 free relays from public communities — 1 paid and 8 free injected malicious code into returned tool calls (tool calls being commands the AI runs on your machine, like package installs); 2 timed their strikes, one example targeting only fully automated sessions; 17 touched deliberately planted AWS keys; 1 drained a researcher's Ethereum wallet — lightly funded, losses under 50 US dollars. The demonstrated alteration was subtle: swapping "requests" for the near-identical "reqeusts" in an install command, invisible at a glance (national)
Note
Grade B: one study, preprint (the pre-publication version). Mostly free relays — only 28 paid — so "what share of relays are dirty" is uncomputable. Some media inflated the theft to $500,000; the paper says under 50 dollars. Benefit "medium" is sized by consequence: key and code thefts range wildly, with no amounts to apply. Having used an unknown relay: revoke and regenerate every key that passed through it, cloud services and code repositories included. Through relays, never let the AI auto-execute — review commands before release. Running a relay carries criminal risk: Section 11, item 19. Beneficiary: you.
Sources (2 references)
国家安全部 (2026). 「AI中转站」，风险要防范. https://www.szzg.gov.cn/2026/xwzx/szkx/202606/t20260608_533…（数字中国建设峰会官网转载国家安全部微信公众号）；Liu H, Shou C, Wen H, Chen Y, Fang RJ, Feng Y. (2026). Your Agent Is Mine: Measuring Malicious Intermediary Attacks on the LLM Supply Chain. arXiv:2604.08407. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08407

15. Renting and buying

9 entries

Metric: money. Renting loses money most easily through deposits and agents; buying, through loan interest and everything the seller knows that you don't.

1

The rental deposit's amount, refund time, and deduction conditions must be written into the contract

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

How much, refunded when, deductible under what — written before signing. Deduction reasons absent from the contract can't be used against your deposit.

Cost
Free. Ten extra minutes at signing. The hard part: raising it in front of the landlord.
Benefit
The administrative regulation is plain: "where the lessor collects a deposit, the housing lease contract shall stipulate the deposit amount, refund time, and deduction circumstances; beyond the contractually stipulated circumstances, the lessor may not deduct without justified reason." Three things in the contract: amount, refund time, deduction conditions. Unwritten reasons can't touch your money
Note
On departure day, photograph and video together with the landlord: utility meters, walls, floors. Deposit docked without cause: complain to the housing-rental administration first; small claims for small amounts — Section 8.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2025). 住房租赁条例（国令第 812 号，2025 年 9 月 15 日施行）（第十条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032956…
2

Water or power cut, locks changed, door-knocking threats: report to police first — these eviction methods are barred

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Landlords may not cut utilities, change locks, or threaten in person to force termination or vacancy — expressly prohibited. On it happening, report; the response record is your evidence for later damages. Don't confront physically.

Cost
Free. One phone call, done on the spot.
Benefit
The regulation is plain: "lessors may not use violence, threats, or other illegal means to force lessees to terminate housing leases or vacate leased housing." Report first, preserve evidence; no physical confrontation
Note
Reporting creates the response record that later proves the claim. Notify the housing-rental administration simultaneously.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2025). 住房租赁条例（国令第 812 号，2025 年 9 月 15 日施行）（第十二条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032956…
3

Agents may not collect or disburse rent and deposits — money goes straight to the landlord

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Rent and deposits may not pass through agents; pay the landlord directly. Every intermediary hop is one more chance of the agent absconding — your rent paid, your tenancy gone. Verify the payee against the property certificate.

Cost
Free. Verify the payee before paying, minutes. The hard part: withstanding the agent's "transfer to us."
Benefit
The regulation lists "collecting and disbursing housing rent and deposits" among real-estate brokerage prohibitions: agents may not receive your rent or deposit on the landlord's behalf. Every hop adds absconding risk
Note
Verify the payee against the certificate; a non-owner demands explanation plus written authorization. Agents may charge only the matchmaking service fee.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2025). 住房租赁条例（国令第 812 号，2025 年 9 月 15 日施行）（第二十五条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032956…
4

Long-term apartment operators: check the supervised-funds account first; never pay a year up front for the discount

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Paying a year up front buys a sliver of discount; the company's collapse takes your deposit and a dozen-odd months of prepaid rent. Rent-loans are worse: the operator runs, the installments stay yours. Check for a published supervised-funds account before signing.

Cost
Free. One check, a dozen-odd minutes.
Benefit
The regulation requires subleasing operators to "establish a housing-rental supervised-funds account and publicize it." Subleasing operators master-lease from landlords and re-lease to you. The year-up-front discount never offsets collapse risk — deposit plus remaining rent vanishing together — and attached rent-loans multiply it
Note
Read for loan bindings at signing: an installment app paying the operator the year while you repay monthly means the operator's flight leaves your installments running. Don't sign that contract.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2025). 住房租赁条例（国令第 812 号，2025 年 9 月 15 日施行）（第十九条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032956…
5

Home sold mid-lease: the lease stands, no moving

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Sold mid-lease, your lease survives; the new owner honors the existing contract to term. No moving, no renegotiating — provided you lawfully occupy, with contract, transfer records, and move-in evidence kept.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
The Civil Code's "sale does not break the lease": a change of ownership during the lease term does not affect the lease contract's validity. The new owner honors the original contract to term
Note
The precondition is lawful possession — keep the contract, transfers, and move-in timing evidence.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第七百二十五条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
6

Before signing: verify the property certificate and mortgages; every payment by transfer with purpose memos

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

The two classic total losses: rent paid to a non-owner, and a long-mortgaged house later seized. Check ownership and encumbrance at the real-estate registration center before signing. All money moves by transfer, memoed "[address] rent for [month]" — direct evidence in any dispute.

Cost
Free. One check, half an hour.
Benefit
The two classic total losses: rent paid to a non-owner, and a mortgaged house later seized. Transfer memos of "[address] rent for [month]" serve as direct evidence
Note
Ownership is checkable at the local registration center. The landlord attends in person or delivers a written power of attorney. Subletters need the original landlord's written consent.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献；证据留存与转账备注同理见第 8 节关于彩礼和借条的两条
7

Second-hand purchases through agents: funds must move via the agent's dedicated bank transaction account

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

The purchase price — hundreds of thousands to millions, this book's largest single sum — routed through an agent must move via its dedicated supervised bank account, never WeChat to a salesperson. Two agencies collaborating on one deal may charge one commission; loan and title agency services require separate contracts and upfront fee disclosure.

Cost
Free. The hard part: insisting on the dedicated account, possibly over the agent's objections.
Benefit
The rules are plain: where the parties agree to route transaction funds through a brokerage, the funds "shall be transferred through the client transaction settlement funds dedicated deposit account opened by the brokerage at a bank" — a supervised account, not the agency's own and not a salesperson's private one
Note
Hundreds of thousands to millions — this book's largest single transaction — never WeChat to a salesperson. Two common overcharges: joint-agency deals charging two commissions (one allowed), and loan/title agency fees without separate contract or upfront disclosure. Every payment by transfer with memos — item 6.
Sources (1 references)
住房城乡建设部、国家发展改革委、人力资源社会保障部 (2011). 房地产经纪管理办法（令第 8 号，2016 年第 29 号令修改）第二十四条：「房地产交易当事人约定由房地产经纪机构代收代付交易资金的，应当通过房地产经纪机构在银行开设的客户交易结算资金专用存款账户划转交易资金。」第十八条「房地产经纪服务实行明码标价制度……在经营场所醒目位置标明房地产经纪服务项目、服务内容、收费标准」；第十九条「两家或者两家以上房地产经纪机构合作开展同一宗房地产经纪业务的，只能按照一宗业务收取佣金，不得向委托人增加收费」；第十七条代办贷款、代办房地产登记等其他服务「应当向委托人说明服务内容、收费标准等情况，经委托人同意后，另行签订合同」. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1918920.htm
8

Don't rent partitioned rooms: the minimum rental unit is the originally designed room; kitchens, bathrooms, and balconies house no one

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The minimum rental unit is the room as originally designed; kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and underground storage house no one. When such units get busted, you move. And mid-lease, landlords can't raise rent at will either.

Cost
Free. The price: living farther or smaller on the same budget.
Benefit
The rules are plain: the original designed room is the minimum unit — no re-partitioning into sub-rooms; per-capita floor area no lower than the local minimum; kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and underground storage barred for habitation; and lessors may not unilaterally raise rent mid-lease
Note
When illegal partitions get busted, the tenant moves, deposit and prepaid rent usually unrecoverable. Safety suffers too: partition walls block escape routes, and crowded units share one circuit. Three things to check at viewing: walls added later, windows present, and meters sized for the headcount.
