住房和城乡建设部 (2010). 商品房屋租赁管理办法（令第 6 号）第八条：「出租住房的，应当以原设计的房间为最小出租单位，人均租住建筑面积不得低于当地人民政府规定的最低标准。厨房、卫生间、阳台和地下储藏室不得出租供人员居住。」第九条：「出租人应当按照合同约定履行房屋的维修义务并确保房屋和室内设施安全……房屋租赁合同期内，出租人不得单方面随意提高租金水平。」http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1845070.htm
9

Urban hukou dreaming of country life: rent farmhouses only — never buy homestead land or the houses on it

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Urban-hukou residents may not buy rural homestead land, farmhouses, or "small-property" housing — state documents prohibit it outright. The village's "just write a contract" doesn't help: money out, house still not yours. For long country stays: lease, 20 years maximum per contract, renew on expiry.

Cost
Free. The price: the house never becomes yours, leases run 20 years maximum per signing, renewed by renegotiation.
Benefit
The State Council notice is plain: "urban residents may not go to the countryside to purchase homestead land, farmers' dwellings, or 'small-property housing.'" The same document bars farmers who sold or leased out dwellings from new homestead applications. The 2019 central rural-office and agriculture-ministry document repeats it: "strictly prohibited for urban residents to purchase rural homestead land" — and provides the lawful path: urban residents may lease farmhouses for living or business, contracts capped at twenty years, renewable by new agreement
Note
Homestead land is allocated by the village to its own members only. Lease with a written contract covering term, rent, renovation rights, and how renovation costs settle at expiry. Twenty years is the cap — no "50-year" or "70-year" leases, no multi-year lump payments. The documents also ban villas, compounds, and private clubs on homestead land — don't fund "joint builds" with villagers.
Sources (2 references)
国务院办公厅 (2007). 关于严格执行有关农村集体建设用地法律和政策的通知（国办发〔2007〕71 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_239…；中央农村工作领导小组办公室、农业农村部 (2019). 关于进一步加强农村宅基地管理的通知（中农发〔2019〕11 号）第五、六部分. https://www.moa.gov.cn/govpublic/NCJJTZ/201909/t20190920_63…

16. Living with a chronic illness

9 entries

Metrics: overall mortality and money. A chronic-diagnosis life often runs decades more; this section manages those decades.

1

Take the full course as prescribed — never stop because you feel better

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Those completing their medication ran about half the death risk of sporadic takers over the same period. Discount that figure: even placebo-completers died less, meaning part of the benefit is "people who stick to pills take better care generally." But stopping's harms are certain — antihypertensives, anticoagulants, and anti-rejection drugs above all.

Cost
Free — it saves future complication money. Daily dosing takes minutes; the hard part is never missing a day.
Benefit
Pooling 21 studies, 46,847 people (meta-analysis): versus sporadic takers, full-course takers ran about 44% lower death risk. Original value odds ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.50–0.63 (the confidence range). Restricted to genuinely effective treatments, about 45% lower (0.55, 0.49–0.62)
Note
Contested — this is the book's most discount-worthy number. In the same pool, even placebo-completers died less (0.56, 0.43–0.74), marking a real healthy-adherer effect. But stopping's harms stand clear, antihypertensives, anticoagulants, and anti-rejection drugs especially
Sources (1 references)
Simpson SH, Eurich DT, Majumdar SR, et al. (2006). A meta-analysis of the association between adherence to drug therapy and mortality. BMJ, 333(7557), 15. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.38875.675486.55
2

Outpatient chronic/special-disease certification first, cross-region registration second — hypertension, diabetes, chemo-radiation, dialysis, and anti-rejection settle directly out of province

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Hypertension, diabetes, malignant-tumor outpatient chemo-radiation, uremia dialysis, and post-transplant anti-rejection — these five also settle insurance directly at out-of-town clinics: no fronting money and reimbursing back home. But first the outpatient chronic/special-disease certification at your enrollment locality, then the cross-region registration — both together work.

Cost
Free. One cross-region filing on the insurance app before departure, done from the phone.
Benefit
The NHSA document says it's been done: "basically achieved county-level accessibility of cross-province direct settlement for the five outpatient chronic/special diseases — hypertension, diabetes, malignant-tumor outpatient chemo-radiation, uremia dialysis, and post-organ-transplant anti-rejection treatment." "County-level accessible" means handleable at county level. The document adds five more diseases on top
Note
The precondition is both filings — chronic/special certification first, cross-region registration second. The five added diseases roll out unevenly; your local insurance office's publications govern.
Sources (1 references)
国家医保局办公室、财政部办公厅 (2024). 关于稳妥有序扩大跨省直接结算门诊慢特病病种范围的通知（医保办发〔2024〕19 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202409/content_6974467…
3

Follow-ups at the doctor's intervals; log every result in one notebook

Grade CValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Chronic disease watches change over time, not single readings. Log dates, values, current drugs and doses in one place. Changing hospitals, you show it — no repeating tests, no repeating costs.

Cost
Each check runs tens to hundreds of yuan; hospital trips and waiting take time. The hard part: recurring visits keep slipping.
Benefit
Chronic disease reads how values move over time; single readings don't suffice. One log adds the switching-hospital benefit: no duplicate testing, no duplicate spending
Note
Record at least four things per visit: date, values, drugs then in use, doses. Photographing lab slips works — keep them in one place, not scattered.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献
4

Never drop regular treatment to try folk remedies or supplements

Grade CValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Stopping medication's harm is certain; remedies' and supplements' benefits are not. That trades a certain loss for an uncertain gain. Want to try supplements? Tell your attending physician first — some affect blood levels of anticoagulants and anti-rejection drugs.

Cost
Free — saves the supplement money too. No time. The hard part: holding out against repeated urging.
Benefit
Stopping's harm is certain; folk remedies' benefit is not. Section 6 lists the common no-effect categories
Note
Tell the attending physician before trying supplements — some interact with prescriptions, anticoagulant and anti-rejection blood levels included.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献；相关证据见第 6 节
5

Stable chronic patients: community clinics can dispense 12 weeks at once

Grade AValue: highMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Stable condition, unchanged medication: community centers dispense up to 12 weeks at once, sparing the monthly half-day of hospital queuing. Within the same insurance region, primary-hospital reimbursement runs about ten points above the next tier.

Cost
Free. One question at the community health center — whether long-term prescriptions are available.
Benefit
No monthly hospital round-trips for refills. Within one insurance pooling area, primary-hospital reimbursement exceeds the next tier by about 10 percentage points in principle
Note
"Qualified" is the doctor's judgment — generally clear diagnosis plus stable regimen. Same drugs, spared monthly half-days and registration fees. When the primary tier lacks your drug, ask about shortage registration and delivery. The same document phases tertiary hospitals out of routine refill clinics and moves the same specialists' clinics into communities — using the big hospital as a refill point gets harder.
Sources (1 references)
国务院办公厅 (2026). 关于加快建设分级诊疗体系的若干措施. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031…：「对于符合条件的慢性病患者，基层医疗卫生机构单次可开具不超过12周用药的长期处方。」；同文「原则上统筹地区内医疗卫生机构住院报销比例逐级拉开10个百分点左右的差距」，并要求上级医院在基层开设高血压、糖尿病、慢性阻塞性肺疾病等常见病慢性病门诊；同文「三级医院要聚焦急危重症和疑难复杂疾病，加强转诊会诊和住院服务，逐步酌减常见病复诊和诊断明确、病情稳定的慢性病等普通门诊」，「并将专家团队普通门诊向基层医疗卫生机构延伸」
6

Before signing with a community family doctor, ask what insurance covers and what's self-paid

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The basic service package bills insurance per regulation; personalized packages pay entirely out of pocket. When someone pitches an "upgrade package," ask: basic or personalized, filed or not, how much a year.

Cost
Free. One extra question before signing, a minute.
Benefit
Basic service packages are insurance-paid per regulation; personalized packages are fully self-paid and must file with the county health authority
Note
Signing's value is someone long tracking your condition — not how many bundled items. Three questions on any "upgrade" pitch: basic or personalized, filed or not, annual cost.
Sources (1 references)
国务院办公厅 (2026). 关于加快建设分级诊疗体系的若干措施. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031…：「加强基层门诊付费与签约服务政策联动，基本服务包按规定纳入医保支付；个性化服务包由签约基层医疗卫生机构按程序向县级卫生健康部门备案，费用由个人支付。」
7

On diabetes diagnosis: one dilated fundus exam, then per the doctor's intervals; feet checked yearly

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Diabetes damages retina and feet almost silently before blindness or ulceration. Early finds are treatable. Type 2: one dilated exam at diagnosis; type 1: starting 5 years after onset. One or two clear exams with on-target glucose stretch to every 1–2 years. Feet yearly.

Cost
A dilated fundus exam runs tens to hundreds of yuan; foot exams usually ride inside the consult. The hard part: remembering while eyes and feet still feel fine.
Benefit
Retinal damage is retinopathy; foot damage is the diabetic foot — both nearly symptomless before trouble. Early finds are treatable; waiting for blindness or rot is too late
Note
Type 2 screens at diagnosis because it has usually simmered for years; type 1 starts 5 years in. Clear exams with on-target glucose stretch to 1–2 years. Dulled foot sensation: daily sole checks, mirrors included.
Sources (1 references)
美国糖尿病学会 (2026). 糖尿病诊疗标准 2026·第 12 章 视网膜病变、神经病变与足部护理. Diabetes Care："People with type 2 diabetes should have an initial dilated and comprehensive eye examination by an ophthalmologist or optometrist at the time of the diabetes diagnosis." "Adults with type 1 diabetes should have an initial dilated and comprehensive eye examination by an ophthalmologist or optometrist 5 years after the onset of diabetes." "If there is no evidence of retinopathy from one or more annual eye exams and glycemic indicators are within the goal range, then screening every 1–2 years may be considered." "Perform a comprehensive foot evaluation at least annually to identify risk factors for ulcers and amputations." https://doi.org/10.2337/dc26-S012
8

After kidney stones: drink to 2.5–3 liters daily, salt under 6 grams

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

First-time calcium-stone formers doing nothing re-form at about one in four within five years. Adequate daily drinkers recur at just over one in ten — more than half off. The UK guideline: 2.5–3 liters of water daily, salt under 6 grams.

Cost
Free. Making water ever-available habitual; sweaty days demand more. The hard part: daily remembering.
Benefit
A 5-year randomized trial took 199 first-time idiopathic calcium-stone patients: one arm drank at least 2 liters daily, the other nothing. Five-year recurrence: 12/99 (12.1%) versus 27/100 (27.0%), P=0.008 — smaller P meaning less likely chance. Mean recurrence interval: 38.7±13.2 versus 25.1±16.4 months, P=0.016. Baseline 24-hour urine ran markedly lower in stone formers: men 1,057±238 versus 1,401±562 mL (P<0.0001); women 990±230 versus 1,239±440 mL (P<0.001). NICE NG118, 1.8.1: adults 2.5–3 liters daily, children and adolescents 1–2 by age; fresh lemon juice fine, no carbonated drinks, salt under 6 grams
Note
About 55% fewer recurrences, free — by this book's ordering, the section's best value. Watch 24-hour urine volume, target above 2–2.5 liters, not intake. Heavy sweaters and hot-environment workers drink more. The trial covered first-episode idiopathic calcium stones; uric-acid, infection, and cystine stones take their own approaches — recurrent formers deserve stone analysis and 24-hour urinalysis before adding drugs. Never quit calcium to prevent stones — Section 6, item 21. Acute flank colic means hospital, not flushing; painless hematuria has its own workup — Section 1, item 27.
Sources (2 references)
Borghi L, Meschi T, Amato F, Briganti A, Novarini A, Giannini A (1996). Urinary volume, water and recurrences in idiopathic calcium nephrolithiasis: a 5-year randomized prospective study. The Journal of Urology, 155(3), 839-843. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-5347(01)66321-3；National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2019). Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management. NICE guideline NG118，第 1.8.1 条. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng118/chapter/Recommendations
9

Diagnosed gout: stay on urate-lowering drugs long-term, holding uric acid below 360 µmol/L

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Gout means long-term urate-lowering below 360 µmol/L — not painkillers only when it hurts. Nurse-led titration reached 95% at target by two years versus 30% usual care; hitting target never licenses stopping. Diet alone can't reach the line — quitting alcohol lowers uric acid just 1.6 mg/dL.

Cost
Allopurinol runs a few to a few dozen yuan monthly; early titration checks every few weeks, stable phases every few months; the first 3–6 months add a flare-preventing drug. The hard part: continuing while painless.
Benefit
A randomized trial of 517 adults flared within 12 months: the nurse-led arm, educating patients and titrating to target, versus usual GP care. At 2 years, uric acid below 360 µmol/L (6 mg/dL): 95% versus 30% — target likelihood 3.18× usual (RR 3.18, 95% CI 2.42–4.18), P<0.0001. Year-2 flare frequency, tophi, and quality of life all favored the arm; each quality-adjusted life-year cost £5,066. The follow-up study, 438 surveyed, 82% returned: median flares in the past 12 months — 0 (IQR 0–0) in the target arm versus 1 (0–3), P<0.001 (the bracketed range being the interquartile). Still on urate-lowering drugs: 1.19× usual (adjusted RR 1.19, 1.09–1.30). The ACR 2020 gout guideline strongly recommends starting urate-lowering for three kinds: subcutaneous tophi, imaging-visible bone erosion, and 2+ flares yearly — continuous monitoring titrated to target, below 6 mg/dL. Allopurinol first-line, stage-3-plus CKD included, starting ≤100 mg/day, with anti-inflammatory prophylaxis 3–6 months at initiation. The same guideline cites a case series: well-controlled patients stopping drugs with uric acid still under 7 mg/dL — only 13% (27/211) went five years without a flare. Diet: alcohol-limiting runs 1.6 mg/dL lower than unrestricted; a beer raises uric acid 0.16 mg/dL; healthy, Mediterranean, and DASH diets matter less. First-choice drug splits: the ACR strongly favors allopurinol — effective at full dose, well tolerated, safe, cheap — and conditionally recommends switching febuxostat in cardiovascular history or new events when alternatives exist, matching the FDA's boxed warning. One basis, the CARES trial: 6,190 gout patients with cardiovascular disease randomized — febuxostat ran all-cause death at 1.22× allopurinol (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01–1.47, about 22% higher), cardiovascular death 1.34× (1.03–1.73, about 34% higher). Europe's FAST trial disagreed: 6,128 patients over 60 with cardiovascular risk factors — febuxostat showed no more major cardiovascular events (HR 0.85, 0.70–1.03), deaths 7.2% versus 8.6%. For uricosuric users, the ACR conditionally advises against alkalinization — no evidence of effect, very low certainty — while insisting on fluids and barring the class with kidney stones or stage-3-plus CKD
Note
Contested: first-choice drug differs across guidelines — the US favors allopurinol with febuxostat swaps for cardiovascular patients, while European FAST saw no added danger. Benzbromarone, a uricosuric, remains available domestically; the Chinese Medical Association's 2019 and 2024 guidelines give separate recommendations on drug choice and alkalinization. Whether benzbromarone pairs with sodium bicarbonate, the US guideline finds no evidence — follow your physician, never skipping the water. Han Chinese starting allopurinol should test HLA-B*5801 first: a congenital immune-response genotype, tested once, valid for life — carried by 7.4% of Han, Korean, and Thai populations versus 0.7% of whites and Hispanics; Asian and Black allopurinol users run 3× the severe hypersensitivity risk, potentially fatal with massive skin peeling; the ACR 2020 guideline suggests considering pre-testing both groups. Starting urate-lowering provokes flares — the guideline mandates 3–6 months of anti-inflammatory prophylaxis; "it hurt more, so I stopped" is the classic failure. When pain comes, add anti-inflammatories per orders — never stop the urate-lowering. Targets differ in writing: <6 mg/dL ≈ 360 µmol/L, with Chinese lab slips favoring µmol/L. Checkup-found high uric acid without ever flaring is another matter — Section 6, item 19. Sugary drinks and alcohol: Section 2, items 7 and 19.
Sources (6 references)

17. When there's an elder at home

10 entries

Metrics: money and personal freedom. With elders, most trouble isn't insufficient money — it's words unsaid and papers unsigned in time. The last three entries — bedsores, cataract surgery, and dog-walking fractures — count in mortality terms, not compared with the rest.

1

While the elder is lucid: appoint the future guardian in writing

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

While clear-headed, spend a few hundred yuan on a notarized paper naming their future guardian. Without it, incapacity means the court appoints who signs and who manages the money — and family disagreement drags it longer.

Cost
Notarization runs a few hundred yuan; one conversation settles it. The hard part: speaking of the day they can no longer manage, face to face.
Benefit
The Civil Code lets fully capable adults arrange their future guardian in advance — close relatives or any willing individual or organization — "determining their guardian in written form." On total or partial incapacity, the named person takes over; without the paper, court designation decides who signs and who manages
Note
The instrument is "agreed guardianship" — one's own advance designation, ranking ahead of the statutory order. Elders living alone, children far away, complicated families: all the more reason to arrange early. Notarization recommended.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第三十三条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
2

Make the will; remember later wills revoke earlier ones, and notarized wills no longer outrank

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Six will forms are legal, but formal defects void the whole document — the classic failure. The handwritten kind must be written, signed, and dated entirely in one's own hand. Multiple conflicting wills: the last stands. Since 2021, the notarized copy no longer ranks automatically first.

Cost
A handwritten will is free; notarization runs hundreds to a thousand-odd yuan. The hard part: raising death with family.
Benefit
The Civil Code recognizes six forms — self-written, ghost-written, printed, audio-video recorded, oral, and notarized — each with mandatory formalities. Multiple conflicting wills: the last governs. Since 2021, notarization confers no priority
Note
Self-written wills: wholly handwritten, signed, dated. Printed wills need two-plus witnesses, with testator and witnesses signing and dating every page. Heirs, named beneficiaries, and their close relatives cannot witness. Formal errors void the whole thing — the classic failure.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第一千一百三十四条至第一千一百四十二条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
3

The elder's money in a separate account, with a two-person confirmation rule above a threshold

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Supplement, collectible, and wealth-product scams against elders share one playbook: months of rapport, then one harvest. Agree in advance: spending past a set amount gets mentioned to a named person — delaying the payment past the impulsive moment.

Cost
Free. One family conversation sets the threshold. The hard part: raising it without sounding suspicious of them.
Benefit
Elder-targeted supplement, collectible, and wealth scams all bank months of trust before the single harvest. A pre-agreed "past X yuan, mention it to Y" delays the payment decision past the impulsive crest
Note
Frame it not as "we fear you'll be scammed" but "the household keeps joint books" — easier to accept. Don't move all the elder's money to children: that breeds its own disputes.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献；防骗通则见第 8 节和第 13 节
4

Arm the elder with one ever-ready refusal: "I need to go home and discuss it with my family"

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Sales and fraud run on in-the-moment pressure that makes refusal awkward. Pre-agree the sentence — "I'll discuss it with my family at home" — and the elder holds a graceful exit on the spot. Better than reasoning afterward.

Cost
Free. One rehearsal conversation, minutes.
Benefit
Sales and fraud both press in the moment. One pre-agreed exit line hands the elder a step down — more effective than after-the-fact reasoning
Note
Use with item 3. Run the home fall-proofing in passing — Section 1. The line gives the elder a step down, not a shield against them; the hardest part of being cornered is refusing before a roomful — harder than judging truth.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献
5

Any elder-paid-upfront "investment retirement" is off-limits: membership cards, bed purchases, retirement apartments, residential tours, and elder-product sales are one illegal-fundraising set

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Elder-pay-first, return-promising retirement schemes are one scam family: membership cards, bed purchases, retirement apartments, residential tours, meeting-sold elder products. Losses are self-borne by regulation. One ring took 136 million yuan for "reserving retirement-apartment beds," burning 2,100-plus people. The only interceptable step is the payment.

Cost
Free. Read the formats to the elder once, minutes. On encounter: refuse outright — no lectures, no tours, no phone numbers left. The hard part: elders already attending and befriended pull back reluctantly.
Benefit
The civil-affairs ministry lists five formats — judging by format beats judging by face. First, impersonating elder-care institutions — no entity, rented venues, fake cooperation agreements. Second, "elder-care services" — VIP, member, and prepaid cards collecting "service fees" far beyond bed capacity. Third, "elder projects" — stakes in wellness bases, fictional retirement apartments, long-term bed leases, "time banks," fronted as refund sales, sale-leasebacks, and repurchase promises. Fourth, "elder products" — buybacks, consignment sales, consumption rebates, free checkups, gifts, meeting marketing, wellness lectures, expert clinics. Fifth, "residential retirement" — cheap or free travel, stored-value rebates, points-based retirement. The money is unrecoverable: Article 25 of the anti-illegal-fundraising regulation — "losses from participation are borne by the participants themselves." Official cases: Dai and others raised 136 million yuan reserving retirement-apartment beds, 2,100-plus victims — Dai drew 15 years plus a 400,000-yuan fine for fundraising fraud; Cao raised 13.207 billion yuan through "elder-industry investment," 110,000-plus people involved — life imprisonment with political-rights deprivation and full confiscation. Supplement meeting-sales run as fraud: Ni wined, gifted, and chauffeured elders into lectures where instructors fabricated anti-cancer claims through "false personas, false cases, and inflated bargaining," selling "dihydroquercetin" at tens of times cost — 620,000-odd yuan in sales; Ni drew 10 years 3 months plus a 120,000-yuan fine (national; regulation since 2021-05-01)
Note
Judge not by "this one looks legitimate" but by "pay first, promised returns?" Elder care sells services; the moment the talk turns to investment, rebates, or principal back — disbelieve. Lectures, tours, and clinics themselves are lawful and hard to block; the payment is the interceptable step — pair with item 3's confirmation rule. Already paid: 110 or 96110 for the stop per Section 8, item 2, plus reports to the local anti-illegal-fundraising lead department. House-for-retirement is another path — item 6.
Sources (5 references)
民政部 (2023). 关于养老服务领域非法集资的风险提示. https://www.gov.cn/lianbo/bumen/202306/content_6886556.htm（中国政府网发布）；民政部、中国银保监会 (2021). 关于养老领域非法集资的风险提示. https://www.mca.gov.cn/n152/n164/c36171/content.html；国务院 (2021). 防范和处置非法集资条例（国务院令第 737 号，第二、二十五、三十条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-02/10/content_558…；最高人民检察院 (2022). 检察机关打击整治养老诈骗犯罪典型案例. https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202206/t20220617_560010.…；最高人民法院 (2025). 依法惩治涉民生领域诈骗犯罪典型案例（案例五 倪某荣诈骗案）. https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/482861.html
6

Beyond insurers' reverse-mortgage pension insurance, no "house-for-retirement" — and never mortgage the house to buy wealth products

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

The only legitimate form is insurers' reverse-mortgage pension insurance, still piloted. Door-to-door versions are unrelated — tricking elders into mortgaging the house, then buying the visitor's recommended products. Some never knew their house was mortgaged: house gone, loan still on their back.

Cost
Free. The property certificate goes to no door-to-door "house-for-retirement" visitor; mortgage, guarantee, and loan agreements get a child's eyes before signing. The hard part: visitors run warm and numerous, and elders hate refusing.
Benefit
The regulator's consumer-protection bureau drew the line. The only legitimate form: "elderly housing reverse-mortgage pension insurance" — elders with full lawful title mortgage to an insurer, continuing to live in, use, and rent the house, disposal subject to the mortgagee, drawing pension payments until death — still piloted, thinly practiced. The fraud version is "completely unrelated" to the pilot, "borrowing state policy to stage illegal fundraising" — inducing elders into property mortgages, investing the borrowed money in recommended products, "often a Ponzi scheme of new repaying old." The consequence, verbatim: "some participants didn't even know their property was mortgaged, ultimately losing the house while still carrying the loan." The return line: "question products promising above 6%, treat 8%+ as dangerous, above 10% prepare to lose all principal — 'guaranteed principal, high returns' is financial fraud." The same notice demands "treating contract signing with care — never sign blank contracts" (national, June 2021)
Note
Grade B: regulator risk notices and experience, not research. The 6/8/10 lines are consumer reference points, not legal thresholds. The banking regulator has merged into the NFRA; the original page is down — cited via the provincial reprint. Product losses come second: a mortgaged house leaves the elder owing a loan exceeding any principal. Signing and blank contracts generally: Section 8, item 17; payment stops: Section 8, item 2.
Sources (2 references)
中国银保监会消费者权益保护局 (2021). 关于警惕「投资养老」「以房养老」金融诈骗的风险提示（2021 年第三期）. https://dfjrjgj.hunan.gov.cn/dfjrjgj/yhlj/202106/t20210608_…（湖南省地方金融监督管理局转载）；民政部、中国银保监会 (2021). 关于养老领域非法集资的风险提示（第四种表现形式：以宣称「以房养老」为名非法集资）. https://www.mca.gov.cn/n152/n164/c36171/content.html
7

A bedridden or severely disabled elder at home: apply for long-term care insurance at the enrollment locality — it isn't elders-only

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Long-term care insurance pays for hired care. Severe disability persisting half a year or more: apply at the enrollment locality. No fronting — employee-enrolled reimbursement runs about 70%, resident-enrolled about 50%, excluding bed and board fees. No age floor: severely disabled young people qualify too.

Cost
One application at the local insurance office plus one disability-grading assessment; first-pass assessments are fund-paid.
Benefit
Qualified long-term care costs carry no deductible (the front-until-threshold amount — waived here). Employee-policy participants: fund-paid around 70%; unemployed-resident-policy participants: around 50%. Annual caps run no higher than 50% of the pooling area's prior-year per-capita resident disposable income
Note
Disability must persist "generally 6 months or more" — weeks of hospitalization doesn't qualify. A 6-month waiting period precedes benefits. Bed and board fees and medical costs payable by basic insurance are excluded, as is overlap with work-injury nursing allowances. This money and the disability nursing subsidy (Section 7, item 8) are separate procedures and separate sums — no conflict. Home- and community-based care carry favorable rates; institutional admission isn't required. Rollout is phased and assessment standards vary — call 12393 or the local office first. Failed assessment isn't final: reapply as disability deepens.
Sources (2 references)
国家医保局等八部门 (2026). 关于印发《加快建立长期护理保险制度实施方案》的通知. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202603/content_7063915…：保障对象为「按规定参保缴费且失能状态长期持续（一般为6个月以上），经申请通过评估认定的失能人员」，「制度起步阶段保障重度失能人员」；「待遇享受不设起付标准。符合规定的长期护理服务费用，按未就业城乡居民参保政策参保的，基金支付比例为50%左右；按单位职工参保政策参保的，基金支付比例为70%左右，退休人员享受单位职工参保待遇」；「参保人员基金年度最高支付限额不超过统筹地区上年度城乡居民人均可支配收入的50%」；「待遇享受固定等待期原则上按照6个月设置」；另见中共中央办公厅、国务院办公厅《关于加快建立长期护理保险制度的意见》. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12666/202604/content_…
8

With someone bedridden long-term, treat pressure ulcers as enemy number one: powered air mattress, scheduled turning, daily inspection of bony prominences

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Hip-fracture patients with preoperative pressure ulcers ran about 20% higher 30-day mortality. Powered air mattresses cut new ulcers by about 60%; genuinely executed turning schedules, about 70%. Keep people off their fronts for long. Daily checks of sacrum, heels, hips, and shoulder blades; non-blanching redness means nurse or doctor the same day.

Cost
A home alternating-pressure air mattress runs from a few hundred yuan; each turn takes minutes. The hard part: every 2–3 hours through the night — beyond one person alone.
Benefit
19,520 hip-fracture surgical patients (US NSQIP 2016–2019): preoperative pressure ulcers tracked higher 30-day mortality, holding after adjustment (OR 1.2, 21% odds increase, P=0.004), plus deep-vein thrombosis (OR 1.59), pneumonia (OR 1.39), unplanned readmission (OR 1.43), and 0.4 extra hospital days. Among 324 hospitalized elders (mean 86), median 18-month follow-up: pressure ulcers independently predicted long-term death (HR 1.500, 95% CI 1.059 to 2.126, P=0.020) — independently meaning after other factors drop out. A network meta-analysis of 65 randomized trials: powered active-airflow support surfaces versus standard hospital mattresses ran RR 0.42 (95% CI 0.29 to 0.63, moderate certainty); powered hybrid airflow, RR 0.22 (0.07 to 0.66). A Cochrane review (2026, 11 trials, 4,462 participants): 2-hourly versus 4-hourly turning indistinguishable (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.39, very low certainty), likewise other intervals. A 1,226-patient ICU trial using wearable sensors with visual alerts enforcing genuine 2-hour turning ran lower ulcer incidence (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.75, moderate certainty). A 116-patient trial: prone positioning ran higher ulcer rates than supine (RR 4.55, 95% CI 2.31 to 8.98)
Note
Grade B three ways: the mortality studies show "ulcer bearers fare worse," not "prevention lowers mortality"; the turning-interval trials are shaky; and the mattress evidence, though stronger, compares hospital surfaces — extrapolating to home beds. Daily checks of sacrum, heels, hips, and shoulder blades for non-blanching redness are standard nursing practice without separate literature. Insurance-covered care: item 7. A suddenly swollen leg: Section 13, item 11. The long-bedridden stretch after falls: Section 1, item 34.
Sources (4 references)
Porter SB, Pla R, Chow JH, et al. (2022). Preoperative Pressure Ulcers, Mortality, and Complications in Older Hip Fracture Surgery Patients. JAAOS Global Research & Reviews, 6(11). https://doi.org/10.5435/JAAOSGlobal-D-22-00117；Ottaviani S, Rondanina E, Longo E, et al. (2026). Impact of pressure ulcers and frailty on long-term mortality: a prospective cohort study of hospitalized older adults. European Geriatric Medicine, 17(2), 665-672. https://doi.org/10.1007/s41999-025-01331-8；Shi C, Dumville JC, Cullum N (2018). Support surfaces for pressure ulcer prevention: A network meta-analysis. PLoS ONE, 13(2), e0192707. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0192707；Latimer SL, Chaboyer WP, Probst S, et al. (2026). Repositioning for pressure injury prevention in adults. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 6, CD009958. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD009958.pub4
9

When cataracts affect the elder's walking: ophthalmic evaluation for surgery; with both eyes involved, don't let the second wait too long

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: highTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Women over 70 having prompt first-eye surgery fell about 34% less often over a year, with fewer fractures — though the count of fallers didn't drop. Second-eye surgery showed no clear fall difference. Operated elders ran about 16% lower hip-fracture odds within a year.

Cost
One accompanied eye exam for the surgeon's judgment; most hospitals run day surgery — home the same day. Both eyes mean two operations. Out-of-pocket depends on the intraocular lens (the artificial lens implanted) chosen and local insurance — ask beforehand.
Benefit
A randomized trial took 306 women over 70 with cataracts: half had first-eye surgery within about 4 weeks, half waited 12 months. Over a year, prompt surgery cut fall counts about 34% (rate ratio 0.66, 95% CI 0.45 to 0.96). At-least-one-fall rates — 49% surgical versus 45% waiting — didn't drop; two-plus falls ran 18% versus 25%; fractures struck 4 (3%) versus 12 (8%). The Cochrane review included it: first-eye surgery reduced fall counts in women, second-eye didn't. The second-eye trial, 239 women over 70, ran 32% lower fall rates but possibly by chance (rate ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.19). In a 5% Medicare sample of 1,113,640 cataract patients over 65 (2002–2009), observational only, the operated ran about 16% lower hip-fracture odds within a year (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.81 to 0.87) — an absolute difference of 0.20 points, about 2 fewer per 1,000
Note
Contested: pooled, the two randomized trials left faller counts unimproved (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.17). Western Australia's whole-population records found fall-injury hospitalizations up 27% in the year after first-eye surgery — 2.14× preoperative levels between operations — though before-after designs can't separate surgery from aging. Another Australian cohort found the biggest fall drop after the second eye. So with both eyes involved, don't let the second wait; between operations, extra care on stairs. Cochrane also carries a vision-management trial where falls rose about 57% — surgery fixes clarity; fall prevention still needs Section 1, item 13's balance work, and bones need items 39–40 there. The national eye-health plan notes cataract restoration is routinely available at county level — no need for the big-city hospital. Beneficiaries: your parents and grandparents.
Sources (9 references)

10

Elder dog-walkers: leash in the palm, never wrapped; keep it short; train the dog out of lunging first

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: small

US over-65s fracturing bones while leash-walking rose from about 1,700 to about 4,400 yearly, 80% women. Hip fractures lead, nearly three in ten hospitalized. Among leash-injured hands, about three-quarters came from wrapped cords and a dog's pull. Hence: palm grip, short leash, trained dog.

Cost
Grip and shortening are free — one accompanied walk and lesson. Lunge-training takes time, self-taught or hired (prices vary widely). The hard part: weaning elders off retractables and wrist-wrapping habits.
Benefit
US emergency surveillance projected nationally: over-65 leash-walking fractures ran about 1,671 in 2004 and 4,396 in 2017, the rise statistically significant; 78.6% of the fractured were women, 28.7% hospitalized; by single site, hips led at 17.3%; by class, upper limbs at 52.1%. Another national emergency dataset (2001–2018) projected about 360,000 leash-related injuries (356,746 exactly): 193,483 pulled by dogs, 136,767 tripped or entangled; injuries per million rose from 25.4 to 105.5. A hand-surgery clinic took 443 leash-injured hands over 5 years: about three-quarters (337, 75.9%) from wrapped hands or fingers pulled by dogs; about one-fifth (96, 21.6%) needed surgery. CDC: 2001–2006 averaged about 86,629 fall injuries yearly involving cats and dogs, 88.0% dogs; of dog-related falls, 26% occurred while walking and 21.2% from being pushed or pulled over
Note
Palm grip, never wrapped, is the hand clinic's advice — it protects fingers and wrists, not the pulled-down walker. They also recommend short leashes: short denies the dog running speed, softening the yank; long lines entangle and trip. Retractables at full extension are long lines — but no study compares retractables directly, a 2024 review noting leash-type data absent. CDC and the fracture paper both commend lunge-training, the latter adding smaller breeds for elders considering dogs. No study prices these habits in falls — hence "small" by judgment. Bone readiness: Section 1, items 39–40; balance: item 13; walking volume credit: Section 2, item 44. Beneficiaries: your parents and grandparents.
Sources (5 references)
Pirruccio K, Yoon YM, Ahn J (2019). Fractures in Elderly Americans Associated With Walking Leashed Dogs. JAMA Surgery, 154(5), 458-459. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamasurg.2019.0061；Forrester MB (2020). Dog leash-related injuries treated at emergency departments. American Journal of Emergency Medicine, 38(9), 1782-1786. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajem.2020.05.082；Plusch K, Givner D, Wiafe B, Lutsky K, Beredjiklian P (2026). Hand and Wrist Dog-Leash Injuries in the Outpatient Setting: A Review of 443 Cases. Hand, 21(4), 582-586. https://doi.org/10.1177/15589447241299128；CDC (2009). Nonfatal fall-related injuries associated with dogs and cats — United States, 2001-2006. MMWR, 58(11), 277-281. https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/mm5811a1.htm；Rosa R, Buckley RE (2024). Leash-related injuries associated with dog walking: an understudied risk for dog owners? Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association, 262(7), 973-978. https://doi.org/10.2460/javma.23.11.0608

18. Is raising children worth it?

6 entries

This section counts money and time. Like Section 10's marriage accounting, it splits the accounts for you without deciding for you. Already pregnant and working through procedures: Section 27.

1

Count what's payable first: the national childcare subsidy, 3,600 yuan per child yearly, paid to age 3

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Children born from 2025-01-01 onward, under 3: this money pays. One parent applies at the child's registration place. 3,600 yuan per child per year, running to age 3 — income-tax exempt, and uncounted as household income for dibao-style assistance.

Cost
Free. One trip to the child's household-registration locality to apply.
Benefit
The central plan states: infants born from 2025-01-01, under 3, paid "3,600 yuan per child per year," claimed by a parent or other guardian — the subsidy "exempt from individual income tax" and "not counted toward family or personal income" in assistance determinations
Note
This is the national floor; some provinces and cities stack local subsidies on top. Three years total 10,800 yuan — a small slice of child-rearing costs, no basis for the have-or-not decision.
Sources (1 references)
中共中央办公厅、国务院办公厅 (2025). 育儿补贴制度实施方案. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_12206/202508/content_…
2

Maternity leave: 98 days, with the maternity allowance paid by the birth-insurance fund at the employer's prior-year average monthly wage

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

At least 98 days' leave, 15 usable prenatally; difficult labor adds 15; each additional baby adds 15. The pay during leave is the maternity allowance, from the birth-insurance fund; uninsured employers pay it themselves.

Cost
Free. The employer files; you run nowhere.
Benefit
The State Council sets the days: "female employees enjoy 98 days of maternity leave, of which 15 may be taken before childbirth; difficult labor adds 15; multiple births add 15 per additional infant." The pay is the maternity allowance: insured, "paid by the maternity insurance fund at the standard of the employer's prior-year average monthly employee wage"; uninsured, paid by the employer at your pre-leave wage standard
Note
98 is the national floor; provincial population regulations typically add 60-plus reward days, usually totaling 158 or more. Who pays the reward days varies by province.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2012). 女职工劳动保护特别规定（国令第 619 号，第七条、第八条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-05/07/content_658…
3

Know this one: no wage cuts or dismissal for pregnancy, childbirth, or nursing

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Cutting wages or firing you during pregnancy, childbirth, or nursing is illegal — fined 1,000–5,000 yuan per person affected. With a baby under one, you get a daily nursing hour, and no overtime or night shifts may be assigned. Claims: Section 19.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
The State Council provides: "employers may not reduce wages, dismiss, or terminate labor or employment contracts of female employees on account of pregnancy, childbirth, or nursing." Nursing mothers of infants under 1 receive one nursing hour daily, with no extended hours or night shifts. Violations draw 1,000–5,000 yuan per person
Note
Wrongfully dismissed: Section 19's claim path. Evidence priorities: written transfer and pay-cut notices plus chats — keep both.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2012). 女职工劳动保护特别规定（国令第 619 号，第五条、第九条、第十三条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-05/07/content_658…
4

The child-rearing time account counts "whose time is consumed," not "how hard it feels"

Grade CValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Convert daily childcare hours and nightly wake counts into time, multiply by the caregiver's hourly rate. The result usually dwarfs formula and diapers. So settle the division before conceiving.

Cost
Free but time-consuming: under 3, days are essentially fully consumed. The hard part: every single day, no teeth-gritting through a finite stretch.
Benefit
Convert daily care hours and nightly wakes into hours times the caregiver's hourly rate — a figure usually far beyond formula and diaper money. Unpaid care, cooking, and night duty still enter the cost this way. The method matches Section 10's housework accounting: agree the division before deciding to conceive
Note
Precision is unnecessary. What helps is two people, before conceiving, negotiating over one shared sheet — sparing the fights after.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献；口径见第 10 节
5

The money account splits three ways: 0–3, compulsory schooling, and after

Grade CValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: highTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

0–3 money goes to caregiving — yourselves, grandparents, or hired care. Primary through junior high goes to housing and extracurriculars. After that, to the education track. The three spend nothing alike; mixed, they yield only a frightening total.

Cost
No fixed total — cities and child-rearing styles vary wildly. The hard part: sitting down to split the three accounts instead of guessing one intimidating number.
Benefit
0–3's bulk is the care arrangement; compulsory schooling's bulk is housing and extracurricular spending; thereafter, the schooling path. The three differ wholly in where money goes — pooled, they produce only a scary total
Note
Count the certain money first — childcare subsidy, maternity allowance, insurance reimbursements — then see the gap. Don't decide by the internet's "raising a child costs X million": unclear scope, unknown inclusions and omissions.

6

For the elders, for the marriage, for old age — keep separate accounts

Grade CValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Others wanting you to bear a child may count as a factor — but time and money post to your own ledger. "Raising children against old age" takes its own account: it wagers on another person's means and willingness twenty years out. Write the consequences of not bearing children too, and set the two side by side.

Cost
Free, but one earnest conversation. The hard part: saying it plainly, not around.
Benefit
Same frame as Section 10. Others' expectations may factor in; the costs stay on your ledger, not theirs. "Old-age insurance by children" especially needs its own account, assuming another person's economic capacity and willingness two decades ahead
Note
Write the consequences of not bearing children too, and compare them side by side with the consequences of bearing them.

19. On the job, leaving the job, and work injuries

19 entries

This section counts money: how it computes, what to sign, how deadlines run. The first three entries cover money due while still employed; six cover departure; seven cover occupational disease and work injury. Work-injury money runs an order of magnitude above layoffs, on harder deadlines — and occupational damage never comes back. Four entries close the section: workplace bullying, separation certificates, the income tax on severance, and moving social-insurance relations between cities.

1

Overtime at 1.5×, 2×, 3× — unpaid means a labor-inspection complaint, and late payment adds 50%–100%

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Weekday overtime pays 1.5×; rest-day overtime without compensating rest, 2×; statutory holidays — New Year, Spring Festival, Labor Day, National Day — pay 3×, uncompensable by time off. Unpaid? Complain to labor inspection. Ordered to pay and still not paying adds 50%–100% of the arrears.

Cost
Free. Routinely keep punch records, rosters, and overtime approvals; screenshot work-chat assignments too. The hard part: remembering monthly.
Benefit
Statutory hours: no more than 8 daily, 44 weekly on average. Ordinary overtime generally caps at 1 hour daily; special reasons, 3 daily and 36 monthly. Three overtime bands: weekday extension, no less than 150% of wages; rest days without compensating rest, no less than 200%; statutory holidays, no less than 300% — the last with no compensatory option in the statute. Overtime arranged but unpaid draws a labor-administration payment order; overdue, an additional 50%–100% of the payable amount as compensation (national)
Note
Rest days and statutory holidays count separately — statutory holidays number only the legally designated days; swapped long-weekend days count as rest days at 200%. "Overtime needs approval" and "I stayed voluntarily" don't cancel payment but complicate your proof — keep assignment and approval records. Comprehensive and flexible working-hour schemes need labor-administration approval, not company say-so. Dispute limitation: Section 8, item 19.
Sources (2 references)
全国人大常委会 (2018). 劳动法（2018 年第二次修正，第三十六、四十一、四十三、四十四条）. https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/bgt/art/2023/art…（国家市场监督管理总局刊登）；全国人大常委会 (2007). 劳动合同法（第八十五条第三项）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
2

Annual leave by cumulative service: 5, 10, 15 days; untaken days pay 300% of the daily wage

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Cumulative service 1–10 years: 5 days yearly; 10–20: 10; 20+: 15 — accumulated across employers. Where the employer can't schedule it and you agree to forgo, those days pay 3× daily wages. Sign the "voluntary waiver" and only normal wages remain.

Cost
Free. Total your years across all employers — contribution records prove them. The hard part: not signing the "voluntary waiver" form.
Benefit
Twelve months of continuous work earns leave. Days follow cumulative service across all employers: 1–10 years, 5 days; 10–20, 10; 20+, 15. Statutory holidays and rest days don't count against leave. Where work demands genuinely prevent scheduling and you consent to forgo, untaken days "pay annual-leave wages at 300% of the employee's daily wage income" — the 300% already including the ordinary day's pay, so the extra take-home is 200%. Daily wage = monthly wage ÷ 21.75; monthly wage averaged over the prior 12 months excluding overtime. Part-year entrants prorate by the remaining calendar days; departures settle by the year's worked duration, over-taken leave never clawed back. Neither scheduled nor paid: correction order, then, past deadline, the leave wages plus an equal sum as compensation (national; since 2008-01-01)
Note
Cumulative service spans employers — don't count only the current one. Only when the employee "for personal reasons and in writing forgoes leave" may the employer pay normal wages alone — don't sign the waiver. Personal leave over 20 accumulated days without wage deduction suspends that year's leave; sick leave beyond the tier thresholds (2 months under 10 years' service, 3 at 10–20, 4 over 20) likewise. Family-visit, marriage-leave, bereavement, maternity, and work-injury recuperation don't consume annual leave.
Sources (2 references)
国务院 (2007). 职工带薪年休假条例（国务院令第 514 号，第二、三、四、五、七条）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2008/content_859865.htm；人力资源和社会保障部 (2008). 企业职工带薪年休假实施办法（人社部令第 1 号，第三、四、五、十、十一、十二、十五条）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2009/content_1265995.htm
3

Probation has legal caps, wages no less than 80%, and one probation only

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Contracts under 1 year: probation caps at 1 month; 1–3 years: 2 months; 3-plus and open-ended: 6 months. One probation per company — a second after transfer is illegal. Probation wages can't fall below 80% of the post's floor or the contracted wage, nor below local minimum wage.

Cost
Free. Minutes before signing, cross-check contract term against probation length.
Benefit
Contracts of 3 months to under 1 year: probation no more than 1 month; 1 year to under 3: no more than 2; 3-plus and open-ended: no more than 6. Task-completion contracts and those under 3 months admit no probation. "One probation period per employer per worker." Contracts stating only a probation term: the probation fails and the term is the contract term. Probation pay "no less than 80% of the employer's lowest wage for the same post or the contracted wage, and no less than the local minimum wage." Overlong probation actually served pays additional compensation at the post-probation monthly wage for the excess. In-probation terminations require the statutorily listed grounds with reasons stated (national)
Note
Three common violations: a 1-year contract with 3-month probation; re-probation after transfer; and "no social insurance during probation" — insurance runs from day one, employer duties per Section 12, item 16. Probation dismissal isn't compensation-free: it turns on whether the ground is statutorily allowed; wrongful terminations compute 2N under item 6.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大常委会 (2007). 劳动合同法（第十九、二十、二十一、八十三条）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
4

Laid off: compute N first — one month's wage per full year, half a month under six

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Severance computes: one month's wage per full year; six months to a year counts as a year; under six months, half a month. Monthly wage means the trailing 12-month average, bonuses and allowances included. Wages above three times the local prior-year average cap at three times, with service capped at 12 years.

Cost
Free. One calculator pass, ten minutes.
Benefit
The statutory severance — the N everyone cites — computes: "one month's wage per full year... six months to less than one year counts as one year; less than six months, half a month's wage." Monthly wages above three times the local prior-year average employee wage cap at three times, with service capped at twelve years
Note
Monthly wage means the 12-month pre-termination average — bonuses, allowances, and subsidies included, not base salary alone, the commonest undercount. Income tax on severance: item 18.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大常委会 (2007). 中华人民共和国劳动合同法（2008 年 1 月 1 日施行）（第四十七条）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
5

Terminated without 30 days' notice? One extra month's wage

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Termination for post-illness incapacity, incompetence, or changed circumstances without 30 days' written notice adds one month's wage beyond N — the N+1. Negotiate it listed separately, never folded into N.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
The law offers two routes: "thirty days' prior written notice to the worker" or "payment of an additional month's wage, after which the contract may be terminated." Immediate departure costs the extra month — the "notice pay," separate from N, computed on last month's wage while N uses the 12-month average: different bases
Note
The extra month exists only under Article 40's three situations: post-medical-period incapacity for the original and reassigned work; incompetence persisting after training or transfer; and major change in objective circumstances failing negotiation. Economic layoffs (Article 41) require only 30 days' notice to the union or staff; mutually agreed terminations carry N; serious-misconduct dismissals carry nothing; unlawful termination carries 2N. Under Article 40: negotiate N and 1 separately.
Sources (2 references)
全国人大常委会 (2007). 中华人民共和国劳动合同法（2008 年 1 月 1 日施行）（第三十六、三十九、四十、四十一、四十六、四十七、八十七条）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm；国务院 (2008). 劳动合同法实施条例（国务院令第 535 号）第二十条：「用人单位依照劳动合同法第四十条的规定，选择额外支付劳动者一个月工资解除劳动合同的，其额外支付的工资应当按照该劳动者上一个月的工资标准确定」. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2008/content_1107604.htm
6

Unlawful termination: compensation at double the severance standard

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Unlawful terminations pay double the severance standard — the 2N. Whether unlawful depends on the facts; consult legal aid or a lawyer before choosing negotiation or arbitration.

Cost
Free, but arbitration waits months. The hard part: staying the course.
Benefit
The law: terminations violating it "shall pay compensation at twice the economic-compensation standard of Article 47" — compute one severance, then double it
Note
This is the 2N. Unlawfulness is fact-specific — consult legal aid or a lawyer first (Section 7).
Sources (1 references)
全国人大常委会 (2007). 中华人民共和国劳动合同法（2008 年 1 月 1 日施行）（第八十七条）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
7

Never sign "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" — that signature forfeits N

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Signing "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" usually forfeits both severance and unemployment benefits. Resignations fall outside compensable grounds — save employer fault like wage arrears or unpaid insurance. Nothing forces same-day signing: sleep on it.

Cost
Free. The hard part: withstanding the pressure to sign on the spot.
Benefit
Severance grounds are statutorily enumerated; workers resigning on their own sit outside them, save statutory employer fault like arrears or unpaid insurance. Signed "voluntary resignation" usually forfeits severance and unemployment benefits together
Note
The classic script is "sign now to smooth the process; compensation separately." Get it written into the agreement on the spot or don't sign. Refusing today carries no legal consequence — sleep on it.

全国人大常委会 (2007). 中华人民共和国劳动合同法（2008 年 1 月 1 日施行）（第三十八条、第四十六条）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
8

Before leaving: save pay slips, attendance, contract, insurance records, and chats

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Once the laptop and accounts return, pay slips, attendance, contracts, insurance records, and chats are gone. Arbitration still turns on your own materials for wages and overtime. Save your own employment materials — company source code and client lists stay.

Cost
Free. Half an hour of archiving. The hard part: remembering before you go.
Benefit
Returned equipment means unrecoverable records. Burden allocation may tilt employer-ward, but wages and overtime still ride on your own evidence
Note
Save your own employment materials only — taking source, client lists, and technical documents risks Section 11. Demand the separation certificate too: item 17.
Sources

9

Before entering dust, noise, or chemical posts: check the contract for hazard disclosure; the three occupational health exams are employer-arranged and employer-paid

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

The contract must state the post's occupational hazards, protections, and benefits truthfully; concealment licenses refusal without dismissal. Three exams — pre-employment, in-service, departure — are employer-arranged and employer-paid; without the departure exam, no termination.

Cost
Free. Read the occupational-hazard disclosure clause by clause at signing; keep a copy of every exam report. The hard part: asking aloud and collecting materials on the spot.
Benefit
The Occupational Disease Law requires four disclosures at signing: hazards the work may generate, consequences, protection measures, and benefits — "truthfully informing the worker and written into the labor contract, without concealment or deception." Later reassignment to undisclosed hazardous work requires renewed disclosure and contract amendment. On failure: "the worker has the right to refuse operations with occupational hazards, and the employer may not terminate the contract for that refusal." Three exams: pre-post, in-service, departure — "occupational health examination costs borne by the employer," results delivered in writing. No pre-post exam, no hazardous assignment; contraindicated workers, no contraindicated operations; work-related damage found means reassignment and proper placement. "Workers without pre-departure occupational health examinations may not have their labor contracts terminated." On departure you "have the right to obtain copies of your occupational health surveillance file, which the employer shall provide truthfully and free of charge, stamping the copies" (national)
Note
Three interview questions size up the employer: any occupational hazards in this post, will the contract state them, who pays the pre-post exam. Evasive answers mean your own risk math. The departure exam is the most missed — it bars termination and anchors any future occupational-disease diagnosis; collect the file copy before leaving. Occupational disease itself routes through work injury: items 11 onward.
Sources (1 references)
全国人大常委会 (2018). 职业病防治法（2018 年修正，第三十三、三十五、三十六条）. https://www.beijing.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengcefagui/qtwj/201711…（北京市人民政府转载）
10

Dust, noise, and chemical damage is irreversible: protective equipment must be employer-provided; unprotected work may be refused

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Pneumoconiosis, noise deafness, and chemical eye burns are statutory occupational diseases; lungs and hearing never come back. You may know the hazards, demand protective facilities and equipment, and refuse unprotected work; retaliation in pay or dismissal is void.

Cost
Free. The hard part: wearing respirators, earplugs, and goggles always, and refusing unprotected tasks — sometimes earning "difficult" from colleagues.
Benefit
Statutory occupational diseases, from 2025-08-01: 12 classes, 135 kinds, with 4 open clauses. Class one: pneumoconioses — silicosis, coal-worker's, graphite, carbon-black, asbestosis, talc, cement, mica, potter's, aluminum, welder's, founder's, plus an open clause. ENT-oral class: noise deafness and blast deafness. Eye class: chemical eye burns and arc-eye. All irreversible — no therapy restores lungs or hearing. Four on-the-spot rights: knowing the workplace's hazards, consequences, and protections; demanding compliant protective facilities, personal equipment, and improved conditions; criticizing and reporting violations and life-threatening practices; and "refusing unlawful directives and coerced work without occupational-disease protections" — with any wage, benefit, or contract retaliation for exercising these rights "void" (national)
Note
Match the mask: particulate respirators stop dust; gauze and surgical masks don't. No employer earplugs? Buy your own — a few yuan, hearing never returns. "Two years to save and go" fails for silicosis, which strikes years after leaving dust and keeps progressing — hence the departure exam's weight (item 9). The new catalog adds musculoskeletal disease (carpal tunnel, long-repetition manufacturing only) and mental-behavioral disorder (PTSD, emergency responders only). Chemical splashes: Section 13, item 21.
Sources (3 references)
国家卫生健康委、人力资源社会保障部、国家疾控局、全国总工会 (2024). 职业病分类和目录（2025 年 8 月 1 日起实施）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6992843…；新版目录 12 大类 135 种的口径见国家卫生健康委 (2024). 新版目录将职业病调整为 12 大类 135 种. https://www.gov.cn/lianbo/bumen/202412/content_6992838.htm；全国人大常委会 (2018). 职业病防治法（第三十九条）. https://www.beijing.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengcefagui/qtwj/201711…（北京市人民政府转载）
11

Injured at work or in a commute crash: work-injury determination first — the employer won't file, you file

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

On-the-job injuries count; commute crashes without primary fault count too. Without the determination, medical costs, recuperation wages, and disability benefits all vanish. The employer files within 30 days; unfiled, you, family, or the union file within a year.

Cost
Free. One trip to the social-insurance administration with three documents: the application form, proof of employment, and the medical diagnosis.
Benefit
Without determination, medical costs, wage-and-benefit-preserving recuperation pay, and disability subsidies all fall away. Past 30 days of employer silence, the interim benefits are the employer's own bill
Note
Take the one year seriously — but delay not your own fault doesn't count: force majeure, restricted liberty, employer causes, defective registration, or labor-relation arbitration and litigation. Employer-dragged-past-deadline: file anyway, with evidence of the delay. Refused acceptance or adverse conclusion: administrative review or suit. Employer denial puts the burden on the employer — but keep your own materials: same-day photos, colleagues' contacts, treatment records, attendance. Article 16 lists three exclusions: intentional crime, drunkenness or drugs, self-harm or suicide. Article 15 adds "deemed work injury": death from sudden illness during work hours at the post, or rescue failing within 48 hours.
Sources (2 references)

12

Don't believe "make it to your desk and it counts": sudden illness means 120 first, not clocking in

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Rushing to the office during sudden illness buys no money. Deemed-work-injury requires onset during work hours at the post — en-route illness without arrival never qualified, and rescue past 48 hours disqualifies too. The minutes spent qualifying trade away your survival odds.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
Deemed work injury requires onset "during work hours and at the work post," with death or failed rescue within 48 hours. Delaying care to satisfy two conditions pays with survival chances for compensation you may never collect
Note
Both conditions simultaneously: during hours and at the post. En-route never applies; onset at the post followed by being sent home or to hospital with death within 48 hours may. It reads where illness struck, not where death came. Short videos recasting this as "reach the office for money" have it exactly backward — what changes outcomes is reaching a hospital within the first minutes. And 48 hours is a hard line: rescue past it disqualifies.

No work-injury insurance paid? The benefits still exist — the employer pays them in full at the same standard

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Uninsured employment doesn't erase work-injury benefits — the employer pays the same items and standards in full. Non-enrollment is the employer's added penalty: back-payment orders, 0.05% daily late fees, and 1–3× arrears fines. "No insurance, no compensation" is a lie.

Cost
Free, though employer denial means arbitration or suit, months minimum. The hard part: staying the course.
Benefit
The regulation states plainly: employers that should have enrolled but didn't pay the work-injury benefits per the regulation's items and standards — the same sums, from the employer's own pocket
Note
"No insurance, no compensation" is the classic lie here. Non-enrollment only adds the employer's penalties; your benefits never shrink.

Once stable: labor-capacity assessment — disability grades convert straight into money

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Once the condition stabilizes, assess. Grades convert to money: the one-time disability subsidy runs on your wage — grade 5, 18 months; 6, 16; 7, 13; 8, 11; 9, 9; 10, 7. Before results, sign no "lump-sum settlement."

Cost
Free. One assessment process with waiting on both ends.
Benefit
The one-time disability subsidy converts grades into months of wages paid at once: grades 5 and 6 at 18 and 16 months, 7 at 13, 8 at 11, 9 at 9, 10 at 7 of one's own wage
Note
Grades 5 and 6 retain the employment relationship with monthly disability allowances; grades 7–10 draw two further sums on contract expiry or worker-initiated termination — the fund's one-time medical subsidy and the employer's one-time employment subsidy, provincially set. Work-related death: three sums — funeral grant, dependents' pension, one-time death benefit

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Work death pays three sums — negotiate all three. Funeral grant: 6 months of the locality's prior-year average monthly wage. Dependents' pension: monthly on the deceased's wage — spouse 40%, other dependents 30% each. One-time death benefit: 20× the prior-year national urban per-capita disposable income — one number nationwide.

Cost
Free, one round of paperwork.
Benefit
Three sums. First, the funeral grant: 6 months of the pooling area's prior-year average employee monthly wage. Second, dependents' pensions: monthly on the deceased's wage — spouse 40%, other dependents 30% each, childless elders and orphans plus 10 points. Third, the one-time death benefit: 20× the prior-year national urban per-capita disposable income, one figure nationwide, region-blind. For 2026 work deaths, that sum runs about 1.13 million yuan (1,130,040) — the prior year's 56,502 yuan × 20
Note
The one-time death benefit is nationally uniform, updating yearly with the statistics release. Accept no "our local standard is lower."

16

Long-run bullying, humiliation, obstruction at work: don't just endure — document first, then complaint, police, or arbitration by nature

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

The bullied run about 60% higher heart-disease and stroke risk, rising with exposure; bullied workers run about double the suicidal-ideation odds years later. Verbal abuse isn't a small thing you shrug off.

Cost
Free, but time: log dates, witnesses, verbatim words; keep chat and email originals. Arbitration and suit run months. Leaving costs most — your own math.
Benefit
Health first: three Swedish-Danish cohorts pooled, 79,201 employed adults 18–65, initially cardiovascular-disease-free, average 12.4 years' follow-up; 9% reported past-year workplace bullying. The bullied ran about 59% higher cardiovascular disease (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.28–1.98) — coronary and cerebrovascular; workplace-violence exposure, about 25% higher (HR 1.25, 1.12–1.40); both dose-responsive. A Norwegian nationally sampled longitudinal survey, 1,846 workers, three waves two-to-three years apart: the bullied ran about double the later suicidal-ideation odds (OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.08–3.89); the reverse didn't hold. Legally, China has no dedicated workplace-bullying statute — match the conduct: insult, corporal punishment, beating, illegal search, or detention of workers draws administrative punishment, damages, or criminal liability; coerced labor licenses immediate contract termination without notice plus severance; employers must prevent and stop sexual harassment through authority and hierarchy, with victims entitled to civil recourse. Arbitration concludes within 45 days of acceptance, extendable 15
Note
Why B: health figures are observational, self-reported bullying. Four first steps: (1) log from today — recordings per Section 8, item 41; (2) written internal reports, kept; (3) beatings, confinement, public humiliation — police; (4) forced out by arrears or unpaid insurance — items 7 and 8 here. Severance math: item 4. Pure cold-shouldering and obstruction map to little law — internal complaint, transfer, or leaving. Arbitration caps at 60 days; first instance 6-plus months; attorney fees yours. Overwhelmed: 12356 first, Section 1, item 25. No blanket advice to quit on the first insult — the price of leaving is yours to compute.

On leaving: demand the separation certificate stating contract term, end date, post, and years of service

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Dismissed, expired, or resigned — the employer issues the separation certificate and transfers files and insurance within 15 days. The certificate states contract term, end date, post, and years served. Unemployment registration needs it. Refusal draws correction orders plus damages for losses caused.

Cost
Free. Demand in person before leaving or by written message, keeping the request record. The hard part: asking amid fallout. Employer stalling means complaint or arbitration — weeks to months.
Benefit
The law requires the certificate on termination or expiry — regardless of who initiated: expiry without renewal, resignation, dismissal alike. The employer completes file and insurance transfers within 15 days. The implementation regulation fixes four contents: contract term, termination date, post, and years at the unit. The unemployment regulation requires the certificate for timely unemployment registration — benefits run from registration. Non-issuance draws labor-administration correction; damages caused are compensable. New employers hiring workers not yet separated from the old bear joint liability for the old employer's losses — the certificate is your written proof of separation (national)
Note
The statute never conditions the certificate on handover — only severance waits for handover. On stalling: one more written demand, then 12333 or labor inspection — free, investigated within 60 working days, extendable 30. Damages need arbitration within the year — free, 45 days plus 15 — with your own proof, e.g., delayed unemployment registration or a rescinded offer. Appeals run to court, 6-plus months, filing 10 yuan per case, attorney fees yours. The four required contents exclude departure reason — a certificate stating "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" contrary to fact gets challenged on the spot (item 7). Unemployment benefits: Section 7, item 1.

Severance in hand: check the tax — within 3× the locality's prior-year average wage it's exempt; the excess taxes separately, never merged with salary

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

One-time termination compensation within 3× the locality's prior-year average wage is income-tax exempt; the excess taxes alone on the comprehensive schedule, never pooled with the year's salary. Withholding the lump into monthly wages? Question the employer, then 12366.

Cost
Free. Look up the local prior-year average wage and audit the employer's withholding; the individual-income-tax app shows every filing.
Benefit
The MOF-STA document: one-time compensation for terminated labor relations — severance, living subsidies, and other allowances — is exempt within 3× the locality's prior-year average employee wage; the excess, unmerged with comprehensive income, taxes on the comprehensive schedule (3% to 36,000, 10% to 144,000, graded to 45%). Example: local average wage 100,000 yuan; 3× = 300,000. A 360,000-yuan package taxes only the 60,000 excess: 3,480 yuan. The full 360,000 on the schedule would cost 58,080. In force since 2019-01-01, no expiry stated (national)
Note
In the same document, the annual-bonus clause carries an expiry, extended to 2027-12-31; the termination-compensation clause carries none and doesn't follow the bonus's. The document names severance, living subsidies, and other allowances without separately naming notice pay or unlawful-termination damages — unsure, ask 12366 locally. Which average wage applies follows the local bureau. Severance computation: items 4–6. Early-retirement and internal-retirement lump sums compute otherwise.

Moving cities for work: transfer pension and medical relations to the new locality, years accumulating — never refund-cancel

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Both relations follow you, prior years accumulating. Before pension age, no refund-cancellation or withdrawal. Medical gaps over 3 months may mean waiting up to 6 months for reimbursement in the new city — don't gap long.

Cost
Free. After enrolling and paying in the new city, the new employer or you applies — a window trip or online. Pension waits tens of working days; medical about 15.
Benefit
The Social Insurance Law: cross-region employment carries the pension relation with years accumulating; employee medical likewise. Pensions compute by segments and pay uniformly. Cross-province pension transfers follow the State Council's continuity measures; before benefit age, no termination or refund, with personal accounts non-withdrawable early. Personal accounts transfer in full with interest; the pooled portion transfers at 12% of your actual post-1998 contribution wages per year. Benefits compute from your yearly wages, years, and local averages. Procedure: enroll and pay in the new city, then apply in writing to the new locality — 15 working days' review, 15 to transfer out, 15 more to conclude. The 2020 cross-province service list put this online; applying at the receiving end suffices. Employee medical needs the old locality stopped and the new enrolled; online via the national medical-insurance platform or at windows — old side out in 10 working days, new side in within 5, account balance swept along. Gaps within 3 months, made up per local rules, waive waiting periods and backdate reimbursement; gaps over 3 months wait up to 6 months by local rule (national)

Collection locality sets the average wage in the formula. Intra-province transfer follows provincial rules — ask locally. Already drawing? No transfers. Gap-and-eligibility rules: Section 7, item 18; self-pay without an employer: Section 31, item 11.
