20. Caring for a newborn

14 entries

Metrics: infant mortality and money. Only what bears on the child's survival or your spending enters — and only where differences are large and evidence hard. Soothing and parenting details aren't this book's. Pre-birth and discharge-day procedures: Section 27.

1

Infants sleep on their backs, on firm flat surfaces, same room but not same bed, nothing soft in the crib

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Infants sleep face-up on firm flat surfaces. Adults share the room, never the bed. No pillows, quilts, bumpers, plush toys, or "head-shaping" pillows. Inclined rockers and infant seats carry, never sleep. The US alone loses about 3,500 infants yearly in sleep.

Cost
Free. The mattress goes firm — a few hundred yuan. The hard part: withstanding the elders' ways, consistently.
Benefit
About 3,500 US infants die yearly of sleep-related causes — sudden infant death syndrome, unknown causes, and accidental suffocation in bed. The AAP's safe-sleep environment: "supine positioning; use of a firm, noninclined sleep surface; room sharing without bed sharing; avoidance of soft bedding and overheating." Further risk reducers: breastfeeding, no nicotine or alcohol exposure, on-schedule vaccination, and pacifiers
Note
"Nothing soft" means pillows, quilts, bumpers, plush toys, and shaping pillows all out — the harmless-looking nursing pillow included. Inclined rockers and infant seats aren't sleep places. In this section, nothing differs as much, and nothing takes more elder-pressure endurance.
Sources (1 references)
Moon RY, Carlin RF, Hand I, Task Force on Sudden Infant Death Syndrome and the Committee on Fetus and Newborn (2022). Sleep-Related Infant Deaths: Updated 2022 Recommendations for Reducing Infant Deaths in the Sleep Environment. Pediatrics, 150(1), e2022057990. https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2022-057990
2

The first hepatitis B shot within 24 hours of birth

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The first hepatitis B dose within 24 hours of birth. Infection in infancy runs about 95% chronic; adult infections mostly self-resolve. Earlier is stronger. HBsAg-positive mothers' babies add hepatitis B immunoglobulin simultaneously.

Cost
Free — the vaccine sits in the immunization program. Given at the hospital on day one, no extra trip.
Benefit
WHO: "all infants should receive the hepatitis B vaccine as soon as possible (within 24 hours)" — because "about 95% of infections in infancy and early childhood develop chronic hepatitis." Adult infections mostly self-resolve
Note
HBsAg-positive mothers: add one dose of hepatitis B immunoglobulin at birth — established at prenatal screening, not postpartum. The mother's own screening: Section 1.
Sources (1 references)
World Health Organization. Hepatitis B fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hepatitis-b
3

Complete the national immunization program — fully free; missed doses get made up, not restarted

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Program vaccines are wholly free; clinics cannot charge. Enrollment checks the booklet, and missed doses surface for catch-up. Missed doses补 only the missing ones — no restarting, brand switches fine. Eczema, hives, allergic rhinitis, and asthma when stable all vaccinate normally, physiological jaundice included.

Cost
Free — "vaccination units may charge no fee for immunization-program vaccines," by statute. Monthly trips to the clinic; keep the vaccination booklet safe.
Benefit
Kindergartens and schools verify the booklet at enrollment; gaps get reported for catch-up — missed doses never slip past. The 2026 schedule applies: the HPV vaccine has entered the national program; the pertussis-containing series now starts at 2 months, five doses at 2, 4, 6, and 18 months and 6 years; Japanese-encephalitis vaccine went routine in Tibet, Qinghai, Xinjiang, and the Corps from March 2026. Same-day co-administration: all program vaccines may go together per schedule or catch-up rules; injectables land at different sites, "mixing two or more vaccines into one syringe is strictly prohibited." Non-same-day: two-plus injectable live vaccines space at least 28 days; inactivated and oral-live vaccines space freely. Under-18 catch-up: "only incomplete doses need补种, no restart," and brand switches continue (national; 2026 schedule)
Note
The commonest myth is "weak constitution, delay vaccination." Officially: "allergic constitution," family allergy history, and prior food or drug allergies are no bar — atopic dermatitis, hives, allergic rhinitis, and asthma vaccinate when stable, antihistamines and inhaled steroids included, neonatal physiological and breast-milk jaundice likewise. Only two true bars: prior acute severe allergic reaction to the same vaccine, or severe allergy to a known component. Immunodeficient and chemo-, radiation-, or immunosuppressant-treated children get individualized assessment at the clinic. Hepatitis B first dose: item 2. Self-paid non-program vaccines charge separately — unrelated here.
Sources (2 references)
全国人大常委会 (2019). 疫苗管理法（第四十八、四十九条）. http://ynswsjkw.yn.gov.cn/html/2019/faguiguizhangxin_0731/6…（云南省卫生健康委员会转载）；国家疾病预防控制局、国家卫生健康委 (2026). 《国家免疫规划疫苗儿童免疫程序及说明（2026 年版）》解读问答. https://www.ndcpa.gov.cn/jbkzzx/c100013/common/content/cont…
4

Breast milk only for the first 6 months — not even water; solids from 6 months, breastfeeding continues

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Start feeding within the first hour. First 6 months: breast milk only, no water. From 6 months, add solids — iron-rich animal foods daily — and keep breastfeeding to 2 years or beyond. Insufficient or impossible: formula, guilt-free. What you feed matters far less than sleep position.

Cost
Free, saving formula money — but time-heavy, daily. The hard part: 6 unbroken months.
Benefit
WHO: "initiate breastfeeding within one hour of birth"; first 6 months "exclusive breastfeeding — no other foods or liquids, water included"; then "safe and adequate complementary foods from 6 months, with continued breastfeeding to 2 years or beyond." The national health commission's service guide likewise promotes 0–6-month exclusivity and requires, from 6 months, "daily complementary foods must include iron-rich animal foods"
Note
Insufficient milk or medical bars: formula. The breast-versus-formula gap runs far smaller than safe sleep's. Solid-meal counts: 1–2 daily at 6–8 months, 2–3 at 9–12, covering at least four of seven food groups daily. Severe eczema or egg allergy and peanuts: item 12. Vegan households: item 14.
Sources (2 references)
World Health Organization. Breastfeeding. https://www.who.int/health-topics/breastfeeding；国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2024). 婴幼儿营养喂养评估服务指南（试行）（国卫办妇幼函〔2024〕452 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7002872…
5

Mix formula with water at 70 °C or above; cool before feeding; discard leftovers

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Formula isn't sterile — it may carry Cronobacter. Newborn infection runs 40%–80% reported fatality. Pour hot water first, let it fall to about 73.8 °C, then add powder — the mix still above 70 °C cuts the bacterium below one hundred-thousandth. Cool, feed, discard the rest.

Cost
Free. A few minutes' cooling each time. The hard part: waiting through the crying.
Benefit
Formula isn't sterile and may carry Cronobacter sakazakii; newborn infection fatality reports at 40%–80%. Experiments: hot water poured first, cooling to about 73.8 °C before powder, keeps the reconstituted mix above 70 °C in the vast majority of cases — reducing the bacterium by over 5 log cycles, below one hundred-thousandth
Note
The 70 °C threshold comes from public-health guidance — Beary et al.: "public health guidance for caregivers of high-risk infants recommends reconstituting formula with water heated to at least 70 °C (158 °F) to inactivate microorganisms." Preterm, low-birth-weight, and under-2-month infants run highest risk. No day-old thermos water; no room-temperature holds for the next feed.
Sources (3 references)
Beary MA, Daly SE, Baker J, Snyder AB (2025). Assessing Hot Water Reconstitution Instructions and Labeling of Powdered Infant Formula to Ensure Cronobacter spp. Reduction. Journal of Food Protection, 88(9), 100571. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfp.2025.100571；Sima WG, Legesse T, Girma S, et al. (2025). Emerging microbial risks: Cronobacter sakazakii in powdered infant formula for infants under six months of age in Ethiopia. BMC Microbiology, 26, 307. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12866-025-04380-y；World Health Organization & FAO (2007). Safe preparation, storage and handling of powdered infant formula: guidelines. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241595414
6

No honey under 1 year

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Under 1, no honey — honey water, honey in solids, honey pastries all count. Honey may carry botulism spores; adult flora suppresses them, infants' can't. Homemade pickles and ferments run the same logic.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
The US CDC: "do not feed honey to children under 1" because "honey can contain bacteria that cause botulism." Adult gut flora suppresses the spores (the bacterium's dormant form); infants' cannot
Note
The ban covers honey water, honey-mixed solids, and honey pastries — and, by the same logic, homemade pickles and ferments for infants.
Sources (1 references)
US CDC. Preventing Botulism. https://www.cdc.gov/botulism/prevention/index.html
7

The birth-day vitamin K injection is non-negotiable

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Newborns store little vitamin K; deficiency bleeds, and the late form often bleeds into the brain. Where prevention isn't routine, 478 per 100,000 newborns bleed; the injection cuts an estimated 78.5%-plus. Proper hospitals give it routinely; home or irregular-facility births demand asking.

Cost
0 to a few dozen yuan, usually inside the delivery bill already.
Benefit
Newborn vitamin K stores run low; deficiency causes hemorrhagic disease, the late form often intracranial. The Belgian consensus: "1 or 2 mg vitamin K intramuscularly once at birth." Where systematic prophylaxis is absent, incidence ran 478 per 100,000 — the Tashkent figure from 42,000 newborns — with prevention estimated to cut incidence "above 78.5%"
Note
Proper Chinese hospitals inject routinely — no effort needed. Home or irregular births: confirm actively. Oral dosing underperforms injection; injection here means into the muscle.
Sources (2 references)
Fiesack S, Smits A, Rayyan M, et al. (2021). Nutrients, 13(11), 4109. https://doi.org/10.3390/nu13114109；Tursunov D, Yoshida Y, Yrysov K, et al. (2018). Nagoya Journal of Medical Science, 80(1), 11. https://doi.org/10.18999/nagjms.80.1.11
8

Under 3 months, 38 °C means straight to hospital — no watching at home

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Under 3 months, 38 °C means hospital — no home observation, no fever medicine then waiting. Serious bacterial infection at this age may show fever alone, so "looks fine" is no reason to wait. Under 8 days, guidelines don't even cover it — faster still.

Cost
Registration and tests, a few hundred yuan.
Benefit
The AAP guideline covers well-appearing term infants 8 to 60 days, defining fever as "temperature ≥38.0 °C," with three age bands — 8–21, 22–28, and 29–60 days — each with its pathway. Under 8 days falls outside the guideline entirely: even more reason for immediate care
Note
At this age, serious bacterial infection may present as fever alone — "looks fine" justifies no waiting. No self-dosed antipyretics-then-waiting either.
Sources (1 references)
Pantell RH, Roberts KB, Adams WG, et al. (2021). Evaluation and Management of Well-Appearing Febrile Infants 8 to 60 Days Old. Pediatrics, 148(2), e2021052228. https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2021-052228
9

However exhausted or furious: never shake a baby

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Babies carry heavy heads on weak necks. Hard shaking bleeds the brain and eyes — killing or disabling for life. Gentle rocking to sleep isn't it; uncontrolled violent shaking is. Near the edge: baby back in the crib, you step away minutes — crying alone beats being shaken.

Cost
Free. The hard part: stopping your hands when most depleted or angry.
Benefit
Large head-to-body ratio plus weak neck muscles: violent shaking causes intracranial and retinal hemorrhage — fatal or permanently disabling. Gentle lulling isn't the danger; uncontrolled shaking is. Medicine calls it abusive head trauma — the leading cause of traumatic head-injury death under 2, killing nearly 2,250 US children under 5 from 1999 to 2014
Note
At the edge of losing control: baby into the crib, you away for minutes. Crying alone is far safer than shaking in arms. Solo caregivers running chronic sleep debt need this most. Handling your own state: Section 3.
Sources (2 references)
Spies EL, Klevens J (2016). Fatal Abusive Head Trauma Among Children Aged <5 Years — United States, 1999–2014. MMWR 65(20):505-509. https://doi.org/10.15585/mmwr.mm6520a1；Choudhary AK et al. (2018). Consensus statement on abusive head trauma in infants and young children. Pediatric Radiology 48(8):1048-1065. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00247-018-4149-1
10

Diapers: judge by three things — fit, change frequency, and inspection notices — never brand

Grade CValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

No official body ranks "best brand." Checkable: the market regulator's sampling notices and incident investigations. Expensive ≠ safe; imported ≠ compliant. Small packs for a week first — rash and pressure marks decide — then stock.

Cost
Two-three hundred to over a thousand monthly, by tier.
Benefit
No official "best brand" ranking exists, so this book recommends none. Two checkable sources: SAMR sampling notices and regulators' incident investigations. After the June 2026 "diaper formamide" attention, SAMR convened a joint investigation team
Note
The team promised publication; findings remain unpublished (TODO: verify — as of 2026-09-30, neither the SAMR site nor recent national sampling notices carry conclusions). How to buy: expensive ≠ safe, imported ≠ compliant; small packs for a week first. Diaper rash traces mostly to infrequent changes and poor breathability, brand mattering less than imagined. Sampling-notice lookups: Section 5.
Sources (2 references)
市场监管总局 (2026-06-22). 市场监管总局牵头成立联合调查组核查「婴幼儿纸尿裤甲酰胺问题」：「针对媒体反映的"婴幼儿纸尿裤甲酰胺问题"，市场监管总局、工业和信息化部、国家卫生健康委、国家疾控局高度重视，成立联合调查组，核查婴幼儿纸尿裤甲酰胺有关问题，并依法依规处理。有关情况将及时公布。」. https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2026/art_78c0425db7604b27…；中国政府网转载. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202606/content_7072931.htm
11

Big items in the order "borrow, buy used, buy new" — never one full set at once

Grade CValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Strollers, cribs, swaddles, and toys serve briefly — used markets brim. Borrow first, buy used second, buy new last: thousands saved. Two things never used: car seats and mattresses — crash damage hides from eyes. Confinement clubs and early-education courses: 24-hour cooling before deciding.

Cost
No extra spending; savings usually run to four figures. The hard part: resisting the one-shot setup.
Benefit
Brief service lives leave second-hand supply far exceeding demand. Two true exceptions — car seats and mattresses — where crash-damaged structure stays invisible
Note
Confinement clubs, early-education classes, and infant swim gyms: this book neither recommends nor rejects — but all are optional big spends suiting Section 5's cooling-off.
Sources
作者经验，无直接文献；安全座椅的证据见第 1 节，冲动消费见第 5 节
12

Severe eczema or egg allergy: don't dodge peanuts — add early under medical guidance, but never whole nuts

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Infants with severe eczema or egg allergy eating peanut regularly from 4–11 months ran 1.9% peanut allergy at 5, versus 13.7% among avoiders. Skin-test-positive kids: 10.6% versus 35.3%. See a doctor first. Never whole peanuts — airway.

Cost
A jar of peanut butter runs tens of yuan; feeding a few times weekly is effortless. One doctor's evaluation precedes adding.
Benefit
The UK LEAP randomized trial: 640 infants with severe eczema, egg allergy, or both, enrolled at 4–11 months, randomized to regular peanut consumption or avoidance, assessed at 60 months. Among the 530 initially skin-test-negative, avoidance ran 13.7% allergic versus 1.9% consumption (P<0.001); among the 98 weakly positive, 35.3% versus 10.6% (P=0.004). Serious adverse events didn't differ
Note
Only thinned peanut butter or peanut powder stirred into food — never whole nuts. The health commission's core information is plain: "whole peanuts, nuts, and jelly are easily aspirated, causing choking; infants and toddlers should avoid them." Choking response: Section 13, item 26. This entry targets high-risk children — severe eczema or existing egg allergy. Medical evaluation precedes introduction — never home trials: LEAP skin-tested every child, excluding reactions over 4 mm. General-population evidence runs much weaker: in the 1,162-infant EAT trial, by group assignment early introduction ran 5.6% food allergy versus 7.1% routine, nonsignificant (P=0.32), significant only among actual compliers (2.4% versus 7.3%) — an analysis prone to inflation, the authors themselves conceding per-protocol failed to establish efficacy while confirming safety. Chinese official feeding documents take no position on early-versus-avoid; this entry follows the international trials. Timing: LEAP began at 4 months, China starts solids at 6 (item 4) — high-risk start age and method follow the doctor.
Sources (3 references)
Du Toit G, Roberts G, Sayre PH, et al. (2015). Randomized trial of peanut consumption in infants at risk for peanut allergy. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(9), 803-813. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1414850；国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2020). 婴幼儿喂养健康教育核心信息. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-08/01/content_553…；Perkin MR et al. (2016). Randomized Trial of Introduction of Allergenic Foods in Breast-Fed Infants. New England Journal of Medicine, 374(18), 1733-1743. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1514210（备注里那项一般婴儿试验 EAT）
13

Newborn jaundice red flags — yellow within 24 hours, deepening, unarousable or refusing feeds, pale stools: same-day hospital

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Over 80% of newborns yellow slightly and self-resolve. Yellow within 24 hours, deepening yellow, unusual sleepiness or unarousability, feeding refusal, floppy or stiff body — same-day hospital. Pale stools suggest biliary atresia — prompt workup. Bilirubin high enough injures the brain for life.

Cost
Registration and bilirubin testing, under a few hundred yuan; phototherapy usually runs about two in-hospital days. The hard part: going while the baby still looks fine.
Benefit
The AAP 2022 guideline: "more than 80% of newborns develop some jaundice." High bilirubin causes acute bilirubin encephalopathy and kernicterus — "a permanent, disabling neurologic condition" presenting with athetoid cerebral palsy, upgaze palsy, enamel hypoplasia, and hearing loss. Jaundice "within 24 hours of birth" ranks among risk factors for severe hyperbilirubinemia. The NHS parent guidance splits two tiers: emergency — jaundice with unusual drowsiness or unarousability, feeding refusal, floppy or stiff body, or seizures, or jaundice before 24 hours; prompt appointment — jaundice past 24 hours worsening or persisting, dark or brown urine, pale cream stools. Globally, 2010 saw about 480,000 newborns with Rh disease or extreme hyperbilirubinemia: 24% died, 13% developed kernicterus, and over 83% of kernicterus survivors carried one or more impairments. Pale stools suggest biliary atresia, where Kasai surgery within 60 days markedly improves outcomes: Taiwan's stool-color card in every child-health handbook lifted within-60-day surgery from 60% in 2004 to 74.3% in 2005; a nationwide study found the card era cutting biliary-atresia mortality from 26.2% to 15.9% — before-after, not trial
Note
Phototherapy uses special light on the skin to convert bilirubin into excretable forms. No sun-substitutes: the AAP holds home sunlight can't be made both safe and burn-free — not recommended. No water or glucose water to "flush" — likewise unrecommended. Eyeballing depth misestimates bilirubin; NICE forbids eyes-only judgment — when unsure, measure. Under 38 weeks, prior phototreated siblings, and underfed breastfed infants run heavier. Follow-up per the national basic-service rules: home visit within a week of discharge, clinic follow-up at 28–30 days, jaundice checked both times; doctor-scheduled bilirubin rechecks run on schedule. Term infants yellowing past 14 days, preterm past 21: NICE requires conjugated-bilirubin testing and stool inspection. Jaundice never delays vaccination (item 3). Newborn screening: Section 27, item 13.
Sources (7 references)
Kemper AR, Newman TB, Slaughter JL, et al. (2022). Clinical Practice Guideline Revision: Management of Hyperbilirubinemia in the Newborn Infant 35 or More Weeks of Gestation. Pediatrics, 150(3), e2022058859. https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2022-058859；NHS. Jaundice in babies（2026-03-24 审阅）. https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/jaundice-newborn/；NICE (2010, 2023 修订). Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days (CG98), 1.2.6、1.7.1. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg98/chapter/Recommendations；Bhutani VK, Zipursky A, Blencowe H, et al. (2013). Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and Rhesus disease of the newborn: incidence and impairment estimates for 2010 at regional and global levels. Pediatric Research, 74(Suppl 1), 86-100. https://doi.org/10.1038/pr.2013.208；Hsiao CH, Chang MH, Chen HL, et al. (2008). Universal screening for biliary atresia using an infant stool color card in Taiwan. Hepatology, 47(4), 1233-1240. https://doi.org/10.1002/hep.22182；Lee M, Chen SC, Yang HY, et al. (2016). Infant Stool Color Card Screening Helps Reduce the Hospitalization Rate and Mortality of Biliary Atresia: A 14-Year Nationwide Cohort Study in Taiwan. Medicine, 95(12), e3166. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000003166；国家卫生计生委 (2017). 国家基本公共卫生服务规范（第三版），0～6 岁儿童健康管理服务规范. https://www.nhc.gov.cn/ewebeditor/uploadfile/2017/04/201704…
14

Vegan during pregnancy or nursing: supplement B12 daily; the baby's solids need animal foods — insistence on full vegan needs a doctor

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

B12 lives almost only in meat, eggs, and dairy. Vegan mothers without supplements run deficient milk, and babies typically fail at 4–8 months: poor growth, developmental delay, and prolonged deficiency can leave irreversible neurologic damage. Solids need animal foods daily.

Cost
B12 supplements run tens of yuan a bottle, one daily; eggs, meat, and fish in solids cost little. The hard part: shifting a household convinced vegan is healthier.
Benefit
The US CDC's 2003 report covered two children, both breastfed by vegan mothers, both B12-deficient, both failing to grow and develop. The first mother had eaten vegan 7 years; her child hospitalized at 15 months with severe anemia and MRI-diffuse cerebral atrophy — improving on B12 but still speech- and language-delayed at 32 months. Maternal dietary deficiency is the leading infant cause; breastfed infants typically present at 4–8 months; prolonged deficits can leave irreversible neurologic damage scaled by severity and duration. Reliable unfortified sources are animal foods alone — meat, dairy, eggs; plant B12 mostly lies unusable by humans; fortified cereals, soy milk, and nutritional yeast serve as stable sources. The report asks vegans — pregnant and lactating women especially — to know their B12 intake or consult nutrition professionals. ESPGHAN's 2017 complementary-feeding position: all infants need iron-rich complementary foods including meat or fortified items; vegan diets only under appropriate medical or dietetic supervision, with parents understanding the serious consequences of non-supplementation. The national 2020 core feeding information: solids no fewer than 4 kinds daily, including at least one animal food, one vegetable, and one grain-tuber
Note
Contested: the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics' 2016 position holds well-planned vegetarian and vegan diets appropriate at all life stages, pregnancy, lactation, infancy, and childhood included — while itself requiring reliable B12 sources, fortified foods or supplements, for vegans. The camps split on vegan infant feeding, not on B12 necessity. Lacto-ovo vegetarians run lower risk, though the second mother — 20 years vegetarian, nearly without meat, fish, or dairy — still failed. Early deficiency runs nonspecific; the CDC calls anemia markers unfit for screening. Poor growth or delay: volunteer the household's veganism at the doctor's. Don't refuse prescribed treatment for folk remedies — Section 16, item 4. Solids introduction: item 4; prenatal folic acid: Section 27, item 1.
Sources (4 references)

MMWR, 52(4), 61-64. https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/mm5204a1.htm；Fewtrell M, Bronsky J, Campoy C, et al. (2017). Complementary Feeding: A Position Paper by the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) Committee on Nutrition. Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition, 64(1), 119-132. https://doi.org/10.1097/MPG.0000000000001454；国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2020). 婴幼儿喂养健康教育核心信息. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-08/01/content_553…；Melina V, Craig W, Levin S (2016). Position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics: Vegetarian Diets. Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, 116(12), 1970-1980. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jand.2016.09.025（备注里的反方）

21. Travel abroad and safety overseas

11 entries

This section counts money and personal freedom, with a few entries touching personal safety. Abroad, the destination's law governs you, not China's — and what Chinese embassies and consulates can do has clear limits.

1

Before departure, check the foreign ministry's safety notices once — "do not travel" places stay unvisited

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The ministry grades foreign risk in four tiers, topping out at "do not travel." From 2026-09-15, avoiding high-risk countries is written into administrative regulation, with document and border staff reminding — and where necessary dissuading — travelers. Read the page before departure.

Cost
Free. Minutes on the consular-service site.
Benefit
The ministry publishes graded safety notices, roughly "take precautions," "heighten precautions," "travel with caution," and "do not travel." The new regulation of 2026-09-15 writes the personal duty in: "Chinese citizens shall follow foreign safety reminders and destination risk notices, avoiding travel to and stay in high-risk countries or regions," while requiring the immigration authorities to remind — and "where necessary dissuade" — those heading to top-tier or incident-surging destinations
Note
Notices shift with events; this book copies no list — check the page yourself. As of 2026-09-07, the column carried "do not travel"-class notices for Eswatini (2026-08-25), Palestine (2023-10-10), and Sudan (2023-04-17), plus Afghanistan (2023-02-17), Syria (2023-01-04), Peru (2022-12-29), and Somalia (2022-11-24), with separate notices for northern Myanmar and parts of the DRC. Tour operators carry disclosure duties too — demand written risk statements before joining a tour.
Sources (3 references)
国务院 (2026). 关于出境入境管理的规定（国令第 841 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173…（第二条）；国务院 (2023). 领事保护与协助条例（国令第 763 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761…（第十九、二十一条）；外交部领事司. 安全提醒. https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmzhw/lsbh/aqtx/
2

Save 12308 and the local consulate's protection line in your phone, plus a paper copy in your wallet — not after trouble starts

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

One rescue line exists. Domestic: 12308. Overseas: +86-10-12308. The hotline has answered 3-million-plus calls, with 500,000-plus consular-protection cases handled in the same period.

Cost
Free. Two numbers saved, one copy written, minutes.
Benefit
The global consular-protection emergency hotline runs 24 hours: domestically 12308; overseas +86-10-12308 or +86-10-65612308. Since 2014 it has fielded over 3 million calls, with the ministry and missions handling 500,000-plus cases
Note
The local mission keeps its own protection line, usually faster than the switchboard — look it up by country on the consular site and store both. A lost or dead phone defeats stored numbers: write a copy for the wallet or a family member.
Sources (2 references)
外交部、中国驻缅甸使领馆 (2023). 关于当前缅北地区安全局势的领事提醒. https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmzhw/lsbh/aqtx/202311/t20231109_11…；国务院新闻办 (2023). 国务院政策例行吹风会介绍领事保护与协助有关情况. https://www.gov.cn/xinwen/2023zccfh/11/index.htm
3

Know what consular protection can and cannot do: visits yes, springing you no, and the bills stay yours

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Arrested abroad, the mission can verify your situation, demand lawful and fair treatment, visit you, and observe trial. It cannot overturn verdicts or walk you out. Food, lodging, transport, and medical advanced by third parties revert to your bill. So prepare money and insurance beforehand — "the state will catch me" is not a plan.

Cost
Free. Minutes reading the boundary.
Benefit
On your arrest, the mission verifies with local authorities and demands lawful, fair handling — the regulation's words: "visit or contact per the host country's law and applicable treaties, learn the citizen's needs, and require the host authorities to give the citizen humanitarian and fair treatment." Missions may observe trials and demand protection of your procedural rights, urge emergency rescue when you're injured or disaster strikes, and assist families with aftermath. On money, the regulation is equally clear: "Chinese citizens, legal persons, and non-legal-person organizations that receive food, lodging, transport, medical goods or services from third parties during consular protection shall pay the costs properly borne by themselves" — advanced sums revert to you
Note
Missions pay no fines, medical bills, or tickets, and overturn no verdicts. They provide local lawyer, translator, medical, and funeral referrals, contact relatives, and locate relief channels. Prepare money and insurance yourself.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2023). 领事保护与协助条例（国令第 763 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761…（第九、十、十四、二十六条）
4

Buy insurance covering overseas medical and medical evacuation — not just flight-delay cover

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Overseas care is out-of-pocket: domestic insurance barely reimburses, consulates don't advance. What truly sinks a household isn't the clinic bill but hospitalization after serious injury and getting the person home — charter or medical escort. Two limits matter: overseas medical costs, and emergency medical evacuation and repatriation.

Cost
Short-term travel insurance, tens to hundreds of yuan.
Benefit
Overseas treatment bills are yours: domestic insurance barely reimburses, and consular protection doesn't advance them (item 3, per Article 26). What sinks households is hospitalization and evacuation: repatriation from an overseas hospital takes charter aircraft or medical escort — the priciest class of self-paid items. The US CDC: emergency transport from a remote area to a quality hospital "could otherwise cost more than $100,000." Two limits govern purchase: the overseas medical limit and the emergency-evacuation-and-repatriation limit
Note
$100,000 is a floor statement, not a range — no official or industry range statistics were found, so none quoted. Confirm three things before buying: destination coverage; exclusions on diving, skiing, and motorcycling; and direct-billing versus reimbursement. Visa-free destinations deserve cover equally.
Sources (2 references)
国务院 (2023). 领事保护与协助条例（国令第 763 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761…（第二十六条）；美国疾病控制与预防中心. 5

"Overseas high-pay recruitment" is fraud, full stop — scammed into telecom-fraud compounds, you return exit-barred

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Absurd salaries, no credentials asked, no proper contract, assembly in a border city, passport "kept for you" — go, and neither you nor your passport stays in your hands. Forged exit documents get stopped at the border; overseas crime involvement can bar exit 6 months to 3 years after return.

Cost
Free. The hard part: declining an attractive job with your own hands.
Benefit
The official characterization is blunt: people "deceived abroad or leaving illegally on fabricated grounds to engage in cross-border gambling, telecom fraud, and other illegal activity, gravely endangering people's lives and property." The new regulation tightens both ends. Exit: "grounds for exit, entry, stay, or residence shall be true and lawful" — false materials or statements mean no documents and no departure. Return: "Chinese citizens who engaged in illegal or criminal activity abroad harming national security or interests may... be barred from exit for 6 months to 3 years from the date of return"; administrative detention for fraudulently obtained documents or illegal exit-entry carries the same 6-month-to-3-year bar
Note
The markers are fixed: salaries far above the post, credentials waived, no proper contract, border-city assembly, visa handled and passport held. Northern Myanmar carries dedicated consular notices. Once there, liberty and passport leave your hands together.

6

Overseas cash withdrawal caps at 100,000 yuan yearly — across all cards under your name combined

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The cap isn't per card but across all your bank cards (supplementary cards included), per calendar year, 100,000 yuan. Once exhausted, no overseas withdrawals for the rest of the year and the next. Card spending runs untouched, and the yearly $50,000 FX quota stays unspent.

Cost
Free. Estimate cash needs beforehand and lean on card payments. The hard part: breaking the cash habit.
Benefit
Under SAFE's 2017 notice (effective 2018-01-01): "individuals holding domestic bank cards withdrawing cash abroad — all cards under the person's name (supplementary cards included) may not exceed the equivalent of 100,000 yuan per calendar year; exceeding the annual quota suspends overseas cash withdrawal on domestic cards for the remainder of the year and the following year." Borrowing or lending cards to evade the rules is barred. SAFE daily sends suspension lists to issuers, which must block listed holders' overseas withdrawals from 17:00 Beijing time that day. Listed individuals may query their withdrawal details at SAFE branches with ID. Foreign-currency cards' per-card daily cap moved from $1,000-equivalent to 10,000-yuan-equivalent; RMB cards hold at 10,000-yuan-equivalent. Violations punish under the FX regulations. The Q&A adds: the notice doesn't affect card spending abroad — food, lodging, transport, and shopping pay by card without touching the $50,000 convenience quota. Quotas compute from delayed batch data, "SAFE uses delayed control" rather than real-time interception. In 2016, 81% of overseas cash withdrawals ran under 30,000 yuan (national)
Note
Quotas reset January 1. Only withdrawal suspends; spending runs on. Genuinely needing large cash abroad: purchase FX under the individual FX measures and carry banknotes. Two withdrawal traps per UnionPay's page: dual-logo cards unable to select the UnionPay rail on some foreign ATMs, and local surcharges collected by acquirers, "unrelated to UnionPay." The same page advises debit over credit cards for withdrawal (overdraft interest). Lost, swallowed, or defrauded cards: Section 14, item 5.

7

Photograph passport, visa, and ID into the cloud; lose the passport — police report first, then a travel document

Grade CValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Lose the passport, and the mission issues a return document — provided you can prove who you are. Photos of the data and visa pages plus entry-exit records speed everything. You'll also need the local police report: exit checks and insurance claims honor it. Phones vanish with passports — don't store photos only on the phone.

Cost
Free. A few photos before departure.
Benefit
Missions issue return travel documents on proof of identity; clean photos of data and visa pages and travel records change the speed materially. Report locally first for the receipt — exit checks and insurers want it. The mission's entry point: the two numbers from item 2
Note
Store twice — cloud plus one family member — plus a paper copy apart from originals; photograph bank cards and prescriptions too. Phones die with passports, and cloud logins demanding SMS codes die with the phone: test login from another device before departure. Document photos are sensitive — encrypted storage is safer, but lost passwords lock everyone out, so the family copy is non-negotiable.

8

Overseas self-drive: confirm the destination accepts Chinese licenses — most "international driving permits" sold online are waste paper

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The "IDP" doesn't hold in mainland China: it's a translation instrument under the 1949 Geneva convention among 103 parties — mainland China absent. Nothing anyone issues domestically carries legal force. Whether a Chinese license drives depends on the destination's own rules — unconfirmed, don't drive.

Cost
Free. One regulation check before departure.
Benefit
The "international driving permit" is a translation document mutually recognized among parties to the 1949 Road Traffic Convention (Geneva, 1949-09-19, effective 1952-03-26), currently 103 parties. Mainland China isn't among them — China issues no IDP, and any domestic agency "processing one" produces nothing lawful. Driving on a Chinese license turns on the destination's rules: some accept it with notarized translation, some require local exchange, some reject it outright
Note
In most countries unlicensed driving is criminal or heavily fined — and post-accident insurance mostly refuses to pay, the true cost. Check two ways: the destination's "notice for Chinese citizens" on the consular site, or written confirmation from the rental company. Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, and select states run separate arrangements.

United Nations Treaty Collection. Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 — status of treaties. https://treaties.un.org/pages/ViewDetailsV.aspx?src=TREATY&…
9

Visa, study-abroad, and immigration agents: ask whether they're filed with the immigration authorities first

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

From 2026-09-15, such agents file with the immigration authorities. "Guaranteed pass," "guaranteed visa," "we'll do your documents" sit among the express prohibitions. Your own form errors cost a refusal; fabricated materials leave a stain on your future entry-exit record.

Cost
Free. One filing question, and keep the papers.
Benefit
The 2018 abolition of pre-approval for private entry-exit intermediaries bred rapid growth and problems — "unclear agency numbers, some agencies handling business illegally, harming exit-entry parties' lawful rights." From 2026-09-15, filing management replaces it: agencies report within 15 days of establishment, existing ones within 90 days of effect. Prohibited: publishing false information or exaggerated and misleading solicitation; providing or assisting false materials and irregular visa, stay-residence, or passport processing; leaking, selling, or unlawfully providing privacy or personal information; and organizing or assisting cross-border crime. Offshore entities may not provide such services in China
Note
Agents mouthing "guaranteed pass" are doing the expressly prohibited; discovered, the stain lands on your visa record. Your own errors cost a refusal; fabricated materials cost far more. Unpaid policy consulting and information lookup don't count as intermediary services.

10

Never issue invitation letters for strangers, nor lend your name to entry-exit procedures

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Issuing someone's invitation letter or application materials with false contents bills the issuer: individuals 5,000–10,000 yuan plus confiscation of gains; units 10,000–50,000, handlers another 5,000–10,000. One favor, one bill.

Cost
Free. The hard part: refusing a favor to a face.
Benefit
Issuers answer for truth: "individuals issuing false invitation letters or other application materials for others' exit-entry, stay, or residence applications face immigration-authority fines of 5,000 to 10,000 yuan, with illegal gains confiscated." Units issuing false materials face 10,000–50,000 yuan, with directly responsible managers and other liable persons fined another 5,000–10,000
Note
Same class as Section 8's "never carry for strangers": materials under your name land consequences on you. Public officials and military personnel seeking foreign nationality or residence through agents — agents must refuse and report to the supervision organ.

11

Before departure: send itinerary, lodging, and companions to one family member, and agree on a contact cadence

Grade CValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If you go missing abroad, family can seek the mission, which shares local police procedures and presses cases after filing — provided someone at home knows where you should be and when you should call. Flight numbers, address, companions' phones, and the agreed cadence, sent to one person, suffice.

Cost
Free. One message before departure.
Benefit
When Chinese citizens go missing abroad, relatives may seek the missions — "the diplomatic mission shall provide local reporting methods and other rescue information," pressing local police after filing. All of it starts only when someone at home knows your expected whereabouts and contact schedule
Note
Four items suffice: flight number, lodging address, companions' names and phones, agreed contact frequency. For signal-poor or insecure regions, add the "no news for X days means report to police" line. Every rescue procedure above requires family knowing your itinerary first.

22. How to relax: entertainment venues and stress relief

10 entries

The first half covers which entertainment money is wasted and where the exits are — money and personal freedom. The second half covers stress relief — energy and overall mortality. The two halves never convert into each other. Section 3 covered the first steps when mood sinks; here are the concrete practices.

1

Before entering KTV, bars, or escape rooms: locate the fire exits — locked or blocked means another venue

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

By regulation, venues must keep evacuation routes and exits clear during business — no blocking, no locking, no barriers, no obscured signage. Internet cafés likewise. Failure is unlawful and reportable. Basement rooms, single exits, cluttered corridors: change venues.

Cost
Free. Ten seconds looking up at the door.
Benefit
This is the operator's statutory duty. The regulation: "during business hours, entertainment venues shall keep evacuation routes and safety exits clear, not blocking or locking evacuation routes and safety exits, and not setting fences or other evacuation-impeding obstacles on them," with "conspicuous directional signs on evacuation routes and safety exits, not obscured or covered." Internet cafés: "during business hours, blocking or locking doors, windows, evacuation routes, and safety exits is prohibited," as are open-flame lighting and smoking
Note
Any one of these means change venues: basement rooms, a single exit, cluttered corridors, dead exit signs. These venues burn with thick smoke, narrow passages, crowds, and alcohol — escape windows measured in seconds. The reporting number must be posted on in-venue warning signs.
Sources (2 references)
国务院 (2006). 娱乐场所管理条例（国令第 458 号，第二十、二十一条）. http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297…；国务院 (2002). 互联网上网服务营业场所管理条例（国令第 363 号，第二十一条）. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61788.htm
2

Demand the price list before ordering — venues must post prices; "play first, settle later" gets refused

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Services and goods must be posted and the list shown on request. "Sky-high drink" disputes nearly all involve unseen price lists and verbal post-hoc bills. Request the list on entering, photograph it; request a confirmed order list; disputes mean 12315 on the spot.

Cost
Free. One ask. The hard part: asking prices to a face.
Benefit
The regulation: "entertainment venues providing entertainment services or selling goods shall post prices clearly and present the price list to consumers, and may not force or deceive consumers into accepting services or buying goods." Violations draw statutory penalties. "Sky-high drink" disputes overwhelmingly cluster where no list was shown and settlement followed verbal quotes
Note
Practice: request the list entering the room — paper or electronic — and photograph it; request the confirmed order after ordering; ask prices on every recommended "special blend" or "fruit platter" first; on disputes, 12315 immediately. Never pay first and litigate later — payment multiplies your proof burden.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2006). 娱乐场所管理条例（国令第 458 号，第二十九、五十三条）. http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297…
3

Someone passing "things" around the room: leave at once — harboring and providing aren't "helping a friend"

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Venues may not sell, provide, or tolerate drugs — violations mean 3–6 months' closure, graver, license revocation. Personal use draws administrative punishment. Letting people "use" in your booked room or residence is harboring drug use — criminal. Unknown powders, tablets, or pods offered: leave on the spot.

Cost
Free. Standing up and walking out. The hard part: leaving a full table.
Benefit
The regulation bans venues from "selling or providing drugs, or organizing, forcing, instigating, inducing, deceiving, or harboring others' drug use or injection." Staff may neither use nor facilitate. Violations: confiscation, 3–6 months' suspension; serious, license revocation. Venues must post anti-drug, anti-gambling, and anti-prostitution warning signs with reporting numbers
Note
Unknown powders, tablets, or e-pods offered for a "try" — leave, don't spectate. Your personal exposure outweighs the venue's. Personal use is itself punishable; letting friends "use here" in your room or residence constitutes the crime of harboring drug use.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2006). 娱乐场所管理条例（国令第 458 号，第十四、三十、四十二条）. http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297…
4

No candy or snacks from strangers, no drinks that left your sight, no pods handed over

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Today's drugs don't look like drugs. Synthetic-cannabinoid "high" vapes look near-identical to ordinary ones and get passed around bars, KTVs, and hotels. Tricking someone into use draws 10–15 days plus 1,000–5,000 yuan — and the tricked user draws 10–15 days too. Drinks off-sight get replaced.

Cost
Free. Refuse what's handed over; a drink that left sight gets replaced.
Benefit
Today's drugs don't look like drugs. Synthetic cannabinoids have been scheduled as a class since 2021-07-01; SPP-reported cases describe oils that "can be colored and flavored with food coloring," "essentially identical in appearance to ordinary e-cigarettes," hawked in bars, KTVs, and hotels with minors running nearly four in ten of that year's use cases locally. Etomidate entered the class-2 psychotropics list on 2023-10-01. Inducing, instigating, deceiving, or forcing drug use draws 10–15 days plus 1,000–5,000 yuan; criminal grades run to 3 years, serious 3–7, forced 3–10, minors aggravated. The deceived carry consequences too: use draws 10–15 days plus up to 3,000 yuan; lighter cases up to 5 days or 1,000 yuan; possible 6–12-month entertainment-venue bans; addiction means 3 years' community rehab; refusal or relapse means 2 years' compulsory isolation, extendable 1 (national; punishments law since January 2026)
Note
Not only venues — school gates, gatherings, long rides alike; candy, drinks, or pods all the same. Drugging often precedes robbery, assault, and extortion — no official statistics, experience judgment. Replacing an off-sight drink beats pursuing after the fact. Unknown substances in venues: item 3. Carrying for others: Section 8, item 29.
Sources (5 references)
最高人民检察院 (2021). 江苏苏州吴江区：办案检察官揭秘披着潮流外衣的新型毒品. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202110/t20211011_531831.shtml；国家药监局、公安部、国家卫生健康委 (2023). 关于调整麻醉药品和精神药品目录的公告（2023 年第 120 号）. https://yjj.sh.gov.cn/qtgzwj/20230911/3b612c94e35b4b63abba3…（上海市药监局转载，原文页 nmpa.gov.cn 在本机返回 412）；全国人大常委会 (2025). 治安管理处罚法（2025 年修订，第八十四、八十五条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml；全国人大 (1997). 刑法（第三百五十三条）. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml；全国人大常委会 (2007). 禁毒法（第三十三、三十八、四十七条）. http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/post_2520706.html（广东省人民政府转载）
5

Script-kill and escape rooms: skip those in residential buildings or below basement level one

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The 2022 five-department notice bars script-entertainment venues from residential buildings and below the first basement level. Dark, partitioned, flammable props, doors that open only by puzzle — fires there run far deadlier than in ordinary shops. Check the listing's address and floor; non-compliant means another venue.

Cost
Free. One question about the floor before booking.
Benefit
The 2022 notice is concrete: "script-entertainment business venues may not be located in residential buildings or below the first basement floor (the first basement floor excluded)," with venues implementing the safety and fire laws, "routinely knowing, checking, and correcting fire risks, and improving emergency evacuation and incipient-fire response." The same notice requires age advisories on scripts, bars minors from unsuitable scenarios, and restricts weekday provision to minors
Note
These venues run dark, partitioned, flammable, with puzzle-locked doors — fires there escape harder than ordinary shops. Listing pages show floor and building type; non-compliant, change venues.
Sources (1 references)
文化和旅游部、公安部、住房和城乡建设部、应急管理部、市场监管总局 (2022). 关于加强剧本娱乐经营场所管理的通知. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-06/27/content_569…
6

Mood low: walk or run — exercise's antidepressant effect scales with intensity

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Brisk walking or jogging improves most; yoga, strength training, and tai chi/qigong follow closely. Higher intensity, better effect; strength and yoga stick best. Evidence quality runs low — what's certain is movement over stillness, in whatever form you'll keep.

Cost
Free. Half-hour sessions. The hard part: moving when you least want to.
Benefit
Pooling 218 randomized trials — 495 arms, 14,170 participants meeting major-depression criteria — in a Bayesian network meta-analysis against active controls (usual care, placebo pills), effect sizes in Hedges' g (more negative, more improvement): walking/jogging −0.62 (95% CrI −0.80 to −0.45, the credible interval), yoga −0.55 (−0.73 to −0.36), strength training −0.49 (−0.69 to −0.29), mixed aerobic −0.43 (−0.61 to −0.24), tai chi/qigong −0.42 (−0.65 to −0.21). "The effects of exercise were proportional to prescribed intensity," with strength training and yoga most tolerable
Note
Contested: the authors flag that only 1 of 218 trials ran clean; walking/jogging grades "low" certainty, the rest "very low." Exercise can't blind participants — knowing you exercise colors the report, an expectation that can't be removed. The direction holds: move over stay, intensity not too low, the form you'll keep. This expands Section 3's "move first" and replaces no prescribed treatment.
Sources (1 references)
Noetel M, Sanders T, Gallardo-Gómez D, et al. (2024). Effect of exercise for depression: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. BMJ, 384, e075847. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-075847
7

When anxiety disrupts life, mindfulness-based stress reduction matches a common anxiolytic

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Diagnosed anxiety-disorder patients completing 8 weeks of MBSR improved almost identically to escitalopram. Nearly 80% of the drug arm had adverse reactions, some quitting; the mindfulness arm ran 15%, zero quits. The course must be standardized 8-week MBSR — a meditation app isn't.

Cost
Courses cost a little; 8 weekly sessions plus daily home practice. The hard part: 8 weeks of daily practice.
Benefit
A non-inferiority randomized trial at 3 US academic centers: 276 adults with diagnosed anxiety disorders, 1:1 randomized to 8-week MBSR or flexible-dose escitalopram (10–20 mg); 208 completed. End-point anxiety severity (CGI-S): mindfulness −1.35, drug −1.43; difference −0.07 (95% CI −0.38 to 0.23; P=0.65 — indistinguishable from zero), the lower bound inside the pre-set non-inferiority margin of −0.495. Side effects split widely: drug 78.6% with at least one related adverse event, 10 quitting; mindfulness 15.4%, zero quits
Note
The trial used standardized 8-week MBSR — no meditation app equivalent. It applies to those meeting anxiety-disorder criteria; the doctor still comes first. If side-effect fears have kept you untreated, here's an equally evidenced option.
Sources (1 references)
Hoge EA, Bui E, Mete M, Dutton MA, Baker AW, Simon NM (2023). Mindfulness-based stress reduction vs escitalopram for the treatment of adults with anxiety disorders: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA Psychiatry, 80(1), 13-21. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2022.3679
8

For on-the-spot recovery, 5 minutes of "cyclic sighing": two-stage inhale, long exhale

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Five minutes of breathing daily for a month improved mood and slowed breathing better than equal-time mindfulness. Among breathing patterns, exhale-lengthening cyclic sighing won. Method: nasal inhale, a second small sip to fill the lungs, then a slow mouth exhale to empty. One trial, self-reported — but free.

Cost
Free. Five minutes daily.
Benefit
A home-based randomized trial compared three 5-minute daily breathing practices against equal-time mindfulness over 1 month: cyclic sighing (exhale-emphasized), box breathing (equal inhale-hold-exhale), and cyclic hyperventilation with retention (long inhale, short exhale). Mixed-effects modeling favored breathing over mindfulness — cyclic sighing above all — on mood improvement (P<0.05) and respiratory-rate reduction (P<0.05)
Note
Method: nasal inhale, brief second sip to fill, then a long slow mouth exhale, 5 minutes. One home trial, self-reported, small sample — better than meditation but no problem-solver. Free, 5 minutes, anywhere: high value.
Sources (1 references)
Balban MY, Neri E, Kogon MM, et al. (2023). Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal. Cell Reports Medicine, 4(1), 100895. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2022.100895
9

Treat "regularly seeing people" as a health expense — not just when mood dips

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

The socially isolated run about 30% higher mortality; the lonely about a quarter; those living alone about 30% — stronger under 65. All observational: the already-ill may live alone more.

Cost
A little money and meeting time. The hard part: initiating while feeling fine.
Benefit
Pooling 70 prospective studies — 3.4 million participants, average 7 years — social isolation, loneliness, and living alone each tracked higher mortality. Adjusted weighted odds ratios: isolation 1.29, loneliness 1.26, living alone 1.32 — roughly 30%, a quarter, and 30% higher — effects similar in size and larger under 65
Note
Contested: observational associations, no assignment, causation unsortable — the already-ill isolate more. The authors rank social connection alongside smoking and obesity, but no randomized trial shows added socializing lowering mortality. No conflict with Section 3's "cut draining relationships": that trims what drains you, this preserves what restores you.
Sources (1 references)
Holt-Lunstad J, Smith TB, Baker M, Harris T, Stephenson D (2015). Loneliness and social isolation as risk factors for mortality: a meta-analytic review. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 10(2), 227-237. https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691614568352
10

Count neighborhood greenery when choosing housing — but don't expect park visits to extend life

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Better greenery within 500 meters of home tracks lower mortality — about 4% per 0.1 NDVI. It measures home surroundings, not park visits. Green neighborhoods house wealthier, cleaner-air residents — so read it as a housing criterion, not a longevity prescription.

Cost
Free. Glance at the greenery while viewing.
Benefit
A meta-analysis of 9 cohorts across 7 countries, 8.32 million people, measuring greenness within 500 meters by normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI). Each 0.1 increase ran pooled mortality HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.94–0.97) — about 4% lower, the true value between 3% and 6%. Seven of nine studies found greener-lower mortality beyond chance; two found nothing
Note
Contested: heterogeneity runs extreme (I²=95%); the measure is residential greenness, not park visits; greener-dwelling people run richer, cleaner air, and more exercise — inseparable contributors. Don't read "parks extend life"; the usable part is greenery as a free housing criterion. NDVI: bare ground and concrete near 0, dense canopy near 1 — 0.1 approximates the jump from a bare block to tree-lined streets.
Sources (1 references)
Rojas-Rueda D, Nieuwenhuijsen MJ, Gascon M, Perez-Leon D, Mudu P (2019). Green spaces and mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. The Lancet Planetary Health, 3(11), e469-e477. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2542-5196(19)30215-3

23. What skills are worth learning

23 entries

This section counts money and time — item 2 adds mortality. The first six entries answer one question: keep studying or not? Item 1 states which options the law removes; item 2 counts education against lifespan; item 3 shows where the nation's education levels sit. Item 4 covers funding when unaffordable; item 5 the paths when regular high school is missed; item 6 turns "study or work" into a self-computed problem. The next seven answer: once you decide to learn, how to choose. China's occupation-by-occupation wage statistics resist verification from public official channels, so only sourced items appear: what an extra year of schooling adds to wages (the returns to education), how to verify certificates, where training subsidies come from, and which skill dimensions resist replacement. Specific monthly wages by trade: no numbers here. Items 14–19 answer the third question: how to learn with the least time — counted in time, never converted to money. Items 20–23 answer the fourth: with professional-technical work underway — where to file professional titles, how to sit them, which traps, what they're worth. Entries in this section are grouped by theme, with item numbers in parentheses. Keep studying or not: under 16 means no "go work" option (item 1), education counted in mortality (item 2), the national education structure (item 3), unaffordable means computing by policy first (item 4), paths after missing regular high school (item 5), study-versus-work as one problem (item 6). What to learn: the returns to another year (item 7), check the occupational-qualification catalog before certificates (item 8), training through subsidized channels (item 9), pick hands-on, on-site-judgment skills (item 10), check whether the skill has graded evaluation (item 11), check local shortage lists (item 12), choose job-ready short programs (item 13). Learning efficiently: self-test after closing the book (item 14), spread practice across days (item 15), don't make highlighting the main method (item 16), interleave problem types (item 17), don't pick methods by learning styles (item 18), self-quiz what must be memorized (item 19). Professional titles: find the filing channels (item 20), accounting junior-intermediate titles by national exam (item 21), no agency-filed titles (item 22), a title doesn't equal a raise (item 23).

1

Under 16, "going to work" isn't an option: the hiring unit pays 5,000 yuan monthly per child laborer — anyone willing is operating black

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Junior-high graduates run 15–16, straddling the line. Under 16, hiring you is illegal — 5,000 yuan per child laborer per month. Whoever takes you knowingly breaks the law; when things go wrong, medical bills and compensation have only that unit to answer, and if it stonewalls or runs, no one stands behind it.

Cost
Free. One minute checking your age.
Benefit
Compulsory Education Law Article 11: "children who have reached six shall be enrolled by parents or guardians to accept and complete compulsory education." Article 14: "employers are prohibited from hiring school-age children and adolescents subject to compulsory education." Article 58: failure without justified reason to enroll draws local-government criticism and correction orders. The Prohibition of Child Labor provisions, Article 2: state organs, social organizations, enterprises, institutions, private non-enterprises, and individual businesses "may not hire minors under 16." Article 6: fines "at 5,000 yuan per child laborer per month," doubling to 10,000 on uncorrected continuation; Article 7: introducers fined 5,000 per child placed; Article 10: sick or injured child laborers get employer-funded treatment with full medical and living costs, plus lump-sum compensation for disability or death; Article 13's sole exception: arts and sports units may, with guardian consent, hire professional performers and athletes under 16 (national)
Note
The beneficiary is yourself. Past 16, working is lawful — but the posts open to a 16-year-old without credentials are exactly item 10's most replaceable: fixed procedures, machine-vulnerable. Section 19's overtime, leave, and injury benefits presuppose employment relationships with evidence; black work lacks both, taking the money with it.

Count "is schooling useful" in the mortality account too: each added year of education lowers adult death risk about 1.9%

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: small

Each additional year of schooling runs about 1.9% lower adult mortality — strongest at 18–49 (about 2.9% per year), 0.8% past 70. Those who keep reading usually started advantaged; how much is schooling itself, the design can't split.

Cost
Free — the cost is the years themselves; tuition is item 4's business. The hard part: reading through without dropping out.
Benefit
A systematic review and meta-analysis (literature January 1980–May 2023; 603 studies, 59 countries, 70 sites, 10,355 observations) found a dose-response between education and all-cause adult mortality: each year averages 1.9% lower risk (95% UI 1.8–2.0); ages 18–49, 2.9% (2.8–3.0); past 70, 0.8% (0.6–1.0). No sex difference, none by country development level
Note
Contested: the authors themselves report publication bias (p<0.0001) and extreme between-study spread. All observational, no assignment; years of schooling tangle with family means, region, and occupation — the 1.9% can't isolate schooling from "those who kept reading started ahead." The reverse path tangles too: childhood illness and psychological distress drive both dropout and early death, inflating schooling's apparent effect. So it strongly establishes co-direction, not "attending buys 1.9% longevity." Benefit "small": readers face 3–4 more years, compounding under a tenth by this book's threshold. Beneficiary: yourself.
Sources (1 references)
IHME-CHAIN Collaborators (2024). Effects of education on adult mortality: a global systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Public Health, 9(3), e155-e165. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(23)00306-7

Before judging whether credentials "devalued": the national structure — only 15,467 per 100,000 hold college education (2020 census; 2025 sampling projects about 19%)

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

At the 2020 census, about 15% of the population held associate degrees or above; 2025 sampling projects about 19% — a few points in five years. Junior-high remains the modal attainment both times. The over-15 average ran 9.91 years of schooling — barely past junior high. So junior-high in China isn't "sufficient" — it's the most ordinary tier.

Cost
Free. One glance at the numbers.
Benefit
The Seventh Census (reference moment 2020-11-01): 218,360,767 with college education or above; 213,005,258 senior high (including secondary vocational); 487,163,489 junior high; 349,658,828 primary. Versus the 2010 Sixth Census, per 100,000: college rose from 8,930 to 15,467; senior high from 14,032 to 15,088; junior high fell from 38,788 to 34,507; primary from 26,779 to 24,767. Average schooling of the over-15 rose from 9.08 to 9.91 years; illiteracy from 4.08% to 2.67%. The 2025 1% sample (reference moment 2025-11-01, 20.52 million sampled) projects 1,405.45 million total: 272.33 million college-plus, 242.72 million senior high, 452.83 million junior high, 331.22 million primary — the bulletin omitting per-100,000 figures; computing them, college runs about 19.4% and junior high about 32.2%, still the modal tier
Note
These numbers speak only to scarcity in the population; individual worth gets computed by item 6's method. Note the census counts everyone including children and elders — the young run far more college-heavy, so comparing against all ages overstates your edge. Conversely, using it to rebut "schooling is useless" holds — the denominator is the entire competing workforce. The 2025 figures are sample projections against the census's enumeration; the two run on different frames, so they're listed side by side, the new never replacing the old; 19.4% and 32.2% computed from the bulletin's own counts. Beneficiary: yourself.

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Public secondary-vocational schools waive tuition for rural students, urban agriculture-track students, and hardship cases; vocational and ordinary-senior-high stipends run 2,300 yuan yearly from spring 2025; college stipends 3,700, student loans to 20,000 yearly. Money shortfalls can defer or reroute — rarely must one quit for work now.

Cost
Free. One visit with documents to the school's student-aid office before term.
Benefit
The tuition waiver has run since fall 2012: "all rural (including county-town) students, urban agriculture-track students, and financially disadvantaged students among full-time registered grades 1–3 of public secondary vocational schools exempt from tuition (arts-performance majors excepted)." The 2024 adjustments: college national stipends from 3,300 to 3,700 yuan; the encouragement scholarship from 5,000 to 6,000 (both from fall 2024, the scholarship from 2024); secondary-vocational and senior-high stipends from 2,000 to 2,300 (spring 2025); national student loans — undergraduates "from no more than 16,000 to no more than 20,000 yuan per person per year," graduate students "from 20,000 to 25,000," both from fall 2024, at LPR minus 70 basis points (national)

Beneficiary: you and your children. Waiver coverage and stipend tiers are provincial; private schools subsidize at the local public rate with the gap yours — verify against local documents before enrolling. Student loans are loans, not grants — repaid after graduation — but they split "can't pay now" from "not worth it." Section 7 covered unemployment-period training subsidies and temporary assistance; with income truly cut, apply there first.

Missing regular high school isn't a dead end: secondary vocational runs through-programs and separate exams, and skill-post recruitment may lower credential bars

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The 2022 Vocational Education Law states vocational and general education hold equal standing. Secondary vocational schools run through-programs with higher vocational; higher vocational must reserve plans or separate exams for vocational graduates; employers may not bar vocational graduates. Missing the regular-high cutoff means switching roads, not stopping at junior high.

Cost
Free. One check of the provincial vocational-enrollment platform before exam volunteering.
Benefit
The 2022 law: "vocational education is a type of education of equal importance with general education" (Article 3); secondary vocational schools "may, per state provisions, implement through enrollment and training with higher vocational education in relevant majors," and higher vocational "may enroll by combined academic-quality and vocational-skill assessment," with provincial-plus education departments running unified enrollment platforms (Article 37). Article 53: vocational-school students "enjoy equal opportunity in further study, employment, and career development"; higher vocational and vocational-education universities "shall set aside corresponding proportions or separate examinations to enroll vocational-school graduates exclusively," and "employers may not set application, hiring, or engagement conditions impeding equal employment and fair competition for vocational-school graduates," with public-institution posts carrying skill-grade requirements allowed to "appropriately lower academic requirements" (national)
Note
Beneficiary: you and your children. These are statutory channels, not admission guarantees — through-program majors, quota shares, and vocational-exam subjects are provincial; check the current platform and plans, never transplant another province's experience. Run major choices through item 10's dimensions: on-site, non-standard environments resist replacement. School legitimacy: presence in the current provincial plan; certificates verified by item 8's three steps. Any "guaranteed placement" or "guaranteed pass" promise: refuse.

Study-versus-work as one problem: three years of early wages against decades of annual income difference

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Lay both options side by side. Early work earns three years of low-threshold wages once; continued study buys the yearly increment across the remaining 30–40 years. Urban China's return per schooling year ran 4.0% (1988) to 10.2% (2001) — dated, magnitude only.

Cost
Free. Half an hour of paper arithmetic.
Benefit
Estimates for urban China 1988–2001 — the returns to schooling: "rising sharply from 4.0% per year of schooling in 1988 to 10.2% in 2001," the rise mostly post-1992, tracking the growing higher-education wage premium. This is the usable domestic magnitude for converting "one more year" into annual income difference; the global average sits in item 7
Note
Before computing, deduct item 4's waivers and stipends and add item 2's mortality account. Data end at 2001, urban-only — never today's numbers directly; item 7's global 9% likewise. Results vary by person: expensive tuition, mismatched majors, and long programs can genuinely fail the arithmetic — a verdict on that program, not on schooling. Several items stay outside the formula: statutory credential bars (item 5), replaceability (item 10), and industry mobility. Beneficiary: yourself.

Memorize the baseline first: one more year of education, global average private return, about 9% a year

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Globally averaged, one more schooling year raises personal income about 9% yearly, women's returns consistently above men's. This speaks to formal schooling, not directly to any course. Use it as a ruler: a course demanding 30,000 yuan and half a year must answer whether its income change matches another year of school.

Cost
Free. Memorize the number as the yardstick for every "learn something" scheme.
Benefit
A review spanning 1950–2014, 139 countries, 1,120 estimates: "the global average private return to one additional year of schooling is 9% per year" — private meaning the part landing on one's own income. Higher-education private returns are rising; social returns remain high; women's average returns persistently exceed men's
Note
This is the global average for "one more year of school" — not a course's yield, not China's specific figure, a magnitude reference only. Its use is the ruler: any course demanding 30,000 yuan and half a year must answer for a year-of-schooling-equivalent income change. Averages also hide vast field-level and country-level differences.

Before paying for a certificate: check it against the national occupational-qualification catalog and the filed evaluation-agency list

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Some outfits run disorderly training and fee collection under "new occupation" and "skill grade" banners, some impersonating authorities — the HR ministry has run dedicated cleanup. Three steps before enrolling: is the occupation in the catalog, is the issuer a filed evaluation agency, does the certificate number verify on the official platform? Unverifiable means the fee is lost.

Cost
Free. One check, a dozen-odd minutes.
Benefit
The ministry ran a national cleanup naming the disorders: "some institutions and units arbitrarily hold training, evaluation, and certification under new-occupation qualification and skill-grade names, charging disorderly fees and issuing certificates indiscriminately; some conduct false or exaggerated publicity, even impersonating authoritative institutions." Measures: joint enforcement with cyberspace, public security, and market regulation, "severely striking counterfeit appraisal institutions and evaluation-certificate issuance in the name of HR-filed agencies"; noncompliant promotion shut down; the public guided to "know certificate-verification channels and judge legality and value"
Note
Verify in order: occupation in the National Occupational Qualification Catalog (absent means no national qualification); issuer among HR-filed evaluation agencies; certificate number findable on the official skill-talent evaluation platform. Training through subsidized government channels first — never straight to commercial classes

2025 through end-2027, the state plans 30-million-plus subsidized training seats. Money flows from employment-assistance funds, unemployment insurance, and enterprise education budgets. Cost
Free or heavily reduced; the training itself costs time. The hard part: checking the subsidy catalog before impulse-enrolling.
Benefit
The national scale is explicit: 2025 through 2027, "subsidized training of over 30 million person-times focusing on high-end industries, urgent sectors, and key employment groups." Note
Claiming and amounts are provincial; the entry points are the local HR bureau's training-subsidy catalog and public training bases. Section 7 covered unemployment-period training subsidies (3 claims per person) and social-insurance subsidies; the employed start with the employer's education budget. When picking skills, weigh "does it need hands, does it need on-site judgment" — the hardest for automation to displace

Grade BValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

US estimates put about 47% of jobs at high computerization risk — later task-level estimates ran far lower. The machines' barriers are three: manual dexterity, generating novelty, and dealing with people. On-site, non-standard, judgment-heavy work resists; fixed-procedure information work runs highest risk.

Cost
Free. Run candidate trades through this dimension first.
Benefit
Rating 702 US occupations by "probability of computerization" put about 47% of employment in the high-risk band. The model's drivers are three "engineering bottlenecks" machines hadn't crossed: perception and manipulation — finger and manual dexterity, working in cramped awkward spaces; creative intelligence; and social intelligence. Non-standard environments demanding hand skill and live judgment run consistently lower replacement probability — structural, not incidental. Fixed-procedure, information-processing posts run highest
Note
Contested: this began as a 2013 unpublished working paper rating whole occupations; later task-level work found far lower high-risk shares, and it never dates the transition. Use it for the three bottlenecks, not the 47%. On-site installation, maintenance, and care resist replacement over pure paperwork for exactly this reason — "learning a skill" should favor the on-site, non-standard kind.
Sources (1 references)
Frey CB, Osborne MA (2017). The future of employment: how susceptible are jobs to computerisation? Technological Forecasting and Social Change, 114, 254-280. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.techfore.2016.08.019

Before learning, confirm the skill has graded evaluation — and whether grades convert to money

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The state is pushing the "new eight-grade" worker system, asking enterprises to tie post wages to skill grades, with outstanding workers grade-certified regardless of seniority. It's policy direction with vast local variation. Skills carrying national standards and grade ladders can plausibly rise by grade — check before learning.

Cost
Free. One check.
Benefit
The state is advancing the "new eight-grade" vocational-skill system. The documents explicitly tie grades to pay: "strengthen skill-oriented compensation distribution... guiding enterprises to implement wage allocation doubly linked to post value and skill grade." Localities are to "increase evaluation and appointment intensity and batch counts above senior-worker."
