Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Life policies don't pay for suicide within two years — only the policy's cash value returns. Work injury recognizes nothing; the three work-death sums vanish. Debts carve the estate first, family inheriting the remainder — and carrying the health toll from item 4 besides.

Cost
Free. Just arithmetic.
Benefit
Insurance Law Article 44 governs death-benefit contracts: suicide within two years of formation or reinstatement voids the death benefit, save suicides while legally incapable of civil conduct, with the insurer refunding only the policy's cash value. Life coverage typically runs hundreds of thousands — hence "large." The Work Injury Regulations, Article 16(3): self-harm or suicide is never work injury or deemed work injury — voiding Article 39's three sums (funeral grant at 6 months of local average wages, dependents' pensions, and the one-time death benefit at 20× the prior-year national urban per-capita disposable income). Civil Code Article 1159: estate division first settles taxes and debts; Article 1161: heirs repay only up to the inherited value, and renunciation waives liability
Note
This entry counts only money; this section and Section 1 cover not arriving here. Article 44 covers only the first two years — stated for completeness, never as a timetable. The family's health toll: item 4 (spouses bereaved by suicide ran 70%–80% higher five-year mental-disorder incidence). Thoughts appearing: Section 1, items 25 and 32; rescue aftermath: item 33. Work-death standards: Section 19, item 15; estate procedures: Section 25, item 9.
Sources (3 references)
全国人大常委会 (2015 修正). 中华人民共和国保险法第四十四条. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4…；国务院 (2010 修订). 工伤保险条例（国务院令第 586 号）第十六条、第三十九条. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm；全国人大 (2020). 中华人民共和国民法典第一千一百五十九条、第一千一百六十一条. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…

30. School-age children

18 entries

Section 20 covered the newborn year; Section 18 counted the money and time of raising children. The in-between decade-plus, ages 3 to 18, lives here. The screen-time entry starts at 0 because the official bands are 0–3, 3–6, and school-age — splitting them apart would be less usable. This section answers: when "don't disrupt school" collides with "the body," what cannot wait — things with time windows that don't reopen. Whether academics should be this grueling isn't discussed; only windows and numbers. Entries 1–8, 12 (cycloplegic refraction), 13 (sealants), and 15–18 count death and lasting physical or psychological damage; 16 and 17 cover how households manage — no hitting, no berating, and parent classes teaching concrete methods; 18 covers never sending children into locked-down anti-addiction schools. Item 9 (no "myopia cure" products) counts money. Items 10 (sleep, homework, exercise, ranking rules), 11 (suspension with preserved enrollment), and 14 (gaming) count time. Drowning, traffic, helmets, HPV: Section 1. Infancy: Section 20. Scams and in-game charges: Section 5. Minors' own red lines: Section 9. Recognizing emergencies: Section 13. Parentally bereaved children: Section 29. None repeated.

1

A child reports sudden severe pain that keeps worsening: hospital now — never "hold out until school ends"

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Some illnesses count in hours. A boy's sudden one-sided scrotal pain is testicular torsion — the cord's vessels twisted, blood supply cut. Treated within 6 hours, 97.2% of testicles survive; at 19–24 hours, 42.5%. That pain waits neither for the bell nor the exam.

Cost
Free. Half a day off, emergency registration.
Benefit
A systematic review assembling 30 case series, 2,116 torsion patients — 1,283 banded by 6-hour blocks. Testicular survival from pain onset: 0–6 hours 97.2%; 7–12 79.3%; 13–18 61.3%; 19–24 42.5%; 25–48 24.4%; past 48 hours 7.4%. Banded wider: within 12 hours 90.4%; 13–24 54.0%; past 24 18.1%. The authors: the salvage window can run longer than the usual 6–8 hours — so go even if long delayed, never skip on "too late anyway"
Note
Tell boys in advance: sudden severe pain down there — say so immediately, no embarrassment. Torsion clusters in adolescent boys, many of whom endure in silence. Also hourly-counted: acute appendicitis (perforation with delay), diabetic ketoacidosis, meningitis — per-item delay tables weren't verified here. Their shared signature: sudden onset, steadily worsening, unlike anything before. Recognition and transport: Section 13.
Sources (1 references)
Mellick LB, et al. (2019). A Systematic Review of Testicle Survival Time After a Torsion Event. Pediatric Emergency Care. https://doi.org/10.1097/PEC.0000000000001287
2

Don't defer needed treatment "until exams end" — some windows follow bone age, not exam schedules

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Scoliosis is sideways spinal curvature; the brace is a rigid shell holding the spine straight. Worn while bone grows, 75% of children avoid surgical thresholds versus 42% observed only. The wearable window follows bone maturity, not entrance exams — waiting usually ends in surgery.

Cost
Free — the choice is early versus late; leave and follow-up take time, treatment costs sit elsewhere. The hard part: braces demand 18-plus hours daily, worn through.
Benefit
A multicenter trial took 242 brace-eligible adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis: 116 randomized, 126 preference. Failure pre-defined as progression past 50 degrees; success as staying under at skeletal maturity. By assigned arm regardless of adherence: brace 75% versus observation 42% (OR 4.11, 95% CI 1.85–9.16) — four times the success. Randomized plus preference pooled: 72% versus 48% (adjusted OR 1.93, 1.08–3.46). More daily wear hours, more success (P<0.001). The trial stopped early for clear benefit
Note
Scoliosis is the example because it carries a randomized trial, a clear window, and a school-physical staple (item 7). Same class: strabismus, amblyopia, caries, and elective surgeries like congenital heart repairs — all worse or costlier later. Ask the specialist for windows. School feared disrupted: compulsory-education suspension runs to a year with enrollment preserved — item 11.
Sources (1 references)
Weinstein SL, et al. (2013). Effects of bracing in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1307337
3

A child bullied: report to the school the same day and demand written handling; beatings, robbery, rumor-spreading go straight to 110

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Peer-victimized children run about 2.2× the suicidal-ideation odds and 2.6× attempt odds. Schools must investigate on report, discipline on finding, and report serious cases to police without concealment — so report same-day, demand the determination process, keep written records.

Cost
Free. The class teacher and the school's anti-bullying body; 110 when warranted. The hard part: withstanding "don't blow this up."
Benefit
Pooling 34 studies, 284,375 children: peer victimization tracked suicidal ideation at OR 2.23 (95% CI 2.10–2.37); across 9 studies, 70,102, attempts at OR 2.55 (1.95–3.34). Stable across sex, age, and study quality; cyberbullying ran stronger than offline. The School Protection Provisions, Article 21, list five behavior classes — hitting, kicking, slapping, biting, shoving, pulling; insulting, mocking, derogatory nicknames; seizing, extorting, or destroying property; malicious exclusion; and online fabrication or rumor-spreading — with advantage in age, body, or numbers plus intent, causing bodily, property, or mental harm, qualifying as bullying. Article 22 obliges staff noticing distress or injury to inquire and report; Article 23 obliges immediate investigation on report, referral to the bullying-governance body, parental participation, discipline on finding, and no concealment of public-security or criminal-grade bullying (national; since 2021-09-01)
Note
Unexplained injuries, school refusal, repeated loss of belongings — ask per Article 22's signals. The pooled analysis is observational — bullying alone doesn't provenly cause suicide — but direction and size are clear. The comprehensive-treatment plan separately demands distinguishing bullying from ordinary roughhousing: schools owe a determination, never "kids being kids."
Sources (2 references)
van Geel M, et al. (2014). Relationship between peer victimization, cyberbullying, and suicide in children and adolescents: a meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2013.4143；教育部 (2021). 未成年人学校保护规定（教育部令第 50 号，第二十一、二十二、二十三条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-06/02/content_561…
4

Two hours outdoors daily — the only myopia prevention backed by a randomized trial

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: large

Forty extra minutes of outdoor class daily in first grade cut three-year new myopia from about 40% to about 30%. The health commission's dose: 2 daytime hours daily, or 14 weekly. Cloudy counts; standing outside at recess counts.

Cost
Free, but daily time — mostly squeezed from homework and online classes. The hard part: every day, not a few times.
Benefit
Twelve Guangzhou primary schools randomized by school (intervention 952, control 951, mean age 6.6). Intervention added one 40-minute outdoor class per school day plus parental encouragement. Three-year myopia incidence: 30.4% (259 of 853 evaluable) versus 39.5% (287 of 726) — a difference of −9.1 points (95% CI −14.1 to −4.1, P<0.001). Three-year spherical-equivalent progression −1.42 D versus −1.59 D, differing 0.17 D (P=0.04); axial elongation didn't differ (P=0.07). The Ten Core Points require 2 daily daytime hours or 14 weekly, note cloudy-day benefit, and advise avoiding midday heat
Note
The trial ran 3 years from age 6; the 9.1-point gap protects some children, not all. The same Ten Points add: "one chi, one fist, one cun" reading posture; 20-second distant gazes every 20 near minutes; non-study school-age screens 15 minutes per session, 1 hour daily. "Outdoors" isn't "PE class" — recess outside counts.
Sources (2 references)
He M, et al. (2015). Effect of Time Spent Outdoors at School on the Development of Myopia Among Children in China: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2015.10803；国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2023). 防控儿童青少年近视核心知识十条（国卫办妇幼函〔2023〕278 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284…
5

Screens: none at 0–3, minimal at 3–6, school-age non-study use under 1 hour daily

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

The health commission: no screens 0–3, avoid 3–6, school-age non-study screens 15 minutes per session and 1 hour daily — prolonged near work brings early myopia. Screen evidence runs softer than the 2 outdoor hours.

Cost
Free. The hard parts: taking the screen away and parents cutting their own in view of the child.
Benefit
The Ten Points, article 4: "infants 0–3 do not use phones, tablets, computers, or other screen products; children 3–6 should avoid them as far as possible; school-age non-study screen use per session should not exceed 15 minutes, cumulative daily use not exceed 1 hour," adding that "prolonged near use of screens readily depletes children's hyperopia reserve, a major reason for early and high myopia." The 2018 eight-department plan matches and adds "the younger, the shorter the continuous use." Research runs weaker: a review of 33 studies, 11 pooled, ages 3 months to 33 years — phones and tablets alone OR 1.26 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.60, I²=77%); adding computers 1.77 (1.28 to 2.45, I²=87%); the authors say only "possibly associated," noting none of the 33 measured screen time reliably
Note
Grade B because the official text is banded regulation, not trial numbers; the pooled lower bound sits exactly at 1.00, authors saying only "possibly associated." Treat it as an enforceable house rule, never "no screens, no myopia." The randomized backing belongs to item 4. Preschool eyes: the same document mandates refractive screening at 1–3, 4–6, and past 7 — method in item 12. Language pooling: 42 studies, 18,905 children — more screen time, weaker language (r=−0.14, 95% CI −0.18 to −0.10); co-viewing and educational content ran positive (r=0.16 and 0.13) — correlation, showing only that screens don't substitute for talking with your child.
Sources (4 references)
国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2023). 防控儿童青少年近视核心知识十条（国卫办妇幼函〔2023〕278 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284… ; 教育部等八部门 (2018). 综合防控儿童青少年近视实施方案（教体艺〔2018〕3 号）. http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A17/moe_943/s3285/201808/t201… ; Foreman J, Salim AT, Praveen A, et al. (2021). Association between digital smart device use and myopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Digital Health, 3(12), e806-e818. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2589-7500(21)00135-7 ; Madigan S, McArthur BA, Anhorn C, Eirich R, Christakis DA (2020). Associations between screen use and child language skills: a systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics, 174(7), 665-675. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2020.0327
6

Treat myopia as lasting damage: deeper diopters, more retinal detachment, maculopathy, glaucoma

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Myopia neither self-heals nor recedes, and it isn't just "wearing glasses." Versus the non-myopic, myopic maculopathy odds run over tenfold at low myopia and hundreds-fold past 600 degrees; retinal detachment about 3× low and 13× high. Earlier onset and faster progression mean more to carry later.

Cost
Free. Nothing to do here — the doing sits in items 4 and 5.
Benefit
A review pooling studies to June 2019, banded by diopter: mild (−0.50 to −3.00 D), moderate (−3.00 to −6.00 D), high (≤−6.00 D). Versus emmetropes, myopic macular degeneration ORs 13.57 (95% CI 6.18 to 29.79), 72.74 (33.18 to 159.48), 845.08 (230.05 to 3104.34); retinal detachment 3.15 (1.92 to 5.17), 8.74 (7.28 to 10.50), 12.62 (6.65 to 23.94); posterior-subcapsular cataract 1.56, 2.55, 4.55; open-angle glaucoma mild 1.59 (1.33 to 1.91), moderate-plus-high 2.92 (1.89 to 4.52); vision impairment past 60: 1.71 (1.07 to 2.74), 5.54 (3.12 to 9.85), 87.63 (34.50 to 222.58). The Ten Points match: past 600 degrees counts high myopia with markedly elevated blinding-disease incidence, and "myopia is preventable and controllable but irreversible"
Note
All observational, with unusually large odds ratios; high-myopia maculopathy's CI spanning 230–3104 marks heterogeneity — magnitudes, not precision. Most complications surface in mid-to-late life; myopia itself isn't disability, and the corrected mostly see normally. Still, myopia isn't "just glasses" — worth delaying and controlling. Follow-up after diagnosis: item 12; never buy cures: item 9.
Sources (2 references)
Haarman AEG, Enthoven CA, Tideman JWL, Tedja MS, Verhoeven VJM, Klaver CCW (2020). The complications of myopia: a review and meta-analysis. Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science, 61(4), 49. https://doi.org/10.1167/iovs.61.4.49 ; 国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2023). 防控儿童青少年近视核心知识十条（国卫办妇幼函〔2023〕278 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284…
7

Read the annual school physical report yourself; abnormal findings go to a hospital the same year

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Schools run one physical yearly. Watch for overweight, obesity, malnutrition, spinal abnormality, poor vision, and caries — the most commonly shelved. Don't file the slip after the height-weight glance; abnormal items go to specialists that year.

Cost
Free — compulsory-stage physicals bill school operating funds.
Benefit
The 2021 management measures: yearly physicals covering surgical (head, neck, chest, spine, limbs, skin, lymph nodes) and ophthalmic (appearance, distance vision, refraction) exams; individual reports carrying findings, overall evaluation, and guidance, with overweight, obesity, malnutrition, spinal abnormality, poor vision, and caries as guidance priorities; education authorities filing and following up flagged students; compulsory-stage costs from school funds (national; issued September 2021)
Note
Grade B: this governs schools' procedure, not outcomes — it guarantees yearly checks and flagging, not follow-through. Physicals screen, never diagnose. Poor vision goes to cycloplegic refraction (item 12); spinal abnormality to orthopedics or spine surgery (item 2 — never deferred for exams). Both steps ride on the parent.
Sources (1 references)
国家卫生健康委、教育部 (2021). 中小学生健康体检管理办法（2021 年版）（国卫医发〔2021〕29 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-10/21/content_564…
8

Ages 12–18: one depression screen — and never treat school surveys as diagnosis

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

US guidelines screen 12–18-year-olds for major depression; under 11, evidence runs insufficient. Suicide is the second-leading killer at 10–19. School surveys are censuses, never diagnoses. A child voicing distress, or sudden shifts in eating, sleep, interest, or grades, registers directly at psychiatry or clinical psychology.

Cost
0 to tens of yuan for a clinic questionnaire; 12355 and 12356 are free.
Benefit
The USPSTF 2022 statement: screen adolescents 12–18 for major depressive disorder (grade B); under 11, insufficient evidence (I statement); suicide-risk screening in children and adolescents, insufficient either way (I). Suicide ranks second among 10–19 deaths; adolescent major depression tracks adult recurrence, other disorders, ideation, attempts, and deaths. The domestic Ten Measures build the three-tier system — class teachers, psychological teachers, psychiatrists — with one psychological survey per student per school year, referral-to-treatment and post-recovery re-enrollment mechanisms, and 12355/12356 both engaged (national; issued October 2025)
Note
Grade B: recommendation grades, not convertible numbers; US guidance with no domestic counterpart. Positive screens mean re-assessment, never diagnosis. Suicidal thoughts: Section 1, item 25; household response: Section 29.
Sources (2 references)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2022). Screening for Depression and Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.16946；教育部办公厅 (2025). 进一步加强中小学生心理健康工作十条措施（教基厅〔2025〕2 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528…
9

Never buy products or services claiming to "cure myopia" or "reduce diopters"

Grade BValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The market regulator states plainly: "under current medical technology, myopia cannot be cured." Marketing "recovery," "diopter reduction," "myopia cure" draws strict enforcement. See those words, exclude — no price comparison needed. Eye-care devices are medical devices, and platforms must vet sellers.

Cost
Free — and it saves the money.
Benefit
The regulator's November 2021–March 2022 campaign notice states: "under current medical technology, myopia cannot be cured," ordering strict enforcement against "rehabilitation," "recovery," "diopter reduction," "myopia cure," "myopia nemesis," and similar misleading claims; against TCM-name-borrowing deception; against false advertising with patient before-after imagery or efficacy guarantees; and requiring platforms to verify qualifications for eye devices (national)
Note
Grade B: enforcement criteria, not product trials. But "myopia cannot be cured" agrees across regulators and health authorities — "preventable, controllable, irreversible." The two evidenced measures: outdoor (item 4) and proper refraction and follow-up (item 12). Blue-light glasses: Section 6.
Sources (1 references)
市场监管总局办公厅 (2021). 关于开展儿童青少年近视防控产品违法违规商业营销宣传专项整治行动的通知. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-11/12/content_565…
10

Sleep, homework, exercise, and rankings carry written rules — schools falling short can be pressed

Grade BValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Written: primary students sleep 10 hours, junior high 9, senior high 8; primary mornings no earlier than 8:20, secondary 8:00; 2025 adds 2-plus daily exercise hours and no exam-score ranking. A chronically sleep-short child gets checked against these first — never blamed for dawdling first.

Cost
Free. Know the rules; raise them with the school or education authority when needed. The hard part: raising it.
Benefit
The sleep-management notice: primary 10 hours, junior 9, senior 8; primary start no earlier than 8:20, secondary 8:00; no required early arrival for unified instruction; bedtimes 21:20, 22:00, 23:00; training institutions end by 20:30, online live training by 21:00; no game service to minors 22:00–08:00 (national; March 2021). The 2025 Ten Measures add: daily comprehensive physical activity no less than 2 hours, encouraged "15-minute recesses," no exam-score ranking, no mechanical-repetitive or punitive homework, and a weekly "no-homework day" (national; October 2025)
Note
Both are departmental documents with wildly varying local execution — hence B. Their use: knowing what schools already owe, with grounds in hand when you talk. Adult sleep accounts: Sections 2–3.

11

A child at the breaking point can suspend schooling — enrollment preserved, up to one year

Grade BValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Suspension is a formal institution: guardians apply, schools confirm, superiors approve; one application runs to a year, renewable; enrollment stays preserved; return resumes where due. Provincial details govern — ask the school's academic office or the education bureau.

Cost
Free. Parents or guardians apply to the school. The hard part: accepting a pause.
Benefit
The Student Enrollment Measures, Article 16: guardians apply; schools confirm and report for approval; return processed promptly; one suspension no more than a year, renewed by reapplication; enrollment preserved throughout, with provincial implementation rules (national; January 2025). The Ten Measures add referral-to-treatment and post-recovery re-enrollment mechanisms and campus crisis-response plans
Note
Ask three things first: what medical proof, how enrollment records the period, and whether return means same grade or one down. Grade B: conditions, materials, and re-entry are provincial; nationally only the frame. The School Protection Provisions require registering dropout, suspension, and long-leave students — suspension is routine, never a special exception.
Sources (2 references)

12

Poor vision found: hospital cycloplegic refraction, then follow-up at the doctor's intervals

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Cycloplegic refraction drops the eye's focusing muscle loose before measuring — hospital-based and the most accurate myopia diagnosis. The health commission states the drops don't harm healthy eyes and effects reverse. Never take an optical shop's single autorefraction as diagnosis, never withhold glasses fearing "worse numbers."

Cost
Tens to hundreds for testing and glasses; dilated children face glare and blurred near vision for half a day to two.
Benefit
The Ten Points: cycloplegia with a ciliary-muscle paralytic followed by refraction is the "gold standard" in-hospital medical refraction; the drops don't damage healthy eyes, with transient glare and near blur reversing on stopping. Confirmed myopia gets timely correction — proper glasses correct blur and slow progression. Follow-up with normal corrected vision: preschool and primary every 3–6 months, secondary every 6–12; refractive screening at 1–3, 4–6, and past 7 monitors hyperopia reserve (national; July 2023)
Note
Grade B: official guidance without trial figures. High myopia leads to retinal detachment — follow-up isn't only new glasses. "Poor vision" on school physicals is screening; full eye exams follow (item 7).
Sources (1 references)
国家卫生健康委办公厅 (2023). 防控儿童青少年近视核心知识十条（国卫办妇幼函〔2023〕278 号）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284…
13

Permanent molars in: pit and fissure sealants

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Sealants resin-fill the chewing-surface grooves so debris can't lodge. Two years on, decay odds run about an eighth of unsealed: 16% of unsealed surfaces decayed versus about 5% sealed. Still effective at four years.

Cost
Tens to one-two hundred yuan per tooth; no anesthesia, no drilling, minutes; many regions run free programs for age-eligible children.
Benefit
Cochrane pooling 38 trials, 7,924 children aged 5–16, resin sealants versus none: first permanent molars at 24 months OR 0.12 (95% CI 0.08–0.19) — an eighth the odds — from 7 trials, 1,548 randomized and 1,322 examined, moderate certainty. Control caries at 16% of surfaces: sealed 5.2% (3.13–7.37%); at 40%: 6.25%; at 70%: 19%. At 48–54 months OR 0.21 (0.16–0.28) — a fifth. Conclusion: 11%–51% fewer caries at 24 months; no adverse events across 4 trials recording them; evidence insufficient between materials
Note
First permanent molars erupt around 6, second around 12; seal freshly erupted, undecayed teeth — caried ones get fillings. Many regions list age-eligible sealants free — ask the CDC or community health center; no verbatim national document was found, so no coverage or age details. Caries rides the physical's guidance list (item 7).
Sources (1 references)
Ahovuo-Saloranta A, et al. (2017). Pit and fissure sealants for preventing dental decay in permanent teeth. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001830.pub5
14

A child loving games: watch whether sleep, homework, and outdoor life got displaced — not just hours played

Grade BValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: small

True "gaming disorder" runs two or three per hundred; low-threshold adolescent-questionnaire surveys inflate it. Game companies' real telemetry shows playtime barely moves well-being. Minors legally play 20:00–21:00, Fridays, weekends, and holidays.

Cost
Free. Check weekly: bedtime, homework in, outdoor time.
Benefit
A meta-analysis of 53 studies across 17 countries, 226,247 people: gaming-disorder prevalence 3.05% (95% CI 2.38–3.91); strictly sampled studies 1.96% — variance driven 77% by questionnaire choice, with adolescents, low cutoffs, and small samples inflating. The telemetry study linked six weeks of real playtime for 38,935 players across 7 companies with self-reported well-being: nearly no evidence of playtime affecting well-being. The publishing regulator restricts minors to 1 hour, 20:00–21:00, Fridays, weekends, and statutory holidays (national / international; since 2021)
Note
Grade B: prevalence swings with instruments and the telemetry study ran six weeks. Gaming's commonest cost is displaced sleep and outdoor time — sleep rules (item 10), outdoors (item 4), screens (item 5). Charges and refunds: Section 5, item 9. Grades, sleep, and family relations collapsing together, unresponsive to persuasion: psychiatry or child psychology — never locked-down anti-addiction schools (item 18). Beneficiary: the child.

A child says they're gay: no scolding, no eviction, no "conversion" — the household's stance tracks suicide

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Among Chinese middle-schoolers, same-sex- or both-attracted children ran 3–5.5× others' one-year attempted-suicide rates. Abroad, adolescents strongly rejected at home attempted far more; those sent to "conversion" most of all.

Cost
Free. The hard part: parents digesting their own feelings without harsh words in the moment.
Benefit
The domestic survey covered 506 middle schools across 7 provinces, 150,822 students. Past-year attempted suicide among boys: 2.2% opposite-sex-attracted, 6.9% same-sex, 12.2% both; girls 3.1%, 8.9%, 10.9% — roughly 3–5.5× after adjusting for age, academic pressure, family economics, and bullying: boys OR 3.13 (95% CI 2.28–4.28) and 3.83 (2.85–5.14). The US study of 224 LGB young adults recalling adolescence: high family rejection ran attempts at OR 8.4 versus near-none; parents attempting to change their child's orientation, OR 3.08 (1.39–6.83); parents sending children to therapists or religious figures, OR 5.07 (2.38–10.79) (China / multinational / US)
Note

Legally, parents may neither abuse nor abandon children nor inflict domestic violence, with habitual berating and intimidation counting as violence. Low mood or "wanting to die": 12356 first (Section 1, item 25) or psychiatry (item 8). Why conversion never: Section 6, item 28. Beneficiaries: the child — and you.

Discipline without hitting — and without yelling or "stupid": frequently hit or berated children run more behavioral and emotional problems

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Frequently spanked children run more aggression and psychological problems, more estrangement, and more severe abuse. Whether spanking buys immediate compliance, evidence can't say. Thirteen-year-olds routinely yelled at or called stupid run more misconduct and depression later — parental warmth doesn't offset it.

Cost
Free. The hard parts: stopping hand and mouth in the flash of anger, then replacing the method — the replacement in item 17.
Benefit
Spanking first: a meta-analysis restricted to open-handed swatting pooled 75 studies, 111 effects, 160,927 children — 13 of 17 outcomes significantly and uniformly negative: childhood aggression d = 0.37 (95% CI 0.13–0.61), externalizing 0.41, internalizing 0.24, mental-health problems 0.53, poor parent relationship 0.51, low self-esteem 0.15, lower cognition 0.17, physical abuse by parents 0.64, adult antisocial behavior 0.36, adult mental-health problems 0.24; pooled d = 0.33 (0.29–0.38); immediate compliance unlinked (d = 0.14, −0.19–0.47, five effects). The narrative review of 69 prospective studies: physical punishment consistently predicts worsening behavior, with no long-term benefit; 7 dose studies — 5 finding more hits, worse outcomes. Yelling: 976 two-parent families, harsh verbal discipline at 13 predicting misconduct and depressive-symptom increases at 13–14 regardless of parental warmth — bidirectional, as misbehavior predicts later yelling too. Legally: the Anti-Domestic-Violence Law names beating, binding, maiming, confinement, and habitual berating and intimidation; Article 12 demands civilized parenting; committees must dissuade violations, and authorities may reprimand and order parenting guidance (national)
Note
Contested: nearly all observational; 72% of the spanking pool were correlational or recall-based. Adjusting for prior behavior leaves spanking at 0.07 externalizing and 0.10 internalizing — small, per that author. Another pool found "conditional spanking" beating 10 of 13 alternatives on compliance, while harsh or primary spanking loses. So the counter-side allows: rare conditional swats may not underperform alternatives; heavy, habitual hitting and berating lose by consensus. Occasional swats or a shout don't constitute statutory domestic violence — the law names beating and habitual berating or intimidation. Beneficiary: mainly the child. Others hitting your child: Section 8, item 43 (protection orders). Witnessing chronic abuse: anyone may dissuade or report to police, civil affairs, or education — for strangers' households, 110 or the residents' committee; never intervene physically door-to-door.

A hard-to-manage child and a self that can't stop hitting or yelling: take a parent class teaching concrete methods

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Classes teaching concrete management cut children's hitting and rule-breaking and improve parents' moods — in randomized trials. Parents' own hitting and yelling fall too, most right after the course, persisting smaller at one to two years. Shanghai trials worked as well.

Cost
School, kindergarten, and community parent schools are public and free. The evidenced classes run weekly or biweekly, one to two hours, four to twenty-four weeks, with home practice. The hard part: finishing and practicing daily.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled 13 trials — 10 randomized, 1,078 parents of 3–12-year-olds with conduct problems: child behavior improved, parent-rated SMD −0.53 (95% CI −0.72 to −0.34), independently rated −0.44 (−0.77 to −0.11); parental mental health −0.36 (−0.52 to −0.20); negative and harsh discipline reduced, parent-rated −0.77 (−0.96 to −0.59), independently −0.42 (−0.67 to −0.16) — short-term effects per the authors. The 346-trial screen's 60 trials measuring abusive discipline across 22 countries: abuse down at course end d = −0.46 (−0.59 to −0.33); 1–6 months −0.24; 7–24 months −0.18 — shrinking with time, mostly self-reported. Domestic trials: 81 Shanghai parents randomized to group Triple P beat waitlist on child adjustment, parenting, and mood, holding at 6 months; 191 rural caregivers in a self-directed course plus two group discussions cut abusive behavior about 33% (IRR 0.67) versus booklet-only at two weeks, with child behavior improving by three months (d = −0.40). The Family Education Promotion Law directs parental learning, parent schools at schools, kindergartens, and communities — free, nonprofit, with provincial-plus online schools and hotlines (national; since 2022-01-01)
Note
Grade A: Cochrane and pooled randomized numbers. The trials share features: concrete skills — play, praise, rewards, discipline — rehearsed in class with homework; materials-only and discussion-only were excluded, so single lectures sit outside the evidence. Local free parent schools vary and may not be this class — pick multi-week, practice-teaching courses; familiar names include Triple P, Incredible Years, PCIT; this book recommends no specific providers. The fading effect at one-two years means practice continues after the course. Beneficiaries: the child and you. Severe emotional problems: psychiatry or child psychology (item 8).

Never send a child into locked-down "anti-addiction schools" or "training camps": the law bars harmful methods, and children have died in confinement

Grade CValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

The law flatly bars methods harming minors' health to treat internet addiction. A Hefei special-training school shackled a newly admitted boy in a confinement room; about 44 hours later he was dead. Nanchang's Yuzhang Academy confined students; its principals were imprisoned, and courts refused parents' tuition refunds.

Cost
Free — and it saves the tuition. The hard part: holding back at the child's worst, refusing to hand them to outsiders for "closed management."
Benefit
The Minors Protection Law, Article 68: no organization or individual may intervene in minors' internet addiction by means harming their physical or mental health. Both cases carry judgments. First, Hefei, August 2017: an 18-year-old's parents signed with a training school to cure gaming addiction; staff forcibly removed him into a confinement room, shackled his wrists to the window bars, restricted food, water, and rest, and beat him; roughly 44 hours later he died — heat, restrained posture, deprivation, and trauma causing fatal water-electrolyte disturbance. On 2018-10-31 Hefei Intermediate Court sentenced the school head to 16 years for intentional injury and illegal confinement, four instructors from 1 year to 8 years 6 months; the Anhui High Court upheld on 2018-12-28, noting the school lacked approval and the defendants held no teaching credentials. Second, Nanchang: Yuzhang Academy operated 2013–2017; on 2023-04-28 the Anyuan District court convicted five of illegal confinement — four sentences from 2 years 10 months to 11 months with education-employment bans, one exempted — and refused the parents' tuition and travel claims (national / Anhui / Jiangxi)
Note
Grade C: individual cases without incidence statistics. The Hefei case rests on media reporting of the first-instance and appellate rulings — no court-original text found; the Yuzhang case on Xinhua's report of the verdict. For gaming itself, run item 14's checks. Grades, sleep, and family collapsing together unresponsive to persuasion: psychiatry or child psychology for diagnosis and treatment. A child already inside: bring them home. A child reporting confinement or beatings: 110. Beneficiary: the child.

31. The paths after eighteen

16 entries

This section counts money and time; the military-service refusal entry adds personal freedom. It's a route map, not one road's manual: the legal thresholds side by side, then the things you can only use by knowing — what service pays, the non-civil-service entries into the system, the two majors that lock staffing slots at college-application time, whether credentials can be backfilled, what to look for in a company for work abroad, social insurance without an employer, and the state-subsidized interest loans for starting without capital. The paths after eighteen far exceed these; only those with national public documents — thresholds and benefits verifiable line by line — appear. State enterprises, factories, seafaring, freelancing, continuing to university: all walkable, none with unified documents, none written from impression. Which road is yours. This section offers two things only: where thresholds are written, and which deadlines and qualifications expire. Study-versus-work and skill choice: Section 23. Overtime, injuries, severance: Section 19. Starting a shop: Section 12. Study abroad: Section 32. Unemployment protections: Section 7. None repeated.

1

First match the thresholds: twelve paths with age and education requirements written in black and white

Grade AValue: highMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Working requires 16. Military service: males at 18, relaxed to 24 for bachelor's graduates. Civil service: 18–35 with junior-college-plus. Self-taught exams and sole proprietorship check neither education nor age.

Cost
Free. Ten minutes against the list.
Benefit
Service per the Military Service Law: "male citizens who have reached eighteen shall be enlisted for active service; those not enlisted that year remain subject until twenty-two; university graduates relax to twenty-four, postgraduates twenty-six." Civil service per Article 18 of the recruitment provisions: "aged eighteen to thirty-five" with "junior-college education or above," adjustable with provincial-plus approval; Article 19 lists five exclusions — criminal punishment, dismissal from public office, joint-dishonesty listing. Firefighters: 18–22 with senior-high-plus; college graduates and veterans relax to 24. Military civilian personnel: 18-plus, entry-tier first-hire ceiling 35. Public institutions: society-wide open recruitment. Sole proprietorship: "citizens with business capacity... registered as individual industrial and commercial households." Self-taught exams: "citizens of the People's Republic, without restriction of sex, age, ethnicity, race, or educational attainment" — full-time enrolled students excluded. Government-funded normal students: six ministry universities only, integrated bachelor-master design, tuition and housing on central finance with living subsidies, early-batch admission. Targeted medical students: tripartite agreements before enrollment letters. Overseas labor: companies need commerce-department licensing — unlicensed organizers are illegal, and "no unit or individual may organize laborers to work abroad under the names of business, tourism, or study." Platform gig work carries no statutory education bar — insurance grounds in items 11–12. Employment: the compulsory-education law bars hiring school-age children, and under-16 hiring is banned outright (penalties in Section 23, item 1)
Note
Past the thresholds come political screening, physicals, and assessments — unpublished scoring, untraceable in the statutes. Vocational entries and funding: Section 23, items 4–5. Sole proprietorship ignores education but shops remain hard — capital, personal guarantees, exits: Section 12. Whether the state co-pays interest on startup loans: item 16. The funded-teacher and targeted-doctor paths lock at application day — costs in item 13. Overseas work's threshold sits in the company's license — item 14. No comparison of which road pays.

The year you turn 18: military-service registration by October 31; conscript service runs exactly two years

Grade AValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Registration is a statutory duty, not enlistment — registering doesn't mean serving. Males turning 18 register online by October 31; refusal draws correction orders, then compelled performance and fines. Conscripts serve two years.

Cost
Free — minutes online. Actual service costs two full-time years.
Benefit
The registration provisions: county-level military organs "shall, before October 31 each year, conduct initial registration of male citizens who reach 18 by December 31," primarily online self-registration. Refusal per Service Law Article 57(1): county-set correction deadlines, then compelled service plus fines. The law adds: "conscripts serve two years"; 17-year-olds may volunteer; sergeants "with twelve-plus years or meeting other state conditions" receive government-arranged work; thirty years or 55 brings retirement placement. The conscription regulations prioritize university graduates and allow enrolled students and fresh graduates to enlist from either home or school locality (national)
Note
Registration and enlistment are two different acts at very different prices. The two-year bans in item 3 punish only post-enlistment refusal. Females register voluntarily. Soldier-to-officer paths live in internal military regulations; the law says only that officers come partly from "outstanding active-duty soldiers" and academy admissions escape enlistment ages — no cutoffs or quotas here.

Refusing service after enlistment: two years barred from exit or re-enrollment, plus no civil service or state enterprises

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Registering then refusing costs a chain: no civil-service hiring, no state enterprises or public institutions, two years barred from exit, further study, or school return, and listing as seriously dishonest on national-defense obligations. "Sign up first, back out later" is an expensive idea.

Cost
Free — the price is deciding before registering.
Benefit
Article 57(1)(2) — citizens refusing or evading enlistment — draws the same correction-then-compulsion-plus-fine. Paragraph 2: "those refusing correction may not be hired as civil servants or staff managed under the Civil Servant Law, may not be recruited or engaged by state-owned enterprises and public institutions, may not exit the country or resume schooling within two years, and are entered into the serious-dishonesty list for national-defense obligations for joint punishment." Joint punishment: multiple agencies enforcing the same list. Article 58 extends to the enlisted — service evasion, duty refusal, or desertion ending in discharge, expulsion, or criminal liability draws paragraph 2, discharge adding fines (national; since 2021-10-01)
Note
This counts freedom and employability, not money. The chain punishes two classes — enlistment refusers and the discharged-or-prosecuted — never mere non-registration (item 2). Punishment presupposes "refusal to correct," county-determined; fine amounts are local and unwritten here. Decide before registering.

Student soldiers' two solid blocks: tuition covered up to 20,000 yuan yearly, enrollment preserved two years, dedicated master's quotas

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Enrolled students, fresh graduates, and new admits get their schooling years' tuition paid — actual amounts, junior-college and bachelor's capped at 20,000 yearly, postgraduates 25,000; cheaper tuition tops out at actual. Enrollment holds two years; master's admissions run a dedicated quota for discharged student soldiers.

Cost
Free — post-discharge paperwork, a trip or two.
Benefit
The 2024 four-department notice: tuition compensation, student-loan buyout, and tuition reduction "adjusted to no more than 20,000 yuan per year for junior-college and bachelor's students and 25,000 for postgraduates" from fall 2024, executed at "the higher of actual tuition paid or the national student loan obtained (principal plus interest before full repayment)," amounts above the cap uncompensated — so yearly payment equals the smaller of the higher-of-tuition-or-loan and the cap; 5,000-yuan tuition pays 5,000. Years follow schooling, not service: "years completed before enlistment count as compensation or buyout years; remaining years completed after return count as reduction years," with graduates compensated across the full program. Enrollment: the Veterans Support Law — "admitted or enrolled students retain admission status or enrollment during service, may enter or re-enroll within two years of discharge, and may transfer majors per state rules," with universities admitting veterans through separate plans. Master's: the dedicated "discharged student-soldier plan" — quotas carved out nationally, not convertible, institutions setting their own score floors "generally not above the ordinary plan's," longer service preferred at parity, 532 institutions in 2026 (national)
Note
Two further channels: exam-exempt degree-completion upgrades (junior-college soldiers finishing their diploma applying for bachelor's without the written exams — skill-assessed admission, from the 2022 intake) and +10 points on master's initial exams within 3 years of discharge (not stackable with the dedicated plan). Second-class-merit-or-above holders may skip initial exams. Participating institutions shift yearly — 523 in 2025. Tuition caps moved 8,000/12,000 (2019) → 16,000/20,000 (fall 2023) → 20,000/25,000 (fall 2024); the veterans ministry's 2022 summary still carries the oldest — don't copy it.

Only six situations bring government-arranged post-service work; the self-employed must report within 30 days

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

"Service guarantees assignment" stopped being general. Six situations trigger arranged work; two-year conscripts mostly sit outside. The rest is self-employment — with a hard deadline: report within 30 days of discharge approval, or forfeit placement benefits.

Cost
Free — one trip to the placement locality's veterans affairs office with discharge papers.
Benefit
The Placement Regulations, Article 25, lists six: sergeants with 12-plus years; decorations and honorary titles; third-class combat merit or second-class merit or above; first-grade commendations; war disability grades 5–8; and martyrs' children. Local governments complete placement within 6 months of receiving sergeants and conscripts; employers sign "no-less-than-3-year employment contracts, enterprises receiving sergeants with 10-plus years signing open-ended contracts" — open-ended meaning no end date. Awaiting placement pays local minimum wage monthly; failure to place for reasons beyond the person pays no less than 80% of comparable workers' average wage until placement. Placement barred for those expelled from the Party or criminally punished. Self-employment deadline, Article 51: report within 30 days of approved discharge; "absence beyond 30 days without justification deems waiver of placement benefits" (national; since 2024-09-01)
Note
The same day repealed the 2011 placement regulations — most online guides still cite the old wording ("second-class merit in peacetime or third-class in wartime"). The 30 days bind only self-employment; other placement modes follow their own schedules. Reporting issues the veterans preference card, from which payments and support flow.

Three post-service accounts: one-time discharge payment, service years as seniority, and 20,000 yuan yearly tax deduction for the self-employed

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

First, the self-employed one-time discharge payment by service years, augmented for merit. Second, service years count as seniority and social-insurance years, merging with pre- and post-service contributions. Third, self-employed veterans deduct up to 20,000 yuan of taxes yearly for three years.

Cost
Free — the military transfers your insurance and funds; you complete continuation at the local window.
Benefit
First account: the regulations grant one-time payments "by active-service years," funded centrally, standards set and adjusted by the veterans and military authorities; augmentation in five bands — decorations and honorary titles +25%, first-class combat merit or first-grade commendation +20%, second-class combat merit, first-class merit, or second-grade commendation +15%, third-class combat merit or second-class merit +10%, fourth-class combat merit or third-class merit +5%. Unemployed veterans may claim unemployment benefits with service years "deemed contribution years" — paid-without-paying — except retirees and supported-placement veterans. Second: the Support Law — service years count as seniority, merging with post-service unit years; pension, medical, and unemployment years "merge by law"; conscripts' and sergeants' service "deemed grassroots work experience." The Military Insurance Law: service years deemed employee-medical contribution years, merging with pre- and post-service. Third: the 2023 tax notice — self-employed veterans deduct "in sequence from VAT, urban-maintenance tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, and individual income tax, capped at 20,000 yuan per household yearly over 3 years (36 months), caps floatable to 20% higher" — deduction, not subsidy; enterprises hiring deduct 6,000 per person yearly, floatable 50%; effective 2023-01-01 to 2027-12-31 (national)
Note
The regulations delegate amounts; the checkable official figure remains the ministry's 2020 "4,500 yuan per full year of service," itself marked "adjusted over time," and Guizhou's August 2024 piece still cites 4,500 under the new regulations (TODO: no formal standards document found — provincial August-2024 attestation only). Never confuse local "one-time economic subsidies" — separately set and paid, Yantai's 2024 rate at 6,000 per year — with the central payment; most online "new figures" mix the two without sources. Conscript families also draw family-preference payments, standards locally set with central fixed subsidies — ask the enlisting county. The tax account deducts only against taxes due — unused when business is thin, hence "medium." From 2026-08-01, the Employment and Entrepreneurship Regulations add nationwide recognition of vocational certificates earned in service.

Missed at eighteen, three regular channels remain: self-taught exams, adult college entrance, open university. Exams ignore age and prior attainment — full-time enrolled students barred. Adult exams require senior-high or junior-college completion first. All slow; none asks how you did at eighteen.

Cost
Hundreds yearly in fees and books; the price is long self-study — part-time bachelor's-upgrade runs at least two and a half years.
Benefit
Self-taught exams: Article 3's open admission; Article 20's enrolled-student bar; Article 25's three completion conditions — all courses passed, thesis or practice completed, character assessment qualified — yielding state-recognized diplomas; Article 32: wages for non-employed graduates "identical to ordinary university graduates of the same type." The Higher Education Law recognizes the system. Adult exams: candidates are "practitioners and other members of society outside enrolled students"; senior-track requires senior-secondary completion or equivalent, upgrade-track requires junior-college graduation; minimum durations — full-time 4/2, part-time 5/2.5. Open universities: registration-based entry, credit certificates, credentials, and degrees per conditions (national)
Note
A fourth exists for current junior-college graduates — the ordinary upgrade exam, nationally capped by a 2007 notice at 5% of graduating cohorts, expanded from 2020 (that year +322,000) so the 5% line no longer binds; yearly arrangements travel unpublished ministry letters sighted through provincial forwards; eligibility is provincial and excluded from the main text. Since fall 2025, continuing higher education dropped "correspondence" and "part-time" labels for "non-full-time" — beware old-label marketing. Backfilled credentials and skill choice are different matters: Section 23; fast certificates and counterfeits: Section 23, item 8.

Two paths locking staffing slots at application day: funded normal students and targeted medical students — the price is six years' service

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: large

The state pays first; you serve six years where directed. Funded normal students: six ministry universities, early-batch admission. Targeted medical students: tripartite agreements before enrollment letters. Breach means repayment, penalties, credit records. Decide whether six years works before filling the form.

Cost
Tuition and housing free, living subsidies paid. The price: six post-graduation years without free job choice, breach meaning repayment, penalties, and credit records. The hard part: six years stuck in place.
Benefit
Funded normal students (2024 measures, replacing 2018's): central finance covers tuition, housing, and living subsidies; training targets prefecture-level and below in the central and western regions, "not targeted to municipalities, separately-planned cities, or provincial-capital urban cores (autonomous regions, border provinces, Hainan, Guizhou, Qinghai excepted)"; graduates return to directed prefectures' primary and secondary schools, "committing to 6-plus years of teaching," urban-post workers serving "at least 1 year in rural compulsory schools"; breach enters credit records shared with the national platform and personnel files, barring other public-employment recruitment until completion — "credit repaired upon completion"; unsuitable entrants may transfer to non-normal majors within 1 year by refunding; failure to earn the education master's degree and teaching certificate within the prescribed years counts as breach, with refunds and penalties; staffing resolved "within existing institution totals." Targeted medical students: tripartite agreements before the enrollment letter, "committing to 6 years of service at directed rural grassroots medical institutions," followed by 3 years of general-practice residency with original personnel and wage relations intact; breach records enter personnel files as integrity references for public recruitment, residency admission, and graduate admission; malicious breaches publish nationally on Credit China with joint dishonesty punishment; breached training years don't count toward service; unrefunded fees are legally recovered by county health authorities (national)
Note
The 2024 measures convert funded normal study to integrated bachelor-master; the "teach straight after bachelor's" line circulating online is the repealed 2018 version; pre-existing agreements run on the old terms. "Staffed" never means "walk-in": slots are carved from existing totals and posts are matched with hiring schools. Targeted doctors may leave after service — "upon completion, self-chosen employment should be approved" — and even breached records can clear by serving a further 6-plus years at other rural grassroots institutions, fees unrefunded. Medical adds 3 residency years, lengthening the cycle. Provinces run their own funded-teacher and targeted-doctor plans — check the current provincial documents.

Working abroad: first check the company's overseas-labor license — and it may never charge you deposits

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The law governs not you but the organizing company: only licensed, registered enterprises may send workers abroad. "Tourist visa first, convert later" marks illegality on its face. And the company may never take deposits or property guarantees from you.

Cost
Free — a dozen-odd minutes verifying the license and reading two contracts.
Benefit
The Overseas Labor Regulations: Article 5 — provincial or municipal commerce approval for operating qualification; Article 7 — licensed lists reported to the commerce ministry and embassies, "without the certificate and registration, no overseas labor operation"; Article 8 — "no unit or individual may organize laborers to work abroad under the names of business, tourism, or study"; Article 9 — licensed companies deposit "no less than 3 million yuan" risk-disposal reserves in designated banks, published; Article 10 — reserves covering refused refunds, unpaid wages, damages, and emergency repatriation; Article 11 — no organizing into gambling- or sex-related work; Article 12 — training before dispatch; Article 13 — personal-accident insurance during service; Articles 21 and 23 — written contracts with both foreign employers and workers, dispatch barred otherwise; Article 25 — "deposits or property guarantees may not be collected under any name"; Article 26 — contract filing within 10 working days; Article 29 — companies assist claims when reality diverges from contract, bearing liability when compensation fails; Article 31 — no dispatch where personal safety can't be assured; Article 37 — bad-credit records and publication; Article 39 — unlicensed operation banned and prosecuted; Article 40 — revocation for tourism-study covers, license lending, and vice-industry dispatch; Article 43 — dispatch without contracts or with concealed or false information: 100,000–200,000 yuan fines, responsible persons 20,000–50,000 (national)
Note
The compliant flow: company signs a written labor-cooperation contract with the foreign employer, then a written service or labor contract with you, covering work content, duration, pay, hours, leave, insurance, and safety risks, filed within 10 working days; you receive skills, safety, language, and local-law training and personal-accident insurance. Refused contracts, demanded deposits, and "leave first, paperwork later" mark the companies to avoid. Overseas-recruitment scams and fraud compounds: Section 21, item 5; travel notices and 12308: Section 21. The regulations set no personal education or age threshold — the gates are the company's license and the host country's permission; contracts only with locally approved employers, never foreign individuals. Reserves are tapped by authorities when companies renege — you can't draw them yourself, so complaints go first to the commerce department (Article 20's right). Projects over 100 people to one country require accompanying managers and embassy filing; smaller projects lack even that layer — keep contracts and transfers.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2012). 对外劳务合作管理条例（国务院令第 620 号，第五、七、八、九、十、十一、十二、十三、二十一、二十三、二十五、二十六、二十九、三十一、三十七、三十九、四十、四十三条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-06/11/content_109…
15

Remote work for an offshore company from home: tax-law domestic income — self-file the individual income tax, receive funds as "employee remuneration"

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Domestic or foreign turns on where you work, not where money lands. Remote work from China for an offshore company counts as domestic income, taxed in China; with no domestic withholding agent, you file yourself. Inbound funds travel the "employee remuneration" lane.

Cost
Free — annual reconciliation March 1–June 30 of the following year; annual-quota-exceeding receipts need an employment contract and income proof. The hard part: remembering to file.
Benefit
Implementation Regulations, Article 3: "income from services provided within China through employment, engagement, or performance is China-sourced regardless of payment location." Article 6 defines wages — employment income of all kinds — and labor remuneration — design, installation, testing, medical, legal, accounting, consulting, lecturing, translation, and other services. The Income Tax Law, Article 6: comprehensive income deducts 60,000 yuan plus special and additional deductions; "labor remuneration, authorship, and licensing count income after a 20% deduction" — wages count in full, so the two categories compute differently. Article 9: payers withhold; Article 10: self-filing where "no withholding agent" or "foreign-source income obtained"; Article 11: annual reconciliation March 1–June 30. Inbound funds per the Individual FX Measures: annual-total management with ID-only settlement within quota; Article 7 bans splitting to evade limits and false documents. The Implementation Rules, Article 2: quotas of USD 50,000 per person yearly; Article 10(7): above quota, "employee remuneration: employment contract and income proof" (national)
Note
Category turns on your relationship: an employment contract under the employer's direction means wages; project-by-project delivery means labor remuneration — they compute differently, so settle which you are before filing. Receipts within USD 50,000 settle on ID alone; above, hand the bank the contract and income proof — never split receipts to dodge the quota. This covers staying in China; physically working abroad runs item 14's channel. Four items remain unstated for want of verbatim-checkable grounds: VAT and invoicing; whether long-term operation needs a license or household registration; labor-law claims against offshore employers; and data-export confidentiality.
Sources (5 references)

Starting on your own: startup-guarantee loans first — up to 300,000 for individuals, half the interest paid by the state

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

If borrowing to start, look at the interest-subsidized kind first: individuals borrow up to 300,000 yuan for 3 years with the state paying half the interest. One hard condition often missed: at application, you and your spouse must hold no other loans — student loans, poverty-alleviation microcredit, mortgages, car loans, and consumer credit under 50,000 excepted.

Cost
Free consulting — one eligibility pass at the HR department, then paperwork at the guarantee agency and bank. The hard part: borrowed money returns due.
Benefit
The Special Funds Measures, Article 6: eligibility by key employment group — registered urban unemployed, employment-disadvantaged (including disabled), veterans, released prisoners, university graduates (including village officials and returnees), overcapacity-firm staff and unemployed, returning migrant entrepreneurs, online merchants, lifted-from-poverty persons, and rural self-starters — plus the clean-loan condition: "no other loans for the applicant and spouse at application, save student loans, poverty-alleviation microcredit, housing loans, car loans, and consumer credit under 50,000 yuan (credit cards included)." Article 9: "financial departments subsidize 50% of the actual interest rate; extended or overdue loans receive no subsidy in principle." Article 10: personal loans under 100,000 drop counter-guarantees. Article 11: individual loans capped at 300,000 yuan, terms at 3 years; partnerships flex to 110% of summed caps; rate ceilings banded — east LPR+50bps, central-west LPR+150, poverty counties LPR+250; "actively repaying, employment-driving, quality projects" may reapply up to 3 cumulative times. Article 8: HR eligibility first, then guarantee agency and bank. Article 12: provinces may widen scope and raise ceilings (national)
Note
Half the interest paid changes nothing about repayment. Section 12, item 1's stance holds: start only with money you can lose, never stake the household, never personally guarantee company loans, spouses least of all. Decided to borrow: this policy tier runs the cheapest — never consumer loans or private lending. Ceilings flex upward provincially; approvals follow the local HR department. The 2020 "200,000 individual cap" notice was pandemic-temporary — this 2023 text governs. Shop structure, licensing, taxes, and exits: Section 12; training subsidies: Section 7, item 13.

32. Study abroad: status, work, insurance, and home-country recognition

10 entries

Two accounts — money and personal freedom. No debate over going, no school rankings. Four things cost you if unknown: when visa status breaks, the work-hour caps, which insurance and fees are mandatory, and whether the diploma will be recognized at home. Covers the US, Canada, the UK, and Australia, figures country by country, sourced from immigration authorities and the Ministry of Education. These policies change faster than Chinese regulations do. All figures below are current to September 2026 — re-check every source link before departure and before every renewal. Embassies, 12308, and overseas medical insurance: Section 21. Study-versus-work: Section 23. Stolen accounts: Section 14; telecom fraud: Section 8. None repeated.

1

Before paying tuition: check the school against CSCSE's accredited-institution list

Grade AValue: very highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

For the diploma to count at home — civil service, state enterprises, hukou, professional titles — it must clear accreditation by the Ministry of Education's Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE). Schools outside the accreditable list mean tuition and years wasted. The lookup is free; do it before paying.

Cost
Free. One lookup at CSCSE's "accredited institutions" page, minutes.
Benefit
CSCSE maintains an accredited-institution query — searchable by country or name — covering whether the school's degrees fall within accreditation. The Ministry's cross-border education supervision site additionally publishes Sino-foreign cooperative-program supervision
Note
An agent's "Ministry-recognized" means nothing — your own lookup governs. Lists shift: in at enrollment doesn't guarantee in at graduation, so re-check yearly. 2

Watch the US F-1 rulemaking lawsuit: "four-year cap, 30 days to leave" was set for 2026-09-15 and suspended the day before — for now it's still "duration of status"

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The US tried to cap F-1 at four years with 30 days to depart after finishing; a federal court suspended it the day before effect. For now the old rule holds: stay for the duration of study, 60 days to prepare departure after completion. Suspension isn't repeal — the government can appeal, and the rule can return any time.

Cost
Free. Copy the I-20 program-end date into a calendar with a 90-day alarm — the I-20 being the school-issued eligibility document. Each semester, check the international-student office's notices for case developments.
Benefit
DHS published the rule on 2026-07-17, effective 2026-09-15: F-1 admissions shift from duration-of-status to fixed terms capped at four years, extensions applied for separately; 30 days to depart after study or practical training. On 2026-09-14, Judge Saylor of the federal district court in Massachusetts postponed the rule's effect under APA §705 — nationwide, the whole rule. The court didn't vacate it (vacatur denied without prejudice); the case continues. Under the court's order, F, J, and I entrants still enter duration-of-status, the 60-day grace period holds, and no separate extension applications are required
Note
Current to 2026-09-25. The government may appeal to the First Circuit, or DHS may reissue a revised rule — multi-year students shouldn't assume permanence. The court set an October 2, 2026 status conference; re-read school notices after that date. If the rule later takes effect, extensions need pre-expiry applications — nothing auto-extends. Under the current rule, early withdrawal changes the departure window; ask the international office. J visas sat in the same rule with different details — check your own category.

Work-hour caps are written red lines in all four countries — one hour over is a visa-condition violation

Grade AValue: highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

All four cap student work: exceeding risks visa cancellation, removal, and questions on every future application. US 20 hours weekly; UK 20 for degree-level and 10 below; Canada 24 weekly; Australia 48 per fortnight. Two jobs sum.

Cost
Free. Log your weekly hours. The hard part: employers saying "nobody checks extra hours" — never believe it.
Benefit
US F-1: on-campus work under 20 hours weekly during term; approved off-campus likewise 20; full-time on breaks — 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9). UK degree-level: 20 term-time hours; below-degree 10; part-time courses barred outright, self-employment and professional-sport or entertainment work barred — Appendix Student ST26.1, ST26.5. Canada eligible full-time students: 24 weekly off campus — IRPR 186(v). Australia: 48 hours per fortnight during session; research masters, doctoral students, and their dependants exempt
Note
US off-campus work needs prior authorization — no working while the I-765 pends. Canadian permits printed "20 hours" under the old rule still allow 24 while eligible — current regulation governs. The UK self-employment ban reaches far: freelance gigs, online shops, and self-run businesses all count.

Work permission tracks active full-time study. Leave, withdrawal, expulsion, or a transfer gap ends it on the spot — continuing to work is unauthorized employment. Many assume an unexpired visa means safe status; the status broke earlier.

Cost
Free. Before stopping classes, taking leave, or transferring, ask the international office where your status stands.
Benefit
Canada: no off-campus work during authorized leave, none during transfer non-study periods, resumption only with resumed studies. UK: permission follows course type; part-time courses can't work
Note
Before dropping below full-time, ask where the line sits — course-load breaks hit before work violations do. Expulsion or program termination typically cuts status the same day; never wait for the formal letter.
