33. Living with a disability

20 entries

This section covers life after disability has happened. Preventing disability belongs to Sections 1 and 13, not repeated. Four metrics, never converted. Emergencies and complications count mortality; subsidies, benefits, and litigation count money; schooling and procedures count time; psychiatric hospitalization, capacity, and guardianship count personal freedom. WHO's fact sheet gives three numbers. About 1.3 billion people — 16% of the world, roughly one in six — live with significant disability. People with disabilities may die up to 20 years earlier. They run double the risk of depression, asthma, diabetes, stroke, obesity, and poor oral health. Much of that gap traces not to the disability itself but to untreated illness, unattended school, unemployment, and inability to leave home. So half this section is the body, half procedures and rights. Five things already written elsewhere are pointed to, not repeated: the disability certificate (Section 24, item 10); disability grading timing (Section 24, item 9); the two disability subsidies (Section 7, item 8); work-injury labor-capacity appraisal and their money (Section 19, item 14); and long-term care insurance for severe disability (Section 17, item 7 — filed under elders, but with no age floor; the young draw it equally). Most beneficiaries here are you and family — the top two tiers. Points touching others are noted separately. Entries in this section are grouped by theme, with item numbers in parentheses. Body and rehabilitation: sudden severe headache after spinal cord injury (item 1), pressure-relief cushions for wheelchairs (item 5), no paralysis "cures" (item 6), rehabilitation at proper institutions (item 16), hearing aids (item 17). Benefits and subsidies: ask the federation for the full list at once (item 7), children's rehabilitation assistance (item 8), ramp-and-grab-bar subsidies (item 9), individual income tax reduction (item 11). Work and rights: disclose the certificate when job hunting (item 10), sue over disability-based refusal (item 20). School and travel: guide dogs in public places (item 12), exam accommodations (item 13), schools may not refuse disabled children (item 14), driving with C5 after losing both legs (item 15). Mind and caregivers: suicide risk in the first decade (item 2), caregivers watching their own bodies (item 4). Psychiatric disability and guardianship: voluntary psychiatric admission (item 3), capacity adjudication through the court (item 18), statutory guardian order (item 19).

1

After spinal cord injury: sudden severe headache and sweating — sit upright, loosen clothing, call 120 alongside

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

With spinal cord injury, part of the body's alarm wiring is cut. A full bladder or tight clothing may go unfelt while blood pressure spikes. The signals: sudden severe headache and sweating. Sit the person upright, loosen tight clothing, check for a full bladder — while calling 120.

Cost
Free. Three actions, tens of seconds.
Benefit
The episode is autonomic dysreflexia. A systematic review across Medline, CINAHL, EMBASE, and PsycINFO, 31 studies including 6 randomized trials: acute non-drug management is three steps — upright positioning, loosening tight clothing, removing the trigger — backed by clinical consensus and physiological data (evidence level 5). Antihypertensives come only with persistent elevation, prazosin carrying level-1 evidence and nifedipine and prostaglandin E2 level-2; prevention strategies target the genitourinary and surgical triggers, mostly supported at levels 4–5
Note
Grade B: no randomized trials behind the three field steps, only consensus and physiology; the review itself flags the mostly uncontrolled support. Medication belongs to physicians — no home antihypertensives. Lying flat raises pressure further, hence upright. Family and aides must know the three steps; never outlast it as ordinary headache.
Sources (1 references)
Krassioukov A, Warburton DE, Teasell R, Eng JJ; Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation Evidence Research Team (2009). A systematic review of the management of autonomic dysreflexia after spinal cord injury. Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, 90(4):682-695. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apmr.2008.10.017
2

The first decade after disability is the suicide high-risk window — never "look on the bright side" material

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Emotional collapse in the early post-injury years — your own or family's — is common, not a willpower matter. Two UK spinal centers' long-term follow-up ran five times the general suicide rate, with over 90% of suicides inside the first decade post-injury; those injured by attempted suicide run higher still.

Cost
Free. One phone call or one registration.
Benefit
The study followed 2,304 traumatic spinal cord injury patients admitted 1991–2010, surviving year one, discharged with neurological deficit, followed to end-2014. 63 (2.7%) were injured by their own suicide attempts. 533 died, 4.2% by suicide, 91% within ten years of injury. The age-standardized suicide rate ran 62.5 per 100,000 yearly (95% CI 36.4–88.6, the confidence range) — five times England and Wales' 2014 rate of 12.2. Attempted-suicide injuries versus other causes: death odds ratio 4.32 (P<0.001), suicide 9.46 (P<0.001)
Note
Spinal cord injury only — extrapolating to blindness, amputation, or burns is inference. What it establishes is the window: risk doesn't leave at discharge; watch for ten years. Someone to talk to: 12356 (Section 29, item 11). No stockpiled sedatives or pesticides (Section 1, item 25). Grief stuck past six months: psychiatry (Section 29, item 8).
Sources (1 references)
Savic G, DeVivo MJ, Frankel HL, Jamous MA, Soni BM, Charlifue S (2018). Suicide and traumatic spinal cord injury - a cohort study. Spinal Cord, 56(1):2-6. https://doi.org/10.1038/sc.2017.98
3

Psychiatric hospitalization runs on the voluntary principle — only two situations override consent

Grade AValue: very highMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Neither family nor an employer can hold someone in a psychiatric ward by say-so. The law recognizes two situations only: self-harm done or threatened, and danger to others done or threatened — the first requiring guardian consent. Disagreement with the diagnosis draw re-diagnosis within three days and an independently commissioned appraisal thereafter.

Cost
Free. Memorize both situations so you can say them aloud when needed.
Benefit
Mental Health Law Article 30: "hospitalization for mental disorders implements the voluntary principle." Compulsory admission requires a severe-mental-disorder diagnosis plus either "self-harm already occurred or danger of self-harm" or "harm to others' safety already occurred or danger thereof." Article 31: the first class needs guardian consent — refusal bars admission. Article 32: disputes over the second class support re-diagnosis demanded within 3 days of the conclusion, by two psychiatrists other than the initial diagnosticians; still disputed, an independently commissioned forensic appraisal. Article 35: re-diagnosis or appraisal failing to confirm severe disorder or hospitalization need bars admission. Article 78: deliberately hospitalizing a non-patient bears legal damages (national; since 2013-05-01, amended 2018)
Note
The reverse also holds — nobody can just refuse to send. Article 28: suspected patients who have harmed themselves or others, or pose that danger, are to be stopped and delivered for diagnosis by close relatives, the employer, or local police, and institutions may not refuse the diagnosis. "Send for diagnosis" and "keep hospitalized" are two gates, the first low, the second high. Article 75 sanctions improper restraint and misdiagnosis up to license revocation. Handling threats from someone nearby: Section 8.
Sources (1 references)
中华人民共和国精神卫生法（2018 年修正，第三十条、第三十一条、第三十二条、第三十五条、第七十八条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf744…
4

The person long-caring for a disabled family member needs someone watching their own body

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: large

Caregiver burnout isn't fragility. A US study followed 800-odd elders for four years: those caring for disabled spouses while reporting mental strain ran about 60% higher mortality than non-caregivers; caregiving without strain showed no elevation. What needs watching isn't caregiving itself but the chronic tension.

Cost
Free. Farm out part of the care; get your own physical.
Benefit
The prospective cohort, 1993–1998, average 4.5 years, four US communities: 392 caregivers and 427 non-caregivers, 66–96, all living with spouses. 103 died (12.6%) within four years. After adjusting for demographics, morbidity, and subclinical cardiovascular disease, caregiving-plus-strain ran 63% higher mortality than non-caregiving controls (RR 1.63, 95% CI 1.00–2.65, the confidence range); caregiving without strain (RR 1.08, 0.61–1.90) and disabled-spouse-without-caregiving (RR 1.37, 0.73–2.58) showed no adjusted elevation
Note
Contested: the confidence interval's lower bound sits exactly at 1.00 — no-difference not fully excluded. The population is US spouse-cohabiting elders caring for spouses; extrapolating to those caring for younger disabled family is inference. The direction holds: the strained run higher. Farm out what can be farmed — respite and day-care services through the federation and civil affairs. The caregiver's own chronic medication never stops (Section 16, item 1). Beneficiary: you.
Sources (1 references)
Schulz R, Beach SR (1999). Caregiving as a risk factor for mortality: the Caregiver Health Effects Study. JAMA, 282(23):2215-2219. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.282.23.2215
5

Long-term wheelchair users: pressure-relief cushions, and a daily check of the ischial and tail bones

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Ordinary foam breaks down skin under long pressure; sores heal slowly and infect. Nursing-home elders on pressure-relief cushions showed clearly fewer ischial pressure sores, though adding the sacrum erased the difference. Chairs themselves must be fitted, never one-size-fits-all.

Cost
A relief cushion runs hundreds to over a thousand yuan; the daily check takes a minute.
Benefit
The randomized trial ran in 12 nursing homes, 2004–2008, 232 residents over 65, 6-plus wheelchair hours daily, Braden scores under 18. Everyone got fitted wheelchairs, then randomized: skin-protection cushions (air, viscous fluid plus foam, or gel plus foam) versus 7.6-cm segmented foam, followed 6 months or to ulcer. Ischial-tuberosity ulcers: segmented foam 8 (6.7%) versus protection 1 (0.9%), P=0.04. Ischial plus sacrococcygeal combined: 21 (17.6%) versus 12 (10.6%), P=0.14 — no significant difference
Note
Grade B twice: 232 participants with the primary endpoint's P=0.04 barely clearing, and a frail nursing-home population extrapolated to younger users. Everyone was chair-fitted first — fitting and cushion work together; never swap the cushion alone. Bed-bound pressure care — air mattresses and scheduled turning: Section 17, item 8. Assistive-device subsidies: item 7.
Sources (1 references)
Brienza D, Kelsey S, Karg P, et al. (2010). A randomized clinical trial on preventing pressure ulcers with wheelchair seat cushions. Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 58(12):2308-2314. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2010.03168.x
6

Never buy therapies or devices claiming to "cure paralysis, blindness, or deafness"

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The Advertising Law closes the door: medical, drug, and device ads may not guarantee efficacy, cite cure or effectiveness rates, or feature spokespatients. So "walking after three courses" and "so many already recovered" are themselves illegal ads — no need to study the theory. Non-devices can't so much as mention treating disease.

Cost
Free — it saves money. The hard part: family hope resisting persuasion.
Benefit
Advertising Law Article 16: medical, drug, and device ads may not contain "assertions or guarantees of efficacy or safety; cure rates or effectiveness rates; comparisons with other drugs, devices, or institutions; or recommendations by advertising spokespersons." Article 17: outside those categories, "no advertisement may involve disease-treatment functions, nor use medical terminology or terms confusing the goods with drugs or devices." Article 4: ads may not deceive or mislead; advertisers answer for truthfulness (national; 2021 amendment)
Note
One test: whether it dares overpromise. Legitimate rehabilitation departments never promise walking in N courses. Report such marketing to 12315 or the local market regulator. Health-product scripts run the same route (Section 6, item 10). Refunds for purchases already made: Section 5, item 29. Beneficiaries: you and family.
Sources (1 references)
中华人民共和国广告法（2021 年修正，第四条、第十六条、第十七条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd6bd8…
7

After the disability certificate: one visit to the county federation asking for everything applicable

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The certificate itself pays nothing — it's a key. Behind it sit several independent benefits, each self-applied, never automatic. List them all in the first visit; cheaper than repeat trips.

Cost
Free. One morning at the federation; several departments follow.
Benefit
At least six benefits attach. First, the living and nursing subsidies (Section 7, item 8). Second, children's rehabilitation assistance (item 8). Third, basic assistive-device subsidies under Article 26 of the Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation Regulations. Fourth, home barrier-free renovation subsidies (item 9). Fifth, quota employment and employment services (item 10). Sixth, individual income tax reduction (item 11). Article 26 adds: "state-provided basic rehabilitation services for poor and severely disabled urban and rural residents through key rehabilitation projects, with subsidies for basic assistive-device configuration per state rules." Article 20: county-plus departments and federations use community resources to run rehabilitation venues or purchase services — rehabilitation guidance, daily-living training, rehabilitation nursing, device fitting, information, and referral (national; since 2017-07-01)
Note
The certificate process itself: Section 24, item 10. Standards and procedures are mostly provincial, differing severalfold between provinces. Record each item's name and re-verify against the local federation's site — never take counter oral assurances alone. No single visit exhausts it; re-ask yearly as policy shifts.
Sources (1 references)
国务院 (2017). 残疾预防和残疾人康复条例（第二十条、第二十六条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-02/27/content_517…
8

A child under 7 with disability or autism: apply for rehabilitation assistance at the county federation

Grade AValue: highMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The state runs a rehabilitation-assistance system for disabled and autistic children 0–6, covering surgery, assistive devices, and rehabilitation training — prioritizing difficult households, with localities free to widen ages and relax income conditions. This window carries the best rehabilitation returns; never wait for school age. Institutions come from the federation's designated list.

Cost
Free. One application at the county federation, then choosing among designated institutions.
Benefit
The State Council opinion covers qualified 0–6 children with visual, hearing, speech, physical, or intellectual disabilities and autism — including dibao households, registered poor households, welfare-institution children, disabled orphans, those under destitution support, and other economically difficult families, with the remaining determination by county-plus governments. "Regions with capacity may expand the age range and relax family-economic restrictions." Funding standards are set by county-plus governments by local capacity, beneficiary numbers, and disability category, with dynamic adjustment. The statutory basis — Article 26 of the regulations: "gradually achieving free surgery, assistive-device provision, and rehabilitation training for 0–6 visually, hearing, speech, physically, and intellectually disabled children and autistic children" (national; since 2018)
Note
Standards are provincial — search the local federation's site for the implementation measures; the designated-institution list sits with the federation. The documents require entry-and-exit supervision of designated institutions, periodic inspection, comprehensive evaluation, and blacklisting. Undesignated institutions mean full self-payment and hard recourse. Beneficiary: your child. Institutions promising "guaranteed recovery" get item 6's treatment.

9

Home ramps, grab bars, and bathroom renovations: apply for subsidies from county-plus governments

Grade BValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The Barrier-Free Environment Law writes it: county-plus governments support and guide home barrier-free renovation, granting appropriate subsidies to qualifying disabled and elderly households. Projects usually lead through the federation with annual quotas — register early. Amounts and scopes sit locally.

Cost
Application free; renovations mostly subsidized with possible self-top-ups. Runs through the federation and subdistrict.
Benefit
Article 19: "county-plus people's governments shall support and guide home barrier-free renovation, granting appropriate subsidies to qualified disabled and elderly households." Article 18: existing non-compliant buildings, complexes, public venues, transport, and roads get targeted renovation plans. Article 62: any organization or individual may complain of violations; authorities "shall handle and reply promptly." Article 63: procuratorates may issue procuratorial suggestions or public-interest litigation over public-interest violations (national; since 2023-09-01)
Note
Grade B: the law says only "appropriate subsidies," amounts and eligibility wholly local — no national figures. Search the federation's site for "difficult severe-disability household barrier-free renovation." Quotas run annually — queue early. Elevator retrofits ride a separate housing-construction process. Non-compliant public facilities: complain under Article 62, which obliges answers.

Job hunting: disclose the disability certificate — hiring you saves the employer real money

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Employers must staff at least 1.5% disabled workers (provincially set); shortfalls pay the disability-employment fund per missing head at last year's average wage. Hiring you isn't charity — it's real savings. Say it plainly; the employer does the math.

Cost
Free. One extra sentence at the interview. The hard part: saying it.
Benefit
The Employment Regulations, Article 8: "no less than 1.5% of total staff, specific ratios set provincially." Article 9: shortfalls pay the fund. The fund formula, Article 8 of the collection measures: "annual payment = (last year's headcount × provincial ratio − last year's actual disabled staff) × last year's average wage." Article 16: small enterprises under 20 staff within 3 years of registration exempt. The Protection Law, Article 36: employers meeting or exceeding the ratio enjoy tax preferences (national; regulations since 2007-05-01)
Note
The argument fails for under-20 firms inside three years — don't bank on it. Fund relief keeps changing; the year's MOF notices govern. Quota employment demands real work: nominal-employment wage-drawing schemes defraud the fund and implicate you. Employment-difficulty certification and social-insurance subsidies: Section 7, item 12; training subsidies: item 13. Beneficiary: you.
Sources (3 references)

Disability reduces individual income tax — call the provincial tax bureau for the amount

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

The Income Tax Law allows reduced tax on disabled persons' income — amounts and durations delegated to provinces, so local rules differ, some capping yearly reductions, some cutting by percentage. Call 12366 or check the income-tax app's deduction items.

Cost
Free. One checkbox at filing or one filed record.
Benefit
Article 5: "reductions may apply, with specific magnitude and duration set by provincial governments and filed with the standing committees: income of the disabled, childless elders, and martyrs' families; and major natural-disaster losses." Article 36 of the Protection Law adds tax preferences for self-employed disabled persons and exemption from administrative fees (national; since 2019-01-01)
Note
Benefit "small": the law gives no numbers, and most provinces' relief runs hundreds to a few thousand yuan yearly. Modest money, but filed once it lasts — worth the trip. Only the local bureau's notices count; circulating comparison tables are perennially stale. Self-employed: administrative fees exempt — raise it at licensing.

中华人民共和国个人所得税法（2018 年修正，第五条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf724…；中华人民共和国残疾人保障法（第三十六条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c…

Guide dogs enter public places and transit; blind riders ride city transit free

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The law obliges public venues and transit to accommodate guide, hearing, and service dogs. Blind persons ride city buses, metros, and ferries free with valid documents; disabled persons carry necessary aids free. Say both aloud when blocked; complain when refused.

Cost
Free. The hard part: citing the statute when blocked, possibly standing your ground.
Benefit
Barrier-Free Law Article 46: "public venue operators and transport facilities and vehicles shall accommodate disabled persons' guide dogs, hearing dogs, and other service dogs." Article 35: hotlines and emergency systems gradually gain voice, large print, braille, and one-touch access. Article 62: anyone may complain of violations, with prompt handling and replies. Protection Law Article 50: "blind persons ride city buses, trolleybuses, metros, and ferries free with valid documents; braille materials post free." Counties-plus give transit convenience and discounts, with necessary aids carried free (national; since 2023-09-01)
Note
The law says "accommodate" without penalties — standoff moments may not resolve instantly. A statute screenshot on the phone beats memorized numbers. Unresolved on the spot: complain under Article 62, which obliges replies. Rail and aviation run their own rules — call ahead. "Valid documents" vary locally; ask the federation which count.

中华人民共和国无障碍环境建设法（第三十五条、第四十六条、第六十二条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80818188d7430b0189018493…；中华人民共和国残疾人保障法（第五十条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c…
13

Exam accommodations for disabled examinees: braille papers earn 50% more time

Grade AValue: averageMetric: timeMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Disabled examinees may request braille or large-print papers, exemption from foreign-language listening, separate exam rooms, hearing aids and wheelchairs in, and extended time. None arrive automatically — written applications on the provincial schedule, with a second-generation-plus disability certificate. Results contestable through the provincial education department.

Cost
Free. One written application within the province's window, plus on-site confirmation.
Benefit
The management provisions, Article 5, list twelve accommodations — braille, large-print, or standard papers for the visually disabled; listening exemption for the hearing disabled; permitted devices from braille styli and slates through electronic magnifiers, white canes, hearing aids, cochlear implants, wheelchairs, and walkers; the extensions: "braille-paper users gain 50% beyond the standard duration; large-print or standard-paper users and those unable to write normally gain 30%." Plus priority entry, separate standardized rooms, guides, and sign-language interpreters. Article 7: formal written application per provincial rules with the certificate; expert on-site confirmation and evaluation; the province issues a Notification Letter. Article 8: disputes go to the provincial education department for review. Article 9: listening-exempted foreign-language scores compute as written score × total / written total. Article 18: other national education exams may refer to these provisions (national; effective 2017-04-07)
Note
Application windows are provincial and printed in the year's enrollment rules — missed is gone, so confirm timing on the provincial examination authority's site in the fall of senior year. Article 18 extends by reference to graduate exams and adult exams. Schools not refusing enrollment: item 14. Beneficiary: you or your child.

Disabled children applying to school may not be refused; those unable to attend get home-delivered teaching arranged by the education bureau

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Kindergartens and schools of every level may not refuse qualifying disabled applicants, ordinary vocational schools included. Children needing full-time care, unable to attend, get home-delivered or remote teaching arranged by the county bureau — with enrollment. Admission and transfer decisions come from the bureau's expert committee, never the school alone.

Cost
Free. One application, possibly one evaluation; escalation to the education bureau when schools stall.
Benefit
The Education Regulations, Article 7: "preschool institutions, schools at all levels, and other educational institutions implementing disability education may not refuse qualifying disabled applicants." Article 29: ordinary vocational schools may not refuse disabled applicants meeting national admission standards. Children needing personal care and unable to attend receive compulsory education via home-delivered or remote teaching arranged by county education authorities, enrolled in the records. Article 20: county bureaus with health, civil affairs, and the federation establish expert committees assessing physical condition, educability, and school adaptation, with admission and transfer recommendations — the results the child's privacy, confidentiality-bound. Article 23: mainstreamed disabled students may follow ordinary curriculum with "moderately flexible" requirements. Article 52: necessary support and accommodations available on request for national exams (national; since 2017-05-01)
Note
A school's oral "we lack the facilities" counts for nothing — demand it in writing and take the letter to the county bureau. The evaluation comes through the bureau's expert committee. Article 23's "moderate flexibility" is potent when grades are used to push children out. Bullying evidence and school procedures: Section 30, item 3. Exam accommodations: item 13. Beneficiary: your child.

Losing the right leg or both legs still licenses driving — the class is C5

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: highTime: highWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Missing or immobile right or both legs, but able to sit independently with qualifying arms, licenses the disabled-person automatic small-car class — C5. A missing palm qualifies too. Monocular vision and hearing impairment each carry their own classes. Physicals run at provincially designated hospitals.

Cost
Tuition near ordinary licenses — a few thousand yuan mostly. The car needs hand controls. Physicals every three years.
Benefit
The licensing regulation's Annex 1, item 8: "right or both lower limbs missing or functionless but able to sit independently, upper limbs meeting item 5, may apply for the disabled-person automatic small passenger class; one palm missing, the other thumb sound with two other sound fingers, upper limbs normal and lower limbs meeting item 6, likewise." Item 6: isolated left-leg loss with a sound right leg licenses small automatics. Vision: "monocularly impaired with the better eye at 5.0-plus corrected or naked, horizontal field 150 degrees" licenses small cars, automatics, low-speed trucks, tri-wheelers, and the disabled class. Hearing: aided discrimination of sound direction licenses small cars and automatics, worn while driving. Article 85: disability-class physicals issued by provincially designated institutions; holders examine every three years, certificates submitted within 30 days of the scoring cycle's end. Article 78: the disabled-vehicle sign displayed while driving (national; Order 172, since 2025-01-01)
Note
Far lower-threshold: the powered wheelchair — the Road Traffic Law lists it as a non-motor vehicle, no license; Article 58 caps it at 15 km/h in bike lanes. C5 cars need hand throttle and brake from qualified converters, then registration change at the DMV. Missing three consecutive physicals within a year cancels the license.

16

Rehabilitation at proper institutions with rehabilitation-medicine departments — intensity follows the therapist, never more-is-better

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: highTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Taking the person home to rest and wait out natural recovery is the commonest mistake. Organized multidisciplinary stroke-unit care leaves more people alive and home-dwelling at one year. But never self-escalate: earlier-and-harder activity within 24 hours of stroke worsened three-month outcomes. How much and when — the rehabilitation physician and therapist decide.

Cost
Inpatient rehabilitation runs hundreds daily, self-paid portions varying; months of daily, tedious practice.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled 29 trials, 5,902 participants, organized inpatient stroke-unit care versus alternatives: at final follow-up (median 1 year), poor outcomes (death, disability, or institutional care) OR 0.77 (95% CI 0.69–0.87, the confidence range), death OR 0.76 (0.66–0.88), death-or-dependence OR 0.75 (0.66–0.85), moderate certainty — per 100 treated, 2 more alive, 6 more living at home, 6 more independent. Conversely AVERT randomized 2,104 patients across 56 acute stroke units in 5 countries to usual care versus very-early high-intensity mobilization: good 3-month outcomes (modified Rankin 0–2) 480 (46%) versus 525 (50%), adjusted OR 0.73 (95% CI 0.59–0.90, P=0.004); deaths 88 versus 72, no difference (OR 1.34, 0.93–1.93, P=0.113)
Note
Contested: both bodies of evidence come from stroke — extrapolating to spinal cord injury, amputation, and burns is inference. AVERT refutes "earlier and harder," not "early activity" — nearly everyone in both arms mobilized within 24 hours; the difference was frequency and total dose. Pick institutions by rehabilitation-medicine departments and credentialed therapists, not the word "rehabilitation" on the sign. Referrals and deductibles: Section 24, item 1. Community rehabilitation and devices: item 7.
Sources (2 references)
Langhorne P, Ramachandra S; Stroke Unit Trialists' Collaboration (2020). Organised inpatient (stroke unit) care for stroke: network meta-analysis. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 4:CD000197. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000197.pub4；AVERT Trial Collaboration group (2015). Efficacy and safety of very early mobilisation within 24 h of stroke onset (AVERT): a randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 386(9988):46-55. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)60690-0
17

Hearing loss: get hearing aids — for hearing now, not to prevent dementia

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: highTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

"Hearing aids prevent dementia" hasn't held up. A near-thousand-person three-year trial found no overall difference — effects appeared only in the already higher-risk subgroup. Fit hearing aids to hear, converse, and catch oncoming traffic — not for a brain decades out.

Cost
Hearing aids run thousands to tens of thousands, mostly self-paid, with fitting and repeat tuning.
Benefit
The ACHIEVE trial, 4 US communities, 977 participants aged 70–84 with untreated hearing loss and no marked cognitive impairment, randomized to hearing intervention (counseling plus aids) or health-education control, follow-up every 6 months, primary endpoint 3-year global-cognition change. In the pooled primary analysis, no significant difference: intervention −0.200 (95% CI −0.256 to −0.144) versus control −0.202 (−0.258 to −0.145), difference 0.002 (−0.077 to 0.081), P=0.96. A prespecified sensitivity analysis found effect heterogeneity across the two source populations (interaction P=0.010): the long-running cardiovascular-cohort participants were older, richer in decline risk factors, lower at baseline — leading the researchers to conclude hearing intervention may reduce 3-year cognitive change in higher-risk populations, not in lower-risk ones. No attributable serious adverse events reported
Note
Contested: the circulating "aids cut cognitive decline nearly in half" comes from one subgroup, not the primary result — the primary result showed no difference. Fit the aids; drop the dementia rationale. Hearing-disabled examinees: listening exemption, item 13. Hearing-impaired drivers wear devices: item 15.
Sources (1 references)
Lin FR, Pike JR, Albert MS, et al.; ACHIEVE Collaborative Research Group (2023). Hearing intervention versus health education control to reduce cognitive decline in older adults with hearing loss in the USA (ACHIEVE): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 402(10404):786-797. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(23)01406-X

Declaring an adult "unable to manage their affairs" takes a court application — family say-so doesn't count

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: lowTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Whether an adult lacks or has limited civil capacity is for the court alone — neither family, employer, nor residents' committee decides. Interested parties or organizations apply; recovery supports restoration applications. The procedure both restricts and protects.

Cost
Court filing tens to about 100 yuan; appraisal fees usually thousands, advanced by the applicant; months to conclude.
Benefit
Civil Code Article 21: adults unable to discern their own acts are without civil capacity, represented by statutory agents. Article 22: those unable to fully discern hold limited capacity, acting through agents or with consent-ratification, while independently performing purely beneficial acts or acts fitting their condition. Article 24: interested parties or organizations — residents' and villagers' committees, schools, medical institutions, the women's federation, the disabled persons' federation, elders' organizations, civil affairs — may apply for the determination, and later for restoration to limited or full capacity. Article 23: guardians of the incapacitated are their statutory agents (national; since 2021-01-01)
Note
The special procedure runs faster than ordinary litigation yet still takes months — hospital diagnosis submitted, courts usually commissioning forensic appraisal at thousands advanced by the applicant. Signing or disposing of property without it risks invalidation — even a sold house can come back. And limited capacity never means nothing: acts fitting their condition and purely beneficial ones they do themselves — never blanket-proxy. Guardians: item 19.

中华人民共和国民法典（第二十一条、第二十二条、第二十三条、第二十四条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…
19

Adult guardianship follows the statutory order; guardians pay for the ward's harm to others

Grade AValue: averageMetric: freedomMoney: noneTime: mediumWillpower: someBenefit: medium

On incapacity, guardians come in order — spouse; parents and children; other close relatives; then willing persons or organizations. Disputes go to committees or civil affairs for designation, courts on appeal. While lucid, a written future guardian can be named. The ward harming others: the guardian pays.

Cost
Free; disputes run through committees, civil affairs, or courts.
Benefit
Civil Code Article 28's order: "(1) spouse; (2) parents, children; (3) other close relatives; (4) other willing individuals or organizations, with the consent of the residents' or villagers' committee or civil affairs of the ward's domicile." Article 31: designation disputes go to those bodies, courts on appeal or directly, "respecting the ward's true wishes and the most-favorable principle"; interim guardianship where protection gaps. Article 33: fully capable adults may agree their future guardian in writing. Article 1188: the incapacitated harming others — guardians bear tort liability, mitigated by diligent guardianship; damages paid first from the ward's own assets, shortfalls by the guardian. Article 1189: delegated care leaves the guardian liable, delegates liable for fault (national; since 2021-01-01)
Note
Article 33 is agreed guardianship — naming the person in writing while lucid forestalls most disputes (Section 17, item 1). The liability paragraph warns: delegating care to institutions or relatives leaves the guardian responsible, delegates liable only for fault — making guardian-liability insurance meaningful. Article 78 of the Mental Health Law: guardians abandoning patients or breaching duties bear damages.
Sources (1 references)
中华人民共和国民法典（第二十八条、第三十一条、第三十三条、第一千一百八十八条、第一千一百八十九条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…
20

Refused hiring, denied confirmation, or underpaid over disability: you can sue — but price the process first

Grade AValue: averageMetric: moneyMoney: highTime: highWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

The law bars disability discrimination in hiring, confirmation, promotion, titles, pay, and insurance. You may complain to the authorities or sue — but winning doesn't shift your attorney fees. So complain first, apply for legal aid alongside, then weigh litigation.

Cost
Attorney fees thousands to tens of thousands, yours; first instance 6-plus months, extendable; evidence self-preserved.
Benefit
Protection Law Article 3: "discrimination on the basis of disability is prohibited; insulting and infringing disabled persons is prohibited." Article 38: no discrimination "in hiring, confirmation, promotion, title evaluation, remuneration, welfare, leave, or social insurance," with employers owing appropriate conditions, protection, and workplace adaptation. Article 64: discriminating employers face correction orders; disabled workers may sue. The Employment Regulations, Article 4: "discrimination against disabled persons in employment is prohibited"; Article 13 bars discrimination in promotion, titles, pay, insurance, and welfare. The Legal Aid Law, Article 42: applicants proving membership in "specific groups — minors, elders, disabled persons without fixed income —" skip means-testing; Article 45: aid bodies provide barrier-free facilities and services (national)
Note
Process costs come first: first instance 6-plus months extendable, simplified 3; attorney fees sit outside Article 6's litigation costs, and Article 29's loser-pays excludes them. So the two cheap roads first — complaints to HR authorities or the federation for correction orders, and legal aid with means-testing waived for disabled applicants. Evidence is the hardest gate: refusals rarely leave written reasons — record what you can. Already employed: labor arbitration, evidence and deadlines per Section 19, item 8. Beneficiary: you.
Sources (3 references)
中华人民共和国残疾人保障法（第三条、第三十八条、第六十四条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c…；国务院 (2007). 残疾人就业条例（第四条、第十三条）. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_664…；中华人民共和国法律援助法（第四十二条、第四十五条）. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817b6472a3017b657782…

34. Don't let the home medicine cabinet hurt you

11 entries

Fever reducers, painkillers, cold medicines, stomach remedies, anti-diarrheals — most buyable without prescription. No prescription never means no rules. This section skips which drug for which illness, picking only the one-action items that dodge grave outcomes. All entries count mortality endpoints — liver failure, gastric bleeding, neonatal kidney failure included. The benefit mostly reads "one fewer serious incident," without research quantifying percentages; magnitudes follow consequence severity, with each note stating its grounds. Already covered: swallowed drugs or cleaners first aid (Section 13, item 20); finishing chronic medication (Section 16, item 1); prescription review for online drug purchases (Section 28, item 6). Beneficiaries: you and family — the top two tiers.

1

Before taking two cold or pain medicines together: read the ingredients — acetaminophen may appear only once

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Many cold medicines embed acetaminophen; two boxes together means a double dose, and overdose injures the liver. Among US acute liver failure from it, nearly three in ten died awaiting transplant. Domestic labels cap at 2 grams daily — and no alcohol while dosing.

Cost
Free. Reading each box's ingredient list, a minute or two.
Benefit
22 US hospitals prospectively registered 662 acute liver failures over 6 years; 275 (42%) were acetaminophen-caused, median ingestion 24 grams. Of the 275, 131 (48%) were unintentional overdoses — and 38% of those had taken two-plus products containing the ingredient. 27% died before transplant, 8% were transplanted. The 2020 NMPA revision requires OTC labels to state: overdose causes serious liver injury, with a suggested daily maximum of 2 grams, and avoidance of combination with other acetaminophen or antipyretic-analgesic products. US rules require the first liver warning to name three risks: exceeding the daily maximum, combining with other acetaminophen products, and drinking 3-plus alcoholic drinks daily while dosing.
Note
Acetaminophen is also paracetamol. Compound cold medicines whose generic names carry "氨酚" (as in 氨酚伪麻, 氨咖黄敏) contain it. Unsure — show every box to the pharmacist. Grade B: the US figures are case registries without controls — how many incidents label-reading prevents is uncomputable. Benefit "large" by consequence: nearly three in ten of those liver failures died outright.
Sources (3 references)
Larson AM, Polson J, Fontana RJ, et al.; Acute Liver Failure Study Group (2005). Acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure: results of a United States multicenter, prospective study. Hepatology, 42(6):1364-1372. https://doi.org/10.1002/hep.20948；国家药监局关于修订对乙酰氨基酚常释及缓释制剂说明书的公告（2020年第15号）及附件2《对乙酰氨基酚常释制剂非处方药说明书修订要求》（湖南省药品监督管理局转载）. http://mpa.hunan.gov.cn/mpa/xxgk/tzgg/wjtz/202003/t20200311…；21 CFR 201.326(a)(1)(iii)(A) Liver warning. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-…
2

Children's fevers: no aspirin, no nimesulide, no metamizole — including metamizole-containing cold medicines, none for minors

Grade BValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

None of the three for children's fevers. Aspirin links to Reye's syndrome — brain and liver injury, about 30% mortality in US surveillance, cases falling over 90% after warnings. Nimesulide is banned under 12; metamizole under 18.

Cost
Free. One glance at generic names and ingredients when buying.
Benefit
Reye's syndrome brings encephalopathy and hepatic steatosis, typically after influenza or varicella. US national surveillance 1981–1997 logged 1,207 cases under 18; 82% had detectable salicylates (the aspirin class). Overall case fatality 31%. Warnings began in 1980 — that year's 555 cases were the peak; from 1987, never more than 36 yearly. The 2011 SFDA notice bans nimesulide oral preparations under 12; the 2020 NMPA notice bans metamizole tablets under 18, with compound products (青蒿安乃近片, 重感灵片 and capsules) banned equally.
Note
Metamizole isn't first-line for adults either — labels warn of agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, and anaphylactic shock, reserved short-term for grave illness without alternatives. 重感灵 ("double-cold relief") sounds ordinary and contains metamizole. What children should take and by weight: ask pediatricians or pharmacists. Under 3 months, 38 °C means hospital directly (Section 20, item 8). Grade B: surveillance data — the case decline followed warnings temporally, without trials. Benefit "large" by the 555-to-36 drop.
Sources (3 references)
Belay ED, Bresee JS, Holman RC, Khan AS, Shahriari A, Schonberger LB (1999). Reye's syndrome in the United States from 1981 through 1997. New England Journal of Medicine, 340(18):1377-1382. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199905063401801；关于加强尼美舒利口服制剂使用管理的通知（国食药监安〔2011〕209号）. https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/xxgk/fgwj/gzwj/gzwjyp/2011051514510…；国家药监局关于修订安乃近相关品种说明书的公告（2020年第34号）及附件1至3. https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/directory/web/nmpa/xxgk/ggtg/ypggtg…
3

Over 60, prior gastric bleeding, or on anticoagulants or steroids: ask a doctor before ibuprofen-type painkillers

Grade AValue: very highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Ibuprofen, naproxen, and aspirin-type painkillers injure the stomach. In high-dose trials, ibuprofen users ran about 4× the risk of gastric bleeding or perforation. Older age, prior bleeding, concurrent anticoagulants or steroids, and daily drinking raise it further.

Cost
Free. One question to a doctor or pharmacist.
Benefit
The class — nonsteroidal anti-inflammatories, common ones being ibuprofen, naproxen, and diclofenac — was pooled against placebo across 280 randomized trials, 124,513 people. Upper gastrointestinal perforation, obstruction, or bleeding versus placebo: ibuprofen RR 3.97 (95% CI 2.22–7.10, about 4×), naproxen 4.22 (2.71–6.56), diclofenac 1.89 (1.16–3.09). All roughly double heart-failure risk. US rules require OTC stomach-bleeding warnings naming six higher-risk groups: over 60; prior ulcer or bleeding; on anticoagulants or steroids; combining another of the class; 3-plus drinks daily while dosing; dosing beyond label directions or duration.
Note
The paper's conclusions speak to high-dose use; a day or two at label doses isn't separately quantified. Many compound cold medicines carry the class — stacked with painkillers, duplication — read ingredients first. Doctor-ordered low-dose aspirin for clot prevention: never stop it yourself, never add another painkiller on top. Menstrual use and gynecology referral: Section 3, item 25.
Sources (2 references)
Coxib and traditional NSAID Trialists' (CNT) Collaboration; Bhala N, Emberson J, Merhi A, et al. (2013). Vascular and upper gastrointestinal effects of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: meta-analyses of individual participant data from randomised trials. Lancet, 382(9894):769-779. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(13)60900-9；21 CFR 201.326(a)(2)(iii)(A) Stomach bleeding warning. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-…
4

Children under 2 with colds: never self-dose compound cold and cough medicines

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The NMPA requires warnings on 14 pediatric compound cold medicines: parents shouldn't self-administer under 2; use under physician or pharmacist guidance. In pediatric trials, cough and antihistamine ingredients beat placebo not at all.

Cost
Free — and it saves the drug money.
Benefit
The 2021 No. 57 announcement revised 14 products' labels — including 氨酚麻美 oral solution, 小儿氨酚黄那敏 granules, 小儿氨酚烷胺 granules. The added warning: "parents or guardians are not advised to use this product on infants under 2 without professional guidance; use under physician or pharmacist direction." Precautions add "use strictly per label dosage to avoid overdose" and "avoid combining cold medicines with the same or similar active ingredients." A Cochrane review, 29 randomized trials with 10 in children: none of the classes beat placebo in children — cough medicines, antihistamines, antihistamine-plus-decongestant, cough-plus-bronchodilator. 21 trials reported adverse events, with antihistamine and dextromethorphan preparations running more.
Note
Many of the 14 carry "氨酚" — acetaminophen — doubling up with fever reducers (item 1). One reviewed trial found honey beating placebo, but never under 1 year (Section 20, item 6). Grade B: few trials per class, no pooled numbers. Benefit "medium" by judgment: no demonstrated benefit in small children, with overdose and duplication the risks.
Sources (2 references)
国家药监局关于修订氨酚麻美口服溶液等14个品种药品说明书的公告（2021年第57号）及附件. https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/directory/web/nmpa/xxgk/ggtg/ypggtg…；Smith SM, Schroeder K, Fahey T (2014). Over-the-counter (OTC) medications for acute cough in children and adults in community settings. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (11):CD001831. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001831.pub5
5

Past 20 weeks of pregnancy: no self-dosing with ibuprofen-type painkillers

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Past about 20 weeks, most amniotic fluid is made by the fetus's kidneys; this class can injure those kidneys and thin the fluid. US reports include neonatal deaths. Doctor-prescribed low-dose aspirin is exempt.

Cost
Free.
Benefit
The FDA's October 2020 safety communication: NSAID use from about 20 weeks can cause fetal renal problems leading to oligohydramnios — covering both prescription and OTC, including aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, and celecoxib. Reviewing reports to July 2017, the FDA found 35 cases of oligohydramnios or neonatal renal impairment, all serious — including 5 neonatal deaths, all with renal failure. Literature shows most oligohydramnios resolving within 72 hours to 6 days of stopping. The FDA advises avoiding the class past 20 weeks absent explicit medical direction; the 81-mg low-dose aspirin prescribed for pregnancy-specific conditions is exempt; for pain and fever, acetaminophen and others, after asking pharmacist or doctor.
Note
The FDA reminds that many OTC cold, flu, and sleep products carry the class — read ingredients. US OTC labels previously warned only for the final 3 months; this moved the line to about 20 weeks. Low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia: Section 27, item 5. Grade B: adverse-event reports without denominators — dosed-but-fine counts unknown. Benefit "medium" by judgment: severe outcomes, rare occurrence.
Sources (1 references)
U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2020-10-15). FDA recommends avoiding use of NSAIDs in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later because they can result in low amniotic fluid. Drug Safety Communication. https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-…
6

Self-bought omeprazole for reflux: 7 days maximum; swallowing difficulty, vomiting blood, or black stools means hospital

Grade BValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Omeprazole enteric tablets went OTC in 2022 — with labels limiting self-use to 7 days and no repeat within two months. Swallowing difficulty or pain, vomiting blood, bloody or black stools: don't self-dose — those signal serious conditions. The drug can also mask stomach cancer and delay diagnosis.

Cost
Free. Follow the label's day count.
Benefit
The 2022 No. 68 announcement converted omeprazole enteric tablets to OTC with a label template: indication "short-term relief of heartburn and acid reflux from excess stomach acid"; use not exceeding 7 days, unrelieved symptoms prompting physician or pharmacist consultation; no repeat within 2 months, recurrence prompting immediate care; never during swallowing difficulty or pain, vomiting blood, bloody or black stools; marked weight loss, repeated vomiting, or those alarm symptoms require ruling out malignancy first, since treatment may mask symptoms and delay diagnosis; over-55s with new or changed symptoms should consult; clopidogrel users should avoid concurrent omeprazole.
Note
Clopidogrel is the anti-clot drug common after stents and infarctions; omeprazole weakens it — ask first. Grade B: label rules without outcome studies. Benefit "medium" by judgment: what's avoided is delayed gastric bleeding or cancer, while most reflux stays benign.
Sources (1 references)
国家药监局关于奥美拉唑肠溶片处方药转换为非处方药的公告（2022年第68号）及附件2《非处方药说明书范本》. https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/yaopin/ypggtg/20220826171517123.html
7

Ordinary colds: don't ask the doctor for antibiotics

Grade AValue: highMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Antibiotics don't speed cold recovery; adults on them ran over double the adverse-reaction risk. Purulent runny nose under 10 days gains no certain benefit either.

Cost
Free — and it saves the drug money.
Benefit
A Cochrane review pooled 6 randomized trials, 1,147 people. Antibiotics versus placebo for colds: no significant difference in unimproved or persistent symptoms (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.60–1.14, nonsignificant). Adverse reactions ran 1.8× placebo (1.01–3.21) — adults 2.62× (1.32–5.18), children no increase (0.91, 0.51–1.63). Acute purulent rhinitis under 10 days: no clear benefit (RR 0.73, 0.47–1.13) with more adverse reactions (RR 1.46, 1.10–1.94, about 46% higher). The authors recommend against routine antibiotics in either condition.
Note
This 2025 republication's search ran to 2013. Antibiotics are prescription-only domestically — pharmacies sell on prescription, and leftovers aren't for self-dosing. Benefit "medium" by judgment: adverse reactions prevented, not deaths.
Sources (1 references)
Kenealy T, Arroll B (2025). Antibiotics for the common cold and acute purulent rhinitis. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 11:CD000247. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000247.pub4
8

Diarrhea: rehydrate first with oral rehydration salts; children under 5 get no anti-diarrheal drugs

Grade AValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: lowTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The priority in diarrhea is replacing water, not stopping stools. Mix ORS per label — never substitute juice drinks, whose sugar worsens dehydration. Under 5: no loperamide-type anti-diarrheals — severe cases bring paralytic ileus, potentially fatal.

Cost
A box of ORS runs a few to a dozen-odd yuan — keep one at home.
Benefit
WHO's treatment manual states plainly: "anti-diarrheal" drugs and antiemetics offer no practical benefit in acute or persistent childhood diarrhea — they neither prevent dehydration nor improve nutrition, some carry dangerous, sometimes fatal side effects, and must never be given under 5. Motility-slowing drugs like loperamide can cause severe paralytic ileus, fatal, and may prolong infection. Drinks too sweet in sugar draw water into the gut causing hypernatremic dehydration — soft drinks and commercial juice beverages named. WHO's recommended low-osmolarity formula (245 mOsm/L) cut unplanned IV infusions 33% versus the old formula; a Cochrane pool of 8 trials concurred (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.45–0.79, about 40% fewer).
Note
Buy by osmolarity on the label — the low-osmolarity formula. Bloody stools usually mean bacterial dysentery — medical care and antibiotics, not home rehydration alone. Benefit "medium" by judgment: the numbers compare two ORS formulas, not drinking versus not.
Sources (2 references)
World Health Organization (2005). The treatment of diarrhoea: a manual for physicians and other senior health workers, 4th revision. https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/43209；Hahn S, Kim S, Garner P (2002). Reduced osmolarity oral rehydration solution for treating dehydration caused by acute diarrhoea in children. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (1):CD002847. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002847
9

Painkillers: no more than 15 days a month, compound painkillers no more than 10 — or the headache itself may be drug-caused

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Chronic headache met with daily painkillers can worsen the headaches. The international classification calls it medication-overuse headache: ordinary painkillers 15-plus days monthly, compounds 10-plus, for over 3 months, qualify. Most improve on withdrawing the overused drug.

Cost
Free. The hard parts: counting dosing days and not popping pills reflexively.
Benefit
ICHD-3 sets the criteria: a pre-existing headache disorder plus 15-plus headache days monthly plus regular overuse beyond 3 months. Non-opioid painkillers — acetaminophen, aspirin, ibuprofen — threshold at 15-plus days monthly; compound painkillers (two-plus analgesic classes, or added caffeine or codeine, e.g., acetaminophen plus codeine) at 10-plus; alternating non-opioids sum their days. The classification notes multinational epidemiology placing over half of 15-plus-day headachers in this category, with most patients improving on withdrawal and preventive treatment working better.
Note
Painkiller names carrying "咖" generally add caffeine — compound, 10 days. Headache days climbing monthly means neurology, not more pills. Grade B: diagnostic thresholds, not trials. Benefit "medium" by judgment: headache-free days regained, deaths uninvolved.
Sources (2 references)
Headache Classification Committee of the International Headache Society (2018). The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition. Cephalalgia, 38(1):1-211. https://doi.org/10.1177/0333102417738202；ICHD-3 在线版 8.2 Medication-overuse headache（含 8.2.3、8.2.5）. https://ichd-3.org/8-headache-attributed-to-a-substance-or-…
10

Expired and leftover drugs: clear them out periodically, package into hazardous-waste bins — never keep them home

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Of children's unsupervised ingestions, nearly half are prescription tablets; about three in ten of those belong to grandparents. Clearing leftovers removes one thing a child can find. Cleared drugs go packaged into hazardous waste, or to pharmacies collecting old medicines.

Cost
Free. One annual medicine-cabinet sweep, a dozen-odd minutes.
Benefit
US emergency surveillance estimated about 640,000 ED visits (640,161) for unsupervised medication ingestions under 6 from 2004 to 2013 — about 59,000 (59,092) in 2013 alone. 2010–2013: oral prescription tablets led at 45.9%, opioids (13.8%) and benzodiazepines (12.7%) topping the prescriptions. Five US poison centers surveyed callers in 2017: of children ingesting prescriptions, 30.7% took a grandparent's; over half (51.5%) of the prescriptions had been removed from original packaging before the child reached them. The domestic National Hazardous Waste Catalog (2025 edition) lists household waste medicines and packaging as hazardous household waste; Shanghai's sorting guide files waste medicines — expired drugs, capsules, tablets, inner packaging — under hazardous waste, "discarded medicines should be deposited with packaging intact," with pharmacies' collections staged by district market regulators. The FDA calls take-back sites the best disposal route.
Note
Sorting catalogs vary locally — your building's posted list governs; Shanghai files herbal dregs under wet waste. Kept medicines stay in original boxes — never decanted into pill organizers — stored out of children's reach (Section 13, item 20). Leftover antibiotics: item 7. US fallback — mixing with coffee grounds or cat litter before trash, toilet-flushing for a few potent opioids — is the American practice; domestically, follow local sorting. Grade B: registries without a cleared-versus-not comparison. Benefit "small": the numbers are ED visits, not deaths, and the sweeping effect is unmeasured.
Sources (6 references)
Lovegrove MC, Weidle NJ, Budnitz DS (2015). Trends in Emergency Department Visits for Unsupervised Pediatric Medication Exposures, 2004-2013. Pediatrics, 136(4):e821-e829. https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2015-2092；Agarwal M, Lovegrove MC, Geller RJ, et al. (2020). Circumstances Involved in Unsupervised Solid Dose Medication Exposures among Young Children. Journal of Pediatrics, 219:188-195.e6. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpeds.2019.12.027；生态环境部等 (2024). 国家危险废物名录（2025年版），附录《危险废物豁免管理清单》第 1 项. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_11906/202503/content_…；上海市绿化和市容管理局 (2024). 上海市生活垃圾分类投放指引（2024版）（沪绿容〔2024〕278号）. https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/gwk/search/content/40b9feaa-53d…；上海市绿化和市容管理局、上海市环境保护局、上海市食品药品监督管理局 (2018). 关于规范生活垃圾分类有害垃圾全程管理的通知. https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/nw12344/20200813/0001-12344_574…；U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2025). Where and How to Dispose of Unused Medicines. https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/where-and-ho…
11

On cephalosporins or metronidazole: no alcohol during and 7 days after — including alcohol-bearing medicines like 藿香正气水 and cough syrups

Grade BValue: averageMetric: mortalityMoney: noneTime: lowWillpower: someBenefit: small

Some cephalosporins and metronidazole-class drugs meeting alcohol cause flushing, palpitations, chest tightness, and vomiting — severe cases dropping blood pressure. Not just liquor: alcohol-bearing medicines like 藿香正气水 and cough syrups trigger it too. Nothing from dosing through 7 days after.

Cost
Free. A week-plus without alcohol, and an ingredient check for ethanol before other medicines.
Benefit
The disulfiram-like reaction: Fujian's drug regulator's 2023 safety note — certain cephalosporins before or after drinking can trigger reactions that "seriously harm health or even endanger life": flushing, sweating, palpitations, breathing difficulty, blood-pressure drops, anaphylactic shock. Per the Pharmacopoeia's clinical handbook: cefazolin, ceftriaxone, cefoperazone, metronidazole, tinidazole, furazolidone, among others. "Alcohol and alcohol-containing medicines and foods are prohibited within 7 days of dosing" — chocolate liqueurs and 藿香正气水 the examples, the inhibited enzyme needing 4–5 days to recover. A Guangzhou hospital's 2-year series of 82 cases: cephalosporins 57 (69.51%), nitroimidazoles 10 (12.20%); alcohol from beverages 40 (48.78%), from ethanol-bearing medicines 31 (37.80%) — 藿香正气水, cough syrups, motherwort fluidextract; 68 mild, 9 moderate, 5 severe, relief within 1–3 hours, no deaths. The US metronidazole label bars alcohol during and 3-plus days after, including propylene-glycol products.
Note
Not every cephalosporin does it — laypeople can't tell them apart, so treat all alike, the cheapest rule. When prescribed, mention recent drinking. The note suggests 3 days before dosing too, admitting no authoritative interval exists. Flushing and palpitations: stop the alcohol; mild cases self-resolve, severe need the hospital. No alcohol with acetaminophen either — item 1. Grade B: case series and labels, no controls. Benefit "small": all 82 eased within hours, 5 severe, no deaths.
Sources (3 references)
福建省药品监督管理局（福建省药品科普与监管数据中心）(2023). 2023年"全国安全用药月"原创科普小知识——为什么吃头孢不能喝酒. https://yjj.scjgj.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/kpzl/qgaqyyy/202312/t2…；房财富, 涂星, 刘韬, 黄红兵, 邱孟, 梁蔚婷 (2015). 我院双硫仑样反应82例分析. 中国药房, 26(29):4089-4091. https://doi.org/10.6039/j.issn.1001-0408.2015.29.19；Pfizer (2026). FLAGYL 375 (metronidazole) capsules, prescribing information: Contraindications, Interaction with Alcohol. DailyMed. https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=a2…
